Welcome to the Smith Funeral Home Ltd.’s Website, 
serving families in the Brooks and County of Newell since 1951. 
We value our reputation for providing the highest quality and dignified funeral services with respect, compassion and personal attention to details to help your family through this difficult time. Our professional staff is committed to providing, assistance to every family. Recognizing that each family is unique, our staff provides personalized assistance to create a meaningful service that honors the life and memory of your loved one.
Smith Funeral Home Ltd. is locally owned and operated since 1951, by the Dale and Ron Smith Family.
Smith Funeral Home Ltd. own and operate the only local Crematorium
in the City of Brooks and area, since 2015
In order to give you peace of mind, we are now able to complete your loved one’s cremation in our local crematorium. 
We also offer many types of urns, including custom made urns personalized to your loved one's lifestyle. Urns maybe buried, kept at your home 
or placed into a Columbarium, which is now located in the City of Brooks Cemetery.
Smith Funeral Home Ltd. is excited to announce our
“Partnership” with The Heritage Inn, Brooks
1217 – 2nd Street West (1/2 a block West from the City of Brooks Cemetery).
We are now able to offer to all of our families, an “Exclusive Rate” for families to have a 
Funeral Service and Funeral Reception in one convenient location
and for anyone travelling, The Heritage Inn will also offer “Exclusive Room Rates” for all Smith Funeral Home Ltd. guests.
This simplifies the planning process by offering all services in one location.
These exclusive rates are only available through Smith Funeral Home Ltd. 
Please click here for booking information.
Please contact us for details of our Columbarium.

MONUMENTS
Smith Funeral Home Ltd. are agents for Southern Monument of Lethbridge, Alberta.
Southern Monument are the only memorial company in Southern Alberta with the ability to create a personal memorial from raw granite. Their craft people, which include design specialists and granite sculptors, can offer you a choice of many designs, as well as being able implement your personal touches to the memorial.
Each memorial starts with stone sourced from one of the premier granite manufacturers in the world – Rock of Ages.
Installation of Monument in surrounding area cemeteries
Inscriptions on monuments, niche doors and granite wall
Removal of grave covers
Aligning stones that have shifted
Sandblasting on stone (must be able to bring to shop and have flat surface & be sandblast-able)
Smith Funeral Home Ltd. are proud to be partnered with
ETERNITY'S TOUCH since August, 2013
Eternity’s Touch prides ourselves on providing families with exceptional customer service, quality and unique fingerprint keepsakes. We offer a wide variety of items through our extensive catalogue Our "patent pending" process digitally captures, transfers, and creates an exact replica of a person’s fingerprint, so you can be assured that as your loved one your keepsake is one of a kind.
With our quality and the speed our fingerprint keepsakes are crafted, we can achieve our goal to provide fingerprint keepsakes for the visitation or funeral service and provide comfort in your time of need.
Come and speak with Smith Funeral Home Ltd. about our products or visit our website at:
https://www.eternitystouch.com/

City of Brooks’ Handibus Specialized Transit Service. 
The City of Brooks will transport seniors and those with cognitive and physical disabilities
as well as anyone in the community that will require the service with short term disabilities to and from any local Funeral Service.
The cost to utilize the Handibus Specialized Transit Service is $4 per one-way trip.
Please browse our website to find additional information about our staff and services, as well as other resources to help you in your time of need. You can also reach us any time, day or night, at 403-362-4636 or Toll Free 1-866-362-4652.

Parkland Funeral Home | Red Deer | Eckville
Call us anytime - 24 hours service.
Eckville 403-746-2024
Proud to be the ONLY Locally Family Owned Funeral Home and Crematorium on site in Red Deer
"Honouring Families Since 1999" 
The only locally owned and operated Funeral Home and Crematorium
in Red Deer, Eckville and Blackfalds
Welcome
Welcome to Parkland Funeral Home. Whether you are looking for information about prearranging, funeral planning, cremation options, grief support, or assistance after the loss of a loved one, we are here to guide you every step of the way. As Red Deer, Blackfalds, and Eckville’s only locally owned and operated funeral homes, our priority is caring for families in our community with honesty, respect, and compassion. From the first call through to the final details, our dedicated team takes care of every aspect of funeral service, including transportation, arrangements, documentation, cremation, burial coordination, personalized services, receptions, memorialization, and aftercare support. We understand that planning a funeral can be overwhelming, which is why we provide everything your family needs in one place, with one caring team committed to making the process as simple and stress-free as possible. If you have questions or need assistance, our team is available by phone, email, or in person. We are honoured to serve Central Alberta families and take pride in providing trusted care when you need it most. Parkland Funeral Home is also proud to be the exclusive Central Alberta provider for the Cooperative Memorial Society, offering affordable cremation and funeral service options while providing the same compassionate, professional care our families have come to expect. We assist eligible families with applying for available government funeral assistance programs, including Alberta Funeral Benefits, Income Support, AISH (Assured Income for the Severely Handicapped), and other provincial programs available to support low-income Albertans during a difficult time. Formerly known as the Memorial Society of Red Deer & District, the Cooperative Memorial Society continues to provide families with access to affordable, dignified funeral and cremation options through Parkland Funeral Home.

If you have immediate need of our services, we're available for you 24 hours a day.

Alberta Owned & Operated.
Where Families Are Always First.
Burial, Cremation, Funeral Services 
Airdrie | Calgary | Claresholm | Didsbury | Red Deer 
Together... We'll See This Through
Alberta's Prairie Rose Cremation & Funeral Services was founded to provide all Albertans with affordable, dignified, and inclusive options to honour and remember a loved one who has passed. Locally run and operated, with over 25 years of experience providing compassionate and mindful guidance, we have refined our process to ease the stress and uncertainty of making final arrangements for a loved one. Our model of service places families first within the context of the communities that support them.
Our process could include meeting where families wish to facilitate easy and convenient planning, and the flexibility to help you coordinate the service that will be most meaningful to your family. We focus on options for burial and cremation that allow families to honour and respect their loved one as they see fit. We believe that every family is unique and our tailored services are designed to meet your family's needs. The amount of money that is spent on a funeral is in no way indicative of how much you loved that person.
When You Need Us, Where You Need Us
Your comfort is our priority. When you lose a loved one, simple tasks like leaving the house can take a lot of effort. You need a safe and comfortable space to ease the decision-making process.
This is why we come to you for a personalized consultation, in a space that works for you. At your consultation, we will explain your burial and cremation options including casket and urn choices. Almost all of the necessary tasks can be completed from your home so you and your friends and family can gather together with very little interruption.

text:
Froc, Dora Clara - Legacy Funeral Home
DORA CLARA (WOODS) PRETE (FROC), passed away in Cardston, Alberta on 8 June 2026 at the age of 92 (a hotly debated topic) 
Clara was born on 11 February 1934 (date also debated) near Melfort, Saskatchewan, the fourth of eight children, seven girls and one boy, to Ernest Henry Woods and Velma Adeline Lucy Snider. The family farm was near the hamlet of Pathlow and that is where she attended school. At an early age she learned to play the piano and later the accordion and as a teen she played the organ for the United Church congregation in Pathlow and the accordion with a group of friends for community dances and socials. 
She and her sister, Trudy who is barely a year younger than her, were always very close, “joined at the hip” you might say. They did everything together. Trudy began dating a handsome Italian from a neighbouring community and he, as customs were at the time, brought his brother along to chaperone. Well, the electricity was immediate and eternal. The two couples were married 24 July 1953 in a double wedding ceremony. They even went on their honeymoon together. The two couples moved to the Prete farm near Shannonview, Saskatchewan. Eventually, economics led Lyle and Trudy to move to Alberta and after a few years Norman and Clara followed.
Six sons were born to Norman and Clara during the Saskatchewan years. When circumstances prevented having more children they added five wonderful daughters through other means. And because of her immense capacity to love, she mothered dozens more through the years. After Norm’s death she remarried an old friend (one of the members of the musical group from her teens) Marcel Froc. At that time she began mothering his two children. 
Most of her working career also involved mothering only then it was seniors she cared for. She worked several years at the Grandview Nursing Home in Cardston, Alberta then as matron of the Chinook Lodge. After her remarriage and move to Massachusetts, she took another job, again in a Senior’s facility where she served until she retired. During that time she also cared many years for 2 handicapped seniors in her home, a motherless Albanian teenage girl who was alone in America for serious surgeries and many others who needed a place to stay, a wedding dinner or a shoulder to cry on. As a result of all this mothering, she never learned to cook for less than 20.
Clara joined the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter Day Saints shortly after her marriage to Norman and served in many capacities through the years. She especially enjoyed her time as a missionary in the Bishop’s storehouse with Marcel in Boston and as a temple worker in the Boston temple.
She and Marcel moved back to Cardston to be close to Clara’s family and only a year later Marcel passed away. She has spent her last years mothering and grandmothering her large posterity, colouring countless pictures, playing the piano and her accordion (when she thought no one would hear) and making sure the cookie jar and treat drawer were always full.
She is predeceased by her parents, six siblings, five children and two husbands.
Please rejoice with us in celebrating a life well lived and the reunion she is experiencing on the other side of the veil.
A Funeral Service will be held at the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, Temple Street Chapel (355 - 3 St W, Cardston) on Friday, June 12th, 2026 at 1:00 p.m. Friends may meet the family from 12:00-12:45 p.m. prior to the service. Interment will follow at the Cardston Cemetery. ​​Click to Send Condolences to the Family

Hull, Bernie - Legacy Funeral Home
BERNARD ROY “BERNIE” HULL, our beloved husband, father, grandfather, great-grandfather, brother, uncle, and friend, passed away Monday, June 1, 2026, at the age of 82 years. He was born October 17, 1943, in Cardston, Alberta, Canada, to Roy Wilmot and Elizabeth Ellen (Harker) Hull, and was the youngest of seven siblings: George (Mabel) Hull, Norman (Catherine) Hull, Mary (Arden) Draper, Winifred Hull, Audrey (Eric) Creber, and Maurine (Preston) Johnson.
Bernie completed his primary and secondary education in Cardston and attended Lethbridge Junior College for a year. He then served a served a full-time mission for The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints to the Navajo Nation in Arizona—an experience he treasured throughout his life. He developed a deep love for the Navajo people and spoke fondly of his time among them.
Following his mission, Bernie earned a Bachelor of Science in math with a minor in chemistry from the University of Alberta and later completed a Bachelor of Education from the University of Lethbridge. He then devoted 25 years to teaching high school chemistry and math in towns in Alberta such as Manyberries, Ellerslie, Warner, and Cardston. A dedicated educator, he had the privilege of teaching countless students over the years, including his own children, nieces, and nephews.
On September 10, 1966, Bernie married Dawn Adele Wight in the Cardston, Alberta Temple. They built a wonderful life over 38 years together until Dawn passed away from leukemia on May 19, 2005. Bernie was blessed to later reconnect with his former classmate, Charlene Walker, and they shared 21 supportive and loving years of marriage until his passing.
Bernie had many interests and talents. He was a master gardener and accomplished artist—whatever he set his mind to he could do well. He was also a jack-of-all-trades, and had the uncanny ability to fix anything, whether it was a washer or dryer, dishwasher, blow dryer, or lawn mower. After retiring from teaching, he raised Shetland sheepdogs, and also fulfilled his dream of becoming a sheep farmer, where he enjoyed spending long hours caring for all 200 of them on his beloved acreage in Aetna. Always a teacher at heart, even though his body started to feel the effects of his age, he was happy to help the college students in his family with math and chemistry problems right until the end of his life.
Bernie was a quiet man of faith who loved the Lord, and was a devoted member of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. He loved and cherished his family, often spending hours helping and serving them in any way he could. He will be deeply missed.
He is survived by his wife, Charlene; sister, Maurine Johnson; two children, Katrina (McRay) Murdock, and Ben Hull; and six grandchildren: Mackenzy, Brig, Jackson, and Hunter Murdock; Caesar and Sophie Hull.
He is also survived by Charlene’s children: Cari Conrad, Audrey (Jeff) Salmon, and James Conrad; her grandchildren, Jennifer (Tyler) Parker, Matthew Jackson, Stephanie, Nicole, and Natalie Wilcox, Cheyenne (Shawn Daye-Finley) Conrad, and Jayden (Michael Curry) Rushton; 15 great-grandchildren, and many nieces and nephews. He is predeceased by his first wife, Dawn Wight; his parents, Roy and Elizabeth Hull; and his siblings, George Hull, Mary Draper, Norman Hull, Winifred Hull, and Audrey Creber; their spouses, Mabel Hull, Arden Draper, Catherine Hull, Eric Creber, and Preston Johnson; and great-granddaughter, Evie Parker.
The Funeral Service will be held at The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints,
​Cardston Alberta Stake Centre, 338 5th Ave. E., Cardston, on Thursday, June 11th, 2026 at 11:00 a.m. Interment to follow in the Aetna Cemetery.

Scout, Simone - Legacy Funeral Home
With heavy hearts, we share the passing of our beloved, dear sister, niece, auntie, friend, and relative, Melva Simone Scout (Piitaaipottaakii– Eagle Flying Woman). Many knew her as Simone, the cherished daughter of the late Shannon Faye Red Crow-Shade and Simon Donovan Scout-Chief Moon. Simone was a member of the Fish Eaters Clan (Mamioyiiksi) and a direct descendant of Chief Red Crow through the Chief Moon family line. She is lovingly remembered by her two children, Kendrick and Kendra. On her father's side, her lineage includes Chief Red Crow, Chief Moon, Dan Chief Moon, Jordan Chief Moon Sr, Simon Donovan Scout-Chief Moon, Melva Simone Scout. On her mother's side, her lineage includes Helen Cochrane, Dina Red Crow, Lois Melva Red Crow, Shannon Faye Red Crow-Shade, and Sarah Margaret Red Crow. Her paternal aunts are Lenora Scout (Horace Shouting), Arlene Scout (Todd Soup), Chantal Scout, Nitasha Scout (Nicholas Many Fingers), and Tyne Shouting (Cyrus Weaselfat). Simone is also survived by her great-aunt Rose Ann Scout (Justin Yellow Horn), her great uncle Charlie Scout, and many great-aunts and great-uncles. Her maternal brothers are Jonathon Travis Daniel Red Crow, Adrian Derek Red Crow, Seth Red Crow-Old Shoes, and Ty Red Crow. Her paternal brothers are Simon Danny Scout, Tyreese Chev Scout, Donovan Roan Scout. Her paternal sisters are Taylor Crow Spreads His Wings (Joey), Danika Freeman (Mason), and Montana Freeman. She is also survived by many cousins, nieces, nephews, extended relatives, and loved ones. Simone was predeceased by her parents, Shannon Faye Red Crow-Shade and Simon Donovan Scout-Chief Moon; her grandparents, Jordan Sr Chief Moon and Rosetta Scout-Chief Moon; her aunts, Melody Jolaine Scout and Kim Scout; her uncle, Kristian Scout; and her cousin and sister, Kristen Scout. She was also predeceased by her great-grandparents, Ben Scout, Sarah Scout (Stabs Down-Blue Wings), Dan Chief Moon, and Philomena Morning Owl Chief Moon. Simone will be lovingly remembered by her extended Scouts, Chief Moons, Morning Owls, Stabs Downs, and Blue Wings families, as well as many other relatives, friends, and loved ones. The family apologizes for any names have been missed.

The Wake Service will be held on Sunday, June 7 from 6:00 - 11:00 pm at Senator Gladstone Hall, Blood Reserve. The Funeral Service will be held on Monday, June 8 at 11:00 am at Senator Gladstone Hall. Interment will follow in Pioneer Cemetery.

Her maternal brothers are Jonathon Travis Daniel Red Crow, Adrian Derek Red Crow, Seth Red Crow-Old Shoes, and Ty Red Crow. Her paternal brothers are Simon Danny Scout, Tyreese Chev Scout, Donovan Roan Scout. Her paternal sisters are Taylor Crow Spreads His Wings (Joey), Danika Freeman (Mason), and Montana Freeman. She is also survived by many cousins, nieces, nephews, extended relatives, and loved ones. Simone was predeceased by her parents, Shannon Faye Red Crow-Shade and Simon Donovan Scout-Chief Moon; her grandparents, Jordan Sr Chief Moon and Rosetta Scout-Chief Moon; her aunts, Melody Jolaine Scout and Kim Scout; her uncle, Kristian Scout; and her cousin and sister, Kristen Scout. She was also predeceased by her great-grandparents, Ben Scout, Sarah Scout (Stabs Down-Blue Wings), Dan Chief Moon, and Philomena Morning Owl Chief Moon. The family apologizes for any names have been missed.

Wegwitz, Kathryn - Legacy Funeral Home
Kathryn “Kathy” Doreen (Roe) Wegwitz, age 77, passed away June 3, 2026 in Lethbridge, AB, one day before her 78th birthday.
Born on June 4, 1948, Kathy was the beloved daughter of Lawrence and Mona Roe. She was cherished by her younger siblings: Donna Rasmussen (David), Robert Roe (Deborah), Randall Roe (Ivana), and Cari Bevans (Cory).
Kathy shared nearly 59 years of marriage with her husband, Leonard “Len” Wegwitz. Together they built a life centered on faith, their family of 10 children, and service to others. Her life and legacy remain an inspiration to her family and by many who knew her.
Her greatest priority and joy was her family. She is survived by Len; their children Marsha Johnson (Byron), Karla Colenutt (Stanley), Lawrence Wegwitz (Jennifer), Naomi Kaupp, Kelby Wegwitz (Cheri), Leisa Paxman, and Jeromy Wegwitz; 32 grandchildren; 51 great-grandchildren; and her siblings. She was predeceased by her parents; her children Samuel, Alice, and Aaron; and her grandson Quinn.
Kathy will be remembered for her devotion to her family, her faith, and the care she showed to those around her. Those who knew Kathy will remember her for her compassion, her strength, and her willingness to put the needs of others before her own. She created a home where people felt welcome, loved, and accepted. Her legacy is found not only in the family she raised but also in the countless lives she touched through her example of love and service. Kathy was known for her kindness, generosity, and willingness to help others. Her home was always open to family, friends, and neighbors, and many were blessed by her quiet acts of service and encouragement.
Though her passing leaves a deep sense of loss, her family finds comfort in the memories she created, the lessons she taught, and the faith and values she passed on. They invite all who knew and loved her to join them and celebrate her life marked by faith, love, sacrifice, and devotion to family.

The Funeral Service will be held at The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, Taylor Street Chapel, Raymond, Alberta on Monday, June 8th, at 11:00 a.m. Friends may meet the family from 10:00 - 10:45 am prior to the service. Interment to follow in the Temple Hill Cemetery, Raymond, Alberta.

openGraph.content: Nora Red Crow-Stabs Down, Naatoiyiipi’ksaakii (Sacred Bird Woman) , age 72, of the Blood Reserve, passed on May 26, 2026, surrounded by her loving family. She belonged to the Aakaiksamaiksi /Many...

text:
Red Crow, Nora - Legacy Funeral Home
Nora Red Crow-Stabs Down, Naatoiyiipi’ksaakii (Sacred Bird Woman), age 72, of the Blood Reserve, passed on May 26, 2026, surrounded by her loving family. She belonged to the Aakaiksamaiksi /Many Tumor Clan. On her maternal side, she was a proud descendant of the 5th generation of Chief Red Crow (Mikaisto), and Iron (Miiksskim). From her earliest days into her young adult years, she was raised in the heart of Blackfoot sacred traditions. As the child of long-time Horn Society members and Thunder Pipe holders, her youth was shaped by her parents’ sacred roles. Reflecting this profound heritage, she was a co-owner of the Horse Thunder Medicine Pipe. While her life’s journey led her in a different direction, and she did not actively participate in the ceremonial way of life, she maintained a deep respect for our Nitsitapi traditions, teachings, and ceremonial ways throughout her life. Throughout the years, she supported and took pride in family members who carried on the traditions and cultural practices.
Life brought its trials, but Nora met them with quiet bravery. She shared twelve years of building a family with the father of her children, Ralph Weasel Fat, before his untimely passing. Left to navigate life as a young widow, her dedication to her children never wavered. Demonstrating her characteristic hard work, she bravely chose to return to school at Red Crow Community College later in life to study library science at SAIT in Calgary. She successfully achieved her goals and went on to work at Red Crow Community College, spending twenty dedicated years as a librarian, sharing the love of her books while quietly serving her community, supporting students, staff and community members who walked through the doors. Nora retired from her career in 2023.
She was a deeply cherished mother, grandmother, sister, and aunt who dedicated her life entirely to her home and the people she loved. Nora was a quiet, gentle soul who channeled her generational strength into her family. A true homebody who found her greatest peace within her home. She focused her whole heart on her domestic life, creating a warm haven for her family. She was an exceptional cook, who loved hosting family dinners and gatherings, bringing family together through food, conversation, and laughter. She was an avid reader and had a lifelong passion for books. Her treasured book collection will be preserved as a family library for family and future generations to enjoy. Whether it was a planned vacation, a road trip, or simply time spent exploring together, she valued the memories made and the time shared with loved ones. While she enjoyed seeing new places, her most treasured memories were always anchored in her childhood growing up at Old Agency. Above all, she was fiercely devoted to her children and grandchildren - instilling in them a deep sense of hard work and perseverance. While she shared special close bonds with some, every one of her grandchildren held a cherished place in her heart and brought her great joy.
Nora is survived by her children: Pam, Bonnie, Lorraine, Freddy and Norman (Nikita). Her love, teachings and legacy live on through her fourteen grandchildren and seven great-grandchildren, all of whom brought her pride and joy. She is also survived by her loving sisters: Isabelle Healy, Leona, Evelyn, Myrna and Lena (Newton) Bull Shields; one brother Harrison (Billy); her longtime friend Verdun Morning Owl (Hind Bull), as well as numerous nieces, nephews, and relatives from her extended family.
Nora was predeceased by her late husband of 12 years, Ralph Weasel Fat; a special friend Bryce Vaile; her parents Fred and Agnes Stabs Down; brothers Roy, and Wallace (Melvin); her sisters, Irene Red Crow, Sara Scout, and Angela Singer; and her beloved nieces and nephews, Jamie Red Crow, Susan, Zoe, Peyton Stabs Down, Terrance Tailfeathers, Eldon Singer, and two son in-laws Kevin Scout and Chris Healy.
Nora- Natoiyiipi'ksaakii leaves behind a legacy of unconditional love, quiet strength, resilience, and devotion to her family. She touched the lives of many through her kindness, generosity, wisdom, and unwavering support. Her presence brought comfort, her guidance brought strength, and her love created a foundation that will continue to live on through her children, grandchildren, great-grandchildren, and all who were fortunate enough to know her.
Her family is heartbroken by her passing and will deeply miss her warmth, her gentle spirit, her stories, and the countless memories she helped create throughout her life. While it is difficult to say goodbye, we find comfort knowing that her suffering has ended and that she is now at peace. Though she may no longer walk beside us, her love, teachings, and memory will remain in our hearts forever.
Until we meet again, Mom, Grandma, Sister, Auntie, and Friend, your journey continues, and your spirit will never be forgotten.
The family would like to thank everyone for their prayers, support, and kindness during this difficult time. 

A wake service will be at Old Agency Hall, Blood Reserve, Alberta on Friday June 5, 2026 from 6:00 - 10:00 pm. The Funeral service will also be held at Old Agency Hall, Blood Reserve on Saturday, June 6, 2026 at 11:00 am. Interment to follow at Stabs Down Cemetery.
​

text:
Many Fingers, Troy - Legacy Funeral Home
In Loving Memory of Gordon Joseph Troy Manyfingers “Okaan”
Born: May 9, 1972
Died: July 11, 2026
It is with great sadness that we announce the passing of Gordon Joseph Troy Manyfingers, “Okaan.” He was surrounded by his loving family: Louy, Dwight, Mason, Sloan, Markee, and Jayden; his extended Heavy Shield, Day Chief, and Manyfingers families; and his work family.
Okaan was born on May 9, 1972, in Cardston, Alberta, to Gordon Okaan Heavy Shield and Theresa Rosanne Manyfingers.
Troy was raised by his maternal grandmother, Margaret, née Soop-Manyfingers, along with his older sister, Sheryl Day Chief. Okaan held a special place in his heart for his auntie-mom, Faye Heavy Shield, who always took his children as her own. Troy also found comfort and guidance in Lavern First Rider and Dorothy Day Chief, his adopted grandmothers, from whom he sought guidance and advice.
Okaan began his educational journey in Cardston, Alberta, where he received his high school diploma. Soon after, he attended Mount Royal College, where he earned a certificate in Social Work. He later attended Bow Valley College, receiving a certificate in Security. Troy was employed by various departments of the Blood Tribe throughout his career.
Troy excelled in athletics as a gym teacher and coach for the many sports offered through the Kainai Board of Education (KBE). Okaan promoted and encouraged excellence in athletics, participating in and coaching all the sports Kainai had to offer.
In 2008, KBE transferred Troy to an elementary school, where he became a gym teacher. Troy recognized the tremendous athletic talent among the youth in the community. At Saipoyi Elementary School, he created the largest youth running club in Alberta. Through his love of running, he met many friends and inspired countless young people. Troy often credited Andrew “Animal” Manyfingers for inspiring his love of running, as Andrew was also an avid runner.
In 2014, Okaan decided to return to school and earned an Addictions and Mental Health Diploma from Red Crow College. After receiving his diploma, he was employed with Kainai Wellness as a Case-Client Coordinator, where he was instrumental in guiding Blood Tribe members along their roads to recovery. It was during this time that Troy began challenging Blood Tribe members to become healthier.
Okaan organized numerous fun runs for the community. As a result of his desire to create a healthier community, thousands of people came out to support his runs.
As a cross-country runner, Troy developed an interest in triathlons. In 2008, he began his journey toward competing in the Ironman Triathlon, considered one of the most gruelling endurance competitions in the world.
His first triathlon took place in 2008, when he and his seven-year-old daughter, Markee, competed in their first official triathlon in Fort Macleod, Alberta. They both caught the triathlon bug and spent the rest of 2008 participating in weekend triathlons throughout Southern Alberta.
In 2013, Troy entered and successfully completed the Sylvan Lake Canadian Half Ironman. After that, he set his sights on completing a full Ironman.
In 2015, Troy entered the Lake Tahoe Ironman, choosing this specific race because it was considered one of the hardest in the Ironman community. Unfortunately, the race was cancelled due to forest fires. Over the following years, wildfires continued to prevent him from entering Ironman competitions throughout Canada and the United States.
In 2022, Troy entered the Subaru Ironman in Penticton, British Columbia, where he missed his bike-to-run transition by only five minutes.
Finally, in 2023, Troy successfully completed his first full Ironman in Tempe, Arizona, becoming Kainai’s first Ironman—an accomplishment of which he was immensely proud. The dedication and perseverance he demonstrated in completing an Ironman competition from beginning to end truly reflected his deep passion for physical well-being and his determination to overcome challenges.
Troy also had a great passion for hockey. He played with Machine and the Kainai Golden Chiefs. His most recent team was the River City Raiders, where he played alongside his daughter.
Troy was also a strong supporter of women’s hockey. He coached the Piikani Lady Warriors from 2017 to 2018 and later went on to coach Junior A teams, including the Southern Sage and the Chinook Blazers.
Troy is survived by his loving wife, LouAnn “Louy,” and his children: Dwight (Mandy), Mason (Chelsi), Sloan (Kyle), Markee (Tealson), and Jayden.
He leaves behind his beloved grandchildren: Richard, Peyton, Addison, Destiny, Brielle, Tealson Jr., Nyjah, Desai, Floral (Rozee), Daxton, and Brenlee.
He is also survived by his sister, Sheryl, and his adopted parents: Gramma Evangeline Provost; Marjorie and Randolph Manyfingers; Joyce First Rider; and Bertha Chiefmoon.
His godchildren include Katie Weasel Fat and Jolene Russell.
Troy is also survived by his siblings: Edgar (Wanda), Donna Manyfingers, Jolaine Manyfingers, Brett Yellow Face, Chris Heavy Shield, Heidi Heavy Shield, Haley Heavy Shield, Henry Heavy Shield, and Donny Heavy Shield.
He is survived by his aunties, including Barb (Lyman Tailfeathers), Jordan, and Stephen Heavy Shield.
Predeceased are Lena (James Russell), Evelyn (Les Healy), Mary (Ed), Herman (Mousie), Ed (Marion), and John.
From the Manyfingers family, he is survived by Mildred Melting Tallow, Clara, Sylvia Tail Feathers, Marie (Don), and Burton (Verna). Predeceased are Albert Jr., Gordon (Loretta), and Herbert (Mary Rose).
Troy is also survived by his special nephews: Myles, Mitch, Wyatt, Guy, Hunter, and Taylor “Bronc,” and his nieces: Tamara, Lana Lee, and Jiggs Day Chief.
Troy will be missed by his friends: Aaron D, Ian C (Karsen), Warren DC(Skilee), Denny NR, Skip GS, Paul'BooBoo' GS, Andy MF(Nicole), Lana CH(Rod), Vanessa PB, Brad H(Charlene), Craig 'Soup' B, Charles MC, Shane SG(Joni), Teri-Lyn Fox, Marvin MC(Lydia), Dean Shade, Chad BSB, Danny WF
We apologize for any names we have missed. Troy played a big part in our community and had countless friends and family. 
A very special thank-you to the Day Chief families for the tremendous amount of love and support they shared with Okaan throughout the years.
We also extend our heartfelt gratitude to the Moatokiiks for helping and supporting him throughout his illness.
Okaan’s legacy will live on through his family, his community, the athletes he coached, the people he encouraged, and all those whose lives he touched through his kindness, strength, determination, and love of health, sport, and community.

# Many Fingers, Troy - Legacy Funeral Home

**In Loving Memory of Gordon Joseph Troy Manyfingers “Okaan”**  
**Born:** May 9, 1972  
**Died:** July 11, 2026

It is with great sadness that we announce the passing of **Gordon Joseph Troy Manyfingers, “Okaan.”** He was surrounded by his loving family: Louy, Dwight, Mason, Sloan, Markee, and Jayden; his extended Heavy Shield, Day Chief, and Manyfingers families; and his work family.  
Okaan was born on May 9, 1972, in Cardston, Alberta, to Gordon Okaan Heavy Shield and Theresa Rosanne Manyfingers.  
Troy was raised by his maternal grandmother, Margaret, née Soop-Manyfingers, along with his older sister, Sheryl Day Chief. Okaan held a special place in his heart for his auntie-mom, Faye Heavy Shield, who always took his children as her own. Troy also found comfort and guidance in Lavern First Rider and Dorothy Day Chief, his adopted grandmothers, from whom he sought guidance and advice.  
Okaan began his educational journey in Cardston, Alberta, where he received his high school diploma. Soon after, he attended Mount Royal College, where he earned a certificate in Social Work. He later attended Bow Valley College, receiving a certificate in Security. Troy was employed by various departments of the Blood Tribe throughout his career.  
Troy excelled in athletics as a gym teacher and coach for the many sports offered through the Kainai Board of Education (KBE). Okaan promoted and encouraged excellence in athletics, participating in and coaching all the sports Kainai had to offer.  
In 2008, KBE transferred Troy to an elementary school, where he became a gym teacher. Troy recognized the tremendous athletic talent among the youth in the community. At Saipoyi Elementary School, he created the largest youth running club in Alberta. Through his love of running, he met many friends and inspired countless young people. Troy often credited Andrew “Animal” Manyfingers for inspiring his love of running, as Andrew was also an avid runner.  
In 2014, Okaan decided to return to school and earned an Addictions and Mental Health Diploma from Red Crow College. After receiving his diploma, he was employed with Kainai Wellness as a Case-Client Coordinator, where he was instrumental in guiding Blood Tribe members along their roads to recovery. It was during this time that Troy began challenging Blood Tribe members to become healthier.  
Okaan organized numerous fun runs for the community. As a result of his desire to create a healthier community, thousands of people came out to support his runs.  
As a cross-country runner, Troy developed an interest in triathlons. In 2008, he began his journey toward competing in the Ironman Triathlon, considered one of the most gruelling endurance competitions in the world.  
His first triathlon took place in 2008, when he and his seven-year-old daughter, Markee, competed in their first official triathlon in Fort Macleod, Alberta. They both caught the triathlon bug and spent the rest of 2008 participating in weekend triathlons throughout Southern Alberta.  
In 2013, Troy entered and successfully completed the Sylvan Lake Canadian Half Ironman. After that, he set his sights on completing a full Ironman.  
In 2015, Troy entered the Lake Tahoe Ironman, choosing this specific race because it was considered one of the hardest in the Ironman community. Unfortunately, the race was cancelled due to forest fires. Over the following years, wildfires continued to prevent him from entering Ironman competitions throughout Canada and the United States.  
In 2022, Troy entered the Subaru Ironman in Penticton, British Columbia, where he missed his bike-to-run transition by only five minutes.  
Finally, in 2023, Troy successfully completed his first full Ironman in Tempe, Arizona, becoming **Kainai’s first Ironman**—an accomplishment of which he was immensely proud. The dedication and perseverance he demonstrated in completing an Ironman competition from beginning to end truly reflected his deep passion for physical well-being and his determination to overcome challenges.  
Troy also had a great passion for hockey. He played with Machine and the Kainai Golden Chiefs. His most recent team was the River City Raiders, where he played alongside his daughter.  
Troy was also a strong supporter of women’s hockey. He coached the Piikani Lady Warriors from 2017 to 2018 and later went on to coach Junior A teams, including the Southern Sage and the Chinook Blazers.  
Troy is survived by his loving wife, **LouAnn “Louy,”** and his children: **Dwight (Mandy), Mason (Chelsi), Sloan (Kyle), Markee (Tealson), and Jayden.**  
He leaves behind his beloved grandchildren: **Richard, Peyton, Addison, Destiny, Brielle, Tealson Jr., Nyjah, Desai, Floral (Rozee), Daxton, and Brenlee.**  
He is also survived by his sister, **Sheryl**, and his adopted parents: **Gramma Evangeline Provost; Marjorie and Randolph Manyfingers; Joyce First Rider; and Bertha Chiefmoon.**  
His godchildren include **Katie Weasel Fat and Jolene Russell.**  
Troy is also survived by his siblings: **Edgar (Wanda), Donna Manyfingers, Jolaine Manyfingers, Brett Yellow Face, Chris Heavy Shield, Heidi Heavy Shield, Haley Heavy Shield, Henry Heavy Shield, and Donny Heavy Shield.**  
He is survived by his aunties, including **Barb (Lyman Tailfeathers), Jordan, and Stephen Heavy Shield.**  
Predeceased are **Lena (James Russell), Evelyn (Les Healy), Mary (Ed), Herman (Mousie), Ed (Marion), and John.**  
From the Manyfingers family, he is survived by **Mildred Melting Tallow, Clara, Sylvia Tail Feathers, Marie (Don), and Burton (Verna).** Predeceased are **Albert Jr., Gordon (Loretta), and Herbert (Mary Rose).**  
Troy is also survived by his special nephews: **Myles, Mitch, Wyatt, Guy, Hunter, and Taylor “Bronc,”** and his nieces: **Tamara, Lana Lee, and Jiggs Day Chief.**  
Troy will be missed by his friends: **Aaron D, Ian C (Karsen), Warren DC(Skilee), Denny NR, Skip GS, Paul'BooBoo' GS, Andy MF(Nicole), Lana CH(Rod), Vanessa PB, Brad H(Charlene), Craig 'Soup' B, Charles MC, Shane SG(Joni), Teri-Lyn Fox, Marvin MC(Lydia), Dean Shade, Chad BSB, Danny WF**  
We apologize for any names we have missed. Troy played a big part in our community and had countless friends and family.   
A very special thank-you to the Day Chief families for the tremendous amount of love and support they shared with Okaan throughout the years.  
We also extend our heartfelt gratitude to the **Moatokiiks** for helping and supporting him throughout his illness.

text:
Wiltse, Maureen - Legacy Funeral Home
It is with deep sorrow that we announce the passing of Isabelle Maureen Wiltse (nee McKinnon). Maureen (or Moe, as she was usually called) was born in Salmon Arm, BC on March 2, 1934 and passed away July 1, 2026, in Cardston, AB. She goes to join her beloved husband, Charles Robert (Bob), who passed away December 30, 2025.
Maureen was predeceased by her daughter Colleen, parents Angus and Martha McKinnon, and by her siblings Walter (Florence) McErvel, Kathleen (Jim) Presley, Robb (Belva) Mackinnen, and Colleen (Freddy) Fredrickson. Maureen loved her family deeply and leaves to mourn: her children, Joanne Hlina of Vernon, BC; James (Colleen) Wiltse of Kanata, ON; Steven (Sally) Wiltse of Gainford, AB; Patrick (Lisa) Wiltse of Cardston, AB; Karen Wiltse of Cardston, AB; 17 grand-children and 19 great-grandchildren as well as numerous nieces and nephews.
Maureen had a wonderful sense of humour and a razor-sharp wit; she believed puns were the highest form of humour. She loved being with people and despite having poor health for much of her life, Maureen never complained and instead often uplifted those who came to comfort her.
She had a beautiful voice and loved to sing; musical sessions with Bob, Karen, and Pat playing guitars and everyone singing were frequent occurrences in their home. Badminton was a favourite sport that she shared with her children.
Maureen and Bob enjoyed hunting and fishing and explored fishing lakes and forests all around BC and Alberta. She was an excellent cook and baker, and spent many summers and autumns preserving fruit, vegetables, meats, fish, and jams.
As a member of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter Day Saints, Maureen was a dedicated missionary and loved to welcome people into the church. She loved to learn and especially loved teaching the gospel.
Special thanks go to the staff of Lee Crest Retirement Home who took such wonderful care of Maureen in her final days.
​Service will be held at Temple Street Chapel, 355 3rd St. W., Cardston, AB, on Saturday, July 11 at 1:00 p.m. Read More

openGraph.content: Monica Arlene Chief Moon (Sattsitapiaakii) - Southern Belle May 9, 1955 – July 2, 2026 It is with immense pain and sadness that we announce the passing of our beloved Matriarch, Monica Chief Moon...

text:
Chief Moon, Monica - Legacy Funeral Home
Monica Arlene Chief Moon
(Sattsitapiaakii) - Southern Belle
May 9, 1955 – July 2, 2026
It is with immense pain and sadness that we announce the passing of our beloved Matriarch, Monica Chief Moon (Satsitapiakii) at the age of 71. Monica was the eldest daughter of the Late Lucy Rose Prairie Chicken (Si ka kii). Monica was not fortunate enough to have known or met her biological father before his passing; however, she developed a father-daughter relationship with the Late Reggie Bottle Sr., whom she lovingly called Dad. Reggie was elated to have this title bestowed upon him. Her Maternal Grandfather was Tom Prairie Chicken (Imiitaoh’sokoi), and her grandmother was Mini Mountain Horse.
Monica was born in a house and delivered by Suzette Spotted Bull, and also raised in the Moccasin Flats/Moses Lake Community on the Blood Reserve. This is where she made many lifelong relationships. She attended school at the St. Mary’s Residential School in her younger years, then went to high school in Cardston, where she was the first in her immediate family to graduate from high school, which was one accomplishment of many that she was proud of. In her High School years, she met her best friend, the late Oral Chief Moon, who soon led her to her life partner and sweetheart of 52 years, John Chief Moon Jr. After being in a relationship for over a year, they became pregnant with their first child. Monica often told the story of her experience of becoming a first-time mother. She said she went into labor while she was helping John lift poles and such, for a fence he was building. He drove her to the Cardston Municipal Hospital and dropped her off at the entrance, then John went home, not realizing that he was to stay with her. After some time, his mom got a call that Monica had a baby girl. His Mother went to tell him the happy news, and his response & reaction to his wife having the baby was tsaa aaa! 
Monica moved to Calgary, where she not only began to raise her family but also began her post-secondary education. Her academic credentials include a Bachelor of Science Degree (Computer Information Systems) from DeVry Institute of Technology, and Phoenix, Arizona; an Accounting Certificate from Hollingshead Business College, Calgary, Alberta; and one semester at Mount Royal College in Calgary. Monica did not finish her time at Mount Royal College, as this is when she lost her hero, her brother Ross, and Monica was not able to navigate through the pain. Monica’s first job after moving to Calgary was a house-cleaning position. She then went on to work for the Nova Corporation and later became an accountant with the City of Calgary. She then made her career change to work in the education department and began working for Treaty Seven Economic Development. After several years with Treaty 7, Monica devoted over 20 years working in education in an administrative capacity with the First Nations Adult and Higher Education Consortium (FNAHEC). Through her employment with FNAHEC, she was able to travel to such places as Ontario, Nova Scotia, Quebec, Winnipeg, and Tennessee. She also played a huge role in hosting the World Indigenous Peoples Conference on Education, which brought Indigenous visitors to Stoney Nakoda from all over the world. She and John both worked for Heritage Park, and she stated at that time that it was the best job she had, as she was able to teach our ways and have non-Indigenous people see us through a properly educated lens, which was very rewarding to her. Throughout her career, she has served on several boards, including Trelis and the Elizabeth Fry Society Elders board, and was most recently the treasurer of the Elders’ Knowledge Circle Society. In her latest position, she was also a Knowledge Keeper, Blackfoot instructor, and Traditional Parenting instructor for EFRY Calgary. Through Monica’s employment, she has met many, many colleagues, built new lifelong friendships, and taught anybody who would listen to her about our culture, language and traditions. Despite leaving the reserve at an early age, Monica never lost touch with her roots and remained very much involved in her Blackfoot culture and ceremonies. This included being transferred into the Thunder Short Medicine Pipe Society. Recently, Monica has become more involved in the Calgary community as a knowledge Keeper on various committees, assisting our non-indigenous communities in understanding our First Nations people better so that we can all move forward in a positive and empowering manner.
Monica was a beautiful, loving, caring, and kind woman; she valued her family above all else in life. When her mother passed, Monica immediately took on the role of Matriarch. Everyone respected Monica and looked up to her for guidance; she wasn’t afraid to tell you what you needed to hear either. Monica also gained her mother's nurturing heart. If Monica were able to have people in her house, it would never be empty. Monica was also a lover of dogs; her dog now is very vicious, Cujo-like, and therefore Monica would have to visit with friends and family outside so they wouldn’t get eaten for supper. She had another dog named Brian, whom she loved so much. Approximately 7 years ago, Monica was diagnosed with a brain aneurysm deep in her frontal lobe. After a day or so of feeling bad, someone told the dog, Brian, to kiss Grandma; she’s sick. So, Brian went to Mom and started kissing and licking her feet. Not long after, her dog got sick, and he ended up getting heart cancer, and later had to be put down. Monica had to go for her next check-up for her aneurysm, and the films and other imaging came back negative; the brain aneurysm was completely gone, which is why she has such a love for dogs, but especially Brian, for he had taken her illness from her.
Monica leaves behind her Husband of 52 years, John Chief Moon; four children, Annie Chief Moon, John Ross Chief Moon, Ty Chief Moon, and Devon Little Shields; and four grandchildren, Tegan Chief Moon, Jovin Eagletail, Lucy Prairie Chicken, and Cashius Old Woman. Traditional Parents, Ruth Scalplock and Francis Melting Tallow. Monica will also be missed by all her siblings: Shirley Prairie Chicken (Barnabus Tall Man), Julie Crazy Bull, Lorna Prairie Chicken, and Felicia Little Shields. Traditional siblings: Daniel Crazy Bull, Wesley Crazy Bull, Sandra Many Feathers (Jason O’Hara), and Carol Bird; and Goddaughter Bonnie Calf Robe. She will be so missed by her best friend, Debbie Eli; her children, Mervin Black Kettle and Paige Black Kettle, whom Monica also considered her grandchildren; her bestie, Steven Kellier, whom she gave the name Spiitsapikwaan; and Roy Bare Shin Bone. She will also be missed by her traditional daughters, Trina Sleigh (Kevin Sandy) and Louise Black Plume. So many nieces, nephews, cousins, and her brother’s and sister’s in-laws, and all her friends she made through the years.
Monica was predeceased by her mother, Lucy Prairie Chicken; father, Reggie Bottle Sr.; and brothers Ross Prairie Chicken, Lorne Prairie Chicken, Calvin Prairie Chicken, and Andrew Prairie Chicken. Sister-in-law, Brenda Mistaken Chief. Her nieces: Stephanie Prairie Chicken, Noel Chief Moon, Samara Chief Moon, Cassidy Chief Moon; Great Nieces: Gina Good Dagger, Stephanie Good Dagger; Great Nephew: Justin Little Shields; and her God children: Marvin Bird and Jason Bird. 
She had a very special relationship with all her nieces and nephews, and they all looked up to Monica and loved her so much. Monica had many relatives from the Prairie Chickens, Heavy Runners, Calf Robes, Chief Moons, Crazy Bulls, Newbreasts, Melting Tallows, Big Heads, and Birds.
The Family would like to extend their utmost appreciation to the nursing staff on Unit 38 at the South Health Campus for their round-the-clock love and care for our mother during her last days. A special thanks to Nurse Jewel for your amazing love and support for both Monica and her daughter, Annie, and for ensuring they were always well looked after.

​
The Wake Service will be held on Sunday, July 12 from 6:00 - 11:00 pm at Senator Gladstone Hall, Blood Reserve. The Funeral Service will be held on Monday, July 13 at 12:00 pm at the Cardston Civic Center (67 3rd Ave West, Cardston). Interment will follow in the Chief Moon Family Cemetery.

openGraph.content: MARSHA (MO) MARIE JENSEN WRIGHT passed away unexpectedly at the age of 72 years, leaving behind a legacy of faith, service, compassion, and unwavering love and devotion to her family and community....

text:
Wright, Marsha - Legacy Funeral Home
MARSHA (MO) MARIE JENSEN WRIGHT passed away unexpectedly at the age of 72 years, leaving behind a legacy of faith, service, compassion, and unwavering love and devotion to her family and community.
Born on November 5, 1953, Marsha was the beloved daughter of the late Blanche and Dewain Jensen.
While attending Rick’s College in Rexburg, ID, Marsha faced one of her greatest challenges when she experienced kidney failure. Following a successful kidney transplant, she demonstrated remarkable resilience and continued to pursue her education at Brigham Young University in Provo, UT. She graduated with a Bachelor’s degree in Communications, earning an outstanding 4.0 GPA. Later, she returned to BYU to complete her teaching certification.
Mo dedicated many years to teaching special education. She loved teaching and always saidit was the best job she ever had. Yet, the most important decision she ever made was leaving her “really good job” in order to become a mother through adoption. Her and her husband, Harvey, lovingly adopted their three sons – Trenten, Travis, and Gunnar – who became the greatest joy in her life. Above every accomplishment,Mo’s most notable role was that of “Mother”. 
She was also a proud and loving grandmother to Sebastian, Ellie, Rexten, and Hunter. Her grandchildren brought immense happiness in her life.
Mo shared her life with her husband, Harvey Wright, for43 years. She treasured every opportunity to create memories with her family. She especially loved pulling the family trailer somewhere every summer. Her favourite spots were Fernie, BC and Silverwood in Idaho. She could also always find a beautiful lake nearby as she loved kayaking, her favourite past-time.
Mo was a passionate supporter of the performing arts and devoted more than 40 years to the Cardston Community Theatre. Throughout those decades, she faithfully served as Board member, Director, and Past President, helping enrich the cultural life of her community while mentoring and encouraging generations of performers.
Service was the hallmark of Marsha’s life. A devout member of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, she faithfully served in numerous callings throughout her life. Her favourite calling was serving as Young Women’s leader, where she loved teaching, encouraging, and uplifting the young women with her testimony. Her motto was, “Girls just want to have fun.”
Her dedication to the community expanded when she was elected as Town Councillor. She served as Councillor for the past 4 years, striving to make her community a better place through thoughtful leadership and genuine care for others. 
Marsha is lovingly remembered by her husband, Harvey Wright; her 3 sons, Trenten (Nikki) Wright, Travis (Savannah) Wright, and Gunnar Wright; her 4 cherished grandchildren, Sebastian, Ellie, Rexten, and Hunter Wright; her 2 sisters, Wendy (Rick) West of Cardston, AB and Brenda (Leonard) Browne of Eugene, Oregon; and many loved nieces and nephews. She was preceded in death by her parents, Blanche and Dewain Jensen, and her brother in-law, Peter Coombs.
Those who knew Marsha will remember her strength in the face of adversity, her fearlessness, resiliency, generous heart, steadfast faith, love of theatre, and her remarkable ability to love and value everyone around her. Her life was one of quiet courage, selfless service, and enduring love – a legacy that will continue through her family and all whose lives she touched. She will be dearly missed by all who knew her.
Friends may meet the family at The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, Cardston Alberta Stake Centre (338 5th Ave. E.), Cardston, AB, on Friday, July 3 from 10:00-10:45 am. The funeral will commence at 11:00 am. Interment to follow in the Cardston Cemetery.

text:
Campbell, Lester "Kim" - Legacy Funeral Home
Lester Malcom (Kim) Campbell passed away on April 22, 2026, in Lethbridge, AB at the age of 80. Kim was born on August 25, 1945, to Lester and Wilma Campbell and raised on the family farm in Jefferson, AB.
Kim was raised in a home where education and hard work were important. His dad taught him about farming, and his mom inspired him as a teacher. He served a mission for The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-Day Saints in France. This experience taught him many things and allowed him to help his children pass French class in school.
He attended BYU for his post-secondary education and during that time he reluctantly went to a New Year’s Eve dance and met the love of his life. Kim and Verla (Greene) were married in the Cardston Temple on Nov. 28, 1970, and started their life together.
Kim followed in his mother's footsteps and became a teacher. After teaching in a grade one class and catching the mumps twice he knew he needed to take another path in education. He got his job in Lloydminster, AB, where he started a family and a career at LCHS High School. He taught for over thirty years and inspired many people. He taught agriculture and many other subjects with humor and love. He also was able to judge the 4-H programs and help the future farmers.
When he retired, he finally had to move away as they kept calling him back to teach. Kim and Verla returned to their roots and settled back in Cardston, AB. Kim was able to be back near the family farm and help wherever he could. He had a love for motorcycles, fishing, his Corvette, and especially his family. He would do anything for his family and loved spending time with his grandkids.
He is survived by his wife Verla and his three children. Carrie Kim of Lethbridge, Chad Allen (Kathy) of Calgary, and Douglas Kent (Ashley) of Taber. He also is survived by his grandchildren: Emily, Jude, Cooper and Sophie.
A celebration of life will be held at Tanner Senior Centre, Cardston on Saturday, July 11, 2026 at 2:00pm.

It is great sadness to announce the passing of Kellan Duke First Rider on June 17, 2026 at the tender age of 11 years old. Kellan was born November 10, 2014 to the parents of Thomas Goodrider and Kirsten First Rider.
Kellan is survived by his loving parents, and brothers: Christopher (Sabrina) Goodrider, Leland First Rider and Declan Old Shoes. His nieces: Octavia Young Pine and Nova Goodrider. His Grandparents Janine First Rider and the late Kevin Vielle and Linda and Craig Fox. His great grandmother Joyce First Rider, godparents: Lucille First Rider and Les Singer.
He is also survived by his aunties: Kelly Old Shoes, Germaine (Gregory) Cat Face, Brandi Fox, Tamari Fox, Vanessa Vielle, Melanie Old Shoes, Marlene Goodrider, Leslie White Bull . His uncles: Kyle and Marshall Vielle, Patrick First Rider, Darcy Whitebull, and Joey White Man. His great aunties: Lucille First Rider, Rolanda (Les) First Rider, Tammy Healy and Rita Calf. Great Uncles: Charles (Trina) First Rider, Melvin (Christine) White Man, Patrick White Man, Jeff (Doreen) Fox. Kellan comes from a large family stemming from First Rider, Fox, Vielle, Wolf Child, Good Rider, White Man, and Whitebull.
Kellan was born a month earlier than his due date and spent time in the NICU at the Lethbridge Regional Hospital. He was loved by all who came to visit. He was released from the hospital a week later, and was welcomed home by his loving parents, his brothers and sister. When he was a month old, he developed RSV and spent another week in the pediatric ward.
He was spoiled by everyone and was everyone’s baby and was protected by all. Growing up he was close to his big brother Leland and they did everything together. He learned a lot from his older siblings and tried to follow them. He was a fast learner in everything that he was being taught by his parents and siblings.
He started preschool in the year 2018 at the Park Meadows Elementary School. He loved going to school and was eager to go every day. He got along with all his schoolmates and all his teachers. His favorite thing to do in school was recess and music therapy, where he would join in on all the dancing and even following his schoolmates.
In the year 2020, he started online schooling but did not feel comfortable because he preferred to be in class. He tried hard to succeed in online school only to find it difficult to listen to the teachers.
In 2021, he was diagnosed with nonverbal autism. It was noted that when he progressed in certain aspects in life he would go back a couple of steps. He started to get better when he learned about the iPad and all the things he can do. He became smart using the programs/apps it had and started to progress where he should have been.

Gordon Cyrus Card, of Magrath, passed away at the Good Samaritan Garden Vista on July 7th, 2026 at the age of 83. He was predeceased by his wife Barabara, his parents, Cyrus and Marie and grandson Clay Card. 
Gordon will be deeply missed by his children and grandchildren Gord (Marie), Rhett (Talia) and Janelle and Shandy (Mark), Kent Tilley, Tatiana (Josh), Jessica and Grant.

Livestreaming will be available here on the Service day. However, due to wifi strength in the area if the livestream fails the full
recording of the service will be uploaded here following the graveside. 
Richard Clinton Law (Clinton), born May 5, 1924 in Cardston, Alberta, Canada to Richard Franklin Law and Sarah Greene Law, passed away on June 15, 2026.
Clinton was the third child of ten. As a young man growing up in Glennwood, Alberta he learned to work hard, run fast, and love fiercely. He grew up working with his dad, hauling milk to Ft. McCloud by horse drawn wagon through all kinds of weather.
From 1945-1947 Clinton served as a missionary for the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-Day Saints in Eastern Canada.
Shortly after, he immigrated to the United States where he was drafted into the U.S. Army to serve as a mechanic and driver during the Korean War. He completed his service in 1952 as a U.S. Army Corporal.
It was during this time of service that Clinton met his future wife, Thelma Lybbert, at a weekly mutual meeting in Moses Lake, Washington. Thelma attended her first prom with Clinton in the Spring of 1951, and they were married just months later, on November 14, 1951, in the Cardston, Alberta Temple.
They moved to Ft. Lewis, WA, where Clinton finished military service. They welcomed a daughter at the end of 1952, just after he was released from the army.
Clinton and Thelma lived in Moses Lake until 1956 where they gave birth to a daughter and one son before moving to Medicine Hat, Alberta, Canada so Clinton could work with his brother, Keith Law, managing the Law Transport Trucking company. During their time in Medicine Hat, Clinton also served as a bishop for their ward in the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-Day Saints from 1962-1965, and him and Thelma had three more daughters.
In 1965, the family moved to Ephrata, Washington. They helped work the Lybbert Family Farm while Thelma’s father recovered from back surgery, and gave birth to their youngest daughter.
The summer of 1968 Thelma and Clinton moved their family to Salt Lake City. Clinton worked many different jobs to support his family including; construction work, remodeling a train station, building motor homes, managing janitorial staff, and finally working as a truck driver.
They eventually settled in Payson, Utah for his work and stayed until their children were grown. In 1990, Clinton and Thelma fulfilled their wish to serve a mission together for the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-Day Saints. They were called to Paris, France and fell in love with the people they got to serve there.
Shortly after their mission, Clinton and Thelma decided to return home to Glennwood Canada. Clinton built their home and they were able to move in in 1996.
Clinton and Thelma served in their church and community for many years, including working in the Cardston Alberta Temple. They are often remembered in their community for their kindness and service.
Thelma became ill with lung cancer in 2006. Dad helped to care for her and take her to a big family reunion in the summer of 2009 so they could see of their posterity before she passed away on November 26, 2009.
Despite this loss, Clinton continued to serve in his church and community, always sharing the love of God with others. He often travelled during the following years to visit his posterity. He never missed out on weddings, mission farewells, or other life events for his children or grandchildren.
In 2018 his son and daughter-in-law moved to Canada to help care for him. Though even then in his 90’s he was still working in the garden everyday and serving those around him.
In 2023, after a year recovery from a fall and broken hip at his daughter’s house and another long trip to visit family, Clinton’s days of travel were over. He spent the next three years at home until another fall took him to the hospital on Saturday night, and he passed peacefully two days later.
Clinton was proceeded in death by his parents, Richard and Sarah Law, his wife, Thelma Law, his daughter, Angela Law, his brothers, Joseph Franklin, Edwin Curtis (Ted), William (Keith), Daniel Jordan, Ephriam (Allen), his sister Adeline Hansen, and 3 grandchildren.
He is survived by Son, Steven Kent Law (wife: Edith), daughters, Vondell Clayton (husband: Tom), Margaret Anne Aubrey (husband: Arlen), Teresa Lynn Hancock (husband: Aaron), Betty-Jean (husband: Glen) Anita Colleen Griffin (husband: Scott) and 47 grandchildren, 92 great-grandchildren and 7 great-great-grandchildren.
Friends may meet the family on Friday, June 26th, from 7:00 - 8:00 pm at Legacy Funeral Home, Cardston, or at the Church on Saturday from 10:00 - 10:45 am, prior to the service. The Funeral Service will be held at The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, Glenwood, Alberta on Saturday, June 27th, 2026 at 11:00 a.m. Interment to follow in the Glenwood Cemetery.

text:
Homan, Donald - Legacy Funeral Home
Donald Leslie Homan was born on October 3, 1935 in Coronation, Alberta to William and Azie Homan. They lived in Ponoka, Stettler and Veteran, where Don met Ivy and they were married in 1955. In 1956, their first of four daughters, Georgia, was born. Debbie followed in 1957, Barb in 1959 and Connie in 1963. Les was born in 1967 and Lorne in 1969, completing the family of six children. In 1970, the family moved from Veteran to Cereal, where they lived for two years, before moving to Calgary in 1972. In 1980, Don, Ivy, Connie, Les and Lorne moved north to the Peace River country. As empty nesters, Don and Ivy planned and built a log home on their own, which home they took great pride in. In Don’s early years, he worked on a seismic crew in Alberta and British Columbia. When the family started growing, he worked with his father running a trucking company in Veteran, then a local garage. When he moved to Cereal, he started long haul trucking, which he loved for many years and continued driving the big rigs when they moved to Calgary. When he moved to the Peace Country, he traded in the big rig for a school bus, and he and Ivy raised Hereford cattle, along with other various farm animals. Once retired, Don and Ivy travelled to many places, including all parts of Canada, the USA, Mexico, Hawaii, Alaska and a few cruises. 
Throughout their marriage, Don and Ivy enjoyed socializing, dining and dancing and continued that passion while they physically could. Music was always a part of their home. Another huge passion was rodeos, taking their kids to all local rodeos and once the kids were grown, they continued to attend any rodeos or stampedes they could, even taking in the Canadian Finals Rodeo and on at least one occasion, the National Finals Rodeo in Las Vegas. Don passed away peacefully in Lee Crest, Cardston, Alberta on June 18, 2026. 
He is survived by the love of his life, Ivy, and his daughters, Georgia (Ray), Debbie (Jerry), Barb, Connie (Dale), daughters-in-law, Jenny and Mira, and many grandchildren, great-grandchildren and great-great-grandchildren. He was predeceased by his parents, William and Azie, his siblings, Margaret, David and Darlene, his sons, Les and Lorne, sons-in-law, Mike, Odean and Al, and great-grandson, TJ.

text:
Stef, Shirley - Legacy Funeral Home
​Shirley Ann Bischler Stef was born in Prince Albert, Saskatchewan to Vera and August Bischler on June 26, 1946. Her first home was on a small farm in the district of Silver grove Saskatchewan where her first memories were of sitting in a rocking chair where she would play footsies with “angels” that always appeared on the floor!! This was the shadows and sunlight coming in the home, but she fully believed she was with angels. Shirley was a true follower of Christ, from her first memory through all of her days.
She loved all the farm animals other than Tom the turkey who loved to terrorize people and chased them until her dad built a fence around the old farmhouse to keep her safe. Sister Edie was born two years later, and the youngest in the family was Sister Dixie. Their mom would dress them in handmade clothing that made them feel very fashionable. They played dress up and enjoyed the outdoors making mud pies for their dolls or cats who did not really appreciate their chef skills. Shirleys Dad August and his brothers along with neighbors built the local Church where they played among the gravestones. This church stands to this day as a Saskatchewan historical site! Shirley's dad then sold their tiny farm and bought 3/4 section just outside Leask Saskatchewan where there was a small old log house for them to call home and a bunkhouse for the hired men. August built a 3-bedroom house which allowed her and her two sisters to have a shared room in a home which felt like a palace … schooling was in Leask the next eleven years which she remembers the importance her parents felt about education as they rode to school in a heated caboose even during the Saskatchewan blizzards. Shirley was mostly interested in things like drama and preparing school yearbooks but did manage to win a curling jacket for her team’s effort! She also won first prize for her doll carriage dressed like the queen for the coronation; thanks to her mom’s talents! 
August then decided to sell the farm and move to Saskatoon where Shirley completed grade 12 and took the Teachers Diploma course and began her teaching career in Shellbrook, Saskatchewan staying in the attic of a boarding house with a hot plate clearing a whole $199 a month for wages. She finished that year then moved to Alsask Saskatchewan where she taught Grade one at the Department of National Defence school. It was a happy year with many friends, and she then moved on to teach Grade 5 at a Department of National Defence school in Cold Lake. Where she met her first husband Carl. They were married in January of 68 and she settled into the life of a squadron wife and moved to Larh Germany.
Christy her daughter was born in Germany and spent some time in a 30-pound cast from waist down but the help of squadron friends she managed that baby girls care … even managing a ski trip to Ober Lech in Austria! Military Postings saw them go to Moose Jaw – where her son Ryan was born then on to Ottawa and Cold Lake. Shirley then returned to University in Saskatoon where she completed her Teaching Degree and moved back to Cold Lake where she taught Kindergarten and raised her two children.
Once her children moved to Edmonton for University and College, Shirley taught school for a year at Chilliwack East Elementary school in BC. The rain drove her back to sunny Alberta and Cold Lake where she continued to teach in Cold Lake and be close to many dear friends. Shirley then moved onto a farm by Fort Assiniboine, Alberta and taught school in Swan Hills and then Fort Assiniboine. Shirley loved the years on the farm especially when her family was able to spend time visiting, hunting and feasting on the meals, desserts and snacks she loved to prepare.
Again, Shirley moved back to Cold Lake – and onto an acreage in Cherry Grove. She continued to teach at the Department of National Defence schools until she transitioned to full time gardener, church worker, canner, cook, neighbor gatherer, fisherman and volunteer at the food bank.
In 2024 Shirley moved into a condo in Lethbridge. This gave her the opportunity to spend more time with family in Southern Alberta. Shirley was diagnosed with terminal cancer on April 9, 2026. Previous to this she loved getting at least her 10,000 steps in a day, yoga and swimming in her condo pool. This diagnosis was a shock for sure but not once did Shirley complain or fear the end of life. Shirley spent the last two months living with her son and daughter-in-law and thought that every day she saw another sunrise was a gift. Shirley was a pure example of keeping her faith, sharing her testimony of the Savior, and enduring to the End.

text:
Bevans, Marjorie Lorna - Legacy Funeral Home
Marjorie Lorna (Klingbell) Bevans was born October 19, 1940 in Beausejour Manitoba to William Klingbell and Evelyn Phyllis (Miller) Klingbell. Marge passed away June 9, 2026 in Cardston Alberta with her loving husband by her side. Marjorie was pre-deceased by her parents, her brothers Bill, Fred and George Klingbell.
Marjorie is survived by her loving husband Brent Bevans, their combined families of 10 children, 34 grandchildren, 11 great grandchildren and 1 great great granddaughter, Lilly. Marge is also survived by her twin brothers Edward and Elvin Klingbell.
Marge spent her early growing years in and around the Beausejour area. She remained there in her early adult life and went on to become a hair-dresser. She owned and operated her own Beauty Salon in Beausejour. The iconic building she owned and operated from, to this very day is a Beauty Salon, with living accommodations in the upstairs. She was so proud of her accomplishments there. In the years to follow, she returned many times to visit and reminisce with the owners and the customers.
It was here in Beausejour that two of her five children were born. Bryan and Brenda were to share with their mother many memories that each of them came to cherish through the years.
In the early 70’s, Marge came out west to eventually settle in the Cardston area. This is where she really found herself and settled permanently. She said many times that once she saw the mountains, she knew she was home. This is where she went on to develop her talents and love for life. This is where the next additions to her family came to be. Michael was an unexpected blessing she was forever grateful for. Marcia and Justin brought with them an unexpected flare of excitement to her life. She went on to become a great lover of the theatre and the world of costume creations. She tells that back in her earlier school days that she couldn’t abide the “organized” home-ec. courses for fledgling sewers, and simply had to break-out on her own. 
Over the years, Marjorie has dedicated 45 years of service to the “Carriage House Theatre” world, as their costume specialist. Her favorite piece she ever created was the amazing techni-colored coat that Joseph wore in that production. 
She also created over the years, countless wedding gowns, graduation dresses, formal gowns, and a multitude of other creations. Her motto regarding sewing possibilities was, “You’re only Limited by your Imaginations. If you can Imagine it, I can create it.”
She was a very accomplished artist. Her paintings, mainly scenic panoramas are priceless. Her favorite subject was our land mark, “Chief Mountain”. 
Her greatest love and accomplishment was that of her family. When she found the love of her life, they together spent countless days, months and years cultivating meaningful relationships with their children, grandchildren and extended families. Music continues to be that binding force that holds our family together. Where relationships were tested throughout the years, together they stayed committed to rebuild what once was broken. To the very end, nothing was more important to Marjorie Lorna Bevans than her husband, kids and family.
​
Friends may meet the family on Sunday, June 14th, from 7:00 - 8:00 pm at Legacy Funeral Home, Cardston, or at the Church on Monday from 10:00 - 10:45 am, prior to the service. 
The Funeral Service will be held at The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, Leavitt, Alberta on Monday, June 15th, 2026 at 11:00 a.m. 
Interment to follow in the Leavitt Cemetery.

# Bevans, Marjorie Lorna - Legacy Funeral Home

![Picture](https://www.legacyfuneralhome.ca/uploads/1/3/3/9/13390033/published/bevans-marjorie-1.jpg?1781294204)

**Marjorie Lorna (Klingbell) Bevans** was born October 19, 1940 in Beausejour Manitoba to William Klingbell and Evelyn Phyllis (Miller) Klingbell. Marge passed away June 9, 2026 in Cardston Alberta with her loving husband by her side.  Marjorie was pre-deceased by her parents, her brothers Bill, Fred and George Klingbell.  
Marjorie is survived by her loving husband Brent Bevans, their combined families of 10 children, 34 grandchildren, 11 great grandchildren and 1 great great granddaughter, Lilly.  Marge is also survived by her twin brothers Edward and Elvin Klingbell.  
Marge spent her early growing years in and around the Beausejour area.  She remained there in her early adult life and went on to become a hair-dresser.  She owned and operated her own Beauty Salon in Beausejour.  The iconic building she owned and operated from, to this very day is a Beauty Salon, with living accommodations in the upstairs. She was so proud of her accomplishments there.  In the years to follow, she returned many times to visit and reminisce with the owners and the customers.  
It was here in Beausejour that two of her five children were born.  Bryan and Brenda were to share with their mother many memories that each of them came to cherish through the years.  
In the early 70’s, Marge came out west to eventually settle in the Cardston area.  This is where she really found herself and settled permanently. She said many times that once she saw the mountains, she knew she was home.  This is where she went on to develop her talents and love for life.  This is where the next additions to her family came to be.  Michael was an unexpected blessing she was forever grateful for.  Marcia and Justin brought with them an unexpected flare of excitement to her life.  She went on to become a great lover of the theatre and the world of costume creations.  She tells that back in her earlier school days that she couldn’t abide the “organized” home-ec. courses for fledgling sewers, and simply had to break-out on her own.   
Over the years, Marjorie has dedicated 45 years of service to the “Carriage House Theatre” world, as their costume specialist.  Her favorite piece she ever created was the amazing techni-colored coat that Joseph wore in that production.   
She also created over the years, countless wedding gowns, graduation dresses, formal gowns, and a multitude of other creations.  Her motto regarding sewing possibilities was, “You’re only Limited by your Imaginations.  If you can Imagine it, I can create it.”  
She was a very accomplished artist.  Her paintings, mainly scenic panoramas are priceless.  Her favorite subject was our land mark, “Chief Mountain”.   
Her greatest love and accomplishment was that of her family.  When she found the love of her life, they together spent countless days, months and years cultivating meaningful relationships with their children, grandchildren and extended families.  Music continues to be that binding force that holds our family together.  Where relationships were tested throughout the years, together they stayed committed to rebuild what once was broken.  To the very end, nothing was more important to Marjorie Lorna Bevans than her husband, kids and family.  
​  
Friends may meet the family on Sunday, June 14th, from 7:00 - 8:00 pm at Legacy Funeral Home, Cardston, or at the Church on Monday from 10:00 - 10:45 am, prior to the service.    
The Funeral Service will be held at The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, Leavitt, Alberta on Monday, June 15th, 2026 at 11:00 a.m.    
Interment to follow in the Leavitt Cemetery.
