Olsen, Georgean - Legacy Funeral Home
Mary Georgean (Caldwell) Olsen passed away peacefully in her home on the Ranch with all her children by her side on Tuesday, June 9, 2026 at the age of 95 years.
Georgean leaves behind her cherished posterity: children Nolen (Vicky) Olsen, Terrie (Drew) Bullock, Mary (Robert) Woolf, Maxwell (Keiko) Olsen, Paula (Locke) Marshall; 17 (plus their spouses) Grandchildren; 48 Great-Grandchildren; 3 Great-Great-Grandchildren; as well as numerous extended family. Besides her beloved husband Ben, Georgean is predeceased by her infant daughter Lynna.
Georgean was born on September 24, 1930, in Calgary, Alberta, and was lovingly adopted as an infant by Maxwell and Mary Caldwell of Hill Spring, Alberta. Their devotion and unwavering love shaped the foundation of her remarkable life. 
A gifted pianist from childhood, Georgean earned her ARCT music degree and shared her talents generously throughout her life. She was sought after and well known for her talents and abilities in music. She served as church pianist and organist for many years and taught piano lessons to generations of students, inspiring a love of music that became part of her enduring legacy.
In March of 1954, Ben Royce Olsen walked into her life at the Treasury Branch Bank where she was working. After a quick courtship they were married on July 22, 1954, and then sealed for time and all eternity in the Cardston Alberta Temple. They lived life to the fullest together for 62 years before Ben passed away. Together they built a life centered on faith, hard work, hospitality, and family.
Georgean and Ben made their forever home on the Ranch between the Crooked Creek and the Waterton River, where they raised their family and created a gathering place filled with laughter, music, and love. She made her home a safe place, with her listening ear, open heart, and an abundance of delicious food. Surrounded by the beautiful Rocky Mountains she loved, Georgean enjoyed the blessings of nature that surrounded her. She enjoyed growing plants and flowers inside and out; her home was always filled with the proof of her green thumbs.
A faithful member of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, Georgean served diligently throughout her life in many callings, especially with music. Alongside Ben, they dedicated 23 years of continuous service in the Cardston Alberta Temple on Thursday afternoons and made many cherished friends. Her love of the Savior guided her life. 
Though she will be deeply missed, her legacy continues in the lives of her children, grandchildren, great-grandchildren, extended family, students, and countless friends whose lives she touched.
The Funeral service will be held Monday, June 15th, 2026 at 11:00 AM at The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-Day Saints in Mountain View, Alberta. Friends may meet the family from 10:00 to 10:45 prior to the service. Interment to follow in the Mountain View Cemetery.

text:
Kolibar, Andrew - Legacy Funeral Home
Andrew (Andy) Robert Kolibar, husband of the late Wanda Wright Kolibar, celebrated his 92nd birthday just the way he wanted—graduating on to be with his wife and family on the other side. He was born on June 7, 1934, in Leross, Saskatchewan, to Joseph Nemeth and Anna Kolibar.
Raised by immigrants during the Depression and wartime years, Andy knew hardship from the very beginning of his life. His family moved to Barnwell, Alberta, when he was a young boy. There, he worked in the sugar beet fields and often missed school because there was work to be done. As a result, he received very little formal education. When Andy lost his mother at the age of 15, he learned to make his own way in the world, working as a farm hand and developing the resilience, resourcefulness, and strong work ethic that would shape the rest of his life.
When he shared those stories of his life, he rarely focused on what he lacked. Instead, he remembered the people who helped him, the lessons he learned, and the funny things that happened along the way. He became incredibly resourceful, and it showed in everything he did. He taught himself the skills he needed to get by and enjoyed learning so that he could do what needed to be done without having to rely on others.
As a young adult, Andy worked on a survey crew which brought him to Cardston as they worked on the St Mary’s Dam. This is where he saw his bride to be walking down the street. He knew he had to meet her. They were married on March 30, 1955. Andy and Wanda started their early married life with Andy working on oil and pot ash rigs for a few years, but when he realized that was not the life he wanted for his family they moved back to Cardston. 
He had the opportunity to attend mechanic school, where he excelled and graduated at the top of his class. He worked as a mechanic at Central Service before owning the Cardston Texaco Station and later opening Andy's Auto Service.
Andy was well known for his accordion playing and performed at many dance halls and weddings throughout the years as a member of the Foothills Five. He and Wanda loved to dance and attended many dances together. They also served as lead instructors for several church youth dance festivals, sharing their love of music and dancing with others.
He also had a passion for flying and had the opportunity to co-own an airplane for a few years. Family and friends loved going up flying with him. He flew many community members to various destinations.
Andy worked hard, but he also knew how to enjoy life, especially with his close friends and family. There were many boating, waterskiing and camping adventures in the summer and snow skiing in the winter. He worked hard so that his children could experience many of the things he never had while growing up.
He is survived by his five children: Bob (Karen) Kolibar, Colleen Leavitt (Khuram Fancy), Kendall (Karen) Kolibar, Karen (Gerald) Bevans, and Barb (Jesse) Wilson; 22 grandchildren; and 33 great-grandchildren.
He is now reunited with his wife Wanda, his parents, and his siblings, Martin, Mike, Margaret, and Irene.
​A viewing and opportunity to meet the family will be held on Friday, June 12, from 7:00 to 8:00 p.m. at Legacy Funeral Home. A graveside service will be held on Saturday, June 13, at 12:00 p.m. at the Beazer Cemetery.

text:
Small, Julee - Legacy Funeral Home
It is with great sadness that the family of Julee Alice Small announces her passing on 16 May 2026 peacefully at her home in Cardston.
Julee was born in the City of Calgary on 25 Jan 1952. Despite a bad snow storm Theron and Alice Smith drove up because Theron was positive to adopt the girl, a story he would share with his grandson decades later.
Julee happily grew up with her brother Terry and Randy, brothers who loved their sister. She also loved her cousins Darlean, Ford, Shannon and Ron. She would become friends with Randy’s wife Val and their two children Kandice and TJ.
While at university down in Logan Julee met her life long best friend Aloha, both would go on to have many adventures together.
After university she went on to teach, where she befriended Judy. While delivering Judy’s husband, Fred lunch one day Julee met the love of her Life, Fred’s friend, Ronald James Small. The two eventually married and had one son Jeff Small. Ron was the only person to call her “Jules”, something she fondly remembered. While they lived in Lethbridge she befriended Kyomi and Dot as well as family friends Ginia and her husband Ron. 
The Small Family would have many travels together, one favourite place was the BC coast where Ron’s family lived, often staying at his sister’s Wendy place with her husband Gene and two daughters Stacy and Josee. As well as visiting Anne & William and their family, Jo Ann, Jesse and David. Also visiting more of Ron’s family including Brian, Bill & Marlean and Sam & Mary.
Eventually when Ron retired they would travel in their RV. After that they moved to Cardston, where they would celebrate many Christmases together by having their annual tradition of watching National Lampoons Christmas Vacation and Alister Sim’s Scrooge. Christmas shopping together was a favourite of theirs.
In Cardston Julee made friends and acquaintances with many people including Mel.
Julee loved to travel including going on cruises, either with Ron or later with her good friend Aloha where they would visit Europe twice.
Sadly in June 2024 Ron passed away, Julee and Jeff helped each other through this sad and difficult time, with also the help of their beloved family and friends, until Julee’s passing. Julee is survived by her son Jeff Small. 
Julee’s skills with people and social situations were second to non, and her warm loving personality made her lots of friends, only to be surpassed by her great devotion to her family and her love for them. She will be greatly missed and remembered fondly. Goodbye Mom “I can no longer hold you in my arms, so I will hold you in my Heart” – Jeff Small 2015
There will be a private memorial for Julee at a later date as well as a private burial ceremony. Those who wish to give their condolences can do so at rememberingjuleesmall@outlook.com 
Those wishing to remember Julee in a special way are invited to make a donation in her memory to either the Heart and Stroke Foundation of Canada, Diabetes Canada, or the Canadian Mental Health Association.

Obituary information for Rosalyn Tomassetti (nee Boyenko)
September 25, 1944 – Saskatoon, Saskatchewan
July 23, 2026 – Calgary, Alberta
It is with profound sadness that we announce the passing of our beloved Mom, Nonna, Zia, Auntie, and dear friend, Rosalyn Tomassetti (née Boyenko), who passed away peacefully on Thursday, July 23, 2026, at the age of 81.
Rosalyn was born on September 25, 1944, in Saskatoon, SK, to John and Caroline Boyenko. She was raised near St. Denis, SK, alongside her five siblings, who have predeceased her: brothers, Harry, Freddy, and Billy; and sisters, Linda and Adeline.
After marrying the love of her life, Aldo Tomassetti, Rosalyn moved to Calgary, AB, and later settled in Airdrie, AB, where her two daughters were raised, and together they built a life filled with love, laughter, lifelong friendships, and treasured family memories. After six decades of marriage, Aldo sadly predeceased Rosalyn on January 17, 2022. Rosalyn was a devoted wife, a loving mother, and a proud Nonna, whose greatest joy was her family.
She is lovingly remembered by her daughters, Kelly Babic (Ivan) and Tracy Tomassetti; her cherished grandchildren, Laurisa, Matteo, Adriana, and Dante; as well as her extended family and many dear friends whose lives were enriched by her kindness, generosity, and quiet strength.
Rosalyn had an adventurous spirit, a keen wit, a caring heart, and a remarkable gift for making everyone feel welcome. She found happiness in spending time with family and friends, tending to her flowers, enjoying coffee, cooking, playing cards, the Nino, dancing, travelling, and creating a warm and welcoming home where everyone felt loved.
After a courageous battle with cancer, Rosalyn passed away peacefully, surrounded by the love of her two daughters.
Although our hearts are broken, we take comfort in knowing she is now reunited with the love of her life, her beloved husband, Aldo.
The family extends their heartfelt gratitude to the compassionate staff at Dulcina Hospice for the exceptional care, kindness, and dignity they provided to their mom during her final days.
Rosalyn will be deeply missed, forever loved, and always remembered. Her love, wisdom, kindness, and generosity will live on in the hearts of all who were fortunate enough to know her.
Funeral Services will be held at McInnis & Holloway (Chapel of the Bells, 2720 Centre Street North, Calgary, AB), on Thursday, August 6, 2026, at 2:30 p.m.
Family and friends who are unable to attend in person are invited to join Mrs. Tomassetti’s service streamed live (see link below) on the day of the service. For those who are unable to view live, a recording of the service will be posted.
In lieu of flowers, donations in Rosalyn's memory may be made to the Alberta Cancer Foundation, www.albertacancer.ca, or to Dulcina Hospice through the Covenant Foundation, www.covenantfoundation.ca.
Condolences, memories, and photos may be shared and viewed with Rosalyn’s family here.
In living memory of Rosalyn Tomassetti, a tree will be planted in the Ann & Sandy Cross Conservation Area by McInnis & Holloway Funeral Homes. Additional memorial trees will be planted through Canadian conservation and reforestation initiatives, as a result of memorial contributions. McInnis & Holloway, Chapel of the Bells, 2720 Centre Street North, Calgary, AB T2E 2V6, Telephone: 403-276-2296.

Obituary information for Louise Margaret Sunstrum
May 25, 1941 – Parry Sound, Ontario
July 23, 2026 – Calgary, Alberta
Louise Sunstrum of Calgary, AB, passed away on Thursday, July 23, 2026, at the age of 85 years.
Louise was born in Parry Sound, ON, on May 25, 1941.
She travelled extensively and lived in a number of different cities before settling in Calgary, AB, in 1980.
She graduated from Laurentian University with a degree in Education and was an elementary school teacher in both Ontario and Alberta for more than 30 years.
She was a member of the Alexandra Writers Centre Society and spent many of her retirement years dedicated to writing poetry, short stories, and plays. She was also a member of the Silver Stars Musical Revue and spent many years singing and dancing with the group to Broadway numbers.
Louise was an avid traveller and enjoyed seeing the world with her sisters, friends, or solo, visiting exotic locations, such as South Africa, Peru, Mexico, California, Antarctica, and parts of Europe.
She had a love of nature and especially enjoyed hiking in the Rocky Mountains. She lived in Cochrane, AB, for a time in her later years so she could see the mountains every day.
Louise believed joy could be found in any situation, and she found beauty and happiness in the simple pleasures of life, whether that was visiting with old friends, making a new friend, going for a bike ride or a nature walk, dancing, singing, listening to music, or writing.
Louise is survived by her daughter and son-in-law, Natika Sunstrum and Jeremy O’Connor of Calgary, AB; and two grandchildren, Noah and Sam O’Connor of Calgary, AB.
She is also survived by her brothers, Andre (Pat) Roy of Tillsonburg, ON, Robert (Diane) Roy of Barrie, ON, and Gourley Roy of Britt, ON; sisters, Kathleen ("Tiss") Roy of North Bay, ON, Betty (Pat) Courneene of Sault Ste. Marie, ON, and Adrienne Ethen of Sault Ste. Marie, ON; as well as numerous nieces, nephews, cousins, and friends, including niece, Anna (Wayne) Paulson of Blackie, AB; and niece, Donna (Andy) Lloyd of Calgary, AB.
She was predeceased by her parents, Louisa (Gourley) and Onesime Roy, of Britt, ON; her brother, Onzie Roy Jr., of Britt, ON; and sisters, Joan (Roy) Biassucci, of Sudbury, ON, and Frances Secord Roy, of Elliot Lake, ON.
Memorial Services will be held at McInnis & Holloway (Fish Creek, 14441 Bannister Road SE, Calgary, AB) on Friday, August 7, 2026, at 2:30 p.m. Reception to follow in the Hospitality Centre at the Funeral Home. The family encourages attendees to wear their brightest colours or white in celebration of Louise’s love of life and joy.
If friends so desire, memorial tributes may be made directly to Covenant House Vancouver, www.covenanthousebc.org.

Obituary information for Sandra Dianne Follett
February 6, 1945 – Calgary, Alberta
July 22, 2026 – Calgary, Alberta
Sandra Dianne Follett, 81, of Calgary, AB, passed away on Wednesday, July 22, 2026, due to complications of Multiple Myeloma.
Sandra was born in Calgary, AB, to Isobel Snowdon and F. Bertram (Bert) Follett on February 6, 1945. She received her early education in Montreal, QC, Kamloops, BC, and Calgary due to her father's military career.
She earned a BSc in Nutrition from the University of Alberta in 1966 and completed her dietetic internship at Montreal General Hospital in 1967. Sandra worked as a Registered Dietitian in Montreal in both clinical and long-term care settings before concluding her career in Food Services Management at Foothills Medical Centre in Calgary.
Following her retirement, Sandra felt blessed to spend ten years as the Program Lead and instructor for the Nutrition Manager Program at Bow Valley College, where she shared her knowledge and experience with future professionals. Throughout her career, she was an active member of the Alberta Dietetic Association and Dietitians of Canada.
Sandra filled her life with music, both instrumental and choral, embracing classical music through the University of Alberta Mixed Chorus and Festival Chorus, as well as folk, jazz, and bluegrass. She loved nature and treasured time spent camping, travelling, and gardening. She was a lifelong active member of the United Church of Canada, where she formed, acquired, and developed a compassionate faith.
Sandra is survived by her sister, Lorna McNeill (Terry), her daughter, Jessica Horvath, and her children, all of Montreal, QC; and a loving extended family of nieces and nephews.
She was predeceased by her mother and father; her sister, Karen Follett, and her husband, Norris Bick.
Sandra always cherished her many professional colleagues and friends. She was caring, cheerful, and had an inquisitive mind.
A Celebration of Sandra’s Life will be held at Summit View Church (3303 Capitol Hill Crescent NW, Calgary, AB), on Monday, August 24, 2026, at 2:00 p.m. Reception to follow at the church.
If friends so desire, memorial tributes may be made directly to Multiple Myeloma Canada, www.support.myeloma.ca.
Condolences, memories, and photos may be shared and viewed with Sandra’s family here.
In living memory of Sandra Follett, a tree will be planted in the Ann & Sandy Cross Conservation Area by McInnis & Holloway Funeral Homes. Additional memorial trees will be planted through Canadian conservation and reforestation initiatives, as a result of memorial contributions. McInnis & Holloway, Crowfoot, 82 Crowfoot Circle NW, Calgary, AB T3G 2T3, Telephone: 403-241-0044.

Obituary information for Jean Emily Temple (nee Brothwell)
August 23, 1928 – Leicestershire, United Kingdom
July 21, 2026 – Calgary, Alberta
Jean Emily Temple departed this world on Tuesday, July 21, 2026, at the age of 97 years, in Calgary, AB.
Born Jean Emily Brothwell on August 23, 1928, in Leicestershire, UK, she was the daughter of Florence Courten and Wilfred Brothwell. She grew up in the village of Countesthorpe, UK, alongside her two sisters, Eileen and Margaret, and her brother, Bob.
Jean leaves behind her five beloved children, Ian, Kathryn, Christopher, Nicholas, and Mark. Together with seven grandchildren and two great-grandchildren, we have much to reflect on, remember, and celebrate within her remarkable life.
Raised in the English countryside, Jean's childhood was shaped by the lingering effects of the First World War and the realities of the Second. She was a gifted pianist and helped her parents in their humble greengrocer shop. She met and married Alan George Temple, and together with baby Mark, they immigrated to Canada. Settling in Ajax, ON, she gave birth to four more children. It was in Ajax that she provided for and raised her family with her love, courage, and dedication whilst Alan pursued a successful career with Litton Systems Canada. Her home was often a beehive of neighbourhood children.
Jean was a gifted pianist. Throughout her life, she developed her talents in art, photography, gardening, travel, and golf. She made birthdays, anniversaries, and Christmas special occasions. Jean welcomed everyone who visited to her dinner table. It was this selfless love that endeared so many friends, family, and loved ones to the Temple household. She loved dogs, sunshine, and the outdoors. Her home always had tea, crumble, or a little something to put jam on. She served love, laughter, and stories of life and resilience.
As a mother, she gave birth to more than children. She planted seeds for the moment and acorns for the future. Her home and her cottage were campfires for gatherings, conversations, and lifelong relationships. Her memory will live long and strong for all those who encountered her. As a wife, she was the strength behind Alan as he contributed to Canada’s technology, growth, and commerce. Together they played an important role in the Etobicoke Swim Club and Olympium. She was an inspiration and mentor to many young people. The independence and singular nature of her children speak with gratitude and humility for their roots.
Jean’s life in The Kingsway and finally in Qualicum, BC, was filled with friends, her art, gardening, and music. From Qualicum, she travelled to California to play golf, bike ride, and pursue her art in January and February each year. She continued to grow friendships and hospitality to all who came to her table. She was often seen with her faithful dog in the golf cart playing an early round. She earned two hole-in-ones in her lifetime.
Her years in Qualicum Beach were the most rewarding years of her life. From Eaglecrest Drive, the relationships she built, the music evenings, the outdoors, and the community were among the greatest rewards for a life worth living. The amazing group of friends added years of golf and pleasure to Jean and Alan’s life.
Jean will be remembered for her strength, selfless caring, and deep love of friends and family. Her friends and children will sorely miss her.
“Whoo Hoo...”
Life flows on within you and without you - music and living one and the same.
Beethoven's Moonlight Sonata
Love you, mum…
As per Jean’s wishes, a private family service will take place.
Condolences, memories, and photos may be shared and viewed with Jean’s family here.

Obituary information for Carla Reed
January 10, 1937 – Shanghai, China
July 21, 2026 – Calgary, Alberta
Carla Reed, 89, passed away peacefully on Tuesday, July 21, 2026, in Calgary, where she had lived during her last year, with family by her side.
She was born on January 10, 1937, in Shanghai, China, to Leila Vennewitz (née Croot) and Hans Melchers. She spent her early childhood in Shanghai during the Second World War, an experience that shaped her perspective and stayed with her throughout her life.
After the war, she and her parents moved first to England and then to Vancouver, BC, Canada, where she attended high school. After beginning her university studies at Pomona College in California, Carla returned to Vancouver to complete her undergraduate degree and Master of Social Work at the University of British Columbia.
In Vancouver, Carla met her husband, Leonard David Reed. They married in 1961 and began a life together that took them to Prince Rupert, BC, before returning to Vancouver and then eventually settling in the Fraser Valley. Together, Carla and Len raised three daughters: Julia, Jennifer, and Jill.
Family life included many shared experiences—camping, hiking, skiing, travelling, and, especially, time spent at their favourite family place, Bowen Island, BC. Carla had a wide range of interests and passions. She loved the outdoors and was deeply interested in nature conservation.
She enjoyed travelling, reading, gardening, and volunteering, and these interests remained important parts of her life. She was also proud of her four grandchildren and one great-grandchild, who were an important part of her later years.
Carla is survived by her three daughters, Julia Reed (Sergio), Jennifer MacPherson (Gord), and Jill Constable (Scott); her four grandchildren, Alison, Owen, Lucas, and Sydney; and one great-grandchild, Elliot.
The family has chosen not to hold a formal service. Instead, her ashes will be scattered in a place she loved.
Those wishing to remember Carla are invited to consider a donation to Nature Conservancy Canada, an organization that was important to her. Donations may be made at www.natureconservancy.ca.
Carla's life was shaped by many places, experiences, interests, and relationships. Her family will carry with them the memories of the life they shared.
Condolences, memories, and photos may be shared and viewed with Carla’s family here.
In living memory of Carla Reed, a tree will be planted in the Ann & Sandy Cross Conservation Area by McInnis & Holloway Funeral Homes. Obituary information for Rosaleen “Rosie” Fox (nee Baptiste)
"Anukâthâ Wîyâ"
December 22, 1969 – Calgary, Alberta
July 21, 2026 – Calgary, Alberta
Rosaleen “Rosie” Lily Fox (nee Baptiste) was called home by our Creator on Tuesday, July 21, 2026, at the age of 56 years. With tearful eyes, we watched you take your last breath and pass peacefully. Although we care and love you deeply, we could not make you stay forever.
Rosie was born on December 22, 1969, in Calgary, AB. She was a very kind-hearted and loving mother who turned no one away and loved everyone around her equally. She did not hesitate to lend a helping hand and always had support for all her friends and family. She would also take the lead in getting family together for birthdays, holidays, and special events. In her teens, she enjoyed playing recreational sports such as volleyball and baseball, which earned her the nickname Dottie from her brother-in-law Reggie. In her later years, she enjoyed spending her time playing darts in the Bow Valley area with her dart family.
Every summer, she loved to plan and take camping and hunting trips up north. She enjoyed cooking and spending time with her sisters and making new memories. She was a very traditional person and did her best to pass her traditions down to her daughters.
Rosie is survived by her children, Julienne (Wendel), Virginia (Trendon), Odessa, Nikki, Madison, and adopted son Wayne (Abby); her grandkids, Micah, Mathis, Mylo, Miguel, and Myles; her siblings, Jubileen (Keith), Jubol (Georgina), Jenny (Reggie), Jolie, Aaron Young, adopted brother-cousin Jerome (Mel) Baptiste, Conlin (Josette), Johnny, and Dallas Powderface; adopted sisters, Shallon and Kylena Powderface, Carrie Labelle, and Sindy and Mandy Bearspaw. She had many adopted siblings.
She is also survived by paternal aunties, Eva Baptiste (auntie-mom), and Corina (Lenny); adopted mom Verna Powderface; paternal uncle Norman Baptiste; maternal uncles, Bruce (Jennifer), Peter (Marcy), Eli, Roderick Labelle, and Murphy (Laura); maternal aunties, Wendy Twoyoungmen and Georgina Labelle; nephews and nieces, Levi (Robin), Holly (Cornell), Chental (Trennen), Clint (Tessa), Logan, Luke, Elyse Poucette, Sidney, Gino Twoyoungmen, Alice (Mitch), Alex, Kelrick (Jayden), Araya (Wahrmun) Tatum, Jaydon Smalleyes, Jovanna, Mariah, Mercedes, Darren Jr. (Tanisha), Denzel (Janet), and Jarron (Alicia) Dixon; and mother-in-law Mary Fox.
Rosie was predeceased by her parents, Raymond Baptiste and Virginia Twoyoungmen; paternal grandparents, Alex and Lily (nee Abenezer) Baptiste; maternal grandparents, Pete Labelle and Florence Twoyoungmen (nee Powderface), and Frank (Norma) Powderface; great-grandparents, Johnny and Annie Powderface (nee Chiniquay); maternal uncles, Harvey and Russell Twoyoungmen, Alvin (Madeline) Young, Geralda (Velma), and Charles and Clifford Powderface; maternal auntie Sherri Powderface; paternal uncles, Sam, Jimmy, Enoch, Genrich, Ronald, and Kenneth Baptiste; paternal aunties, Elsie (Eddie Sr.) Holloway, Helen (Walter) Chiniquay, Mary Baptiste, and Bobbi Stephens; close cousins, Gabriel and Jordan Twoyoungmen, and Felicia and Renita Young; and her niece Brittany Dixon.
Wake Services will be held at the residence of the Late Rosaleen Lily Baptiste Fox (Mînî Thnî, AB) on Sunday, July 26, 2026, and Monday, July 27, 2026.
Funeral Services will be held at Mînî Thnî Gymnasium (Mînî Thnî, AB) on Tuesday, July 28, 2026, at 11:00 a.m. Graveside Service to follow at Bearspaw Cemetery (Mînî Thnî, AB). Friends and relatives are invited to join the family for a Traditional Feast at Mînî Thnî Gymnasium (Mînî Thnî, AB).
Condolences, memories, and photos may be shared and viewed with Rosaleen’s family here.
In living memory of Rosaleen Fox, a tree will be planted in the Ann & Sandy Cross Conservation Area by McInnis & Holloway Funeral Homes. Additional memorial trees will be planted through Canadian conservation and reforestation initiatives, as a result of memorial contributions. McInnis & Holloway, Cochrane, 369 Railway Street, Cochrane, AB T4C 2E2, Telephone: 403-932-4740.

Obituary information for Thelma "Adelene" Sartison (nee Moe)
December 31, 1935 – Camrose, Alberta
July 22, 2026 – Calgary, Alberta
Thelma “Adelene” Sartison (nee Moe) was born in Camrose, AB, on December 31, 1935, and passed away peacefully on Wednesday, July 22, 2026, at the age of 90, surrounded by her family.
She looked forward to joining her family in Heaven: her parents, Adolph and Thora (Olson) Moe; her siblings, Orvel, Maynard, Arnold, Eileen (Ed Salte), Ordien, and Norman (Enid); her parents-in-law, Christian and Mearilda Sartison; and the many friends who have gone before her. She was always known as Adelene or Addy.
Adelene was the youngest of seven children born to Adolph and Thora, who were a part of the Norwegian immigrant families that came to Canada from the Dakotas at the turn of the 20th century to settle and farm in the area around Camrose. A rich heritage of faith, family, community, and song infused her life from birth.
Addy was baptized, confirmed, and married at Scandia Lutheran Church in Armena, AB. Her education began at Thordenskjold School, a one-room schoolhouse west of Armena. She graduated from Camrose Lutheran College in 1953 and then attended the Canadian Lutheran Bible Institute.
Adelene's care and compassion for others led her to pursue a career in nursing. She attended the Royal Alexandra Hospital School of Nursing in Edmonton, AB, from 1955 to 1958, remaining friends with many of her classmates and attending reunions regularly.
She worked as a nurse for most of her life in many capacities and locations, including Red Deer General Hospital; the Royal Alexandra Hospital in Edmonton, AB; Bethany Nursing Home in Camrose, AB; University Hospital in Saskatoon, SK; Bethany Care Centre in Calgary, AB; and, finally, Frank Eliason Centre and Parkridge Centre in Saskatoon, SK. She was a genuine caregiver. Anyone who had Nurse Adelene at their bedside would have felt valued and comforted by her great love, grace, and skill.
Music was central to Adelene's life. She was a skilled pianist and organist who played for church services, choirs, other groups, and soloists. She accompanied her daughter Marla in all her voice lessons and recitals. She learned to play the piano on the old family piano, which now resides in the home of one of her sons. Her children have fond memories of singing on car trips, learning to harmonize, and committing many old hymns to memory.
It was her piano playing that led her to the love of her life. A young man named Telmor Sartison saw her playing the piano at an evening youth gathering at church. He said, "I like the way you play the piano. Can I give you a ride home?" One year after her graduation from the Royal Alexandra Hospital School of Nursing, they were married. This was the beginning of a truly devoted relationship, full of great love. They celebrated their 67th wedding anniversary on July 18, 2026, just four days before her passing.
Telmor and Adelene called many places home. They began their life in Edmonton, before driving their little Volkswagen, with all their belongings and three small children, to Saskatoon, SK, where Addy worked as a nurse while Telmor studied at seminary for four years. Their next move took them to rural Jansen, SK, where they served their first parish for three years and came away with lasting friendships.
A move to Calgary brought them to Faith Lutheran Church, where Addy continued her nursing career and became immersed in the life of the church. Friends from those years shared countless New Year's Eve celebrations and Autumn Trippers adventures with them. Next came a return to Saskatoon, followed by a move to Winnipeg, MB, on the banks of Sturgeon Creek, and finally back to Calgary to enjoy their retirement.
Adelene will live on in memories cherished, stories told, songs sung, lefse parties thrown, and adventures enjoyed by her three children and their spouses: Marla (Paul) Mulloy, Garth (Leslie-Ann), and Paul (Val From); her seven treasured grandchildren: Andraea Sartison (Thomas Jordan), Erik Sartison (Jessica Forgeron), Aviva Mulloy (Lachy Pound), Ben Sartison (Stacey Huculak), Zackary Mulloy, Joseph Sartison (Carlann Scott), and Joshua Mulloy (Karolina Donnelly); as well as Jawad, Maliha, Ahrar, Naqib, and Banmeet; and the new joy of her great-grandchildren: Hawksley and Stellan, Freja and Ada, and Lily; along with many nieces, nephews, in-laws, and friends.
Throughout her life, Addy lived with strength, resilience, and joy in the face of Type 1 diabetes, various other health challenges, and the loss of her sight later in life. She is now at peace, whole and free.
Funeral Services will be held at Advent Lutheran Church (11 Scenic Acres Gate NW, Calgary, AB), on Friday, August 28, 2026, at 2:00 p.m. Reception to follow at the Church Hall.
Family and friends who are unable to attend in person are invited to join the service streamed live (see link below) on the day of the service.
If friends so desire, in lieu of flowers, please consider donating to Canadian Lutheran World Relief, www.clwr.org, Camp Kuriakos, www.kuriakos.ab.ca, or to a charity of your choice.
Condolences, memories, and photos may be shared and viewed with Addy’s family here.
In living memory of Addy Sartison, a tree will be planted in the Ann & Sandy Cross Conservation Area by McInnis & Holloway Funeral Homes. Additional memorial trees will be planted through Canadian conservation and reforestation initiatives, as a result of memorial contributions. McInnis & Holloway, Crowfoot, 82 Crowfoot Circle NW, Calgary, AB T3G 2T3, Telephone: 403-241-0044.

Obituary information for Warren Mathew Schueller
June 23, 1964 – Watson, Saskatchewan
July 22, 2026 – Calgary, Alberta
It is with great sadness that we share the sudden passing of Warren Schueller, of Calgary, AB, on Wednesday, July 22, 2026, at the age of 62.
Warren was born in Watson, SK, on June 23, 1964. He moved to Calgary in 1993, where he started a new chapter in his life on the oil rigs and established the foundation for the years that followed. His years in the oil industry reflected his determination, resilience, and willingness to work hard to provide a good life for himself and those he loved. After years in the oil industry, he chose to follow a different path – one that allowed him to be closer to home. He started his own landscaping company, where he found great satisfaction in working for himself, building something of his own, and seeing the results of his hard work come to life.
He had a lifelong passion for Harley-Davidson motorcycles and found great joy in the freedom of the open road, the adventures along the way, and the friendships he built through riding. He enjoyed the many trips to Mexico with family and friends, where good company, laughter, and time together created lasting memories. Above all, he deeply valued time with his family and took great pride and joy in being a father and grandfather. The memories created with his loved ones will be held in their hearts forever.
Though he often presented a tough exterior, those fortunate enough to know him well discovered a man of remarkable kindness, generosity, and love.
Warren was predeceased by his parents, Sheila and Leonard Schueller.
He is lovingly remembered and deeply missed by his daughter and son-in-law, Christy and Brendan Fynn; and his two grandchildren, Levi and Madison, of Calgary, AB; and the mother of his child, Lynn King, of Calgary, AB, with whom he shared decades of love, friendship, and family.
He is forever remembered with love by his sister, Lory, and her husband, Garry Rintoul; his brother, Terry Schueller; his brother, Clifford, and his wife, Nadine Schueller; his brother, Kevin Schueller; and his sister, Kelly, and her husband, Marty Dick; all of Saskatoon, SK. Along with his immediate family, he leaves behind many nieces and nephews, extended family members, and lifelong friends.
The family would like to thank all those who offered their support and kindness during this difficult time.
Condolences, memories, and photos may be shared and viewed with Warren’s family here.
In living memory of Warren Schueller, a tree will be planted in the Ann & Sandy Cross Conservation Area by McInnis & Holloway Funeral Homes. Additional memorial trees will be planted through Canadian conservation and reforestation initiatives, as a result of memorial contributions. McInnis & Holloway, Fish Creek, 14441 Bannister Road SE, Calgary, AB T2X 3J3, Telephone: 403-256-9575.

His years in the oil industry reflected his determination, resilience, and willingness to work hard to provide a good life for himself and those he loved. After years in the oil industry, he chose to follow a different path – one that allowed him to be closer to home. He started his own landscaping company, where he found great satisfaction in working for himself, building something of his own, and seeing the results of his hard work come to life.

He is forever remembered with love by his sister, Lory, and her husband, Garry Rintoul; his brother, Terry Schueller; his brother, Clifford, and his wife, Nadine Schueller; his brother, Kevin Schueller; and his sister, Kelly, and her husband, Marty Dick; all of Saskatoon, SK. Along with his immediate family, he leaves behind many nieces and nephews, extended family members, and lifelong friends.

The family would like to thank all those who offered their support and kindness during this difficult time.

Obituary information for David Howard Ferguson
June 13, 1940 – Calgary, Alberta
July 20, 2026 – Calgary, Alberta
David Howard Ferguson, a well-known and highly respected musician, teacher, and conductor, passed away peacefully with his three children by his side and comforted by beautiful choral music.
After struggling with vascular dementia for almost two decades, David is now at peace and reunited with his loving and devoted wife of 62 years, Barbara, who passed away last summer.
He will be greatly missed by his son David Ferguson Jr. (and his wife Stephanie) of Calgary, and his daughters Kerry Minchin (and her husband John, his son Sean, and their son David) of rural Lac Ste. Anne County, AB, and Kim Jones (and her husband Evan and their children Carson and Tessa) of Tallahassee, FL, as well as his cousins, nephews, nieces, and their own families. David was predeceased by his parents Howard and Betty Ferguson (née Buckley), and his sisters Dawn Graham (and her husband Gordon) and Diane Valentine, all of Calgary. His remaining sister Danise Ferguson (predeceased by her husband Ron Boorne) lives in Sackville, NB.
David enjoyed a long career as a chorister, soloist, teacher, and conductor, known for working with musicians of all ages and abilities. He was a noted music arranger, vocal coach and clinician, and was frequently engaged as a choral adjudicator and guest conductor.
While he is best known for leading his many choirs and ensembles in Calgary, David will also be lovingly remembered for his kind spirit, his gentle soul, and his love for family, gardening and the natural world.
Born in Calgary in 1940, David Ferguson grew up in a very musical family. His early involvement with sacred music in the United Church of Canada set the stage for what was to become a long and distinguished career.
At Wesley United Church, David performed solos as a boy soprano and was directing Wesley’s Children's Choir by the age of fifteen. Soon after, he began conducting the Calgary United Church Young People’s Choir, a city-wide group of singers that performed for various local congregations. It was through this Young People’s Choir, that David met a lovely alto named Barbara. They were married in 1962 and raised three musical children together.
Though he became a candidate for the Ministry of the United Church of Canada in 1962, it was when David heard Lloyd Erickson’s choir at Central United Church that his focus shifted. No longer would his ministry be delivered through readings and sermons, but instead through choral music and in the accompanying texts of the works he chose. After David and Barbara joined Central United Church, David began vocal studies with Lloyd Erickson and served as assistant conductor of the choir. Under Erickson’s mentorship, David earned his ARCT in vocal performance and was a dedicated member of the Lloyd Erickson Singers.
After receiving his B.Ed. in Music in 1966, David went on to teach at several different elementary and junior high schools before settling into his long-term position in 1970 at Western Canada High School, where he taught until his retirement in 1995. While at Western, he developed and directed a full music programme, teaching orchestra, band, and choral classes, and led several award-winning extra-curricular choirs, chamber ensembles, and Gilbert and Sullivan operetta productions. He founded and conducted the Mount Royal Youth Choir in 1981, and was appointed as the Artistic Director of the Mount Royal Conservatory of Music Choral Program in 1990.
Upon retiring from the Calgary Board of Education in 1995, David formed and directed the adult choir Mount Royal Kantorei and also served for three years as Chorusmaster of the Calgary Philharmonic Chorus. David felt strongly about the importance of performing music by Canadian composers and commissioned choral pieces by Stephen Chatman, Imant Raminsh, and Ruth Watson Henderson. Over the years, his choirs won innumerable music competitions and toured both nationally and internationally. In addition to his choirs’ accomplishments, David received much recognition and many awards for his own achievements over the years, including the Alberta Achievement Award of Excellence, the Calgary Kiwanis Festival Rose Bowl, the Alberta Choral Federation Award of Distinction, and the Choir Alberta Lifetime Achievement Award.
Throughout his life, David maintained a strong connection with the United Church of Canada. After completing his Master’s Degree in Choral Conducting from the University of Colorado in 1977, he served as Minister of Music at the United Churches of Southminster, St. Andrew’s, and St. Matthew’s in Calgary. Upon his retirement from St. Matthew’s, he was honoured with the establishment of the David Ferguson Music Fund. His family is so pleased that this fund will help others to continue his legacy of creating and sharing the joy of music.
David Ferguson’s years of musicianship, service, and faith have changed the lives of everyone who was fortunate to have made music with him, and he will be greatly missed.
The family would like to thank the very kind and knowledgeable staff at AgeCare Glenmore and Wentworth Manor for their care and support over the last five years.
Memorial tributes may be made directly to the David Ferguson Music Fund through the United Church of Canada. Chinook Winds Regional Council Office, PO Box 98, Okotoks, AB, T1S 1A4, telephone 403-306-0192. www.chinookwindsregion.ca/david-ferguson-music-fund
Condolences, memories, and photos may be shared and viewed with David’s family here.
In living memory of David Ferguson, a tree will be planted in the Ann & Sandy Cross Conservation Area by McInnis & Holloway Funeral Homes. Additional memorial trees will be planted through Canadian conservation and reforestation initiatives, as a result of memorial contributions. McInnis & Holloway, 5008 Elbow Drive SW, Calgary, AB T2S 2L5, Telephone: 403-243-8200.

Obituary information for Neil “Jackie” Jeffery Crowchild
One Who Walks At Night - Itł’iyà Gúdúwa Nàníyáshà
March 24, 1954 – Tsuut’ina, Alberta
July 20, 2026 – Tsuut’ina, Alberta
Neil “Jackie” Jeffery Crowchild, One Who Walks At Night - Itł’iyà Gúdúwa Nàníyáshà, of Tsuut’ina Nation, AB, passed away on Monday, July 20, 2026, at the age of 72 years.
It is with great sadness that we announce the passing of Neil “Jackie” Crowchild, who was called home to our Creator to join loved ones and family who passed before him. He lived his final days surrounded by family and loved ones at his home in Tsuut’ina, AB.
Neil was born on March 24, 1954, on Tsuut’ina, AB, to Isaac and Edith Crowchild. He was raised on Tsuut’ina, where he built a life rooted in family, community, hard work, and helping others.
Jackie was a family man who married the love of his life, Patricia “Lady Pat,” on December 13, 1997. Together they built a life centred on love, family, and supporting one another through every stage of life. Jackie and Patricia were inseparable and took great pride in raising their family and spending time with their children and grandchildren.
Jackie enjoyed watching hockey, travelling with Patricia, visiting his grandchildren, playing billiards, working on vehicles, and spending time with family. Whether at home, on the road, or gathered with loved ones, he treasured the time he shared with those closest to him.
Jackie was known to be a very hard worker who was always willing to help family, friends, and anyone who could use a helping hand. Throughout his life, he worked in many different roles, including as a drug and alcohol counsellor, explosive ordnance disposal supervisor, medical transportation driver, and several other professions. No matter where he worked, Jackie approached every job with dedication, reliability, and a strong work ethic.
Above all, however, Jackie was known as a mechanic. He worked professionally as a mechanic with the Buffalo Run and Redwood Meadows Golf Courses, where he was respected for his knowledge and ability to solve just about any mechanical problem. Over the years, countless people in the community relied on Jackie to repair their vehicles, and he was always ready to help. Through all seasons and at all hours of the day, he could often be found working on vehicles and passing along his knowledge to anyone willing to learn. His generosity, skill, and willingness to teach made him someone people could always count on.
Jackie shared many stories about growing up in Tsuut’ina, spending time with the old people, hunting, working in the cow camp, and the experiences that shaped him alongside his family. He often spoke fondly of his parents, Edith and Isaac Crowchild, and the values they instilled in him. These stories reflected his deep connection to his Nation, his upbringing, and the traditional Tsuut’ina way of life.
Jackie held a strong belief in the traditional Tsuut’ina ways and in the Great Spirit. His faith guided the way he lived, treated others, and cared for his family throughout his life.
Jackie is reunited with his beloved daughter, Candace, whom he missed dearly, along with his parents, siblings, and loved ones who went before him. He leaves behind a lifetime of memories that will continue to be shared by his family, friends, and all those who had the privilege of knowing him.
Neil is lovingly remembered and survived by his wife, Patricia; his siblings, Alex, Charlie, Frances, and David Meguinis, who was like a brother; his children, Daphne (Jesse), Hollis (Kristi), Jerreth (Meredith), Jackie (Josh), Steven, Charlee (Richie), Georgia (Drey), Allyssa, Megan, and Terrence; grandchildren, Xavier (Brendan), Akasha, Sapphire, Riley, Chris, Devon, Raymond, Dante, Danielle, Delilah, Derrick, Destiny, Dwyte, Thomas, Rain, Birdie, Ira, Ivy, Bowe, Cassian, Ayana, Safina, Zanyla, Hollister Jr., Keanu, Azrael, Creedence, Tobias, Dolly, Tsisga, Clayton, Cashton, and Lily Belle; as well as numerous nieces, nephews, cousins, extended family members, and friends.
Neil is predeceased by his parents, Isaac and Edith Crowchild; his beloved daughter, Candace; his twin sister, Jacqueline; and his siblings, Bradley, Peggy, Irene, Rita, Allan, Elliott, Emerson, Patrick, Ted, Darlene, and Scamp.
Wake Services will be held at the residence of Hollis Crowchild (70 Many Horses Rd, Tsuut'ina Nation, AB), on Saturday, July 25, 2026, at 7:00 p.m.
Funeral Services will be held at Bullhead Community Hall (114 Bullhead Road, Tsuut’ina Nation, AB), on Monday, July 27, 2026, at 12:00 a.m. Graveside Service to follow at Tsuut’ina Cemetery.
Neil’s family would like to thank everyone for their prayers, kindness, and support during this difficult time.
He will be deeply loved, forever remembered, and greatly missed.
Condolences, memories, and photos may be shared and viewed with Neil’s family here.
In living memory of Neil Crowchild, a tree will be planted in the Ann & Sandy Cross Conservation Area by McInnis & Holloway Funeral Homes. Additional memorial trees will be planted through Canadian conservation and reforestation initiatives, as a result of memorial contributions. Obituary information for Robert James Walker Wheatcroft
December 27, 1981 – Calgary, Alberta
July 20, 2026 – Calgary, Alberta
It is with deep sadness that we share the passing of Rob Wheatcroft at the Arthur Child Cancer Centre in the early hours of Monday, July 20, 2026, holding Kelsey’s hand, with family by his side.
Rob was diagnosed with advanced colon cancer in February 2025. True to his nature, Rob faced his cancer journey with admirable determination, positivity, and courage. He shared his energy, humour, and kindness with those around him until the very end.
Rob was born in Calgary, AB, in 1981. He had an active and adventurous youth playing team sports such as hockey and soccer. Rob found his passion for the outdoors at Camp Chief Hector, where he was a camper and then a counsellor for many years. His experiences at camp shaped his character and developed his deep love of paddling and hiking. Rob’s connections with camp and the friends he made there were very important to him and remained strong throughout his life. He enjoyed many paddling trips with these friends and later loved sharing those skills with his nephews and children.
First and foremost, Rob was a loving husband to Kelsey for twelve years of marriage and a devoted dad to Tim and Arwen. He loved volunteering at their school and was a favourite dad in both the classroom and the schoolyard. Playing with his kids was one of Rob’s favourite things, spending hours playing in the backyard, building LEGO, and sharing his video game expertise. Family witnessed many a living room wrestling match and gymnastics routine.
With a deep love for his family, Rob made a lasting, positive impact on both the Wheatcroft and Lough families. He enjoyed family dinners, camping with family at the lakes in the East Kootenays, BC, extended family gatherings in Kimberley, BC, visits to his in-laws in Canmore, AB, or the Lough cottage in Gatineau, QC, and having nephew sleepovers. Rob was a wonderful uncle who connected with each of his nephews and niece at every stage of their lives; from being on the floor reading books, doing puzzles, or playing peek-a-boo to educating them in the kitchen, challenging them in the water, or guiding them in their individual pursuits.
Rob was a generous host and made everyone feel welcome in his and Kelsey’s home. Though quick to lend a hand, ironically, as a guest happy to take a back seat when it came to food preparation. When others admitted they were nervous to cook for a professional chef, Rob would happily say, “if someone else is willing to cook, I am just happy to eat!” Rob was always there to provide expert guidance and often took the helm to create wonderful meals for family and friends. His recipe for French Toast was legendary!
Inspired early in life by his grandma Aitken, Rob developed a passion for food preparation, and he was proud to obtain his Red Seal Certification from SAIT. He garnered his passion to serve good food in a great atmosphere initially as a sous-chef at Earls Restaurant before climbing the ranks to Head Chef at Earls 16th Ave, and it was there he met the love of his life, Kelsey.
Following his dream, Rob created his own personal chef and event catering business, Red Seal Dining, which flourished. He was a natural mentor and leader, and his influence will be carried forward by all who worked with him. He was tremendously proud of his team.
Rob had a strong presence. He was charismatic, kind, considerate, and always generous to others. He had a quick wit and was always the funniest person in the room. A keen thinker who stayed up to date with world news, he offered a unique perspective and opened the eyes of those around him to new ideas. Rob was appreciative and a helper by nature, and his lightheartedness was uplifting. Rob’s friends and family were at the center of everything he did. He touched our lives in countless meaningful ways. We will miss his boisterous laugh and his infectious love of life.
Rob will be lovingly remembered and missed dearly by his wife, Kelsey, his son Tim (10), and daughter Arwen (6); his parents, Tim and Roberta; sister Brandy (Brad), and nephews, Colter and Ryder; sister Jessica (Danny), and nephew Luke. He is also survived by his in-laws, Chris and Jill; “sister” Jen (Shaun), niece Raelyn, and nephew Kyler, as well as extended family on both sides.
A Celebration of Rob’s Life will be held at YMCA’s Camp Chief Hector in the Fall (1 Bowfort Road, Kananaskis, AB), date to be announced, followed by a gathering around Rob’s favourite place, the campfire, to share memories. All who knew Rob are welcome to attend.
If friends so desire, Rob respectfully requests that memorial tributes may be made directly to Camp Chief Hector YMCA, www.ymcacalgary.org/donate-camp-chief-hector, with funds directed to help “send kids to camp”.
Condolences, memories, and photos may be shared and viewed with Rob’s family here.
In living memory of Robert Wheatcroft, a tree will be planted in the Ann & Sandy Cross Conservation Area by McInnis & Holloway Funeral Homes. Additional memorial trees will be planted through Canadian conservation and reforestation initiatives, as a result of memorial contributions. McInnis & Holloway, Crowfoot, 82 Crowfoot Circle NW, Calgary, AB T3G 2T3, Telephone: 403-241-0044.

Obituary information for Joyce Mary Coughlin
October 22, 1936 – Claresholm, Alberta
July 20, 2026 – Calgary, Alberta
Joyce Mary Coughlin passed away peacefully at the age of 89 after being in palliative care at Calgary’s South Health Campus.
Joyce is survived by her brother, Alan; her four children, Jennifer (Dave), David, Lori (Aaron), and Craig (Caro); and her grandchildren, Jamie, Sean, Liam, and Joe. She was predeceased by her son, Carey Todd; her husband, Maurice; her parents, Jessie and Dennis; and her siblings, Joan, Ross and Jim.
Joyce was born in Claresholm, AB, on October 22, 1936, to Jessie and Dennis Mouser. Joyce and her four siblings were raised on the farm. They spent their childhoods helping outside with the crops and animals or in the garden and farmhouse. Joyce preferred time outside playing ball with her brothers or doing outdoor chores, over the more “domestic” chores indoors.
The Mouser farmhouse was a mile from the Salmon farmhouse (Jessie’s parents), and one of Joyce’s favourite stories was how, at the age of three, her dad put her on the horse and she rode it all by herself to her grandparents’ (there may have been some artistic liberties taken when retelling the story…).
After high school, Joyce obtained her teaching certificate and started her career. She taught math and music to junior and senior high students in Lethbridge, Grande Prairie, and Drumheller. It was in Drumheller in 1958 that she met a handsome young redhead named Maurice. Her extroverted feistiness was well matched with his quiet, yet cheeky character. Maurice proposed soon into their courtship, but Joyce tested his determination by turning down numerous proposals over the next several years. Finally, she succumbed, and they married in 1962.
Joyce and Maurice spent their honeymoon travelling by ship to Wellington, New Zealand, where they taught for two years. Upon their return, they built their home in Willow Park, Calgary, where both Maurice and Joyce lived out the rest of their days.
They started a family in 1966, adopting Jennifer, then David in 1968, and Lori in 1970. Lo and behold, a biological son, Craig, rounded out the Coughlin Clan in 1971. Maurice and Joyce provided a loving home filled with opportunities for the children: sports, music and camping, just to name a few. Joyce was born in Claresholm, AB, on October 22, 1936, to Jessie and Dennis Mouser. Joyce and her four siblings were raised on the farm. They spent their childhoods helping outside with the crops and animals or in the garden and farmhouse. Joyce preferred time outside playing ball with her brothers or doing outdoor chores, over the more “domestic” chores indoors.

The Mouser farmhouse was a mile from the Salmon farmhouse (Jessie’s parents), and one of Joyce’s favourite stories was how, at the age of three, her dad put her on the horse and she rode it all by herself to her grandparents’ (there may have been some artistic liberties taken when retelling the story…).

After high school, Joyce obtained her teaching certificate and started her career. She taught math and music to junior and senior high students in Lethbridge, Grande Prairie, and Drumheller. It was in Drumheller in 1958 that she met a handsome young redhead named Maurice. Her extroverted feistiness was well matched with his quiet, yet cheeky character. Maurice proposed soon into their courtship, but Joyce tested his determination by turning down numerous proposals over the next several years. Finally, she succumbed, and they married in 1962.

Joyce and Maurice spent their honeymoon travelling by ship to Wellington, New Zealand, where they taught for two years. Upon their return, they built their home in Willow Park, Calgary, where both Maurice and Joyce lived out the rest of their days.

They started a family in 1966, adopting Jennifer, then David in 1968, and Lori in 1970. Lo and behold, a biological son, Craig, rounded out the Coughlin Clan in 1971. Joyce enjoyed sewing, needlepoint, and took up oil painting as her own mother Jessie had. Joyce was a doting Nana, always ready to help with Jamie and Sean and cherished her visits with Liam and Joe when they visited from Montreal or when she would travel there.

After losing Maurice in 2010, Joyce struggled with finding joy in life; however, she tried her best to keep painting and playing Bridge, but life no longer had its lustre without her mate of over 50 years. The last five years presented significant health challenges for Joyce. Her son David moved in to help with the house, yard, and appointments. Obituary information for Brian Charles Ogg
August 4, 1940 – Winnipeg, Manitoba
July 20, 2026 – Okotoks, Alberta
Brian Ogg, dearest husband of Carol Ogg (née Lee), of Calgary, AB, passed away on Monday, July 20, 2026, at the age of 85 years.
Brian was born in Winnipeg, MB, on August 4, 1940.
He married Carol in 1966 and moved to Calgary, AB, in 1968, where together they built a loving family. Brian worked at Northwest Trust, ATCO, and Nova Chemicals until his retirement.
Brian loved gardening and volunteered for many years at the Calgary Horticultural Society. He also enjoyed square dancing, hiking, swimming, and photography.
Nothing meant more to Brian than his family. He was incredibly proud of his children and grandchildren and never missed an opportunity to cheer them on.
He enjoyed camping trips with his parents and brothers when he was young. Throughout their marriage, Brian and Carol enjoyed many trips together, including the UK, Paris, New York, and Maui, where Brian discovered his love of boogie boarding at the age of 58.
Brian will be remembered for his kindness, patience, and his signature saying, “it’s my lucky day.”
Besides his loving wife, Carol, Brian is survived by his daughter and son-in-law, Lisa and Ian Shirt of Calgary, AB; son, Steven Ogg and partner, Sarah Clark, of Pasadena, CA; and his precious grandchildren, Alaina and Keenan Shirt, and Bodhi Ogg.
He is also survived by his brother and sister-in-law, Doug and Marilyn Ogg, of Surrey, BC.
A Celebration of Brian’s Life will be held on Wednesday, July 29, 2026. For more information, please contact Lisa or Carol.
The family would like to give their great appreciation to the amazing staff at Tudor Manor in Okotoks, AB, who provided exceptionally loving care to Brian and his family for almost nine years.
If friends so desire, memorial tributes may be made directly to Alzheimer Calgary, (www.alzheimercalgary.ca).

Obituary information for Savannah "Aapooyuhpinahki" Rosar...
May 25, 1996 – Calgary, Alberta
July 18, 2026 – Calgary, Alberta
Savannah Red Gun - Crow Eagle of Calgary, AB, passed away on Saturday, July 18, 2026, at the age of 30 years.
Savannah was born in Calgary on May 25, 1996. She was raised by her grandmother, Lillian Fairbrother, in Pincher Creek, AB, where she attended Canyon school. She then moved to Calgary, where she lived until her sudden passing.
Savannah was a very clean and organized person. She was energetic, outgoing, spontaneous, and a very empathetic. She liked basketball and family get-togethers where they would chill at rivers and enjoy family time.
Her most memorable vacation was when she and her sister, Faith, went to Quebec for summer camp where they spent ten days. She loved the many experiences she had, especially all the new people she had the opportunity meet.
Some of Savannah's favourite songs included "MUT" and "Five More Hours" by Chris Brown, "Rockin' Years" by Dolly Parton, "Wagon Wheel" by Darius Rucker, and "Alive" by The Black Eyed Peas.
Savannah had two loving dogs, Mutsiini and Envy.
Savannah is survived by her spouse, Dean Turning Robe Jr.; her beloved children, Cinthia, Olivia, Mia, Carter, and Baby Lucus; siblings, Steven, Faith, Kirk, Alaska, Bronson, Danzig, Orlando, Brooklynn, Jusalo, Charlie, Layne, Dulton, Jacoby, and Maverick; her parents, Delena Red Gun and Geoff Crow Eagle Jr.; grandparents, Sandy and Hubert Yellow Knee, and Mildred and Geoff Crow Eagle Sr.; uncles, Tim and Roy Fairbrother, Shawn and Sunny Redgun, and Tom Anderson; aunties, Sharon, Susan, Yolana, Trish, Sandra, Sunny, and Angie; cousins, Sapphire, Anna, Jayjay, Kaiman, Tanaka, Nyiesha, Darnell, Fabian, Alex, Shania, Demi, Latoya, Gena, Sheena, and Tais; her nephews and nieces, Darius, Dysis, Sophia, Selena, Anastasia, Trenton, Carter, Atresus, Reyna and Rosen, and A’saan; and many relatives, too numerous to mention from the Siksika Nation and Peigan Nation.
She was predeceased by her uncles, Floyd Crowshoe and Casey Crow Eagle Sr.; her cousins, Casey Crow Eagle Jr., Lennox Dixon, and Emma Dixon; and her great-grandparents, Catherine Crow Eagle (Northpeigan), and Arthur Crowshoe.
REMEMBER ME
Don't remember me with sadness,
Don't remember me with tears,
Remember all the laughter,
We've shared throughout the years.
Now I am contented
That my life it was worthwhile,
Knowing that I passed along the way
I made somebody smile.
When you are walking down the street
And you've got me on your mind,
I'm walking in your footsteps
Only half a step behind.
So please don't be unhappy
Just because I'm out of sight,
Remember that I'm with you
Each morning, noon and night.
Funeral Services will be held at Gordon Yellow Fly Memorial Arbour (Siksika Nation, AB) on Monday, July 27, 2026, at 11:00 a.m. Graveside Service to follow at Little Chicago Cemetery (Siksika Nation, AB). Reception to follow back at Gordon Yellow Fly Memorial Arbour.
Condolences, memories, and photos may be shared and viewed with Savannah’s family here.
In living memory of Savannah Red Gun, a tree will be planted in the Ann & Sandy Cross Conservation Area by McInnis & Holloway Funeral Homes. Additional memorial trees will be planted through Canadian conservation and reforestation initiatives, as a result of memorial contributions. McInnis & Holloway Funeral Homes
Legal Advice
After a death, there are many legal details to work out. While it is not necessary to work with a lawyer, it is strongly recommended. The time following a death of a loved one is extremely emotional, and even the closest family may have disagreements. A lawyer is the easiest way to make sure everything is handled appropriately.
Before getting in touch with a lawyer, there are several important documents that you may wish to gather. 
These include:
Any wills that you are aware of
Deeds
Bank Statements
Insurance Policies
Vehicle and Boat titles
Tax Documents
Bank Accounts
Procedures for bank accounts following death vary regionally. In some areas, bank accounts are automatically frozen after a death. To avoid any complications, the bank should be notified immediately. The bank employees will guide you through the next steps from there. It’s recommended that a joint account stay open for at least six months to allow you to deposit any cheques that are made out to the deceased. To take a name off a joint bank account, banks require a certified copy of a death certificate. If the deceased had a safe deposit box in a bank, the contents may be sealed after death and a certified copy of a death certificate will be required to gain access to the contents.
Death Certificates
A certified death certificate is frequently necessary following a death. A death certificate can be obtained through a funeral director. It is a good idea to obtain multiple copies of a death certificate, as many agencies require a certified certificate and not a photocopy. 
Wills
Everyone knows they should have a will, but the vast majority – about 70% of us – do not. Writing a will is easy and inexpensive, and once you are done you can rest easy knowing your hard-earned money, and property, will be distributed according to your wishes. As well, if you have children, you can leave instructions on who will be left in charge of them if you pass, omitting that decision from the courts hands. Making a will is easy; you just need to be at least 18 years of age and must be of sound mind when the will is written. 
To make a will legal it must:
Expressly state that it is your will.
Be computer generated or typewritten.
Be signed and dated.
Be signed by 2–3 witnesses. *
*Witnesses must be people who don’t stand to inherit anything in the will.
Although you do not need a lawyer to complete a will, it is recommended to do one with a lawyer, as it will avoid any legal headaches after your passing. Once your will is complete, it’s recommended that it is kept somewhere safe and secure outside your home. If you prepare your will through a lawyer, most law firms will store it for you free of charge. Many people keep their wills in a safe deposit box at a bank, but this is not recommended, as the contents could be sealed at the time of death. The executor of your will should be aware of the location of it.
Probate
Probate is the legal process that transfers the ownership of property from the estate of the deceased to their beneficiaries. During the probate process, the executor of your will goes before the courts and identifies all the property you owned, appraises the property, pays all debts and taxes; proves that the will is valid and legal, and distributes the property according to the instructions of the will.
Legal & Probate Information FAQ
Do all Wills have to be taken to a lawyer?
No, some families may choose to look after the estate themselves, including providing the will and dispersing the funds without the assistance of a lawyer.
Do I Need Probate?
If you are administering an estate in Alberta, one of the decisions you will be faced with is whether to probate the Will. You will soon be asked by financial institutions and other organizations whether you will be obtaining probate.
What is Probate?
Probate is the process by which the Executor of an estate applies to the Surrogate Court of Alberta to get the Will “verified” or “approved.” A Judge of the Surrogate Court of Alberta will review the Will and the estate inventory and, if satisfied, will issue Letters of Probate. This will be a document issued by the Surrogate Court, which can be relied upon by everybody dealing with the estate.
How Much Does Probate Cost?
The Alberta Courts charge a fee to process a probate application. In Alberta, the maximum fee the Surrogate Court charges for a probate application is about $600.00. Moreover, if the Executor hires a lawyer to do the application to Court for probate, then there will be legal fees as well.
How Long Does It Take to Get Probate?
To apply to the Surrogate Court of Alberta for probate, you will need to do a very comprehensive and complete inventory of the estate, complete with values of the assets. Once this information is gathered, and the application is complete and submitted to the Surrogate Court, it will usually be processed in about three weeks.
Executors
An executor is the personal representative of your estate. They are the person in charge of taking control of your assets, paying off any debts, and distributing assets to your beneficiaries, per the terms and conditions of your will. You can choose anyone to be the executor of your will, but it is a good idea to choose someone who is both competent and trustworthy. The person you choose to be executor should be outlined in your will. Someone you appoint to be the executor of your will is entitled to refuse, so you should have a backup executor in place just in case.

# McInnis & Holloway Funeral Homes

## Legal Advice  

After a death, there are many legal details to work out. While it is not necessary to work with a lawyer, it is strongly recommended. The time following a death of a loved one is extremely emotional, and even the closest family may have disagreements. A lawyer is the easiest way to make sure everything is handled appropriately.

Before getting in touch with a lawyer, there are several important documents that you may wish to gather. 

###### **These include:**

*   Any wills that you are aware of
*   Deeds
*   Bank Statements

*   Insurance Policies
*   Vehicle and Boat titles
*   Tax Documents

#### Bank Accounts

Procedures for bank accounts following death vary regionally. In some areas, bank accounts are automatically frozen after a death. To avoid any complications, the bank should be notified immediately. The bank employees will guide you through the next steps from there. It’s recommended that a joint account stay open for at least six months to allow you to deposit any cheques that are made out to the deceased. To take a name off a joint bank account, banks require a certified copy of a death certificate. If the deceased had a safe deposit box in a bank, the contents may be sealed after death and a certified copy of a death certificate will be required to gain access to the contents.  

#### Death Certificates  

A certified death certificate is frequently necessary following a death. A death certificate can be obtained through a funeral director. It is a good idea to obtain multiple copies of a death certificate, as many agencies require a certified certificate and not a photocopy.  

#### Wills

Everyone knows they should have a will, but the vast majority – about 70% of us – do not. Writing a will is easy and inexpensive, and once you are done you can rest easy knowing your hard-earned money, and property, will be distributed according to your wishes. As well, if you have children, you can leave instructions on who will be left in charge of them if you pass, omitting that decision from the courts hands. Making a will is easy; you just need to be at least 18 years of age and must be of sound mind when the will is written.  

**To make a will legal it must:**

*   Expressly state that it is your will.
*   Be computer generated or typewritten.

*   Be signed and dated.
*   Be signed by 2–3 witnesses. \*  
    

_\*Witnesses must be people who don’t stand to inherit anything in the will._

Although you do not need a lawyer to complete a will, it is recommended to do one with a lawyer, as it will avoid any legal headaches after your passing. Once your will is complete, it’s recommended that it is kept somewhere safe and secure outside your home. If you prepare your will through a lawyer, most law firms will store it for you free of charge. Many people keep their wills in a safe deposit box at a bank, but this is not recommended, as the contents could be sealed at the time of death. The executor of your will should be aware of the location of it.

#### Probate

Probate is the legal process that transfers the ownership of property from the estate of the deceased to their beneficiaries. During the probate process, the executor of your will goes before the courts and identifies all the property you owned, appraises the property, pays all debts and taxes; proves that the will is valid and legal, and distributes the property according to the instructions of the will.  

###### Legal & Probate Information FAQ

**Do all Wills have to be taken to a lawyer?  
**No, some families may choose to look after the estate themselves, including providing the will and dispersing the funds without the assistance of a lawyer.

**Do I Need Probate?**  
If you are administering an estate in Alberta, one of the decisions you will be faced with is whether to probate the Will. You will soon be asked by financial institutions and other organizations whether you will be obtaining probate.

**What is Probate?**  
Probate is the process by which the Executor of an estate applies to the Surrogate Court of Alberta to get the Will “verified” or “approved.” A Judge of the Surrogate Court of Alberta will review the Will and the estate inventory and, if satisfied, will issue Letters of Probate. This will be a document issued by the Surrogate Court, which can be relied upon by everybody dealing with the estate.

**How Much Does Probate Cost?**  
The Alberta Courts charge a fee to process a probate application. In Alberta, the maximum fee the Surrogate Court charges for a probate application is about $600.00. Moreover, if the Executor hires a lawyer to do the application to Court for probate, then there will be legal fees as well.

**How Long Does It Take to Get Probate?**  
To apply to the Surrogate Court of Alberta for probate, you will need to do a very comprehensive and complete inventory of the estate, complete with values of the assets. Once this information is gathered, and the application is complete and submitted to the Surrogate Court, it will usually be processed in about three weeks.

#### Executors

An executor is the personal representative of your estate. They are the person in charge of taking control of your assets, paying off any debts, and distributing assets to your beneficiaries, per the terms and conditions of your will. You can choose anyone to be the executor of your will, but it is a good idea to choose someone who is both competent and trustworthy. The person you choose to be executor should be outlined in your will. Someone you appoint to be the executor of your will is entitled to refuse, so you should have a backup executor in place just in case.

# McInnis & Holloway Funeral Homes

## Family Care  

McInnis & Holloway’s Family Care Program was started with the sole purpose of helping survivors resolve some of the practical matters that can be more difficult after the loss of a loved one.  

#### Our Family Care Program 

We are pleased to continue offering our Family Care Program as an optional service to support families in the days following the funeral.  
The items listed below will give you an idea of the ways in which we are prepared to help.   
Our practice is to call and arrange a time to meet at your home within a day or two after the funeral. And, because we understand there will be many things on your mind, you need only plan on an hour or so.

###### We Will Provide Assistance With:

###### Canada Pension Plan

*   Death notification and cancellation of benefits
*   Death and Survivors’ Benefit applications
*   Order T-4 slip for filing of estate tax return
*   Check for post-mortem benefit eligibility

###### Old Age Security

*   Death notification and cancellation of benefits
*   Apply for allowance for the Survivor
*   Guaranteed Income Supplement application
*   Order T-4 slip for filing of estate tax return

###### Alberta Seniors’ Benefit

*   Death notification to Alberta Health Care
*   Death notification to Alberta Blue Cross and/or Extended Health Benefits
*   Application for premium subsidy and transfer of medical coverage if required

###### Superannuations (Federal/Provincial)

*   Death notification and cancellation of benefits
*   Assistance with applying for death benefits

###### Income Tax And G.S.T. Payments (CRA)

*   Assistance with transfer/cancellation of GST payments
*   Provide T1/T3 forms & booklets to file Estate tax return

###### Veterans Affairs Canada (DVA)

*   Death notification and cancellation of benefits
*   Assistance with applying for death benefits

###### Alberta Driver’s License

*   Notification of death and surrender of License  
    

###### Housing And Rental Assistance

*   Application for rental assistance or property tax relief
*   Counsel on various Provincial and Federal programs
*   Information provided to transfer titles and registrations

###### Social Insurance Number  

*   Death notification and surrender of S.I.N. card  
    

###### Credit Cards

*   Assistance with death notification and cancellation/amendment on credit cards  
    

###### Telephone Listing  

*   Assistance with death notification for telephone company to make appropriate modifications  
    

###### Utilities

*   Assistance with death notification for utility companies to make appropriate modifications  
    

We have put together a list of documents that may be required when you meet with our Family Care representative.

**List of Documents that may be required:**

*   Original Will
*   Funeral Director’s Statement of Death or original Death Certificate
*   Original Marriage Certificate (For CPP Survivor’s or Alberta Widow’s Pension)
*   Deceased’s Alberta Driver’s Licence
*   Previous bill/statement from Alberta Health Care (or Personal Health Care Numbers)
*   Deceased’s Alberta Blue Cross card (if applicable)
*   Deceased’s Alberta Aids to Daily Living card (if applicable)
*   Deceased’s Social Insurance card (or Old Age Security card if over age 65)
*   Previous year’s Income Tax returns for the deceased and surviving spouse
*   Information or pay stub for all of deceased’s pensions (Alberta Widows’ Pension, Superannuation, Company, etc.)
*   Documents relating to foreign pensions of the deceased
*   If applying for Alberta Widows Pension – proof of legal residence in Canada must be verified by Canadian Birth Certificate, Citizenship card or IMM 1000

#### Other Information To Have On Hand:

If you have a question you would like answered by one of our Family Care representatives (at no obligation), [click here to e-mail us](mailto:info@mhfh.com).
