# Cremation Services Calgary | McInnis & Holloway Funeral Homes

## Cremation Services in Calgary, Alberta  

Cremation is a meaningful choice for many families today. Whether selected for its simplicity, flexibility, or personal beliefs, our team at McInnis & Holloway is here to guide you with clarity and care.

As a locally owned funeral home for over 120 years, with our own crematories, you can trust that your loved one remains in compassionate, professional hands at every step. 

[Call us anytime: 403-243-8200](tel:+14032438200)

![Image](https://d1q40j6jx1d8h6.cloudfront.net/SiteBuilder/ee93aebe-51b2-489e-8a60-5fe98e33065b/516d9ec1-3740-4d03-a800-9ac222bc16f8.webp "Image Title")

### Why Families Choose Cremation With Us

###### Families trust McInnis & Holloway for: 

*   Clean, open, modern cremation facilities
*   Complete transparency and continuity of care
*   Guidance before, during, and after the cremation
*   Options for services or gatherings
*   The opportunity to see or identify your loved one beforehand
*   A tree planted in a Calgary conservation area in honour of your family 

[Discover Cremation Memorial Options](https://www1.mhfh.com/ceremony-of-cremation-2?utm_source=website&utm_medium=button&utm_campaign=cremation)

#### Understanding the Cremation Process

*   Cremation typically takes place within 2–5 days once required documents are complete.
*   A cremation container is needed for safety and dignity.
*   An urn is required to hold the cremated remains.
*   Embalming is not required unless you choose a viewing or ceremony beforehand. 

###### Have questions about what’s required?

[Call us anytime: (403) 243-8200](tel:+14032438200)

![Image](https://d1q40j6jx1d8h6.cloudfront.net/SiteBuilder/ee93aebe-51b2-489e-8a60-5fe98e33065b/89ec906b-c0dc-4f11-9219-98eba21cbbc3.webp "Image Title")

### Cremation Pricing

There are many options available when cremation takes places. Costs will vary depending on the type of service that is chosen. Cremation can occur following a funeral service, or following a visitation, prayer service or informal gathering. Cremation can also occur prior to a Memorial Service.

[Call us anytime: 403-243-8200](tel:+14032438200)

#### Common Questions

Can I choose cremation without a service?

Yes, families may choose cremation only.

Can we be present for the cremation?  

Yes, our facilities allow family presence when desired.  

Why do we have to provide clothing when they will be cremated?  

We ask that you bring in a full set of clothing, including undergarments, as this provides dignity to your loved one. 

Is cremation legal for all religions?

Most allow it; some do not. We can guide you based on your beliefs.

Why is it necessary to purchase a cremation container and an urn?

The Alberta Funeral Service Regulatory Board requires that your loved one be placed in a suitable enclosed container in order to be placed into the crematorium. This is done out of respect for the deceased as well as for safety of the crematorium operator.

It is also very important to select a suitable urn where the cremated remains can be safely held. You may want to put some thought into where the urn will be interred. We have many options available for you.

[Click here for an informational video.](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=R_-Zt53lbGM) 

Is it legal to scatter ashes?

If you want to scatter on private property, make sure you have the owner’s permission. Also be aware that it is illegal to scatter cremated remains in a waterway that is located in a National Park.

Some cemeteries have scattering gardens as well.

[Click here for an informational video.](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Emz69fEZTbI) 

What do you do with cremated remains?

You can choose: 

*   Burial in a cemetery
*   Placement in a columbarium
*   Keeping the urn at home
*   Scattering in a permitted area or cemetery scattering garden 

If you’re unsure, we’ll help you explore meaningful options.

Obituary information for Stephen (Steve) Leonard Whitehall
September 20, 1951 – Derby, England, United Kingdom
July 19, 2026 – Calgary, Alberta
Stephen “Steve” Leonard Whitehall of Calgary, AB, passed away on Sunday, July 19, 2026, at the age of 74 years.
Born in Derby, England, Steve immigrated to Canada in 1971, where he built a meaningful life rooted in family, friendship, and a passion for the print industry. He enjoyed a remarkably long career, including stints at Paperworks Press, Sundog Printing, and MET Printers. Known for his professionalism and integrity, Steve curated a loyal clientele and formed many lasting friendships. His commitment to excellence earned him a well-respected reputation throughout the industry. Everybody in the industry has heard about the ornery Steve Whitehall—but those who truly knew him know how his perfectionism and desire to deliver the best service possible were at the root of everything he did.
Steve’s commitment to family and friendships was just as passionate. He is survived by his daughters, Michelle (Jeff) and Rebecca (Jordan); and grandchildren, Aspen, Austin, Trinity, Lily, and Aradia. He was predeceased by his daughter, Cheryl, in 2025.
He will be sorely missed by his siblings back in England, Linda, Tina, Debbie, David, Danny, and Gary; along with his special nieces and extended family. Steve will be fondly remembered and deeply missed by his most special friend and partner, Nancy; and dear lifelong friends, Peter F., Moe Z., Barry A., Charles M., Peter D., and Paula A. to name just a few.
At the request of Steve, no formal service will be held; however, a gathering to "Raise a Glass" will be announced at a later date.
Condolences, memories, and photos may be shared and viewed with Steve’s family here.
In living memory of Stephen "Steve" Whitehall, a tree will be planted in the Ann & Sandy Cross Conservation Area by McInnis & Holloway Funeral Homes. Additional memorial trees will be planted through Canadian conservation and reforestation initiatives, as a result of memorial contributions. McInnis & Holloway, Fish Creek, 14441 Bannister Road SE, Calgary, AB T2X 3J3, Telephone: 403-256-9575.

August 13, 1947 – Manila, Philippines
July 24, 2026 – Calgary, Alberta
Beatriz Davadilla, beloved wife of Delfin Davadilla, of Calgary, AB, passed away on Friday, July 24, 2026, at the age of 78 years.
Beatriz was born in Manila, Philippines, on August 13, 1947. In 1979, she married the love of her life, Delfin—the beginning of a partnership that would span forty-seven years and carry them halfway around the world.
In 1989, Beatriz and Delfin left the Philippines for Calgary, AB, with their daughter, Dianne, setting aside everything familiar for the promise of a life they had not yet seen. Beatriz and Delfin found a community at the Seniors Club, where they were surrounded by wonderful friends and where they fell in love with the game of Mahjong—a pastime that filled their weeks with laughter, good-natured competition, and the easy company of people who had become family.
She will be most remembered for her sense of humour and her endless supply of jokes and, above all, for her deep faith in God.

Obituary information for Mona Callander (née Himour)
June 8, 1931 – Swift Current, Saskatchewan
July 17, 2026 – Calgary, Alberta
Mona Callander passed away peacefully, surrounded by her family, on Friday, July 17, 2026, shortly after celebrating her 95th birthday.
Mona was born on the family farm in Wood Mountain, SK, on June 8, 1931, to Alex and Fatima Himour. She married Ronald Callander on November 21, 1953, at Knox Metropolitan United Church in Regina, SK. Together they shared 59 wonderful years of marriage.
Over the years, Ron and Mona lived in Regina, where they built their family home, and in several other communities throughout Saskatchewan before moving to Calgary, AB, in July 1971. A highlight for Ron and Mona was the two years they spent living in Brisbane, Australia, from 1994 to 1995. Following retirement, they settled in Carstairs, AB, where they enjoyed returning to the close-knit atmosphere of small-town life. Their final move together was to Diamond Jubilee Manor in Airdrie, AB, where they made many cherished friends. Several years after Ron's passing, Mona moved to Abrio Place, where she appreciated the companionship and, as she would say, "not having to cook anymore."
Mona is lovingly remembered by four of her children, Gregg (Marney), Cindy (Bob), Bruce (Kris), and Laurel (Sheldon); her grandchildren, Shaun (Danielle), Michael (Robynne), Brandi, Ashley (Kyle), Kendra, Jock (Lindsay), Bryce (Jamie), Jarvis (Teya), Justin (Dallas), Matthew (Sherry), and Stephanie (Matt); and her sixteen precious great-grandchildren.
She was predeceased by her beloved husband, Ron; her son, Rod; her daughter-in-law, Lee; her parents; her four sisters, Lila, Phoebe, Anne, and Belle; and her four brothers, Hassen, Ab, Marvin, and Sam.
Mona devoted her life to being a loving wife and devoted mother. She took great pride in caring for her home and family and was known for her wonderful cooking, baking, and meticulous housekeeping. After moving to Calgary, Mona worked at Sears in the catalogue department until it closed, then continued her career in administration in several small offices, creating friendships that she treasured throughout her life.
A woman of strong faith, Mona dedicated countless hours to the United Church, where she sang in the choir, led youth programs, and helped organize fundraising events. In retirement, she remained active in her community, volunteering and participating in organizations such as the Half Century Club in Carstairs.
Above all, Mona treasured her time with her children, grandchildren, great-grandchildren, and the extended Himour and Callander families. She genuinely enjoyed being with people and had a gift for making lasting friendships. Her warmth, kindness, and welcoming spirit will be deeply missed by all who knew and loved her.
The family extends their heartfelt gratitude to the healthcare professionals and staff who cared for Mona over the past several months at Peter Lougheed Centre, Rockyview General Hospital, Abrio Place, Sage Hill Residence, and AgeCare SkyPointe Hospice. Their compassion and kindness brought great comfort to Mona and her family.
A Celebration of Life will be held at a later date.
Condolences, memories, and photos may be shared and viewed with Mona’s family here.
In living memory of Mona Callander, a tree will be planted in the Ann & Sandy Cross Conservation Area by McInnis & Holloway Funeral Homes. Additional memorial trees will be planted through Canadian conservation and reforestation initiatives, as a result of memorial contributions. McInnis & Holloway, Crowfoot, 82 Crowfoot Circle NW, Calgary, AB T3G 2T3, Telephone: 403-241-0044.

# Affordable Green Burial Services | McInnis & Holloway Funera

## Green Burial/Cremation Services  

In Calgary, Alberta  

Green Burial is a statement of personal values for those who seek to minimize their impact on the local and global environment. For people who are mindful of the cyclical nature of life, green burial is a spiritually fulfilling alternative to conventional burial or cremation. It is an environmentally sensitive practice: the body is returned to the earth to decompose naturally and contribute to new life.

[Explore Eco-Friendly Burial Options](https://www1.mhfh.com/green-burial?utm_source=website&utm_medium=button&utm_campaign=green+burials)

McInnis & Holloway Funeral Homes is Calgary's exclusive Green Burial Certified Funeral Home

*   Commitment to an ethic rooted in transparency, accountability, and ecological responsibility

*   Interiors are made with 100% natural unbleached cotton

*   Seagrass is not harvested from delicate marine environments, rather they are cultivated in rice paddy-like fields capable of yearly re-growth
*   Contains no metal

Obituary information for Millie Helen Moore
December 8, 1935 – Regina, Saskatchewan
July 17, 2026 – Calgary, Alberta
Millie (Mimi) Moore, beloved wife of the late Donald Lyle Moore, of Calgary, AB, passed away on Friday, July 17, 2026, at the age of 90 years.
Millie was born in Regina, SK, on December 8, 1935. She and Don moved to Calgary, AB, in 1953 and married later that same year. They eventually moved to Bragg Creek, AB, after Don retired. Following Don's passing in 2014, after 61 years of marriage, Millie moved to Cochrane, AB, and later returned to Calgary to be closer to her family.
When Millie and Don moved from Regina to Calgary in 1953, they eventually built a house in the community of Brentwood in the early 1960s. It was there that they raised their five children and established lifelong friendships within the community. Whether Millie was socializing at the community centre or working at Sears, she enjoyed meeting people and forming new friendships.
Moving to Bragg Creek in the mid-1980s was a highlight not only for Millie, Don, and their children, but also for their grandchildren. Millie and Don lived in Bragg Creek for more than 25 years and were both highly involved in the community and the Bragg Creek Snowbirds. Millie had many close friends in the community and enjoyed helping at the Seniors Chalet, meeting friends for coffee, and feeding the deer in her backyard.
The grandkids loved spending time with their "Mimi" and Don in Bragg Creek. They fondly remember their Bragg Creek sleepovers, that consisted of ‘Mimi's waffles with blueberry syrup’ when they would wake up. The Sweet Shop in Bragg Creek did a brisk business whenever Mimi and the grandkids walked in. Mimi loved her scratch-and-win tickets and often bought them for the grandkids as well.
Mimi loved Christmas and, in her later years, kept her small Christmas tree up year-round. Christmas also meant making Rice Krispies Christmas wreaths for everyone. She was full of fun with her grandkids, building snowmen, instigating snowball fights, having water fights on warm days, and being the humble participant as the girls played hair salon with her.
Millie and Don also owned a cabin in Sandpoint, Idaho, where they spent many months each year. She loved cooking on the old wood stove at the cabin and loved the plum tree that grew in the yard. Her adult children and grandkids also spent much time in Sandpoint and continued to have family camp trips in Idaho long after Millie and Don sold the cabin.
Millie also had fond memories of going to Las Vegas when her brother Gordie married Brenda. She loved her extended family in Regina, and in her later years, her children took her to Las Vegas on two occasions, where the family would all meet on Fremont Street. Sometimes, Millie would be the last to return to her room, with a wallet full of cash after a successful night at the casino.
Elvis Presley was a large presence in her life, whether through the large black velvet-framed portrait that hung in one of the bedrooms in Bragg Creek (the grandkids called it the "Elvis Room," and Mimi may have told them that Elvis was their uncle). The same picture even made the front page of the Calgary Sun when Michelle brought it to the Calgary Corporate Challenge scavenger hunt.
Millie was a loving mother, mother-in-law, grandmother, step-grandmother, and great-grandmother, in addition to being a kind and understanding friend. She loved to sit down with anyone, enjoy a conversation over some of her homemade baking, and a cup of coffee (“one cream on the side”). She accomplished much throughout her life and was particularly proud of her children and grandchildren, whom she adored with all her heart. She lived a beautiful and long life surrounded by family and friends. She will be deeply missed.
Millie is survived by her two daughters, Michelle Scandella (Fabio) of Cochrane, AB, and Melinda Moore (Blair Hay) of Calgary, AB; her three sons, Darrell Moore (Leslie) of Aldergrove, BC, Douglas Moore (Gail) of Calgary, AB, and Daniel Moore (Suzi) of Banff, AB; her eight grandchildren, Candace (Paul) Cottrell of Aldergrove, BC, Brad Moore of Aldergrove, BC, Samantha Moore (Chad Mahura) of Calgary, AB, Rebecca (Tyler) Diehl of Airdrie, AB, Kristin Moore (Eric Blair) of Rossland, BC, Jeremy Vanesveld (Estefany) of Lima, Peru, Madeline Volpi (Reid Gartner) of Calgary, AB, and Evan Volpi of Calgary, AB; six great-grandchildren; and many step-grandchildren.
She is also survived by her brother and sister-in-law, Gordon and Brenda Tashulak of Regina, SK; as well as numerous nieces and nephews, all of whom held a special place in Mimi's heart.
She was predeceased by her husband, Donald; her granddaughter, Melissa Vanesveld; her sisters, Anna, Frances, Rose, Mildred, Lillian, and Joan; and her brothers, Archie and David.
If friends so desire, memorial tributes may be made directly to the Heart and Stroke Foundation of Canada, www.heartandstroke.ca.
There will be a private family gathering to honour Millie’s life.
Condolences, memories, and photos may be shared and viewed with Millie’s family here.
In living memory of Millie Moore, a tree will be planted in the Ann & Sandy Cross Conservation Area by McInnis & Holloway Funeral Homes. Additional memorial trees will be planted through Canadian conservation and reforestation initiatives, as a result of memorial contributions. McInnis & Holloway, Crowfoot, 82 Crowfoot Circle NW, Calgary, AB T3G 2T3, Telephone: 403-241-0044.

Obituary information for Maria Hoffart
August 17, 1952 – Aberdeen, Scotland
July 17, 2026 – Chestermere, Alberta
"I Love You More"
No truer words have ever been spoken than the phrase Maria Hoffart so often shared with her family: "I love you more." Though she passed away peacefully on Friday, July 17, 2026, surrounded by the love of her family after a courageous but brief battle with cancer, her love will remain in our hearts forever.
Maria was born in Aberdeen, Scotland, in 1952. She was raised in England by her parents, Stanley and Melanie, alongside her siblings, Janet, John and Joseph. At the age of eighteen, she bravely crossed the Atlantic on her own to begin a new chapter in Canada. Not long after, her sister, Janet, and devoted mum, Melanie, joined her and together they eventually settled in Calgary, AB. It was there that she met the love of her life—Bob Hoffart. They were married in 1981 and built a beautiful life together, raising three children: Shawn, Nicole (Joel), and Kristina (David).
From the moment she became a mother, Maria devoted herself wholeheartedly to her family. Some of life's most treasured memories were made on family camping trips to Mt. Kidd and on adventures to places like Las Vegas, Kelowna, England, Greece and many more. When her kids took up sports at a young age, Maria didn't miss a game. Whether it was the softball diamond or the basketball court, Maria was always there, cheering loudly beside Bob, who often coached.
As the years passed, Maria and Bob embraced every opportunity to travel together. They created unforgettable memories along the Eastern coast of Canada, in the desert of Palm Springs, and following the Toronto Blue Jays on the road. In her spare time, Maria was passionate about cross-stitch and knitting, always creating meaningful pieces straight from her heart to gift to family and friends. Every couple of months, she joined her close friends on weekend retreats, where the needles never stopped moving, while stories and laughter filled the room.
At home, Maria showed her love through the delicious meals she prepared for her family. From homemade perogies to potatoes and cabbage rolls, every gathering around her table was filled with warmth, laughter, and love. Whether it was dropping off a meal for one of her children or hosting one of her special family dinners, providing for those she loved brought her endless fulfillment.
Her heart grew even fuller when she became Nana. She was blessed with three cherished grandchildren—Emma, Brody, and Callie. They all quickly became the centre of her world. From sleepovers and shopping trips to reading Goldilocks for what felt like the hundredth time, Nana never missed an opportunity to make them feel loved. Her hugs, cuddles, treats and unwavering support created memories they will carry with them forever. They could not have asked for a more devoted and loving Nana. Maria truly lived every moment for her family.
Maria spent her entire life caring for others. We are incredibly fortunate to have been loved by her. Everyone who met her was touched by her warmth, kindness, and genuine compassion. There are simply no words that can fully express how deeply she will be missed or how grateful we are for the love she gave so freely.
"Loved you yesterday. Love you still. Always have. Always will."
A Celebration of Maria's life will be announced at a later date.
If friends so desire, in lieu of flowers, donations in Maria's memory may be made directly to the Alberta Children's Hospital Foundation, www.childrenshospital.ab.ca or the Alberta Cancer Foundation, www.albertacancer.ca.
Condolences, memories, and photos may be shared and viewed with Maria’s family here.
In living memory of Maria Hoffart, a tree will be planted in the Ann & Sandy Cross Conservation Area by McInnis & Holloway Funeral Homes. Additional memorial trees will be planted through Canadian conservation and reforestation initiatives, as a result of memorial contributions. McInnis & Holloway, Eastside, 5388 Memorial Drive NE, Calgary, AB T2A 3V9, Telephone: 403-243-8200.

Making Funeral Arrangements | McInnis & Holloway Funeral Hom
In Calgary, Alberta
Thank You For Selecting McInnis & Holloway And Giving Us This Opportunity To Guide You Through This Difficult Time.
Arrangement Agenda
The arrangement process provides us an opportunity to assist your family in honouring your loved one’s life. When you come in for the arrangements, we ask you to bring in the below items:
A set of clothing for your loved one
Government issued identification showing full legal name, including middle names
Social Insurance and Alberta Health Care
Driver’s License numbers
A photograph of your loved one
We would like to be as prepared as possible for our time with your family and with your help, we can have many documents ready prior to your appointment.
We have included required vital statistics in the below link, you are welcome to print off the attached document and bring this information with you when you come in or fill out the information on the following secure web page.
Required Vital Statistics Form 
1. Obituary
The obituary lets friends and family know about your loved one and it creates a historical document for your family.
You are welcome to answer some of the questions listed in the link provided below to help have this started prior to your appointment.
We also invite you to email us at info@mhfh.com and attach any documents that you have already written or click here to send files including any pictures or videos files.
Obituary Form 
We will not submit the obituary to the newspaper or post on our website until a final copy has been approved by the family.
2. Welcome And Introductions
Answering questions to alleviate any anxieties about the arrangement process. Learning your family’s wishes and understanding your intentions to help make decisions that are good for you. Why have we had funerals since the beginning of time?
3. Discussion Of Funeral Service Options
Including coordination with regard to helping create a meaningful funeral ceremony.
4. Discussion About Location Options
Having a place to gather and visit to celebrate your loved one's life is one of the most healing parts of the grief process. We can help plan services in a special place you designate or at any of our two locations.​
Booking of dates and times, offer input on what days and times family and friends typically find easier to attend services.
Burial Options And Products
A visual presentation of options available for families to consider during the arrangement process.
Cremation Options And Products
A visual presentation of options available for families to consider during the arrangement process.
5. Assisting With Cemetery Arrangements
6. Tour Of Facilities
An opportunity for a guided tour of our modern chapels and reception facilities.
7. Review All Decisions And Signing Of Appropriate Documentation

McInnis & Holloway has been one of Calgary and southern Alberta’s most respected funeral homes since 1903.

###### Memorial Tree Program

If families wish, any family that was served by McInnis & Holloway, we plant a tree in memory of your loved one. In the past, our Memorial Forests locations were Lafarge Meadows in Fish Creek Provincial Park (South of Sikome Lake and 22X) or in our Fletcher Park Memorial Forest located in Airdrie, AB. The Memorial Forest® program offers a special way of memorializing a person who has died and provides families with a meaningful way to deal with a loss.

[View Our Tree Program](https://www.mhfh.com/resources/tree-program)

*   We’re the specialists for providing unique and customized services for families who want ethnic or religious customs and traditions integrated into the funeral ceremony.

McInnis & Holloway offers ideas on making funeral services more personal. Unique ideas and non-traditional funeral rituals are outlined in our publication “Creating A Memorable Funeral Ceremony” written by our Funeral Operations Manager, Kathy Cloutier.

“Creating a Memorable Funeral Ceremony” was developed when McInnis & Holloway Funeral Homes recognized that grieving families were communicating a greater need to express their grief. Advanced planning is the act of preparing in advance for your funeral service. It can be as simple as writing your wishes on paper and attaching them to your will or contacting a funeral home to discuss the many details surrounding the funeral service, and paying for these services in advance.

text:
When Death Occurs | McInnis & Holloway Funeral Homes
Whether a death is sudden or expected, the loss of a loved one is indescribable. When you are in a heightened emotional state, even the most basic decisions can seem staggering. This section seeks to guide you through the immediate hours following a passing.
To schedule an appointment to meet with a Funeral Director
Call or Text (403) 243-8200.
When A Death Occurs At Home Or A Place Of Business
If the person was not under hospice care, the police will have to be notified immediately. The police will be dispatched to the home and will place the call to the coroner or medical examiner. From there, the coroner or medical examiner will remove the body and determine whether further action is necessary. The coroner or medical examiner must release the body before a funeral home can do anything. If the person was under hospice care, contact the hospice representative, and they will notify family members what the proper procedures are to follow.
When A Death Occurs At A Hospital/Nursing Home/Hospice Facility
The staff of a care facility, such as a hospital or nursing home, will notify you and the necessary authorities immediately after a death has occurred. 
If a funeral home has been provided to the hospital or nursing home, they will be notified at the time of passing. 
If you are present at the hospital when the funeral director arrives, they will ask a few questions about the deceased's wishes and set up a time to make arrangements.

# When Death Occurs | McInnis & Holloway Funeral Homes

Whether a death is sudden or expected, the loss of a loved one is indescribable. When you are in a heightened emotional state, even the most basic decisions can seem staggering. This section seeks to guide you through the immediate hours following a passing.  

##### To schedule an appointment to meet with a Funeral Director  
Call or Text [(403) 243-8200](tel:+14032438200).

#### When A Death Occurs At Home Or A Place Of Business

If the person was not under hospice care, the police will have to be notified immediately. The police will be dispatched to the home and will place the call to the coroner or medical examiner. From there, the coroner or medical examiner will remove the body and determine whether further action is necessary. The coroner or medical examiner must release the body before a funeral home can do anything. If the person was under hospice care, contact the hospice representative, and they will notify family members what the proper procedures are to follow.  

#### When A Death Occurs At A Hospital/Nursing Home/Hospice Facility

The staff of a care facility, such as a hospital or nursing home, will notify you and the necessary authorities immediately after a death has occurred.   

*   If a funeral home has been provided to the hospital or nursing home, they will be notified at the time of passing. 
*   If you are present at the hospital when the funeral director arrives, they will ask a few questions about the deceased's wishes and set up a time to make arrangements.

Testimonials
If you feel we’ve gone above and beyond in supporting you through this difficult time or would simply like to reach out and say thanks, contact us to share your thoughts in a testimonial below. It means the world to us to hear from you and know that we’ve made a difference.
Want to share your story? Tell us about your experience. 
S
Szwazrc Anne 
July 15, 2026 
I would like to thank the McInnis & Holloway team for taking care of all the arrangements for my husband, Rick's, Celebration of Life. It is a truly difficult time and Ashley Rauws helped to make the process go smoothly. All the staff was so caring and sympathetic. The graphic artist team created the perfect remembrance card. It really was Rich. The setup for the Celebration of Life was perfect and beautiful. I can't remember her name, but the lady in charge that day was great. MHALL Anne & Family 
T
Thorpe Susan 
July 14, 2026 
We had our celebration of life with you at the Fish Creek location on May 2 for Timothy Thorpe. Again, I want to thank you for a stellar job. You thought of everything. The family and I felt very comfortable in your lovely surroundings. Your staff was amazing. They knew what we needed before we did. I would like to give a special shout out to the graphic design department. Our “baseball” prayer card was a huge hit. Also, I had no idea that the memory book would be so much more than a guest book. The photos and personal details were much appreciated. Thank you again. 
C
Chantel 
June 17, 2026 
All of the staff were very welcoming and compassionate. We would particularly like to recognize Ashley and Hugo. Ashley was very informative and put us at ease immediately. She was patient and professional, while also making us feel comfortable and reassured. Hugo was incredible. He was gentle and easy to talk to, and he made us feel comfortable sharing stories about our loved one. The way he delivered the ceremony was incredibly moving and heartfelt. We can’t thank him enough. 
H
Harvey, Janice 
May 25, 2026 
I would like to give a huge shout out to JT Beck. We first met him at our fathers viewing and to say the least he was amazing. His compassion and care radiated, he was so respectful and helpful. His kindness got us thru that evening. He had set up the funeral arrangements perfect and his attention to detail was very much appreciated. He offered to meet us at the crematorium knowing it would be another hard day for us. Having him there with us was so comforting, he was the friendly face that we had gotten to know. JT is professional yet real, he knows the right things to say and never once made us feel anything but cared for! JT made one of the hardest days easier and for that I am forever grateful. JT is one of a kind and he is truly a very special person. Your company is blessed to have such a dedicated young man representing you and upfront dealing with grieving family’s. Danielle Prentice is another employee that went above and beyond and never treated this as just another funeral and us just another grieving family. She took the time during this process to help us, explain things as well as offer compassion and hugs. I have only good things to say about all the staff we dealt with during this process. Thank you all for helping us in our heavy time of loss. All of your staff was wonderful they never made you feel pressured and they made you feel like you were the most important service they were dealing with. Janice Harvey

Wolochatiuk Cheryl 
May 01, 2026

April 28, 2026

Our situation was not simple—living out of the country, limited information, and a complex family dynamic—but every single one of you met us with understanding, kindness, and grace. You cared for my brother with dignity, and you cared for us in a way I will never forget. I hope no one ever has to go through something like this, but if they do, I hope they are met with the same level of compassion and care that you gave our family. Thank you for everything you did for my brother and for us. I know all of my siblings and mom extend the same thank you. With deepest gratitude, Dylan Brooks-Forseth

Judith and Dave Shewchuk 
April 24, 2026

To all the staff, thank you all for a fantastic job well-done — all the way. We are so grateful!! Sincerely, Judith and Dave Shewchuk

With gratitude, Diane Malesza, Linda Malesza Garrett, Katie and Alexia Bastian Ward and Kim Bastian

Thank you for all your care and compassion during the most difficult time. It was very much appreciated

Thoughts and memories during the funeral tell the story of a lifetime. Sharing this occasion can bring great comfort to those who are unable to attend in person. With our livestreaming funeral service, family and friends from all over the world can participate in viewing the livestream, or watch the recording at their own convenience.
How do I watch a livestream funeral?
Find the tribute page of the deceased who's service you wish to view. You can view all tribute pages by clicking here.
Once on the tribute page, you will see an embedded video immediately below the obituary.
Click on the video box to watch the livestream or recording. The video may start muted and will provide you the option of turning on the audio when you are ready. To turn on the audio click on the audio image that is crossed out and the audio should begin at the volume level that your device is set at - We recommend that you turn your audio to close to maximum volume as some speakers require a high device volume level.
Please note:
The link will be available on the day of the service.
The livestream will begin 5 minutes before service time.
A recording of the service will be available once the service is over. This recording will be accessible for 3 months following the service.
Helpful Tips
It is recommended to view the livestream on an updated internet browser, such as Chrome or Microsoft Edge.
A minimum internet speed of 520 Kbps is needed.
Live Streaming may be interrupted due to network connection beyond our control. Rest assured that a full recording of the service will be available for viewing following the conclusion of the service.

# Live Streaming Funeral Services in Calgary

Thoughts and memories during the funeral tell the story of a lifetime. Sharing this occasion can bring great comfort to those who are unable to attend in person. With our livestreaming funeral service, family and friends from all over the world can participate in viewing the livestream, or watch the recording at their own convenience.  

## How do I watch a livestream funeral?  

Find the tribute page of the deceased who's service you wish to view. [You can view all tribute pages by clicking here.](https://www.mhfh.com/obituaries/obituary-listings)

Once on the tribute page, you will see an embedded video immediately below the obituary.

Click on the video box to watch the livestream or recording. The video may start muted and will provide you the option of turning on the audio when you are ready. To turn on the audio click on the audio image that is crossed out and the audio should begin at the volume level that your device is set at - We recommend that you turn your audio to close to maximum volume as some speakers require a high device volume level.

#### Please note:  

*   The link will be available on the day of the service.
*   The livestream will begin 5 minutes before service time.
*   A recording of the service will be available once the service is over. This recording will be accessible for 3 months following the service.

#### Helpful Tips  

*   It is recommended to view the livestream on an updated internet browser, such as Chrome or Microsoft Edge.
*   A minimum internet speed of 520 Kbps is needed.
*   Live Streaming may be interrupted due to network connection beyond our control. _Rest assured that a full recording of the service will be available for viewing following the conclusion of the service._

###### Please call or text McInnis & Holloway if we can provide any assistance accessing a live-stream (403) 243-8200

text:
Eulogies & Obituaries | McInnis & Holloway Funeral Homes
Whether a death is sudden or expected, the loss of a loved one is indescribable. When you are in a heightened emotional state, even the most basic decisions can seem staggering. This section seeks to guide you through the immediate hours following a passing.
Eulogies
Giving a meaningful, moving eulogy can be a nerve-wracking situation for even the most accomplished public speaker, but it doesn't have to be. How can you summarize somebody’s life in a few short minutes, while being both sombre and funny at the same time? Writing and delivering a eulogy is a therapeutic tool to help deal with your grief, and being chosen to give a eulogy is an honour and should be treated that way. Here are some tips for writing and delivering an eloquent and memorable eulogy.
Gather information. Talk with family members, close friends and co-workers to get important information on the deceased. Some important information to include in the eulogy is the person's family and other close relationships, their education/career, hobbies or special interests, places the person lived or travelled too, and any special accomplishments they had.
Organize your thoughts. Jot down your ideas by whatever means are most comfortable and familiar to you. Create an outline of your speech, and fill in the information that you gathered about the person.
Write it down. This is not a toast at a wedding where you can make off the cuff remarks, and you should not ad lib a eulogy. Writing it all down allows you to include and remember every detail you wanted in your eulogy. When you bring a copy of your eulogy to the podium, make sure it is easy to read. Print it out in a large font or, if it is handwritten, leave a few spaces between the lines. Keep in mind the length of your eulogy; it’s best to keep things on the short side, especially if there are other speakers.
Review and Revise. Your first draft will not be your last. When you think you are done, sleep on it, and look it over in the morning when your mind is fresh again. That will be the time to make any necessary revisions.
Practice, Practice, Practice. Read over your eulogy several times to become familiar with it. Practice in front of a mirror, read it to your friends or family, and have them give you feedback. Become familiar with your speech so you can recite it without making it look like you’re reading from a script. The more practice you have, the more comfortable you will be. 
Make them laugh, but be respectful. A funeral is not a roast; however, there is room for humour in your eulogy. Fondly, remember a story about the person that everyone can relate too. Keep it appropriate, as there will be children and the elderly there that may not share the same sense of humour. Laughter is truly the best medicine, and some well-placed humour will help people cope, and will bring back fond memories of the deceased.
Don’t be afraid to show emotion. Funerals are an extremely emotional event. Nobody expects you not to shed a few tears. However, if you feel that you will be too strongly overcome by your emotions, have a back-up plan in place to have someone you trust deliver the eulogy for you. Give them a copy well in advance if you feel this may be the case.
Have a glass of water as well as tissues handy.
Obituaries
Writing an obituary is a difficult and emotional task. First, you will need to gather information from family and friends of the deceased about their childhood, education, career, hobbies and interests. As well, speak to the funeral home to receive any important information on the date, time and location of any funeral service, or other funeral related events. Using the template below will help make the process easier, and will ensure that you write a properly structured obituary.
Instructions: Replace all items in ITALICS below with the appropriate information.
[GIVEN NAME] [MIDDLE NAME (AND NICKNAME)] [SURNAME NAME], [AGE], of [CITY], [STATE], passed away on [DATE OF DEATH] in [LOCATION OF DEATH].
Funeral service will be held at [LOCATION] on [DATE] at [TIME] with Reverend [NAME] of [CHURCH] officiating. Burial will follow at [CEMETERY NAME], [CEMETERY LOCATION]. Visitation will be held at [LOCATION] on [DATE] at [TIME]. [NAME OF FUNERAL HOME] will be handling the funeral arrangements.
[NAME] was born in [LOCATION OF BIRTH] to [PARENT’S NAMES] on [DATE OF BIRTH]. He/she went to high school at [SCHOOL NAME] and graduated in [YEAR]. He/she went on to earn a degree/certificate in [DEGREE TYPE] from [SCHOOL NAME]. He/she worked as a [JOB TYPE] for [COMPANY] for [NUMBER OF YEARS]. He/she enjoyed [ACTIVITIES/HOBBIES]. He/she received [AWARDS/Honours] and was involved in [CHARITIES/ORGANIZATIONS].
[NAME] is survived by his/her [RELATION], [NAME] of [CITY]. (List of all survivors: spouse children, siblings, parents, grandchildren, nieces and nephews). He/she is preceded in death by his/her [RELATION], [NAME]. (List of predeceased: spouse, parents, children and siblings.)
Memorial donations may be made to [ORGANIZATION NAME], [MAILING ADDRESS]. The family wishes to extend their gratitude to [ORGANIZATION/NAME] [FINAL WORDS].
Remember, most newspapers charge by the word. This template is good for getting all the information necessary included in as few words possible. However, this template is not written in stone. You can make any adjustments you may feel necessary.

Old Grief Resources | McInnis & Holloway
McInnis & Holloway Support Services
For many families and loved ones, getting through a funeral or memorial service is just the beginning. Sometimes, the period following the service can be equally painful because others are getting on with their lives. Often that leaves a person in grief wondering where to turn for support. McInnis & Holloway knows that grieving can take months – and even years – to work through. That’s why we’ve developed Olive Branch, a grief support and educational service for the community. Olive Branch Support Services includes:
Family Follow-up
Support and Referral Service
Education Services for Groups
For information on Olive Branch, call us at (403) 276-2296, or e-mail us at olivebranch@mcinnisandholloway.com.
Family Follow-Up
The staff at McInnis & Holloway believes that caring for families goes beyond services provided at a time of need. Grieving is a process that takes time. There are tremendous resources available, and we are in a unique position to help link families with those resources. Every family served by McInnis & Holloway will be offered a home visit by our Family Support Provider. McInnis & Holloway families will be provided with a package specially tailored to the unique family loss, and will include information on grief and support services available. This is all available free of charge. Whether our families turn to us before the need arises to make advanced plannings, or after a service through Olive Branch, it’s just one of the many things we can do to help. For information on family follow-up, call us at (403) 276-2296 and ask for an Olive Branch Grief Consultant. Or, e-mail us at olivebranch@mcinnisandholloway.com.
Support And Referral Service
McInnis & Holloway Grief Consultants are available to families served by McInnis & Holloway on a limited basis for individual bereavement support and grief counselling. Referrals may be provided to direct the grieving individual or family to one of the many excellent grief support services available in their area. For support and referral service, call us at (403) 276-2296 and ask for an Olive Branch Grief Consultant. Or, e-mail us at olivebranch@mcinnisandholloway.com.
Education Services For Groups
McInnis & Holloway Funeral Homes have been serving families since 1903, and our staff are happy to share the knowledge they have gained during this time. Now, in addition to booklet information, “Cultural Customs and Traditions in Times of Death and Bereavement,” our Grief Consultants offer seminars and support programs for community groups, schools, churches, hospitals, palliative care organizations, civic groups, and long-term care facilities. 
Here are some of the seminar topics we cover through the Olive Branch program:
Is a funeral service necessary?
Customs and traditions surrounding a funeral service.
Life after loss – understand your grief.
Grief and the holidays.
Children and adolescents’ grief.
Suicide bereavement.
Professional training about the grief process and helping those who grieve.
How to facilitate adult or children’s grief groups.
Care Giver’s Life Well Lived.
Life after Loss Bereavement Support Group.
E-mail us at olivebranch@mcinnisandholloway.com to book a presentation, or call us at (403) 276-2296 and ask for an Olive Branch Grief Consultant.

Planning in advance gives you the opportunity to make decisions thoughtfully and without pressure. Our team will help you explore your options, record your wishes, and plan with confidence for the future.

## **Plan Ahead with Confidence**

*   A simple breakdown of what decisions to expect.
    
*   Helpful prompts to clarify your preferences
    
*   A checklist to keep everything organized in one place.
    

## Whether you're planning for yourself or helping a loved one, this guide makes it easier to prepare on your own terms.
