###### What about cultural customs, and traditions for the funeral service?

As the ethnic fabric of our society grows, the customs and traditions surrounding funerals change. Expression of grief is different for every group, but everyone shares a need to mark the passing of a life with affection, dignity and respect.

If you are uncertain about different cultural or religious backgrounds, and this has kept you from attending a funeral or expressing sympathy, a little knowledge can help. Here are a few examples of customs and traditions which can be part of a funeral service (examples may vary according to personal tastes and beliefs):

*   Native or Plains Indians play drums and sing honour songs or personal songs belonging to the deceased. Sweetgrass is sometimes burned as a ritual or prayer.
*   Buddhists ring a bell to the start the funeral. After the funeral service – which takes place in a temple or funeral home – a memorial service is held every 7th day for 49 days, and family and friends are encouraged to attend.
*   Those attending a Chinese funeral may receive a white envelope with candy and money inside. The candy is to sweeten the bitter taste of death, and the money is for luck, since death is considered a bad omen.

If you have a question you would like answered by one of our funeral directors (at no obligation). [Click here to send us an e-mail](mailto:info@mcinnisandholloway.com).  

###### What are my options at Calgary’s Mausoleum?

Mausoleum burial is becoming more popular with many communities as an alternative to ground burial. Calgary’s first mausoleum is housed at Queen’s Park Cemetery, and is a city-owned facility.

A mausoleum provides permanent above-ground entombment, and is based on popular European traditions dating back before the time of Christ.

The casket is placed into the mausoleum wall and sealed. The wall of a mausoleum is generally about five to six caskets in height. In Calgary, crypt panels are made from high-quality Italian marble with plaques or photographs for the deceased as a memorial tribute. Flower vases can be affixed to the wall as well.

Calgary’s mausoleum offers a variety of configurations and prices ranges, starting at about $5,280. For more information, call the Calgary Cemeteries and Mausoleum information line at [(403) 221-3660](tel:+14032213660).

###### What options are there for the cremation urn?

Many options are available for the final disposition of the ashes:

**Burial**

Some cemeteries have urn gardens for burial of an urn, above-ground columbariums, or will allow burial in the family plot, while others have scattering grounds as part of the cemetery.

**Memorial Vessels**

Cremation allows the family to retain the cremated remains, either in one urn or a number of smaller ones to distribute among family. Some people place a small portion of cremated remains in a memorial vessel, such as a necklace or bracelet.

**Scattering**

Scattering cremated remains in a meaningful location can be considered. Sometimes the family marks the site with a small memorial plaque so it can later be revisited. Since scattering is irreversible, it’s best to think about it in advance, as grieving individuals sometimes make choices they later wish they hadn’t.

In Alberta (Canada), scattering cannot occur over water, but is permitted on most crown and public lands, and national parks, but permission must always be obtained ahead of time.

If you have a question you would like answered by one of our funeral directors (at no obligation). [Click here to send us an e-mail](mailto:info@mcinnisandholloway.com).

###### What options are available if I choose cremation?

Many people choose cremation because of religious or cultural reasons, or just because of personal preference. Selecting cremation does not restrict the family’s options when it comes to having a ceremony or funeral service. The family can still choose visitation or viewing prior to the funeral, and some funeral homes rent caskets for this purpose.

Families have a choice between a funeral service, where the casket or cremated remains are present in an urn or other container. They may also select a memorial service where the cremated remains are not present. A memorial service can be held anywhere – in a church, funeral home, chapel, community hall, hotel, private club or family home, and is usually within a few days or weeks of the death.

For final disposition, the urn or container is typically buried in a cemetery plot, placed in a columbarium above ground, or scattered at the cemetery gardens. Or, families can choose to scatter ashes in another place of significance. Cemeteries vary regarding arrangements for ashes, so it’s best to check with the individual cemetery.

If you have a question you would like answered by one of our funeral directors (at no obligation). [Click here to send us an e-mail](mailto:info@mcinnisandholloway.com).

###### What options are available if I choose burial?

Burial is still the most common method of final disposition. Most families have a graveside ceremony immediately after the funeral ceremony, conducted by a clergy member, the funeral director or a friend.

For loved ones, seeing the deceased committed to earth can be a painful but important ritual. It helps some accept the reality of death – often the first important step towards healing.

Direct disposition, where the deceased is buried without a formal viewing, visitation or ceremony, is another option, but experts on grief feel that healing can take longer if the loved one isn’t memorialized in some way. A funeral ceremony or memorial service allows loved ones to share grief together and publicly celebrate the life of the one they loved.

If the family chooses burial, the funeral director helps with the selection of a casket. There is a wide selection of choices and prices ranging from several hundred dollars to several thousand, depending on the type of casket.

Graveside markers are typically added to the cemetery plot, either before the service or weeks later. Find out the options available at your cemetery, as some do have restrictions about the type of marker. Some Calgary cemeteries require the purchase of a vault for burial, while others do not. Be sure to ask about the requirements and options at your cemetery.

If you have a question you would like answered by one of our funeral directors (at no obligation). [Click here to send us an e-mail](mailto:info@mcinnisandholloway.com).

###### Is a funeral service required?

Experts in the grief process universally recognize the value of the ceremony for surviving family and friends.

A ceremony is important for many reasons: in some religions, it is the event which marks the transition from life to after-life; in others, it’s one step towards a higher level of existence.

Whatever your belief, a ceremony provides others the opportunity to acknowledge and remember achievements of the life of the deceased, to mark their passing in a significant way, and provides comfort, sympathy, and meaning to survivors.

A funeral also helps some accept the reality of death, and allows us to share our grief with others. The funeral ceremony can provide the opportunity for friends to show they care about the bereaved, and to offer their support during a difficult time.

If you have a question you would like answered by one of our funeral directors (at no obligation). [Click here to send us an e-mail](mailto:info@mcinnisandholloway.com).

McInnis & Holloway Funeral Homes
Funeral Etiquette
Like everything in society, funeral etiquette has evolved through the years. While common sense is your best guide, here are a few dos and don'ts of funeral etiquette.
Do:
Express your condolences – It’s not easy to come up with the right words for someone who has just lost a loved one. You don’t need to be a poet. Simply saying, “I am sorry for your loss. My thoughts and prayers are with you and your family”, is enough. If you can’t be at a funeral service in person, sending a card or leaving a message on a memorial website is a perfect way to express your sympathy.
Dress appropriately – Gone are the days of dressing up in all black for a funeral, but jeans and a t-shirt aren't acceptable either. You should still dress to impress. Try to avoid any bright or flashy colours. Wear what you would wear to a wedding or a job interview.
Sign the register book – The family will keep the register book as a memento for years. Be sure to include your full name and relationship to the deceased. Please don't hesitate to leave a message.
Give a gift – You don’t need to go overboard with your gift - it is the thought that counts. Suitable gifts include: flowers; a donation to the charity of the family’s choice, or you can make a commitment of service to the family at a later date. A commitment of service can be something as simple as cooking dinner for them, offering to clean up their house, or any of the “little” things that may be neglected while a family deals with death. Make sure you provide a signed card, so the family knows who gave the gift.
Keep in Touch – You may feel that the family needs their space and time to grieve, but a simple phone call or note after the funeral lets the family know you care. With social networking, leaving a quick note is as simple as a click of a mouse. The months following a death are when grieving friends and family need the most support.
Don't:
Bring your cell phone – Your phone ringing will be highly inappropriate and will cause a disturbance. Turn any ringers or notifications off. Even better, leave your phone at home or in your car. A funeral is not the time to be texting or checking your messages.
Allow your children to be a distraction – From a very young age, children are aware of death, and if the funeral is for someone who was close to them (grandparent, aunt, uncle), they should be given the option of attending. If it is not appropriate for your child to be there, or if you feel they will cause a commotion, it might be best to find appropriate care for them for the day.
Be afraid to remember the good times – Funerals are obviously a time of grieving and mourning, but remembering the good times helps with the healing process. Sharing a funny and appropriate story is acceptable, and in some cases, it's precisely what the deceased would have wanted.
Overindulge - If food or drink is served, don't over-do it. Remember that you won't be the only attendee. If alcohol is served, limit yourself to one or two.

# McInnis & Holloway Funeral Homes

## Funeral Etiquette  

Like everything in society, funeral etiquette has evolved through the years. While common sense is your best guide, here are a few dos and don'ts of funeral etiquette.  

### Do:

*   **Express your condolences** – It’s not easy to come up with the right words for someone who has just lost a loved one. You don’t need to be a poet. Simply saying, “I am sorry for your loss. My thoughts and prayers are with you and your family”, is enough. If you can’t be at a funeral service in person, sending a card or leaving a message on a memorial website is a perfect way to express your sympathy.
*   **Dress appropriately** – Gone are the days of dressing up in all black for a funeral, but jeans and a t-shirt aren't acceptable either. You should still dress to impress. Try to avoid any bright or flashy colours. Wear what you would wear to a wedding or a job interview.
*   **Sign the register book** – The family will keep the register book as a memento for years. Be sure to include your full name and relationship to the deceased. Please don't hesitate to leave a message.
*   **Give a gift** – You don’t need to go overboard with your gift - it is the thought that counts. Suitable gifts include: flowers; a donation to the charity of the family’s choice, or you can make a commitment of service to the family at a later date. A commitment of service can be something as simple as cooking dinner for them, offering to clean up their house, or any of the “little” things that may be neglected while a family deals with death. Make sure you provide a signed card, so the family knows who gave the gift.
*   **Keep in Touch** – You may feel that the family needs their space and time to grieve, but a simple phone call or note after the funeral lets the family know you care. With social networking, leaving a quick note is as simple as a click of a mouse. The months following a death are when grieving friends and family need the most support.

### Don't:

*   **Bring your cell phone** – Your phone ringing will be highly inappropriate and will cause a disturbance. Turn any ringers or notifications off. Even better, leave your phone at home or in your car. A funeral is not the time to be texting or checking your messages.
*   **Allow your children to be a distraction** – From a very young age, children are aware of death, and if the funeral is for someone who was close to them (grandparent, aunt, uncle), they should be given the option of attending. If it is not appropriate for your child to be there, or if you feel they will cause a commotion, it might be best to find appropriate care for them for the day.
*   **Be afraid to remember the good times** – Funerals are obviously a time of grieving and mourning, but remembering the good times helps with the healing process. Sharing a funny and appropriate story is acceptable, and in some cases, it's precisely what the deceased would have wanted.
*   **Overindulge** - If food or drink is served, don't over-do it. Remember that you won't be the only attendee. If alcohol is served, limit yourself to one or two.

At McInnis & Holloway, we are honoured to serve Calgary families with compassion, dignity, and care. Heritage Funeral Home carries a long-standing tradition of respectful service, rooted in community values and family leadership. Originally established in 1930 by George and Vera “Ireland” Jacques, Heritage continues to honour its legacy as a locally owned funeral home dedicated to supporting families from all walks of life during life’s most difficult moments. 
Call (403) 299-0100 
Serving Families at Heritage Funeral Home
Located in northwest Calgary, Heritage Funeral Home serves families in Capitol Hill, Mount Pleasant, Briar Hill, Banff Trail, and surrounding communities. The funeral home was created following the purchase and thoughtful renovation of the former Cy Foster-Gooder Funeral Home on 16th Avenue NW, allowing the Jacques family to expand their vision of compassionate, dignified service.
Today, Heritage remains committed to providing a welcoming and respectful environment for families of all cultural backgrounds, offering personalized care that reflects both tradition and individual wishes. 
Call (403) 299-0100 
A Legacy of Care and Community
Originally known as Jacques Funeral Home, and affectionately remembered as “The Little Chapel on the Corner,” the funeral home was first established along 17th Avenue SW in 1930. As the community grew and the need for expanded services increased, the opportunity to create a larger, more accessible location led to the establishment of what is now Heritage Funeral Home.
Purchased by McInnis & Holloway in 2007, Heritage continues to operate as a locally owned family funeral service provider, preserving the values, integrity, and commitment to excellence established by the Jacques family.

## A Legacy of Care and Community

Originally known as Jacques Funeral Home, and affectionately remembered as “_The Little Chapel on the Corner_,” the funeral home was first established along 17th Avenue SW in 1930. As the community grew and the need for expanded services increased, the opportunity to create a larger, more accessible location led to the establishment of what is now Heritage Funeral Home.

Purchased by McInnis & Holloway in 2007, Heritage continues to operate as a locally owned family funeral service provider, preserving the values, integrity, and commitment to excellence established by the Jacques family. 

[Learn More About Us](https://www.mhfh.com/about-mandh/our-people)

### Memorial Services

Personalized memorial services designed to reflect your loved one’s life, values, and legacy.

Planning ahead offers peace of mind for you and clarity for your loved ones. Our team is here to guide you with compassion and care.

# Tree Program | McInnis & Holloway

The Memorial Forest ®   

### A Comforting Symbol Of Life  

For McInnis & Holloway Funeral Homes and the families in Calgary a tree represents quiet strength, beauty, longevity, and peacefulness – an ideal memorial to a person’s life. McInnis & Holloway’s Memorial Forests® program allows McInnis & Holloway Funeral Home to give back to the community, by enhancing the growth of parks in the Calgary area. Families are encouraged to come to one of the Memorial Forests®, and enjoy the protected haven they provide.  

### A Living Tribute  

The Memorial Forests® program offers a special way of memorializing a person who has died and provides families with a meaningful way to deal with a loss. McInnis & Holloway Funeral Homes makes every attempt to find appropriate and lasting ways for loved ones to be remembered. In this case, a tree planted will remain a living memorial for families and friends to return to year after year.  

Each year, McInnis and Holloway plants a tree for every family we serve. In 2020, our newest Memorial Forest was created in the Ann & Sandy Cross Conservation area. Others can purchase, at a minimal cost, one or more trees to add to the Memorial Forest®, through McInnis & Holloway.

Our newest Memorial Forest within the Ann & Sandy Conservation Area has a viewpoint that families can use to reflect and remember and know that trees have been planted to enhance this beautiful protected area.  There are now two forest areas where friends and families of loved-ones past can spend time in a pristine natural haven that welcomes heartfelt reflection and remembrance.   McInnis & Holloway Memorial Forest Viewpoint overlooks our 2020 Forest, where trees were planted from 2020 to 2021.

In 2022 a new site was chosen for planting, where trees will be planted each each into the foreseeable future. In the coming months, this area will be developed to include a walking path, sheltered rest area and signage to direct visitors, all with as minimal an impact on the land and habitat as possible. 

Families can visit the Ann and Sandy Cross Conservation area at any time throughout the year.   

[Click here to open our additional memorial tree online order form](https://forms.mhfh.com/Forms/Memorial-Tree-Order-Form/2080/index.html#form-start)

*   Accessible from 144 St W/Range Road 23 off of highway 22X.
*   Not accessible from education centre or public trails.

###### Directions to New Memorial Forest Area (Future Memorial Forest Pathway Location)

*   Located near our south facing trail head at the top of 160 St West
*   Can be viewed from a locked gate to the left (east) of the trail a short distance from our kiosk
*   \*\*Planting site is not currently accessible to the public\*\*
*   **For your safety, we ask that you do not attempt to open or cross the gate**

![Map of the future Memorial Forest Pathway location](https://d1q40j6jx1d8h6.cloudfront.net/SiteBuilder/ee93aebe-51b2-489e-8a60-5fe98e33065b/0672cc60-ee9e-4d82-bced-5d2fac1c8884.webp "Map of the future Memorial Forest Pathway location")

##### Since the start of our Memorial Forest program in 1996, McInnis and Holloway has planted over 57,842 trees in Calgary and the surrounding areas.  

Our first Memorial Forest was in Fish Creek Provincial Park, between 1996 and 2020 we planted a total of 47,610 trees within four areas of Fish Creek Provincial Park:  

**1996-2002**  
**Glennfield Area**  
12,000 trees were planted  

**2003-2007**  
**Shaw's Meadow**  
7,600 trees were planted  

**2008-2012**  
**Lafarge Meadows**  
10,710 trees were planted  

**2013 & 2020**  
**Burnsmead**  
17,300 trees were planted  

We had a five-year contract with the City of Calgary to plant trees in our Nose Creek Valley Memorial Forest. This contract ended June 2005 when the City of Calgary decided not to renew the contract for this area. Between 2000 and 2005 McInnis & Holloway planted 4,200 trees in Nose Creek Valley Memorial Forest.

We planted trees in Fletcher Park in Airdrie from 2001 to 2010. A total of 1,322 in this Memorial Forest.

McInnis and Holloway then offered Big Hill Springs Memorial Forest from 2011 to 2013 with 2,250 trees planted in this Memorial Forest.

We have included maps of our previous Memorial Forest locations for you below. 

To find out more about the Memorial Forest® program, [click here](https://www.mhfh.com/tree-program/more-information) or contact McInnis & Holloway Funeral Home at [1 (800) 661-1599](tel:+18006611599) or [(403) 243-8200](tel:+14032438200).

Obituary information for Carlton Joachim Martin
It is with profound sadness that we announce the passing of a beloved husband, father, and all-round beautiful human being, Carlton Joachim Martin, who passed away peacefully on the 13th of July 2026 at the age of 88.
Carlton was a devoted husband, father, brother, brother-in-law, uncle and friend whose kindness, strength, and unwavering love, touched the lives of all who knew him. He was known for his humble and generous heart, and the wisdom he shared so freely with those around him.
Born on the 15th of August 1937 in St. Josephs, Marcas, Trinidad & Tobago, his life had very humble beginnings. At a young age, he moved to the village of Siparia, where he began a life rooted in love, family, friendship and quiet generosity. He took great pride in his family and friends, and found immense joy in spending time with those he loved. Whether sharing stories, offering words of encouragement or simply being present when needed most, he leaves behind a legacy of compassion and integrity.
In 1958 he met Merle Rahim and in 1962 they married and embarked on a life which took them to London, England. There he completed his BSc Economics & Sociology, at the London Metropolitan University, (Formerly the Polytechnic of North London / London Guildhall). He then completed his MSc in Industrial Relations at the London School of Economics, and began a long and successful career in labor relations, where he combined the patience of an educator with the discipline of an athlete to fight for fairness and help others thrive.
In 1971 he returned to Trinidad where he worked in the oil and gas industry. In 1977 he moved his family to Canada and lived the remainder of his life in Edmonton, Alberta. He dedicated the next 29 years of his career to serving as a Labor Relations Consultant with the Alberta Provincial Government, where his passion for sharing knowledge earned him a few awards but mostly left an enduring impact.
Carlton greatest joy was his family, and together with Merle created a full and loving life together. Carlton was very involved with his childrens' lives, including in their education and personal lives, always offering his love and support. He also extended this care to all members of his family, the nieces and nephews and his childrens' friends as well. 
Carlton loved to read and was enthusiastic about physical fitness and health. He loved music and dancing to calypso & soca, and in quiet moments listening to the classics on steel drum. He left his mark in the Edmonton community, as a choir member of his church, and mentoring children through the Congress of Black Women (Edmonton Chapter).
He is lovingly remembered by his wife, Merle; his children, Charmaine, Ricardo & Edward; his daughters-in-law, Gaylene & Dixie; his step-granddaughter, Leo Cromack; his sisters-in-law, Maria Rahim, Joan Rahim, Grace Goocool; his nieces/nephews, Jared Abdul, Alyan Abdul-Morris, Donald Gopaul, Donna Mason; his cousins, Theresa Lewis & Joan Walker; and his extended family, the Weathermans, the Josephs, the Charles, the Saunders and the Hintons. These and all his long-time friends who are also
considered family share the loss of this great human being.
Though our hearts are heavy with grief, we find comfort in the countless memories we shared and in knowing that his love will remain with us always. His life was a blessing, his memory a treasure, and he will be forever loved and dearly missed.
A Funeral Mass will be celebrated at 11:00 a.m. on Thursday July 23, 2026, at Annunciation Catholic Church.

# Obituary information for Carlton Joachim Martin

It is with profound sadness that we announce the passing of a beloved husband, father, and all-round beautiful human being, Carlton Joachim Martin, who passed away peacefully on the 13th of July 2026 at the age of 88.

Carlton was a devoted husband, father, brother, brother-in-law, uncle and friend whose kindness, strength, and unwavering love, touched the lives of all who knew him. He was known for his humble and generous heart, and the wisdom he shared so freely with those around him.

Born on the 15th of August 1937 in St. Josephs, Marcas, Trinidad & Tobago, his life had very humble beginnings. At a young age, he moved to the village of Siparia, where he began a life rooted in love, family, friendship and quiet generosity. He took great pride in his family and friends, and found immense joy in spending time with those he loved. Whether sharing stories, offering words of encouragement or simply being present when needed most, he leaves behind a legacy of compassion and integrity.

In 1958 he met Merle Rahim and in 1962 they married and embarked on a life which took them to London, England. There he completed his BSc Economics & Sociology, at the London Metropolitan University, (Formerly the Polytechnic of North London / London Guildhall). He then completed his MSc in Industrial Relations at the London School of Economics, and began a long and successful career in labor relations, where he combined the patience of an educator with the discipline of an athlete to fight for fairness and help others thrive.

In 1971 he returned to Trinidad where he worked in the oil and gas industry. In 1977 he moved his family to Canada and lived the remainder of his life in Edmonton, Alberta. He dedicated the next 29 years of his career to serving as a Labor Relations Consultant with the Alberta Provincial Government, where his passion for sharing knowledge earned him a few awards but mostly left an enduring impact.

Carlton greatest joy was his family, and together with Merle created a full and loving life together. Carlton was very involved with his childrens' lives, including in their education and personal lives, always offering his love and support. He also extended this care to all members of his family, the nieces and nephews and his childrens' friends as well. 

Carlton loved to read and was enthusiastic about physical fitness and health. He loved music and dancing to calypso & soca, and in quiet moments listening to the classics on steel drum. He left his mark in the Edmonton community, as a choir member of his church, and mentoring children through the Congress of Black Women (Edmonton Chapter).

He is lovingly remembered by his wife, Merle; his children, Charmaine, Ricardo & Edward; his daughters-in-law, Gaylene & Dixie; his step-granddaughter, Leo Cromack; his sisters-in-law, Maria Rahim, Joan Rahim, Grace Goocool; his nieces/nephews, Jared Abdul, Alyan Abdul-Morris, Donald Gopaul, Donna Mason; his cousins, Theresa Lewis & Joan Walker; and his extended family, the Weathermans, the Josephs, the Charles, the Saunders and the Hintons. These and all his long-time friends who are also

considered family share the loss of this great human being.

Though our hearts are heavy with grief, we find comfort in the countless memories we shared and in knowing that his love will remain with us always. His life was a blessing, his memory a treasure, and he will be forever loved and dearly missed.

A Funeral Mass will be celebrated at 11:00 a.m. on Thursday July 23, 2026, at Annunciation Catholic Church.

"Those we love don't go away; they walk besides us everyday - unseen, unheard"

Obituary information for Samantha Alice “Sam” Muirhead
On July 7, 2026, our beautiful Samantha Alice Muirhead passed away. She was surrounded by loved ones and is now resting peacefully following her battle with cancer.
Sam will be lovingly remembered and dearly missed by her wife, Mary Gledhow; parents, Alice (Jim) and Hank (Carol); siblings, Andrea (Mark), Christine (Joe), Craig (Stephanie); nieces and nephews, Charlotte, Simone, Ameila, Sawyer, Elliot, Dylan, Reid; Aunty Jen and Uncle Kourch; Beloved in laws, David and Helen Gledhow; sister in law, Theresa (Greg) Piorkowski; and nephews, Thomas, and Arthur. Her beloved dogs, Velma and Stevie; and cat, Tina. She will be dearly missed by all her friends and family.
Sam dedicated her life to working with bees. As Alberta’s first female Provincial Apiculturist (Queen Bee) she travelled around the province inspecting Alberta’s Honeybees. Her “Happy Place” was in the bee yard, and she would describe how working with the bees taught her to be calm, patient, and resilient. That is how she approached her cancer journey, along with unbelievable strength. She travelled internationally doing the things she loved; hiking, eating new foods and learning the culture. She had the ability to make anyone laugh, feel special and seen.
Her adventurous spirit, laughter and love of animals will always be remembered and live through us all. It was both a privilege and a gift to have been loved by Sam, and she will be greatly missed.
A Celebration of Sam’s life will be held at 2:00 pm on Sunday, August 16, 2026, at Connelly-McKinley Funeral Home, 10011 – 114 Street NW, Edmonton, AB. Sam appreciated moments of Joy, and would like attendees to be dressed in cheerful attire; colorful, flowery, and shiny!

A Thoughtful Approach to End-of-Life Arrangements
Planning for the future is a considerate step that offers peace of mind to you and your loved ones. By making decisions about your end-of-life arrangements in advance, you can ensure your wishes are respected and alleviate the emotional and financial burden on your family during a difficult time.
Thinking about end-of-life arrangements isn’t easy, but making these decisions in advance is one of the most profound acts of love and care you can offer your family. It provides clarity, reduces stress, and ensures that your wishes are honoured—giving those you love the freedom to focus on healing, rather than making difficult decisions during a time of grief.
We often wait until a crisis forces us to think about funeral arrangements. But when a loved one passes unexpectedly, families are left navigating overwhelming emotions while trying to make urgent decisions. This can lead to stress, uncertainty, and even family disagreements. Advance planning removes that burden, giving your family the reassurance that they are carrying out your wishes exactly as you intended.
Download Our Free Planning Guide 
To speak to one of our Family Service Consultants, please call 780-590-0626 
Benefits of Advance Planning
Personalized Services: Documenting your preferences allows for a funeral, celebration of life, or memorial service that truly reflects your personality, values, and life story.
Financial Assurance: Pre-arranging can lock in current prices for services and merchandise, protecting against future cost increases and easing financial concerns for your family.
Reduced Family Stress: Having a clear plan in place spares your loved ones from making challenging decisions during a period of grief, allowing them to focus on healing and remembrance.
Preventing Family Conflict: Clearly outlined wishes can help prevent disagreements among family members about your final arrangements.
Key Considerations in Advance Planning
Disposition Choices: Decide between burial, cremation, or alternative options such as green burials.
Service Details: Specify the type of service you prefer, including location, music, readings, and participants.
Financial Arrangements: Explore prepayment options to manage costs and ensure funds are available when needed.
Legal Documentation: Ensure your will, power of attorney, and other essential documents are up to date and accessible.
The Emotional Benefits of Planning Ahead
1. Eases the Weight of Uncertainty
Without a plan, families often wonder: Did we make the right choices? Is this what they would have wanted? These unanswered questions can linger long after the funeral. Advance planning provides clear guidance, bringing peace of mind to those left behind.
2. Allows for a Meaningful Goodbye
When arrangements are made in advance, your family can focus on what truly matters—honouring your life, sharing memories, and supporting one another in their grief. Instead of rushing through decisions, they can take time to create a farewell that reflects your legacy.
3. Reduces Stress During an Already Difficult Time
Grief is emotionally exhausting. Having to make major financial and logistical decisions while grieving can feel overwhelming. Planning ahead gives your loved ones the gift of space—space to grieve, to reflect, and to begin healing without additional pressure.
4. Prevents Family Conflict
In times of loss, emotions run high, and differing opinions about funeral arrangements can lead to tension among family members. A well-documented plan ensures that your wishes are clear, reducing the chance of misunderstandings and difficult conversations.
5. Gives You Control Over Your Legacy
Your funeral is a reflection of your life, your values, and your beliefs. Whether you want a traditional service, a quiet gathering, or a unique celebration, advance planning ensures that your farewell is meaningful and personal.
Why Not Wait?
It’s natural to put off thinking about end-of-life arrangements—no one wants to dwell on loss. But waiting until illness or old age forces the conversation can add unnecessary stress. When plans are made in advance, they are made with a clear mind, without the urgency of declining health or the emotions of an immediate loss.
Advance planning isn’t just about paperwork; it’s about peace. It’s about ensuring your family is taken care of, free from uncertainty, and able to honour your memory in the way you intended.
A Simple Step Towards Peace of Mind
Taking the first step is easier than you think.
By planning now, you’re offering your family a future filled with clarity, comfort, and the space they need to grieve and heal.
Make the choice today to ease their tomorrow.
Steps to Begin Advance Planning
Reflect on Your Wishes: Consider how you envision your end-of-life arrangements, including the type of service and disposition method.
Consult Professionals: Meet with our Licensed Planning Specialists to discuss options and receive guidance tailored to your preferences.
Communicate with Loved Ones: Share your plans with family members to ensure they are aware and can honour your wishes.
Document Your Decisions: Record your choices in writing and store them in a safe, accessible place. We will provide a Personal Planning Organizer to document important information your executor will require.
Review and Update Regularly: Revisit your plans periodically to make adjustments as needed, ensuring they continue to reflect your desires.
By taking these steps, you can create a comprehensive plan that brings comfort and clarity to you and your loved ones.
Book your no cost, no obligation consultation today!

When plans are made in advance, they are made with a clear mind, without the urgency of declining health or the emotions of an immediate loss.

Advance planning isn’t just about paperwork; it’s about peace. It’s about ensuring your family is taken care of, free from uncertainty, and able to honour your memory in the way you intended.

A Simple Step Towards Peace of Mind

Taking the first step is easier than you think.

By planning now, you’re offering your family a future filled with clarity, comfort, and the space they need to grieve and heal.

Make the choice today to ease their tomorrow.

### Steps to Begin Advance Planning

1.  **Reflect on Your Wishes:** Consider how you envision your end-of-life arrangements, including the type of service and disposition method.
2.  **Consult Professionals:** Meet with our Licensed Planning Specialists to discuss options and receive guidance tailored to your preferences.
3.  **Communicate with Loved Ones:** Share your plans with family members to ensure they are aware and can honour your wishes.
4.  **Document Your Decisions:** Record your choices in writing and store them in a safe, accessible place. We will provide a Personal Planning Organizer to document important information your executor will require.
5.  **Review and Update Regularly:** Revisit your plans periodically to make adjustments as needed, ensuring they continue to reflect your desires.

By taking these steps, you can create a comprehensive plan that brings comfort and clarity to you and your loved ones.

What We Offer | Connelly-McKinley Funeral Home in Edmonton, Alberta
For more than 110 years, Connelly-McKinley Funeral Homes has been committed to compassionately serve the families who trust their loved ones to our care. We listen to a family’s needs and then provide customized services to fulfill those needs.
Signature Services: Compassion, Care, and Personalized Excellence
At Connelly-McKinley Funeral Home, we believe every life is unique and deserves a service that reflects its individuality. Our passion is creating meaningful, personal experiences that celebrate life and provide comfort to families.
Whether you’re planning a service for a loved one or preplanning for yourself, our process begins with understanding what made that life special—stories, passions, traditions, and cherished moments. These insights inspire us to craft ceremonies that are as distinctive as the people they honour.
Our Life Celebration Experts are dedicated to helping you create a gathering filled with personal touches and lasting memories. We aim to ease your journey by handling the details, allowing you to focus on honouring your loved one and beginning to heal.
What sets us apart is our unwavering commitment to connection. By learning the true story of your loved one, we help you share their legacy in a way that resonates deeply with family and friends. We believe in the power of story, the importance of legacy, and the beauty of celebrating a life well-lived.
Guided by our Core Purpose—Healing Hearts, Inspiring Trust, and Honouring Legacy—we are here to provide an experience that supports and uplifts you.
From traditional ceremonies to highly personalized celebrations, we offer a range of options to suit your needs. Whether it’s a picnic in the park with hot dogs and S’mores, a formal dinner party, or a unique cultural or religious ceremony, our team will help bring your vision to life.
Our experienced directors and staff are well-versed in diverse traditions, rites, and customs, ensuring your service respects and honours your loved one’s beliefs and values. From a Traditional Ceremony to an entirely original concept, we’re here to help you create a service that brings comfort and healing.
At Connelly-McKinley Funeral Home, we are more than a funeral home—we are partners in honoring lives, supporting families, and creating beautiful memories that last forever.
Services only Limited by your imagination
Celebrate a Life Well Lived, Your Way
Honouring a life well-lived is a deeply personal journey, and the ways to commemorate a loved one are as unique as the individuals themselves. A thoughtfully planned service not only reflects the values and passions of the person who has passed but also brings comfort and connection to those who attend. It provides an opportunity for guests to share cherished memories and create meaningful bonds as they celebrate together.
At our funeral home, our experienced Directors are committed to helping you design a heartfelt tribute that is as unique as your loved one. From traditional ceremonies to creative celebrations, we work with you to craft an event that truly honours their legacy, with no limits on imagination.
We also offer a variety of personalization options and special services, including:
Comfortable accommodations for your family during visiting hours
Memorial DVD video tributes
Live-streaming of the service for those who cannot attend in person
Online obituary access through our website
Custom memorial candles and other keepsakes
Whether you envision a traditional service steeped in timeless rituals or a casual gathering in the park with hot dogs and s’mores, our team is here to guide you every step of the way.
Discover Inspiration
Explore unique service and reception ideas 
here
. Together, we can create a beautiful and memorable farewell.
Traditional Services
The tradition of burying our loved ones is time-honored and sacred. Burial gives us the peace of mind in laying them to rest, and gives us a place in the future to visit, decorate, and remember.
When your loved one has chosen to be buried, the ceremonies you design usually involve the casket being present. Traditions may be followed by a viewing and a funeral service followed by a graveside ceremony. Some families choose to change the order of ceremonies or make certain gatherings private. We are here to help you find the right options for your family and community to help you arrive at the perfect way to gather together.
Traditions are comforting to many people and have remained in practice because of the healing options they offer
A traditional service usually includes a visitation and/or a wake where family and friends come to pay their respects and share memories with the family of the deceased with funeral services conducted at either the funeral home, church, or graveside thereafter.
Traditional Services are usually of a religious or cultural nature and the casket is present at services.
The service can be followed by a time of fellowship with a reception. All our facilities have spacious and fully equipped reception rooms to accommodate your specific needs.
When families choose a traditional burial we provide the setting for the visitation, help you find a place for your ceremony, our chapel or a local chapel, and we coordinate with the cemetery to plan the graveside ceremony. Graveside ceremonies can be just as personalized as the funeral ceremony and can include a sound system to play a favourite song, butterfly or dove release, a bagpiper or a veteran honour guard.
Click here to learn more about Burial Options
Distinctive Services
A distinctive service can be traditionally based by adding some personal touches that make it more tailored to your loved one and your family traditions. Most are not held in a church, but at the funeral home or any other place of your choosing.
They can also include visitation and/or a wake where family and friends come to pay their respects and share memories with the family of the deceased with funeral services to follow.
Distinctive Services are usually not of a religious or cultural nature and the casket is not necessarily present at services but certainly could be.
The service can be followed by a time of fellowship with a reception. All our facilities have spacious and fully equipped reception rooms to accommodate your specific needs.

Click here for More Ideas for Designing Your Ceremony
Cremation Options
With the belief that every life deserves ceremony, we offer both classic and modern ceremonial options with cremation.
Our staff is knowledgeable in all faith traditions and customs so we can attend to each specific ceremony with detail and thoughtfulness. If you are not affiliated with a faith community, we have certified funeral celebrants to preside at your ceremony.
Many may think cremation is the easier option due to a common misconception that cremation is the service. Cremation is simply a disposition. You think burial, it means you’re being buried. Many don’t think of cremation that way.
Being cremated does not mean “being forgotten”, we see it as life being shared in the same way that we would follow other types of services but with the cremated remains of your loved one being the focal point rather than a casket.
With the belief that every life deserves ceremony, we offer both classic and modern ceremonial options with cremation.
Our staff is knowledgeable in all faith traditions and customs so we can attend to each specific ceremony with detail and thoughtfulness. If you are not affiliated with a faith community, we have certified funeral celebrants to preside at your ceremony.
Cremation Facts
Cremation is a process by which the body is reduced to its basic elements, bone fragments. It is a misconception that they are ashes. The extreme heat of the retort also means that little to no traces of the cremation casket or container (regardless of the material) will remain to mingle with your loved one’s cremated remains.
Cremation is not a final disposition process. It is another step in the memorialization process. After cremation takes place, families must make a choice for the final disposition of cremated remains.
Final disposition options include placing the cremated remains in a decorative urn to be displayed in the home, in a niche or columbarium, burying the cremated remains in the family’s preferred cemetery, or scattering the cremated remains.
Services before or following cremation are many and varied. You can have a traditional service or a unique event that exemplifies the life of your loved one. See our Celebration of Life Options and Cremation Planning Guide to help you create an extraordinary service. Our Celebration of Life Experts are here to help.
Click here for our Connelly McKinley 10 Step Cremation Promise
Green or Natural Burial in Edmonton
Many families are now asking about natural or green burials, primarily since the opening of the natural burial section at Rose Hill Cemetery
What is the Definition of a Green or Natural Burial?

We define green burial as a way of caring for the dead with minimal environmental impact that aids in the conservation of natural resources, reduction of carbon emissions, protection of worker health, and the restoration and/or preservation of habitat. Natural burials are carried out with ecological friendly materials including the clothing, shroud or casket that allows the return to earth to have the least amount of impact on the environment as possible.
We recommend that if you are interested in a natural burial that you contact Rose Hill Cemetery to ensure that this will meet your needs. They have restrictions and stipulations that may affect your choice.
As they are currently the only cemetery in Edmonton offering this type of burial, this remains your only choice.
They have allocated a section specifically for green burials
You can find more information about this here.
From the Funeral Home standpoint, we work with each family individually to help them choose the best services and products for their needs. As this is a very personal choice and each family has their own reasons and thought process as to what they would want, we want to ensure we meet those needs.
We have a shroud and selection environment friendly caskets that reflect the Green Burial Society of Canada and the requirements of the cemetery.
Should you wish more information and costs, please call 780-422-2222 one of our Natural Burial Specialists will answer any questions that you may have.
Click here to learn more about Green Burial
Reception & Catering Centres
Connelly-McKinley offers a full selection of menus for everything from catering small gatherings to multi-course, seated meals at one of our locations, your home or another facility. We are dedicated to making your gathering special.
Click here for information on our Reception Centres
Sign Language Interpretation
Streaming the Funeral Live via the Internet
Being with loved ones at their time of need is essential. However, when circumstances do not permit everyone to be there in person, streaming can provide the next best option.
Click here for information on Streaming
Video Life Tributes
Connelly-McKinley can make a world-class, professionally produced DVD tribute to your loved one that draws from the power of imagery and music to create a personalized, enduring celebration of life. Pay tribute to your loved one’s impact and legacy by documenting their life story on DVD.
Click here for information on Life Tributes
Online Bookstore for Books on Grief and Healing
Crematorium
To make certain that proper cremation procedures are followed at all times, Connelly-McKinley Funeral Homes has established its own crematorium. This ensures that your loved one never leaves our care, giving us all peace of mind.
Click here for information on our Crematorium

We define green burial as a way of caring for the dead with minimal environmental impact that aids in the conservation of natural resources, reduction of carbon emissions, protection of worker health, and the restoration and/or preservation of habitat. Natural burials are carried out with ecological friendly materials including the clothing, shroud or casket that allows the return to earth to have the least amount of impact on the environment as possible.  

We recommend that if you are interested in a natural burial that you contact [Rose Hill Cemetery](https://stmichaels-rosehill-cemetery.com/) to ensure that this will meet your needs. They have restrictions and stipulations that may affect your choice.

As they are currently the only cemetery in Edmonton offering this type of burial, this remains your only choice.

They have allocated a section specifically for green burials

You can find more information about this [here](https://stmichaels-rosehill-cemetery.com/).

From the Funeral Home standpoint, we work with each family individually to help them choose the best services and products for their needs. As this is a very personal choice and each family has their own reasons and thought process as to what they would want, we want to ensure we meet those needs.

We have a shroud and selection environment friendly caskets that reflect the Green Burial Society of Canada and the requirements of the cemetery.

Should you wish more information and costs, please call [780-422-2222](tel:+17804222222) one of our Natural Burial Specialists will answer any questions that you may have.

# Connelly-McKinley Funeral Home in Edmonton, Alberta

## History of Connelly-McKinley Funeral Homes  

Serving Families in the Edmonton and Surrounding Areas Since 1908.  

## A Lot Has Changed in 100 Years – And So Have We  

For over a century, Connelly-McKinley has been a trusted name in funeral care, honouring traditions while evolving to meet the needs of today’s families. Established in 1908 by Joseph William Connelly, our funeral home was Alberta’s first incorporated funeral company. Through four generations, we have continued our commitment to compassionate service while embracing new and innovative ways to support families.  

### Our Story: A Legacy of Innovation & Care  

#### The Early Years

Joseph and his wife, Isabelle, immigrated to Alberta in 1904, settling in Riviere Qui Barre. In 1908, he opened the first Connelly-McKinley Funeral Home in downtown Edmonton, offering a place where grieving families could find comfort and support.

We were pioneers in funeral care:

*   **First funeral home west of the Great Lakes** to use an automobile for both a hearse and an ambulance.
*   **Among the first in Canada** to introduce pressure embalming.
*   Isabelle Connelly became **Alberta’s first female embalmer**.

#### Generations of Family Dedication

Joseph’s son, **William James**, joined the family business early, driving the firm’s ambulance at just 12 years old (with special police permission). The second and third generations carried on the legacy, expanding the funeral home and deepening its roots in Edmonton.

By the **1980s**, we had grown significantly, moving to modern facilities while maintaining the personal touch that families have relied on for over 100 years.

#### Connelly-McKinley Today

Now in our **fourth generation**, Connelly-McKinley remains a **family-owned** and **locally operated** funeral home, with **three locations** across the Edmonton area:

*   **Downtown Chapel** (since 1980)
*   **St. Albert Chapel** (since 1982)
*   **Edmonton South Chapel** (since 2001)

We also operate **two crematoriums**, including one at our Edmonton South property, which offers a serene setting for final farewells.

### Honouring Traditions While Embracing the Future

  
We understand that every family is different. That’s why we continue to **modernize our services**, including:

*   **Innovative & personalized services** tailored to your needs
*   **Renovated facilities** all 3 locations and reception centres. Two with gorgeous outside patios
*   **Multiple ways to connect –** Call, text, or chat online

We serve families across **Edmonton & surrounding areas**, ensuring **compassionate, professional, and personalized care** at every step.

Obituary information for Bryan Patrick Reistad
It is with sadness that we announce the passing of Bryan Reistad on July 14, 2026, at the age of 83.
Bryan took immense pride in providing a safe, stable, and comfortable home for his family. He was a hardworking and dedicated man whose strong work ethic defined much of his life. Bryan spent many years working for what was most recently known as Swift Meatpacking Plant as a city truck driver in Edmonton, Alberta. He devoted countless weekends to commuting between Edmonton and Duhamel, Alberta, where he farmed and managed rental properties in Camrose with the unwavering support of his wife, Doris.
Bryan came from a loving family that, while not financially secure, provided him with everything he needed. He spoke fondly of his parents and often acknowledged that they did the best they could with the resources they had. He never went without and was encouraged in all his pursuits, even when that meant using well-worn, hand-me-down equipment to play the sports he loved. An exceptional athlete, Bryan excelled in both hockey and baseball. As a young man, he was selected to attend an elite hockey training camp in Moose Jaw, Alberta—an impressive accomplishment for a small-town country boy who spent much of his youth playing hockey on outdoor ponds. His talent was evident to everyone who watched him play. Many would later remark, “Your dad could sure play hockey in his day.” Known as an outstanding defensive player, he was a goalie’s favorite, a coach’s first choice, and a respected competitor who caught the attention of many. Although he possessed the skill and ability to pursue the sport at higher levels, Bryan chose to leave the training camp on his own accord. A self-described homebody, he preferred the familiarity and comfort of home. Interestingly, his assigned defensive partner at camp later went on to play in the National Hockey League.
Bryan will be remembered by his wife, Doris; son, Scott (Sherry); daughter, Rhonda (Greg); granddaughter, Annalyn; grandson, Marcus; sisters, Joan and Margie; and a wealth of extended family, friends, and neighbours throughout Camrose, the surrounding areas, and Edmonton.
He was predeceased by his brother, Jack in 1983; his mother, Mary in 199; and his father, Ernie in 1997.
In accordance with Bryan’s wishes, cremation has taken place and there will be no public funeral service.
Arrangements entrusted to Connelly-McKinley St. Albert Funeral Home.

Obituary information for Lionel Napoleon Joseph Durand
It is with deep sadness that we announce the peaceful passing of Lionel Napoleon Joseph Durand on July 5, 2026, at the age of 84, at the Westlock Continuing Care Centre, with his beloved wife of 63 years, Joan, by his side.
Lionel was born on June 7, 1942, in Edmonton, Alberta, and was raised on the family farm between Mearns and Morinville. He later established his own livestock and crop farm near Sandy Lake. Farming was more than his livelihood—it reflected the values he lived by—hard work, perseverance, and dedication.
A tragic car accident in 1988 claimed the life of his daughter, Christine, and left Lionel with life-altering injuries. Although he could no longer farm as he once had, he remained determined to stay connected to the land. He sold his livestock, stopped crop farming, and eventually parted with most of the family’s farmland. On the remaining ten acres surrounding the family home, he established a bee farm. His daughter Catherine and her husband, Mat, joined him in growing the honey business, and when declining health no longer allowed Lionel to continue, they carried on the work he had begun.
In addition to farming, Lionel was a skilled welder whose resourceful and inventive nature gave him an extraordinary ability to build, repair, and create almost anything. If something needed fixing, Lionel could fix it. If a neighbour needed help, he was there without hesitation. Lionel was always willing to lend a hand. Whether family, neighbours, or complete strangers, he quietly helped wherever he could, never expecting anything in return.
Lionel was a man of quiet strength, deep faith, and unwavering devotion to his family. He met life’s challenges with resilience and grace. He found joy in simple pleasures—hunting, fishing, sharing stories, watching hockey, and spending time with those he loved. Above all else, Lionel’s greatest pride and joy was his family. He treasured every moment spent with his grandchildren, teaching them something new, sharing a laugh, or simply enjoying being together. Those memories will remain among the greatest gifts he left his grandchildren. Lionel’s kindness, gentle nature, and sense of humour will be fondly remembered by all who knew him.
Lionel is lovingly remembered by his devoted wife, Joan; his daughters, Amy (Robb) Melnyk and Catherine (Mat) Wedman; his cherished grandchildren, Kalin, Ty, Avery, Noah, and Sydney; his brothers, Raymond (Janice) and Pat (Patty); as well as numerous nieces, nephews, extended family members, and dear friends.
Lionel was predeceased by two daughters, Carol Lynne and Christine; his parents, Maurice and Cecile; and his brother, Laurent.
A Funeral Mass will be celebrated on Saturday, July 18, 2026, at 10:30 a.m. at St. Jean Baptiste Catholic Parish in Morinville, Alberta.
A private family interment will take place at a later date at St. Mark’s Cemetery in Sandy Lake.
The family wishes to express their heartfelt gratitude to the physicians, nurses, health-care aides, and staff of the Westlock Healthcare Centre, Smithfield Lodge, and the Westlock Continuing Care Centre. Your compassion, kindness, and dedication brought comfort not only to Lionel but also to our entire family, and your care will never be forgotten.
The family is also deeply grateful to Father Aureus of Westlock and Father Trini of Morinville for their spiritual guidance, compassion, and faithful support.
For those unable to attend in person, a livestream of the funeral service will be available at: https://www.localonline.live/stjbp
May he rest in the peace of Christ.
“Well done, good and faithful servant.”
Matthew 25:23
Arrangements entrusted to Connelly-McKinley St. Albert Funeral Home
