# Connelly-McKinley Funeral Home in E...

## Understanding Grief

### Grief: General  

These thoughtful articles provide guidance and direction for anyone touched by grief.  

### Helping Yourself with Grief  

Someone you love has died. You are now faced with the difficult, but important, need to mourn. Mourning is the open expression of your thoughts and feelings regarding the death and the person who died. It is an essential part of healing. The following articles provide many practical suggestions to help you move toward healing in your unique grief journey.  

### Helping Others with Grief  

One thing that many people ask us is “What do you write in a sympathy card?”  

##### What to Write in a Sympathy Card  

*   Write down a memory or special quality you loved about the person that died.
*   Share a way that they’ve changed your life or perhaps a way in which you plan to remember and honor them.  
    
*   Be truthful. If this is hard for you to write, say that. If you don’t know what to say but you just love them, say that. You can’t mess that up and your honesty will be treasured.  
    

Just know that reaching out in this way is significant and meaningful. It doesn’t need to be elaborate or flowery. Sincere and from the heart – there’s nothing more meaningful than that.  

##### What not to send or say in your card.  

*   Do not use the words “at least” ANYWHERE in your card.  
    
*   Do not make promises you cannot keep.  
    
*   If you do not intend to reach out to them, don’t say you are “here” for them. Grieving people have a well-developed radar for faux-support and that phrase is just that. Proactively reach out again and again with kind, helpful gestures like meals or checking-in with a phone call or text.  
    
*   Don’t say, “I’m sorry for your loss.” They have heard this phrase on repeat and it holds nothing of substance.  
    

A friend has experienced the death of someone loved. How can you help? The following articles provide many practical suggestions for helping others with grief:

### For and About Grieving Children and Teenagers  

Children and teenagers have special needs following the death of a friend or family member. The following articles provide wonderful insight in helping children and teens understand and express their grief.

### Funerals, Memorials, Cremation and Related Topics  

The days following the death of a loved one can be filled with sadness and confusion. The following articles can help you understand the importance of the rituals surrounding death.

Designing Your Ceremony | Connelly-McKinley Funeral Home ...
We believe in creating healing and meaningful ceremonies that tell the unique story of each person we serve.
We offer both traditional and modern ceremony options and actively look for ways to personalize and tailor your ceremony to your family and community’s needs.
Our funeral arrangers listen closely to your story and situation to help you find the ceremony that best honors your loved one. They will also help you select special photographs and find ways to incorporate significant memories, favorite items, and symbolic elements into the ceremony.
We know it can be difficult trying to think of everything when your heart is broken and that is why we will be there with you every step of the way, guiding you, and ensuring that your loved one has the perfect goodbye, whatever type of ceremony you decide on.
Many families these days prefer to plan a funeral or memorial service focused on remembering the deceased as he or she was in life, a service focused on the deceased’s body/remains, or a combination of both. Therefore, you should imagine and plan the funeral or memorial service that you and/or the person who died consider the most meaningful way to say goodbye—something that captures the unique qualities of the deceased; reflects his or her and/or your personal, religious or spiritual beliefs; and provides a memorable, meaningful opportunity for mourners to express their grief while comforting and supporting each other.
You should also consider the following when envisioning your funeral or memorial service to personalize it, as applicable:
Officiant(s) who will lead the service, such as a clergy member, celebrant, funeral director, etc.
Readings, such as poems, prayers, religious or secular passages, etc., and who will deliver them
Eulogist(s), who will write and deliver a eulogy about the deceased
Music, whether contemporary, religious hymns or both
Food/beverages, whether professionally catered, provided “potluck” by attendees, or arranged by the funeral home or provider
Pallbearers, if the final disposition involves a graveside service
Streaming the funeral, or making a recording of the service available later
Personal touches, such as a memory board, memorial video, personal memorabilia, etc.
Think of all the things in life that made them special

How to Prepare a Eulogy
Helping Create a Meaningful Eulogy
by Alan D. Wolfelt, Ph.D.
Planning a meaningful, personalized funeral is one of the most important tasks you will ever undertake. Think of the funeral as a gift to the person who died. It is your chance to think about and express the value of the life that was lived.
When personalized, the eulogy (pronounced EWE-luh-jee) is perhaps the most memorable and healing element of the funeral ceremony. This article will help you choose the right person to give the eulogy as well as offer tips for writing and presenting the eulogy.
What is the eulogy?
Also called the remembrance, the eulogy is the speech or presentation during the funeral ceremony that talks about the life and character of the person who died. The eulogy acknowledges the unique life of the person who died and affirms the significance of that life for all who shared in it. The eulogy typically lasts 15-20 minutes, although longer presentations may also be appropriate.
Who presents the eulogy?
The eulogy can be delivered by a clergyperson, a family member or a friend of the person who died. Instead of a traditional eulogy delivered by one person, you may choose to ask several people to speak and share their memories. There is also a growing trend toward having people attending the funeral stand up and share a memory of the person who died. This works well, especially at smaller or less formal gatherings.
What if the person presenting the eulogy didn’t really know the person who died?
Keep in mind that the eulogy doesn’t have to be delivered by the person leading the service. Only if your clergy person or another person facilitating the ceremony knows your family well and can speak personally about the person who died is this appropriate. If the clergyperson didn’t know the person who died, it’s much more meaningful to have a family member or friend give the eulogy. Or you might ask several people to speak.
If your family would feel comforted by a religious sermon during the ceremony, ask a clergyperson to give one. Just be sure to have someone else (or several people) deliver a personalized eulogy in addition to the sermon.
If you must choose someone who didn’t know the person who died well, make an effort to share with him or her anecdotes and memories that are important to you. Ask yourself, “What stands out to me about this person’s life?” “What are some special memories I’d like to share?” “What were some times I felt particularly close to this person?” “What were some admirable qualities about this person?”
What should be said during the eulogy?
We have already emphasized that the best eulogies are personalized. They include memories and anecdotes of the person’s life. They also try to capture personality. If the person who died was kind, the eulogy would give examples of this kindness. If the person who died had a good sense of humor, the eulogy might relate funny stories or expressions.
The eulogy doesn’t have to cover every aspect of the person’s life, however. In fact, often the best eulogies are those that focus on the eulogy-giver’s personal thoughts and memories. Do try to acknowledge those who were closest to the person who died as well as important achievements in the person’s life, but don’t feel obligated to create an exhaustive biography.
Also keep in mind that the word eulogy comes from the Greek eulogia, meaning praise or blessing. This is the time to give thanks for a person’s life and to honor his or her memory. This is not the time to bring up painful or difficult memories but to emphasize the good we can find in all people.
Some tips for eulogy-givers Writing and delivering a eulogy is a loving, important gesture that merits your time and attention. Though the task may seem daunting right now, you’ll find that once you start jotting down ideas, your eulogy will come together naturally. Afterwards, many who attend the funeral will thank you for your contribution, and your eulogy will be cherished always by the family and friends of the person who died.
Here are some ideas to get you started.
Be brave. The thought of writing a speech and presenting it in public makes many people anxious. Set aside your fears for now. You can do this. Focus on the person who died and the gift you will be giving to all who knew and loved him or her.
Think. Before you start writing, go for a long walk or drive and think about the life of the person who died. This will help you collect your thoughts and focus on writing the eulogy.
Brainstorm. Spend half an hour (longer if you want) writing down all the thoughts, ideas and memories that come to you.
Ask others to share memories. A good way to include others in the ceremony is to ask them to share thoughts and memories, which you can then incorporate into the eulogy.
Look at photos. Flipping through photo albums may remind you of important qualities and memories of the person who died.
Write a draft. Once you’ve brainstormed and collected memories, it’s time to write the first draft. Go somewhere quiet and write it all in one sitting, start to finish. Don’t worry about getting it perfect for now-just get it down on paper.
Let it sit. If time allows, let your eulogy draft sit for a few hours or a day before revising.
Get a second opinion. Have someone else-preferably someone who was close to the person who died-read over your draft at this point. This person can make revision suggestions and help you avoid inadvertently saying something that might offend others.
Polish. Read over your first draft. Look for awkward phrases or stiff wording. Improve the transitions from paragraph to paragraph or thought to thought. Find adjectives and verbs that really capture the essence of the person who died.
Present your eulogy with love. Now you need to present your eulogy. You may feel nervous, but if you can keep your focus on the person who died instead of your own fears, you’ll loosen up. If you break down as you’re talking, that’s OK. Everyone will understand. Just stop for a few seconds, collect yourself and continue.
Speak up. It’s very important that you speak clearly and loudly so that everyone can hear you.
A Final Word
Again, the word eulogy means “praise or blessing.” Your willingness to help create a personalized, meaningful eulogy is, in fact, a very real blessing.

Obituary information for Raymond Frank Dennis
Raymond Frank Dennis ("Ray"), 67, passed away peacefully at Sturgeon Community Hospital on July 13, 2026. Born in Brandon, Manitoba, on August 28, 1958, Ray resided in St. Albert, Alberta, with his family at their beautiful home surrounded by the vibrant garden he lovingly created and maintained. Both during his career as a successful commercial banker and in retirement, Ray was known for his commitment to hard work, exceptional judgment, and kindness.
Ray was a devoted husband to Linda and an inspirational father to his two children: Wendy and Rodney. He is survived by his brothers, David (Carole) and Larry (Chris), and his sister, Carol. He also leaves behind his beloved sisters-in-law and brothers-in-law--Sandra (Kim), Nancy (Stephen), and Sharon (Mark)--and his many nieces, nephews, and dear friends.
Around his family, Ray was known to be an incredible home chef, a dependable driver, a talented artist, a lover of games and stories, a passionate golfer, a skilled gardener, and a man that loved to laugh. He especially enjoyed making unique and delicious meals in the kitchen and gathering his wife and kids in the living room to eat while they watched a great movie or show together. In the summer, Ray would take his family on fun road trips and, in the winter, he would celebrate Christmas and Thanksgiving with lovely celebratory traditions involving food, movies, and more than a few Hot Wheels cars and cookies.
Ray's legacy lives on through the people who knew and loved him. His exceptional example as a father and husband, humour, warmth, and courage in the face of lifelong health challenges have left an unforgettable mark on the hearts of his loved ones. Following his wishes, cremation took place after his passing.
Ray was predeceased by his parents: Rodney and Dorothy.
A memorial celebrating Ray's life will be held in Winnipeg. Details will be announced later.

To avoid any mistakes, you should print rather than write the draft out by hand. If you are typing the obituary, please provide Connelly-McKinley with a hard copy as well an emailed copy or a saved copy on a USB.
What is an Obituary?
An obituary is often the first thing people read in the newspaper each day – and, for many, it will likely be the last thing written about their lives. More than merely a “goodbye” to the deceased, it is a farewell detailing their life in chronological order. An obituary also serves as notification that an individual has passed away and provides information on any services that are scheduled to take place. Since the cost of running an obituary generally varies by length, once you have an idea of what you want to publish, we will submit it and get a cost for you. Should you wish to make any changes to reduce costs, we can do so at that time and resubmit.
People often save obituaries as remembrances of someone they loved, so make sure that the final product is something worthy of a scrapbook and – more importantly – worthy of your loved one’s memory.
What Should Be Included?
Standard pieces of information to include are the announcement, biographical, scheduled services and memorials.
Announcement
A little preparation before the funeral arrangement conference can help make the necessary decisions easier and less stressful for the family.
Biographical Information
Recount, in a concise manner, the significant events in the life of the deceased. This may include the schools he or she attended and any degrees attained as well as their vocations or interests.
Survivors and Predeceased Information
It is customary to list family members who have survived the deceased, as well as immediate family members who predeceased him or her, including:
Spouse/partner, children and/or stepchildren (with their spouses’/partners’ names also noted in brackets, if applicable)
Grandchildren
Parents
Siblings
Half and step siblings
Surviving in-laws
These surviving relatives should be listed by name. Other relatives need not be mentioned by name but may be referenced in terms of their relationship to the deceased: for example, the obituary may say that the deceased leaves behind five grandchildren, seven nieces, etc.
Scheduled Services
Provide details of the scheduled services, including the time, date and address. These may include the funeral, visitations, burial and memorial service as applicable. We do not recommend adding that there will be a reception. Sometimes unwanted guests may attend only for lunch and may not be part of the service.
Memorials
Give the name and mailing address of a foundation or society to which you wish to direct any memorial donations made in honour of your loved one. The decision as to which foundation or society to support may be based upon interests or values that your loved one expressed during life or related to a medical condition which he or she had.
We recommend you refrain from using the phrase “in lieu of flowers” when requesting memorial donations. Instead, start the final paragraph of the obituary with the words “Memorial donations may be made to….”

All information included in the obituary should be verified with another family member. Have them assist you in confirming the dates, those who should be mentioned, correct spelling of names and the details of the scheduled funeral service.
Take into consideration when and in which newspapers (both local and out of town) you wish your funeral director to publish the obituary.
Suggested wording:
“It is with great sadness that the family of (deceased name) announce (his/her) passing….”
“(Deceased name) will be sadly missed by ….”
“Fondly remembered by….”
“Forever remembered by….”
“Lovingly remembered by….”
“Wife/husband and best friend of (number) years….”
“A Celebration of (deceased’s name) life will be held on….”

LAST NAME, first name middle name (Nee:____)
Date of Birth – Date of Death
Ideas for the Beginning Paragraph
On (day, date), (full name of deceased) of (city of residence) passed away at the age of ____ years.
The family of (full name of deceased) of (city of residence) is saddened to announce his/her passing on (day, date) at the age of _____ years.
Our beloved mother, grandmother, great grandmother, sister, aunt and friend,
(full name of deceased) passed away with her family by her side on (day, date) at the age of ____ years.
Following a lengthy battle with __________, (full name of deceased) of (city of residence) passed away on (day, date) at the age of ____ years.
It is with deep sorrow and much love that we mourn the passing of _______________, of (city of residence) on (day, Date), at the age of _____ years.
It is with profound sadness that the family of _____________ announce his/her peaceful passing on (day, date) at the age of ____ years.
Peacefully and surrounded by his/her family, mom/dad passed away on (day, date) at the age of ______ years.
Second Paragraph
Always list family members in the following manner: spouse, children in birth order, grandchildren, great grandchildren, brothers, sisters, other relatives and friends. Some people will state the number of grandchildren instead of listing them all. For example: 15 grandchildren; 23 great-grandchildren. 
He/She will be lovingly remembered by his/her husband of _____ years, Jim; children: John (wife’s name) and Doris (husband’s name); grandchildren: _________, ____________, ____________, and ___________; brother, Michael (wife’s name) last name; sister-in-law, Diane last name; as well as numerous relatives and friends.
She will also be dearly missed by her friends at the _____________
(name of group or location example: Seniors Center)

She was predeceased by her loving husband of ____ years, (name); son, (name); brother, (name); and her parents: (name and name).

Some families like to tell a bit of story about where they were born, the person’s accomplishments, when they moved into the area, what groups they were involved in, their hobbies, and any military history.

A Funeral Mass (Funeral Service, Memorial Service, Celebration of Life, etc) will be held at (time), on (day, date), at _________________________, (full address).
A Memorial Service will be held at a later date.
A Celebration of Life will be held at a later date.
A private service will be held at the family’s request.
At (name of deceased)‘s request, no service will be held.

The family wishes to send a special thank you to the staff at the ____________ (name of hospital or seniors center) for their care and compassion.

Obituary information for Joyce Anne Hendrickson
To view Joyce's memorial slideshow, please click here.
Joyce passed away peacefully on July 12, 2026, at the age of 87, leaving behind a legacy of kindness, resilience, curiosity, and unwavering friendship.
She was a teacher, counsellor, adventurer, storyteller, and lifelong learner.
Raised on a small farm on the Alberta prairie, Joyce carried with her the values of hard work, self-reliance, and compassion throughout her life. After the loss of her sister, Mary, she embarked on a nine-month solo journey around the world, an adventure that shaped her lifelong love of learning, travel, and embracing new perspectives.
Whether through her work, her travels, or her friendships, Joyce met people where they were, leaving a lasting impact on the many people fortunate enough to have crossed her path.
Joyce loved bringing people together. Her home was a place where people felt welcome, where there was always room for one more person, one more story, or one more moment of togetherness. She will be remembered for her generous spirit, gift for storytelling, and ability to make everyone feel they belonged.
Joyce was predeceased by her parents; her beloved husband, Willi; her siblings, Mary and Gordon; her brothers-in-law, Phil and Corey; and her sisters-in-law, Grace and Sonja.
She is lovingly remembered by her siblings, Doris and Jim; her in-laws, Lorraine, Mike, and Trudi; along with many nieces and nephews, their children and grandchildren, her cherished friends, former students, colleagues, and all whose lives were touched by her kindness.
Her greatest legacy lives on in the curiosity she inspired, the friendships she nurtured, and the countless lives she quietly changed.
A celebration of Joyce's life will be held in the fall. Details will be shared at a later date.
In lieu of flowers, donations may be made to the Hendrickson Memorial Endowment at Augustana (University of Alberta) or the Canadian Lutheran World Relief organization.

Carol Waselenchuk, age 69, of Edmonton, Alberta, passed away peacefully on July 14, 2026, after a long, courageous battle with frontotemporal dementia.
Born on January 22, 1957, in Edmonton, Alberta, to the late Peter and Georgina Kosik, Carol was a loving and caring presence to her extended family. She had a generous heart and was always ready to lend a hand, offer comfort, or simply sit and listen. Her warmth made everyone feel welcomed and supported, and she never hesitated to step in when someone needed her.
Above all, Carol was a devoted mother. She raised three children— Mae, Ashley, and Derek —with patience, warmth, and quiet strength. Her greatest joy multiplied when she became "Grandma" to her four grandchildren— Xavier, Zellah, Opal, and Orion, the children of her daughter, Mae. She beamed at their milestones, and her lap was always their favorite place to land. She especially treasured the outings she shared with Mae and the children—creating memories that will be cherished forever.
She found happiness in life's simple pleasures. She loved taking trips to the mountains, Hawaii, and Mexico with her children. The beach was her favorite place to be—the sand, the waves, and the sun brought her the peace she cherished most. At home, she found peace in cleaning and tidying, turning her house into a haven for everyone who walked through the door. She also had a deep love for her three dogs, who brought her endless companionship and joy. And she had a special, whimsical fondness for squirrels—she'd pause at the window, smile, and point out their antics, finding pure delight in their busy little lives.
She made it a point to honor life's milestones—birthdays, anniversaries, and everyday moments alike. She was a patient listener and a steady source of comfort, always offering kindness without expecting anything in return. Even as dementia slowly took pieces of her memory, her gentle heart never wavered—she still lit up at a familiar voice or a grandchild's hand in hers.
She was reunited with those who went before her, and leaves behind a family who will carry her memory forever. She leaves behind her children, grandchildren, and a wide circle of extended family and friends who will miss her radiant spirit.
A Celebration of her Life will be held at 10:00 a.m. on July 23, 2026, at Connelly-McKinley Downtown Funeral Home, 10011 114 Street.
In lieu of flowers, the family suggests donations to Alzheimer Society of Alberta and Northwest Territories, or simply take a moment to watch a squirrel chase its tail—and think of her smiling.
Arrangements entrusted to Connelly-McKinley Downtown Funeral Home.

At Connelly-McKinley, we believe that the deaf and hard of hearing must have access to the communication mode that best facilitates and enhances their full participation in the funeral planning process. It is their right to have such support made available to them.
A Sign Language Interpreter is a person who is fluent in both English and ASL or English and another form of Signed Language. This person acts as a communication link between the hearing and the deaf or hard of hearing by interpreting from one language into the other.
Whether you require an interpreter during the planning phases of the funeral, during the funeral service itself, or even during the after-care, phase we will find one for you.Please contact us to make your ASL, Signed English, Oral or Sign Assist interpreting arrangements. Deaf interpreters are also available for those who require alternative communication services.
Note: Team interpreting (i.e., two or more Interpreters working co-operatively) may sometimes be required depending on the length of the assignment, the number of people who need interpretation and/or the complexity of the task. It is important to consult with the interpreter(s) when determining whether more than one interpreter is necessary.

Obituary information for Judith Lynn Pettit
Following a courageous battle with cancer, our beloved wife, daughter, sister, aunt, and friend, Judith Lynn Pettit (Judy), passed away peacefully on July 17, 2026, at the age of 58.
Judy will be forever loved and deeply missed by her devoted husband of 20 years, Joseph "Joe" Pettit. She will also be lovingly remembered by her father, Pius Sieben; her sister, Joanne Hills, brother-in-law, Thane Hills; and her nieces, Jayleen Hills and Aubree Hills, whom she adored. Judy will also be fondly remembered by her extended family, including her mother-in-law, Linda Pettit; her sister-in-law, Suzanne Pettit Faber; her brother-in-law, Jason Faber; and her nephew, Noah Faber.
Judy was predeceased by her mother, Carol Sieben, on November 13, 2008, and her father-in-law, Elwood Pettit, on July 16, 2025.
Judy loved the life she and Joe built together on their farm near Hay Lakes. She took great pride in preparing quick and hearty meals during the busy harvest season, ensuring everyone was well fed after long days in the field. Outside of farming, Judy and Joe shared a love of adventure and made countless memories traveling and camping. Judy loved gathering around a campfire with her family and enjoying a good game of cards.
When Judy wasn't traveling, she could often be found with a good book in hand, working on a scrapbook, cheering on the Edmonton Oilers, or catching up on her favorite soap opera, The Young and the Restless. She embraced life's simple pleasures and treasured every moment spent with family and friends.
A Celebration of Judy's Life will be held on Wednesday, July 29, 2026, at 10:00 a.m. at Connelly-McKinley Funeral Home, 9 Muir Drive, St. Albert, Alberta. A reception with light refreshments will follow the service.
In lieu of flowers, memorial donations may be made in Judy's memory to the Alberta Cancer Foundation.
The family extends their heartfelt gratitude to the compassionate staff of Units 31 and 40 at the Cross Cancer Institute for the exceptional care, kindness, and support they provided to Judy and her family throughout her journey.

Connelly-McKinley Funeral Home in Edmonton, Alberta
Executor Duties
A Guide for Executors

Losing a loved one is an emotional and overwhelming experience, and if you have been named as their executor, you may be wondering where to begin. This guide is designed to help you navigate the legal and financial responsibilities that come with settling an estate in Alberta. Below, you will find a detailed step-by-step process outlining everything from immediate notifications to the final distribution of assets.
Step 1: Immediate Notifications After Death
Obtain Proof of Death – The funeral home will provide a Funeral Director’s Statement of Death, but you may also need a Death Certificate from Vital Statistics.
Notify Close Family and Friends – Ensure immediate family members and key contacts are informed.
Secure the Deceased’s Home & Assets – Lock the residence, secure valuables, and check for any urgent property concerns (e.g., perishable items, pet care).
Redirect Mail – Contact Canada Post to forward mail to the executor’s address.
Cancel or Transfer Utilities & Subscriptions – Contact phone, internet, cable, and other service providers as needed.
Step 2: Notify Government Agencies & Pension Providers
Service Canada – Notify of the death and cancel applicable benefits.
Canada Pension Plan (CPP) – Notify of the death and apply for the CPP Death Benefit and Survivors Benefit if applicable.
Old Age Security (OAS) – Notify to stop payments.
Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – Notify the CRA to stop benefit payments and discuss tax obligations.
RCMP – Firearms License – Notify to cancel any firearm license held by the deceased.
Assured Income for the Severely Handicapped (AISH) – Notify to stop benefits.
Social Insurance Number (SIN) Cancellation – Inform Service Canada to cancel the deceased’s SIN.
Alberta Seniors Benefits – Contact to cancel provincial senior benefits.
Workers’ Compensation Board (WCB) – Notify WCB of the death.
Alberta Health Care – Return the deceased’s Alberta Health Care Card.
Alberta Blue Cross – Notify to cancel any health coverage.
Alberta Motor Vehicles Division – Notify to update or cancel vehicle registrations and licenses.
Equifax Canada & TransUnion Canada – Notify to prevent identity theft.
Passport Canada – Notify to cancel the deceased’s passport.
Certified Declaration of Legal Marriage – Obtain this document if needed for estate settlement.
Certified Declaration of Common-law Union – Obtain this document if required for benefits or legal matters.
Certified Canada Post Address Change Letter – Request mail forwarding and official notifications.
Certified Declaration for Joint Tenant Land Titles Office – Notify for property title updates.
Step 3: Legal & Financial Responsibilities
Locate the Will & Estate Documents – Determine if a legal Will exists and obtain a copy.
Meet with a Lawyer (if necessary) – Review the Will and discuss probate requirements.
Apply for Probate (if required) – If the deceased owned real estate or had significant assets, probate may be necessary.
Notify Financial Institutions – Contact banks, credit unions, and investment firms to freeze accounts and obtain estate details.
Cancel or Transfer Credit Cards & Loans – Notify creditors and pay outstanding debts as required.
Contact Life Insurance Companies – File claims for any life insurance policies.
Set Up an Estate Bank Account – To manage estate funds, pay bills, and distribute assets.
Determine & Pay Outstanding Debts – Ensure all bills, mortgages, or loans are settled from estate funds.
Step 4: Filing Tax Returns
File the Final Tax Return – A final personal tax return must be filed for the deceased.
Request a Clearance Certificate from CRA – This confirms that all taxes have been paid before distributing the estate.
File an Estate Tax Return (if applicable) – If the estate generates income, an additional tax return may be required.
Step 5: Distribute the Estate
Follow the Will’s Instructions – Ensure assets are distributed according to the Will.
Transfer Property Titles & Vehicles – Contact Alberta Land Titles and Service Alberta for necessary ownership changes.
Close Remaining Accounts – Once all funds are distributed, close the estate bank account.
Provide Final Accounting to Beneficiaries – Share a detailed financial summary of how the estate was settled.
Obtain Executor Release & Discharge – Confirm that all duties have been completed and obtain legal confirmation if needed.
Final Thoughts
Serving as an executor is a great responsibility, but with careful planning and the right resources, you can ensure your loved one’s estate is handled properly. If you require assistance, legal and financial professionals can guide you through the process. If you have questions about estate settlement, our team at Connelly-McKinley is here to support you every step of the way.

Obituary information for Bob Pattison
Bob's Celebration of Life will be livestreamed. To view the service, please click this LINK HERE.
It is with heavy hearts that we announce the passing of Bob Pattison, on July 16, 2026 in Edmonton, Alberta after a brief stay at the Mazankowski Alberta Heart Institute.
Bob was born on May 19, 1952 in Stettler, Alberta. Soon after he was born the family moved to Drayton Valley where he was raised. Bob began working for Northwestern Utilities Ltd. (NUL) where he earned his Gasfitter and Power Engineering tickets. NUL provided a variety of seasonal work while he attended the University of Alberta, completing his Bachelor of Education Degree. He met the love of his life, Cathy, in July 1976 and they were married a year later. Looking to provide a bright future for their intended family, Bob and Cathy moved to Red Deer in 1978 where they began raising their two children. Bob continued with NUL as a serviceman until 1989 when he moved to Sherwood Park, becoming the foreman at the meter shop. He retired from ATCO Gas as a Manager in Customer Service in 2013.
Bob began volunteering as a trainer/equipment manager for Adam's minor hockey team and he continued with a variety of elite hockey, lacrosse, and ball hockey teams that took him to championship tournaments across Canada and Europe. He put his trainer's bag away during the 2016/17 season and was honored by the Sherwood Park Kings Athletic Club with recognition of his long-term commitment to the organization.
In his retirement, Bob kept going to the rink, securing his spot at the end boards, coffee in hand, shooting the breeze with whomever would stop by. Bob's community was large and his impact even greater. He enjoyed sharing stories and his quick wit with his cherished friends and family. One of his favorite things in the last few years was being 'Grandpa Bob', cheering on his grandkids at their many activities.
Bob leaves to remember him, his loving wife of 49 years, Cathy; children, Carrie and Adam (Ashley); three grandchildren, Bennett, Miles, and Briar; siblings David (Sharon) Pattison, Carol Furber (Guy) Runchie, Garry (Janet) Pattison, and Lorraine (Ken) Harrynuck; sisters-in-law Lynne (John) Wilson, Penny Anderson, Karen (Dave) Finlay, and Jackie (Murray) Orr; numerous nieces, nephews, extended family, and friends. He was predeceased by his brother, Don; his parents and in-laws.
Bob was diagnosed with Type 1 Diabetes as a young teen and he always took a keen interest in learning about the latest treatments and research. He was an insulin pump user for 40 years and was always eager to share his knowledge and experience with others. In lieu of flowers, donations can be made to Breakthrough T1D to support ongoing diabetes research. 
A heartwarming Celebration of Bob's Life will be held at 1:00 p.m. on Friday, August 7, 2026 in the Event Centre at Northeast River Valley Park - 903, 153 Ave NE, Edmonton Alberta.

It is with heavy hearts that we announce the passing of Bob Pattison, on July 16, 2026 in Edmonton, Alberta after a brief stay at the Mazankowski Alberta Heart Institute.

Bob was born on May 19, 1952 in Stettler, Alberta. Soon after he was born the family moved to Drayton Valley where he was raised. Bob began working for Northwestern Utilities Ltd. (NUL) where he earned his Gasfitter and Power Engineering tickets. NUL provided a variety of seasonal work while he attended the University of Alberta, completing his Bachelor of Education Degree. He met the love of his life, Cathy, in July 1976 and they were married a year later. Looking to provide a bright future for their intended family, Bob and Cathy moved to Red Deer in 1978 where they began raising their two children. Bob continued with NUL as a serviceman until 1989 when he moved to Sherwood Park, becoming the foreman at the meter shop. He retired from ATCO Gas as a Manager in Customer Service in 2013.

Bob began volunteering as a trainer/equipment manager for Adam's minor hockey team and he continued with a variety of elite hockey, lacrosse, and ball hockey teams that took him to championship tournaments across Canada and Europe. He put his trainer's bag away during the 2016/17 season and was honored by the Sherwood Park Kings Athletic Club with recognition of his long-term commitment to the organization.

In his retirement, Bob kept going to the rink, securing his spot at the end boards, coffee in hand, shooting the breeze with whomever would stop by. Bob's community was large and his impact even greater. He enjoyed sharing stories and his quick wit with his cherished friends and family. One of his favorite things in the last few years was being 'Grandpa Bob', cheering on his grandkids at their many activities.

Bob leaves to remember him, his loving wife of 49 years, Cathy; children, Carrie and Adam (Ashley); three grandchildren, Bennett, Miles, and Briar; siblings David (Sharon) Pattison, Carol Furber (Guy) Runchie, Garry (Janet) Pattison, and Lorraine (Ken) Harrynuck; sisters-in-law Lynne (John) Wilson, Penny Anderson, Karen (Dave) Finlay, and Jackie (Murray) Orr; numerous nieces, nephews, extended family, and friends. He was predeceased by his brother, Don; his parents and in-laws.

Bob was diagnosed with Type 1 Diabetes as a young teen and he always took a keen interest in learning about the latest treatments and research. He was an insulin pump user for 40 years and was always eager to share his knowledge and experience with others. In lieu of flowers, donations can be made to [Breakthrough T1D](https://breakthrought1d.akaraisin.com/ui/InMemory26/p/8e533b59bb574c91a21cb7695100b4b5) to support ongoing diabetes research. 

A heartwarming Celebration of Bob's Life will be held at 1:00 p.m. on Friday, August 7, 2026 in the Event Centre at Northeast River Valley Park - 903, 153 Ave NE, Edmonton Alberta.

Obituary information for Hans "John" Laan
Johannes Pieter Laan — Husband, Father, Grandpa, Big Heart, Quiet Grace
A devoted husband, father, and grandfather, Hans passed away peacefully, leaving behind a family who adored him and a community richer for having known him.
Hans, as he was known to most, was a man of remarkable drive and character. He immigrated to Canada with modest means and an unwavering determination to build a life worth being proud of. Those early years in Canada were spent doing honest, hard work — the kind that shapes a man and sets the course for a life well built.
Through hard work, sharp instincts, and a refusal to cut corners, Hans built and ran a highly successful truck rental and leasing company. He was the kind of businessman people respected — fair, capable, and someone who stood behind what he said. He worked not for recognition, but because taking care of the people he loved was simply what he did.
He was a deeply present father who raised his children with love and intention, and made sure his family saw the world — vacations were a priority, and the memories made on those trips lasted a lifetime. For his granddaughters Marley and Esme, he reserved a love unlike anything else. He would have moved mountains for those two girls, and accepted nothing but the best for them.
Hans gave just as much to his community. He volunteered his time at Edmonton Christian School and contributed countless hours to Trinity Christian Reformed Church, where his faith and his work ethic showed up in equal measure. He was also known to take on the role of Sinterklaas each Christmas — a proud nod to his Dutch roots and a joy to everyone who witnessed it. Hans never waited to be asked. Whether it was his time, his money, or simply showing up when it mattered, he gave freely and without expectation.
A passionate traveller, Hans saw much of the world and brought genuine curiosity and enthusiasm to wherever he landed. Few places on the map were left unexplored by Hans and Carol, and they were all the richer for it. He had a lifelong passion for cars and the kind of enthusiasm for them that was, frankly, contagious. He made it to the water once a year for fishing with his friend George — a trip he looked forward to every time.
He showed his love through the doing, the providing, and the being there — and those who were lucky enough to be in his orbit felt it deeply. He will be remembered as the kind of man you didn't fully appreciate until you stopped to think about how many small, quiet ways he showed up for you. And then you couldn't stop thinking about it.
Hans is survived by his wife of 54 years, Carol; his daughter, Julie and son-in-law, Michael; his son, James and daughter-in-law, Brittney; his granddaughters, Marley, age 6, and Esme, age 5, who brought him a joy unlike anything else; his six brothers and sisters and their families in Holland, who remain a cherished part of the family he came from; and Carol's brothers and sisters and their families.
He was predeceased by his mother, Leentje Laan; his father, Roelof Wijnand Laan; his brother, Ruud; his brother-in-law, Jan Ten Heggeler; and his sister, Ineke Russel and her husband, Jack Russel.
He leaves behind a family who adored him, and a quiet that's going to take some getting used to.
The family would like to extend their heartfelt gratitude to Nurse Heather and the entire ICU team at Misericordia Hospital for the exceptional care and compassion shown to Hans during his final days.
The Funeral Service will take place at Trinity Christian Reformed Church (13427-57 Street, Edmonton, AB) on Saturday, July 25, 2026 at 1:00 PM MDT.
The service will also be livestreamed
All are welcome to join remotely via the link below.
Please click here to watch the livestream.
Arrangements entrusted to Connelly-McKinley Downtown Funeral Home.

Therefore, we cannot be responsible for the protection and privacy of any information which you provide whilst visiting such sites and such sites are not governed by this privacy statement. ###### Controlling your personal information  

You may choose to restrict the collection or use of your personal information in the following ways:  

*   Whenever you are asked to fill in a form on the website, look for the box that you can click to indicate that you do not want the information to be used by anybody for direct marketing purposes.
*   If you have previously agreed to us using your personal information for direct marketing purposes, you may change your mind at any time by writing to or emailing us at [info@serenity.ca](mailto:info@serenity.ca).

  
We will not sell, distribute or lease your personal information to third parties unless we have your permission or are required by law to do so. We may use your personal information to send you promotional information about third parties which we think you may find interesting if you tell us that you wish this to happen.

*   On _date_, _year_ Mr. name _of city/town/prov_, formerly of _city/town/prov_, passed away at the age of _age_ years.
*   It is with heavy hearts that we announce the passing of _name_ on _date_, _year_ at the age of _age_.

  
**Survived by:**

*   _Name_ is survived by ...
*   _Name_ is lovingly remembered by ...
*   His memory will be cherished by ...

**Predeceased by:**

*   He/She was predeceased by ...

  
**May include names of:** _parents, spouse (of how many years married,) name (nee maiden name of wife), children (spouse(s}}, sihlings, grandchildren, great-grandchildren, nieces and nephews, in-lows, special friends, pets._ **May wish to include year of death of parents, spouse, children.**   

  
**Service Information:**

Will there be a _public viewing/visitation?_  
What type of service? _Mass of Christian Burial, Funeral Liturgy, Funeral Service, Celebration of Life, Memorial Service?_ 

*   A _visitation_ will be held at _location(name and address) of funeral home/church/halI_ on _date_ from _time_ to _time_. A _type of service_ will take place on _date_ at _time_ at _location_ with name of _pastor/celebrant_ officiating.

*   The family would like to extend a special thank you to the wonderful staff at _name of facility/unit #_ who cared so much for _name of deceased_ during his/her time there.

  
**Memorial Donations:**

*   Memorial donations in name of deceased's honour may be made directly to name of
*   charity/organization/church.
*   In lieu of flowers, donations in name of deceased's honour may be made directly to name of

About Our Funeral Homes | Serenity Funeral Service
We have been serving our area community for many years. We’re thankful to be an important part of this community and will continue our longstanding legacy of helping families honor their loved ones.
Today, there is no such thing as a general “funeral service”. People are choosing to plan ceremonies or tributes that are more reflective of the person and fit the lifestyle of the family. Created in 1999 by a group of like-minded individuals, Serenity was the first of its kind to not be corporately or independently owned. There is no one owner of Serenity but instead an elected Board of Directors that governs the company.
Our cooperative, The Serenity Family Service Society, is comprised of numerous churches of varying denominations who elect an executive board to determine the direction and monitor the operation of Serenity Funeral Service.
Serenity has and will always endeavor to meet the needs of the families we serve by maintaining the highest ethical standards while being sensitive to the changing needs of our communities. We strive to ensure that all families are treated with the utmost fairness, dignity and respect, and we are also committed to working within the financial means of all families.
As for our wonderful team of staff, we encourage you to visit any one of our locations and meet us. Serenity’s staff of licensed Funeral directors and embalmers are professional, compassionate and ready to serve your family during this difficult time.
There is no cost or obligation, simply stop by and visit us at one of our locations across Alberta to inquire about all that Serenity has to offer.
As a not-for-profit funeral service, we exist to meet families in their grief, provide considerate care, affordable professional service, inspired by Christian compassion and our hope in our Creator’s eternal future.

As for our wonderful team of staff, we encourage you to visit any one of our locations and meet us. Serenity’s staff of licensed Funeral directors and embalmers are professional, compassionate and ready to serve your family during this difficult time.

There is no cost or obligation, simply stop by and visit us at one of our locations across Alberta to inquire about all that Serenity has to offer.

As a not-for-profit funeral service, we exist to meet families in their grief, provide considerate care, affordable professional service, inspired by Christian compassion and our hope in our Creator’s eternal future.

text:
Burial Services | Serenity Funeral Service
Does the idea of being returned to this earth appeal to you? Would you take comfort in having a designated plot where your loved ones could visit? Funeral and burial services have been around for many years, it is tradition of human nature.
For those selecting a traditional burial for their loved one, the ceremony options can be arranged and designed to include three distinct phases: visitation or viewing of the deceased, the ceremony or service and the burial service. Although the three phases of the burial service have been most common for centuries, it’s not the only option available.
Our Funeral Directors work with families and individuals to clarify, inform and educate you on the various options available today. Understanding your needs allow our Funeral Directors to plan and design a ceremony service that meets your needs and preferences.
We offer a number of options for families or individuals to choose from for casket burial of the deceased.
The Funeral, Memorial or Celebration of Life ceremony can take place at Serenity Funeral Service, at a church, a community centre or even at your home. The ceremony, whether formal or informal, serves to acknowledge and recognize a life lived and allows people to come together in a setting of your choosing. Whether the ceremony is traditional or unique, the visitation or viewing and the funeral ceremony can be tailored and personalized to reflect the individuality of the person who has died. The ceremony concludes in the cemetery or mausoleum for burial or entombment.
Visitation, also commonly referred to as “viewing” or “wake”, allows family and friends to gather in a room at the funeral home with the departed loved one. The casket may be open or closed, and gives everyone the neutral opportunity to say goodbye to the deceased loved one on their own terms and according to their own individual needs. The immediate family may choose to be present to receive support and condolences from guests attending or may choose to have their own private visitation.
Immediate burial service is the most basic service that involves the burial or entombment of the loved one’s physical remains without visitation/viewing or any form of ceremony for family and friends.
Graveside, interment or committal services are also available; such services are held at the cemetery plot and allow for family and friends to attend as their loved one is brought to his or her final resting place.

Cremation & Memorial Services | Serenity Funeral Service
At Serenity Funeral Service, we value everyone and anyone, no matter their culture or beliefs. We want to be your advocate during this difficult time and ensure that your service is what you expect. We treat cremation and memorials as the same unique and personal experience as we would a traditional burial. Rest assured your family will have the care and attention that you deserve.
Cremation is another method of final disposition and an alternative to casket burial or entombment. Similar to earth burial ceremonies, we provide various options for those choosing cremation. Individualized ceremonies that provide families and friends with a means of coming together to remember a life lived, sharing of memories while creating a hope for healing and renewal.
Perhaps the most common misunderstanding surrounding those choosing cremation is that there is no opportunity for families to actively memorialize the person who has died. Our cremation options today are no different than the options available for families selecting burial and entombment. Our Funeral Directors will guide you through the cremation and memorial options available to you and help you honor your loved one’s life.

# Green Burials Edmonton, Eco-Friendly Burial Options

A Green burial only allows decomposable materials such as natural wood, wicker, biodegradable containers, and organic burial shrouds, thus minimizing the environmental damage while fostering a greater union with nature.

Green burials nurture the natural cycle of life by offering an eco-friendly process for our body to be returned to the earth and allows for environmentally conscious individuals to care for the environment in life and in death.

For those interested in conservation, parklands, ecology or the simple beauty of nature untouched while living, Green Burial is your perfect option in death.

Serenity Funeral Services uses the [Rosehill Cemetery](https://rosehillcemetery.ca/) and [Northern Lights Cemetery](https://www.edmonton.ca/programs_services/municipal_cemeteries/northern-lights-cemetery) in Edmonton, Alberta. To learn more about Green Burials and our other burial options and funeral planning services please [contact us](https://www.serenity.ca/contact/contact-us). We’re here for you.

[Explore Eco-Friendly Burial Options](https://www1.serenity.ca/green-burial?utm_source=website&utm_medium=button&utm_campaign=green+burial)

## FAQs About Green Burials  

###### CAN I BE BURIED ON MY OWN LAND?  

No, you cannot be buried on your own land. The Alberta Cemeteries Act states “No person shall bury a dead human body in any place other than a cemetery and . . . no new cemetery can be established except for a religious auxiliary, religious denomination or a municipality.” That means no corporate entity or private individual can start a cemetery in Alberta.  

###### IS NATURAL BURIAL LEGAL?  

Yes, natural burials are legal. A Natural or Green burial is becoming increasingly popular and several cemeteries in Alberta offer this option.  

###### CAN A PERSON BE BURIED WITHOUT A CASKET?  

Yes, a person can be buried without a casket. If you are being buried in a Green or Natural Cemetery you can be buried with a shroud or biodegradable container.  

###### CAN YOU BE BURIED IN ANY CEMETERY?  

No, some cemetery’s that are owned by religious auxiliary or religious denominations may have restrictions as to who can be buried in their cemetery.  

###### HOW MUCH DOES IT COST FOR A GREEN BURIAL?  

The cost of a Green Burial will be determined by the funeral home you choose. Most funeral homes have their pricing posted on their website.  

###### UNDER WHAT CIRCUMSTANCES WOULD A GREEN BURIAL NOT BE ALLOWED?  

Green burials will not be allowed if the deceased has been embalmed, if the deceased is in a non biodegradable container, or if the deceased has been cremated.  

###### CAN YOU HAVE YOUR OWN MONUMENT OR HEAD STONE?  

No, individual markers or monuments are not permitted in Green burial cemeteries. Some green cemeteries have communal markers or boulders with multiple names.  

###### WILL ANIMALS DISTURB A GREEN BURIAL SITE?  

No, the decedent will be buried deep enough that animals will not disturb them.  

###### IS CREMATION AN OPTION WITH A GREEN OR NATURAL BURIAL?  

Cremation is not an option with a green or natural burial as the process of cremation leaves a carbon footprint.

Obituary information for Tracey Roderick Thibeau
It is with great sadness that the family of Tracey Roderick Thibeau share the news of his passing on July 23, 2026, in Spruce Grove, Alberta.
Tracey is survived by his loving wife, Connie Thibeau (Benere); his children Raylene Rehill (Kevin), Kerri-Ann Stevens (Paul), and Danielle Thibeau (Brent); his grandchildren Hazel, Hudson, Liv, Adaline, and Leo; his siblings Shelia (Jerry), Raye (Heather), and Colleen (Dennis); and many cherished extended family. Tracey is predeceased by his son, Kyle Thibeau; granddaughter Lennie Stevens; his parents Alyre and Myrtle Thibeau; and mother-in-law, Florence Benere.
Tracey had a deep love of sports, a “true-blue” Maple Leafs and Jays fan and embraced the many roles he had throughout his sporting life: a spirited player, an encouraging mentor and coach, and for 37 years, a dedicated and fair-minded senior official. The values he learned through team sports guided the way he lived and the example he set for others.
Teaching came naturally to Tracey. He had a gift for meaningful conversation, making people feel heard, and offering encouragement when he felt it was needed most. Later in his career, those qualities led him to become a respected instructor in a highly specialized field which took him around the world. He’d light up whenever recounting stories from those years.
Above all else, Tracey’s family was his greatest joy. He was a devoted husband who absolutely adored his wife, Connie. For almost 50 years, they were true partners in every sense, rarely apart and happiest in each other’s company. Their enduring bond is a testament to deep friendship, unwavering commitment, and a love that only grew stronger with time.
Tracey was also a deeply loving and attentive father who watched over, guided, and encouraged his children. They remember him being present for every milestone, big and small. As his family grew, so did his joy; Tracey loved being a grandfather, delighting in making the kids laugh and “taking them for a treat”. He spoke about his children and grandchildren with immense pride, sharing their whereabouts and latest accomplishments with anyone who would listen. The love, pride, and devotion he had for his family were among the greatest gifts he gave them.
Tracey also had a remarkable ability to make people laugh (even complete strangers). Whether it was a well-timed one-liner, a harmless prank, or simply being together with family and friends, there was always laughter when Tracey was there. He had a way of turning ordinary moments into lasting memories and he loved being the one to retell the stories with humour.
Tracey never hesitated to tell the people he loved how much he cared. Until his final days, he would say, "I'm the luckiest man in the world.” He leaves behind a legacy of laughter, wisdom, kindness, and unwavering devotion to his family and loved ones.
Grief and sadness have come to us now, because love came first. We are grateful to you, we are so proud of you, and we will love you always and forever.

How to Plan a Funeral
How to Plan a Funeral
Not sure where to start with planning a funeral service? Although some are certain they want burial services or cremation, the majority of us have not yet done any funeral pre-planning for ourselves or put much thought into what we might want. Much has changed since the time of only having two options. We now have the resources to provide the traditional or alternative funeral services such as Green Burials as well as celebration of life, ceremony or memorial that is tailored to your preferences and ideas on how you and your family have chosen to honour life.
There are so many new ways to celebrate someone’s life. Whether that someone was an avid guitar player, a book lover, or a bird watcher now there are more ways than ever to incorporate those details that really speak to that someone’s personality into their celebration of life.
Download Our Planning Guide 
Create Healing Experiences
One of the most important ceremonies in life happens after we pass on. Different peoples, cultures, and religions around the globe use funerals as a way to honour and remember the departed—and the event represents an important step for the loved ones left behind.
While there are a few traditional ways to conduct and plan a funeral, each service is an individual experience. Your recently departed loved one was unique, and so was your relationship with them. We believe their final farewell should reflect their one-of-a-kind personality and as well the special relationship you shared with them. At Serenity Funeral Service, our professionals strive to create custom funerals and cremation services that display that individuality.

Personalized Funeral Services
The staff at Serenity Funeral Service pride themselves on our service’s peaceful, no-pressure environment. With our support, you design the funeral rather than have someone tell you what you need. With our years of experience, we are there to offer advice and guidance when planning a funeral, but you have the freedom to choose how the funeral will run. Whether you want to have your service at home, in a church, or by the lakeside, we are happy to accommodate your family.

Ways to Personalize
Personal Notes and Drawings: Have the children, grandchildren, family and friends draw pictures on the cremation container at the viewing- this allows people to write a final farewell and is a completely unique way to send off their loved one.
Casket Customization: Pick from a selection of corners and medallions to customize the casket. Some examples include sheath of wheat, piano keys, fishing rod or golf clubs.

Obituary information for John Oleksyn
It is with great sadness and much love that we say goodbye to our beloved father, John, who passed away on July 22, 2026, at the age of 94 years.
John is survived by his wife of 67 years Sheila (nee Rounceville), children Nelson (Joan), Shane (Debbie), Cathy (Tony), Tim (Shelly), Tammy (Coby), Shanna (Greg), Mark (Amber), Katrina (Harlyn), Jason (Jayde), Tasha (Matthew). Grandchildren: Jordan, Jesse, Giancarlo, Zacari, Jake, Emma, Kaleb, Nevada, Madison, Braden, Logan, Tekle, Julia, Wyatt, Aliza, Jude, Jackson.
Great Grandchildren: Trenton, Hudson, Bennet, Abigail, Samuel, Tessa. Along with nieces and nephews and dear friends.
John was predeceased by his parents Kuzma, Anna (Feniak). Siblings James, Peter, Mary, Margaret, Dorothy, Catherine, Pearl, Jean.
Born and raised in Opal, Alberta area (Peaskie), John married Sheila in 1959. Together they raised five sons and five daughters on their farm just NW of Opal. John always jokingly said he was the King of Opal City and mom would just agree.
One of John’s greatest accomplishments was his family. John was so proud of his beautiful, hard-working supportive wife Sheila and proud to be the father to ten children, he often encouraged others to have ten kids too. John had a real love for life, and living off the land. He had a green thumb especially in his retirement years gardening was his hobby, along with fencing, picking mushrooms and blueberries when the season arrived.
John had a tireless work ethic; he worked hard for his family alongside his wife Sheila on their cattle farm for many decades. John truly had an entrepreneur spirit, in his early days in Bon Accord there was the gas station and vehicle repair shop, water well digging, then in 1980 he ventured into the sand and gravel business known as Mill Creek Sand & Gravel, in the 1990’s the restaurant known as Sunset and then Clark & Jane’s are remembered by many in the community.
Many fondly remember waving to John in his pickup truck with the John Deere license plate as he was out and about on his daily tour of the local countryside, sand pit, auctions and stopping at a favorite coffee shop for lunch.
John was baptized as one of Jehovah’s Witnesses and out of love for his God Jehovah and neighbour he willingly shared the good news of God’s Kingdom with others. John was generous soul. He gave to others because he wanted to, not for any recognition. He truly practiced giving Acts 20:35 “There is more happiness in giving than there is in receiving.” and he reaped the benefit of the happiness that comes from giving.
John will be deeply missed by both family and friends. We look forward to seeing him again when his cherished scriptural hope is realized. Revelation 21:3, 4 “And he will wipe out every tear form their eyes, and death will be no more, neither will mourning nor outcry not pain be anymore. The former things have passed away.”
From the family a special thank you to the wonderful care team of doctors, nurses, caregivers, administration, chefs, custodians at Aster Gardens on Unit #3 who extended such kindness, respect and dignity to our dad, we are forever grateful.
A Memorial Service will be held on August 5, 2026, at 11:00 am at the Redwater & District Pioneer Club located at 4916 50 ST, Redwater Alberta. A private family interment will take place on August 5, 2026, 10:00 am at the Redwater Cemetery Community.
The family would like to thank you for all the love and support shown as we say goodbye.
As an expression of sympathy plant a tree or pay it forward with an act of kindness to someone.

text:
Planning | Serenity Funeral Service
Save your family from difficult decisions
Serenity’s End of Life Planning program can help walk you through the steps involved with pre-planning your own funeral for the protection of your survivors, beneficiaries and estate.
Let Serenity’s funeral directors and consultants guide you through the entire funeral planning process and help you create a ceremony that not only meets your needs, but the needs of your family.
Download Our Planning Guide 
Avoid Burdening Your Family with Stress, Extra Work and Unexpected Expenses.
Imagine what funeral pre-planning could do for you today and for your survivors years from now. We hear it all the time – nobody really wants to leave their family or their executors faced with a mountain of hardships, but that’s exactly what you’ll do if you don’t have your end of life plans securely in place.
When a death occurs, more than 70 pieces of information, details and irreversible decisions must be made.
Funeral pre-planning allows you to:
Control funeral costs – and even lock them in at today’s rates (the lowest they will ever be)
Ensure that your wishes are carried out exactly as you want
Eliminate the unexpected financial burden most executors face when settling an estate
Accelerate the settling of your estate
Reduce future probate costs
Give your family the time and space to grieve your passing
End-of-Life Planning goes beyond the funeral. For most people (and even most funeral homes), “preplanning” starts and stops at prepaid funeral expenses, but there’s a lot more involved to a complete end-of-life plan. Serenity End of Life Planning offers a full scope of services to ensure your survivors, executors and heirs are cared for; your estate is protected – and you enjoy full peace of mind.
Prepaid funeral plans:
Our expert team helps you move your preplanning from discussions, ideas and a few jotted notes about what type of funeral you want, into a formalized, written plan that:
Spells out exactly how you want your funeral arrangements to be handled; disposition decision, ceremony details, burial or cremation and more
Guarantees that the financial investment you make into a prepaid funeral is 100 percent protected – securely held in your name
Spells out exactly how your executor will be assisted
Offers peace of mind to you and your heirs
Our guiding approach is knowledgeable and cooperative
We work with you to establish a clear understanding of the necessary steps that will protect your survivors from costly future hardships. Our goal is to ensure that you are informed and content with your completed plan.
A plan specific to you

# Planning | Serenity Funeral Service

## Save your family from difficult decisions  

Serenity’s End of Life Planning program can help walk you through the steps involved with pre-planning your own funeral for the protection of your survivors, beneficiaries and estate.

Let Serenity’s [funeral directors and consultants](https://www.serenity.ca/about/meet-our-team) guide you through the entire funeral planning process and help you create a ceremony that not only meets your needs, but the needs of your family.

[Download Our Planning Guide](https://www1.serenity.ca/preplanning-guide?utm_source=website&utm_medium=button&utm_campaign=preplanning)

## Avoid Burdening Your Family with Stress, Extra Work and Unexpected Expenses.  

Imagine what funeral pre-planning could do for you today and for your survivors years from now. We hear it all the time – nobody really wants to leave their family or their executors faced with a mountain of hardships, but that’s exactly what you’ll do if you don’t have your end of life plans securely in place.

When a death occurs, more than 70 pieces of information, details and irreversible decisions must be made.

Funeral pre-planning allows you to:

*   Control funeral costs – and even lock them in at today’s rates (the lowest they will ever be)
*   Ensure that your wishes are carried out exactly as you want
*   Eliminate the unexpected financial burden most executors face when settling an estate
*   Accelerate the settling of your estate
*   Reduce future probate costs
*   Give your family the time and space to grieve your passing

End-of-Life Planning goes beyond the funeral. For most people (and even most funeral homes), “preplanning” starts and stops at prepaid funeral expenses, but there’s a lot more involved to a complete end-of-life plan. Serenity End of Life Planning offers a full scope of services to ensure your survivors, executors and heirs are cared for; your estate is protected – and you enjoy full peace of mind.

## Prepaid funeral plans:  

Our expert team helps you move your preplanning from discussions, ideas and a few jotted notes about what type of funeral you want, into a formalized, written plan that:  

*   Spells out exactly how you want your funeral arrangements to be handled; disposition decision, ceremony details, burial or cremation and more
*   Guarantees that the financial investment you make into a prepaid funeral is 100 percent protected – securely held in your name
*   Spells out exactly how your executor will be assisted
*   Offers peace of mind to you and your heirs

### Our guiding approach is knowledgeable and cooperative  

We work with you to establish a clear understanding of the necessary steps that will protect your survivors from costly future hardships. Our goal is to ensure that you are informed and content with your completed plan.

### A plan specific to you  

Like you, each funeral plan is unique; you’ll decide what your completed plan should be. Our guiding approach sets the foundation that provides answers, options and solution.

### Planning begins with you and us  

What are you trying to achieve? What are your initial concerns? Discussions with you are necessary to establish where you are in the planning process and where you want to be. A discussion is the first step to reaching an end result.

Planning your own funeral with our expert advice and guided assistance is simple and can save your family from making difficult decisions regarding what you would have wanted. If you’re worried about something happening while travelling, we also offer a [**Guaranteed Travel Assurance Plan**](https://tributecenteronline.s3-accelerate.amazonaws.com/SiteBuilder/Attachments/ce522f09-0192-4eec-a0ec-3c5205a10f60/16b367a3-9207-4ea7-b04e-b90625fe55dd.pdf). Contact our Funeral [Pre Planning Centre in Edmonton](https://www.serenity.ca/contact/pre-planning-center) to get started, or take our pre planning test to see how prepared you are.

# Why Do Funeral Planning? | Serenity Funeral Service

## Why Preplan  

Making funeral arrangements beforehand gives you time to consider all your options and truly plan a service that’s unique to you. If you’re still on the fence, below are a few more reasons why preplanning is a good option.  

## It's Simple

It’s as simple as completing the preplanning form below or meeting with one of our advisors to put your plan in place. No matter your age, anyone can preplan, and you can make changes whenever you wish.

## You Relieve the Burden

Preplanning relieves your family of that burden, so they can focus on grief and remembrance.

## You're in Control

When you preplan, you’re in control of creating a unique celebration of life. You also can include your family members in the planning, so the service reflects their wishes and needs as well.

## There are Prepay Options

We deposit your prepayments into a trust fund where it stays until it’s needed. Prepaying generally means you save money since you’re protected from inflation and price changes, and it also gives your family members peace of mind knowing that the funeral expenses are taken care of.

## How to Begin

Check out our planning checklist to see all your options. Then, you can plan online using our form or you can schedule a meeting with our staff to plan your personalized service details.

Additionally, we keep a record of your preplanned arrangements and prepayments, and they’re easily transferable to any funeral home in North America if you were to move.

[Download Our Planning Guide](https://www1.serenity.ca/preplanning-guide?utm_source=website&utm_medium=button&utm_campaign=preplanning)

# Funeral Pre Planning Checklist | Serenity Funeral Service

## Funeral Preplanning Checklist  

Check out this planning checklist to create your unique funeral arrangements, but remember that you don't need to make all these decisions right now. If you want to talk with one of our advisors about creating personalized funeral plans, please don’t hesitate to contact us.  

## Getting Started

*   Select a funeral home.
*   Note any specific instructions for your services and final disposition.
*   Organize personal information for your obituary.
*   If you wish, choose a charity for any donations.

*   Select burial or cremation.
*   Choose a casket or cremation container.
*   Pick funeral locations and service types.
*   Make a note of any desired traditions or religious rituals.
*   Select the attire you want to be dressed in.
*   Arrange transportation for your physical remains and family members.
*   Select an overall theme for funeral stationery and any décor.
*   Choose floral arrangements.
*   Choose any specific hymns and songs you’d like included.
*   Pick photos and mementos for a memorial display.

## Service Participants  

*   Designate pallbearers.
*   Select a clergy member or officiator for the service.
*   Pick friends or family members to say the eulogy, read scripture, do a speech, or other readings.
*   If you wish, choose any musicians.

## Final Disposition  

*   Choose a cemetery.
*   Select a burial plot or mausoleum.
*   Select a memorial or grave marker and inscription.
*   Decide who will keep your urn.
*   Decide who will scatter your ashes and where.

DNA Banking and Preservation | Serenity Funeral Service
What is DNA Banking?
“DNA Banking is the secure preservation and long-term storage of an individual’s unique genetic material.”
Read video transcript below
Why is DNA preservation and banking important?
Advancements in science and technology have allowed us to look at DNA as more than just an individual’s hair color, eye color, and physical traits. DNA testing and banking can now be used to compare against medical conditions and ancestral roots, giving us more information than ever about the individual who the DNA pertains to. Without DNA collection and preservation, these opportunities are lost forever.
Why do we talk about DNA banking in the funeral profession?
It is crucial that families speak with their loved ones as well as their preferred funeral service provider to ensure that arrangements can be made accordingly. DNA preservation and banking is no longer an available option once cremation or embalming has occurred
Benefits of DNA Banking
Cherish More Than a Memory: DNA Banking is the best option for families who are looking for a meaningful way to remember their loved one. Unlike ashes, hair or other traditional keepsakes, DNA contains the unique genetic ‘blueprint’ of an individual. Preserving DNA gives families an opportunity to capture all this information and establish a connection that will last forever.
Document Hereditary Heart Diseases in the Family: 75% of all diseases can be traced back to our genetic makeup. Many of the genetic mutations that cause cancers and other hereditary diseases have been identified. Banking your family’s DNA is an important step in tracing the root cause of hereditary diseases and paves the way for DNA medical research and targeted treatments in the future.
New Opportunities in Ancestry DNA Testing: Trace your ancestral roots using an ancestry DNA test. As more markers are identified, DNA ancestry testing will become much more powerful than it is today. Keeping a record of your family’s DNA opens new doors in this exciting field and creates opportunities that were never available before.
Store DNA for Future Testing: Banked DNA lasts indefinitely and can be accessed for testing at any time. A wide range of genetic tests are currently available for everything from ancestry testing to disease predisposition testing and more are yet to come.
Open Doors for Personalized Medicine: Studying your family’s DNA may assist doctors in determining which treatment plans will work best for you, and which ones will be ineffective. This technology is already being used as DNA testing for medical tolerance, optimal dosage levels and effectivity of drugs used in heart disease and cancer patients.

Source: SecuriGene DNA Preservation
How to Get Started Preserving Your DNA
Contact us to purchase our DNA banking kit.
Our Funeral Service Provider will take a small DNA sample for collection.
Your DNA sample is then sent to the SecuriGene laboratory for processing.
Your banked DNA is returned to you in a state-of-the-art capsule made from surgical grade stainless steel along with a Certificate of Analysis.
DNA Video Transcript:
“Our unique DNA makes us who we are today. From the soft wavy hair we inherited from our grandmother to the rich hazel eyes of our father, everything is rooted deep within our genetics. Our DNA even reveals health risks that run in the family and offers clues about the origins of our ancestors. After death, all this information is lost… forever.
But now, with the SecuriGene DNA Capsule, families have a chance to capture the entire genetic blueprint of their loved one and preserve their legacy for generations to come. Each capsule is precision-crafted from surgical-grade stainless steel. The DNA within is carefully extracted by the lab, purified of contaminants, and preserved using anhydrobiosis technology. It is then hermetically sealed, inspected, certified for purity, and returned home to your family. A legacy secured forever in life’s purest form.
For genetic analysis, both now and in the future, families can choose from over 3,000 DNA tests at SecuriGene, including DNA ancestry testing, health screening, genetic profiling, and kinship testing. Families with a history of cancer, heart disease, Alzheimer’s, stroke, and other heritable conditions are strongly encouraged to save DNA. Since our genetics are passed down from parent to child, it is crucial to have samples available from previous generations. Enabling doctors to trace the root cause of diseases. Tailor more effective treatment plans and improve the overall health of the entire family.
And this is only the beginning. There is so much we have yet to discover about DNA. Preserving your loved one’s genetic blueprint allows you to make use of all future technologies as they become available. The time we have with our loved ones can be fleeting, so hold onto the most personal kind of hope we have, our DNA. Meaningful, unique, and completely personalized, the SecuriGene DNA Capsule helps you remember your loved one by unlocking the past and opening up the possibilities of the future.”

Download the DNA banking brochure
