Memorial services allow for a great deal of flexibility if additional time is needed to gather together as a family for a service. In fact, it is not uncommon for a memorial service to be held a month or more after the death. Whether you decide on a funeral or a memorial service, it’s important to remember the role that memorialization plays in the grieving process. Spend some time thinking about the type of service that would best encapsulate the spirit of your loved one.
Memorial Service FAQ
What does a typical memorial service look like?
Memorial services are designed with the family and tailored to the sensibilities and wishes of the family in consultation with our professional staff. A customary service might include a musical prelude, a welcome, scripture readings, poetry or other excerpts from literature, tributes from friends, family and colleagues, special music, and a musical postlude.
Which type of service format is right for me and my family?
There's really no way we can tell you which service would be the best in your situation. In fact, we don't believe it's even part of our job to tell you; instead, our work is in showing you the spectrum of possibilities. We can explain your options, make suggestions; all with the goal of empowering you to arrive at the best possible decision.
How much will a memorial service cost?
When you meet with a funeral director to discuss service costs, you can request a copy of a price list which details all the basic professional services included in the price of your loved one's memorial service, as well as the cost of any additional products or services you want to include.
What's involved in planning a memorial service?
Memorial service planning doesn’t have to be difficult; it's empowering. After all, you've got a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to show the world how much your loved one meant to you. Important tasks would include selecting the location, date and time of the service. You'll be asked to identify the specific readings, musical selections, as well as the people you would like to participate in the service itself.
How much will I have to be involved?
Certainly, your funeral director will need you to specify certain details: the where and when, for example. Together you'll make important decisions about other specifics, but once those decisions are made, you can "step back" and let us handle everything or have as much input as you please.
What items will I need to bring to the funeral home?
You'll need to provide information required to complete your loved one's obituary or service cards if necessary. You may also wish to bring in family photographs to be used in making a tribute video or service cards. Other items may be needed at some point, depending on the arrangements made. Your funeral director can provide a list of the things to bring along to the arrangement conference.
What is a civil celebrant? How can he or she help?
A celebrant is a person who has been trained to conduct formal ceremonies, such as weddings, baptisms, and funerals. They are not clergy; instead they are experienced masters-of-ceremony and story-tellers. A celebrant works closely with family to create a service which reflects the beliefs, cultural background, values, and aspirations of your deceased loved one, and your family. If you think you would be best served by a celebrant, please speak with your funeral director.
Will I, or another family member, need to write the obituary?
Commonly the funeral director who met with you during the arrangement conference will assist with writing the obituary. You will support them in doing so by providing them with the necessary information and important details about your loved one's life. If you, or another family member or friend, wish to write the obituary, we can help to guide you through the process.
Can a service be held at the Westlock Funeral Home?
Yes! Our facilities are equipped to meet your needs. Our amazing team is committed to providing quality services to every family, of every culture and faith, in their greatest time of need.
My loved one was religiously observant. Will that be reflected in the choice of clergy? Can my own spiritual/religious leader officiate? Can secular (non-religious) memorial services happen at the Westlock Funeral Home?
We serve all faiths and none, with our diverse staff. Our local clergy/celebrants will assist in planning the service according to the wishes of the family, whether they are religious or secular.

The death of someone we care about can be one of the most difficult experiences in life. Words fail to describe how painful the grief we feel can be. It is more challenging than we, or others, might expect.
These articles are meant to describe different types of grief; their intent is to help you understand your own, or to help you empathize with another person's grief.
These articles were written by Dr. Bill Webster, a Director of Grief Education, and are part of a comprehensive library available on The Center for the Grief Journey website. Dr. Bill is the founder and executive director of the Centre for the Grief Journey. He earned his doctorate at the University of Toronto in 1990, and has been awarded a prestigious fellowship in thanatology by the Association of Death Education and Counseling (ADEC).
Dr. Bill's knowledge of grief exists not just in theory, but from a very difficult personal experience. In 1983, Bill's young wife died suddenly of a heart attack. Her passing left him in the difficult situation of coping with immense loss while raising his two sons, who were only seven and nine when their mother died. Dr Bill has become a recognized author, and a renowned international speaker and seminar leader who draws from 30 years of experience in the field of grief support and counseling.
These articles will help you understand your own grief or the grief of another. Grief is not as simple as it's made out to be -- it is more than just "feeling sad."
These articles will help you understand the dynamics of specific losses, such as the loss of a spouse, or the loss of a pet.
These articles will help you understand the grief process of a child, with tips on how to help them cope.
These articles will provide you with some useful information on how to help someone who is grieving, as well as tips on how to help navigate special days and holidays, which can be especially difficult in the wake of a loss.
Grief can come unexpectedly in life. These articles offer more specific information on certain types of grief, such as grief following a suicide, and grief in the workplace.

What do I do? | Westlock Funeral Home & Crematorium Ltd. ...
Whether unexpected or planned for, it is a life changing moment when someone dies. Having some general knowledge about “what to do” or “who to call” can help guide our thinking.
It can be difficult to make that first call to a funeral home when yourself or a loved one is nearing the end of life. But if you can, contacting the funeral home to gather information and guidance can give you greater peace of mind and help prepare you for the time to come.
When a death occurs, we are available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, to transfer a decedent into our care.
When a death occurs, it can be difficult to know what to do first. If you are with your loved one, there is no need to rush. Take a moment, and when you’re ready, the next steps will depend on the circumstances.
If the death was expected and your loved one was under medical care, such as with a doctor, nurse, or hospice team, you can contact that care provider. They will attend and complete the necessary documentation. 
If the death was unexpected, you should call 911, and emergency services will guide you through what happens next. In some situations, the Office of the Chief Medical Examiner of Alberta may become involved.
Once the appropriate professionals have been contacted, you can reach out to a funeral home. A single call is all that’s needed to begin. Arrangements will be made to bring your loved one into care, and you will be gently guided through each step that follows.
In the days ahead, there will be time to make decisions about burial or cremation, plan a service if you wish, and share an obituary with family and friends. You will also be asked for some basic information about your loved one, but this does not all need to be gathered immediately. As part of the process, the death is registered with Alberta Vital Statistics, and official documents can be obtained when needed.
There will also be practical matters to attend to over time, such as notifying government programs, financial institutions, and handling estate affairs. These things can feel overwhelming, but they do not need to be done all at once, and support is available when you are ready.
If you are unsure what to do at any point, you don’t have to figure it out alone. We are here to support you and walk with you through each step, at your own pace.

Plan Ahead | Westlock Funeral Home & Crematorium Ltd.
Thinking about funeral arrangements in advance is something many people consider, not because it is easy, but because it can bring a sense of clarity and peace of mind. Making these decisions ahead of time allows you to reflect on what feels right for you—whether that’s burial or cremation, a traditional service or something more simple and personal.
Prearranging also eases the burden on those closest to you. During a time of loss, families are often faced with many decisions in a very short period of time. Having your wishes already known can provide comfort and reassurance, allowing them to focus on being together rather than wondering what you would have wanted.
Some people choose to simply document their preferences, while others prefer to make financial arrangements in advance. Both options are available, and there is no expectation or pressure—only the opportunity to plan in a way that feels right for you.
Conversations around planning ahead can be meaningful ones. They create space to share values, traditions, and personal wishes with those who matter most. Many families find that these discussions, though sometimes difficult to begin, become a gift to one another over time.
If you’re considering prearranging, we are here to answer questions and walk you through the options at your own pace. Whether you’re ready to make decisions or simply exploring, you’re always welcome to reach out.

Norah Constance "Connie” Engler (née Thomas) of Barrhead, Alberta, passed away at the Dr. W.R. Keir Barrhead Continuing Care Centre on June 24, 2026. She was a cherished mother, grandmother, and friend, and her presence will be deeply missed.
Connie is survived by children Pamela (Richard) Franklin, Erich (Ruth) Engler, and Gail (James) Verheul; and her grandchildren Nathan (Angela) Franklin, Stephen Franklin, Julia Franklin, Daniel Engler, Sarah Engler, Isaac Engler, Jonathan Verheul, Charrissa Verheul, Joshua (Charlotte) Verheul, and Phillip Verheul.
Connie was predeceased by her beloved husband, Garry Engler; her parents Frances Norah Elizabeth and Albert Thomas Edward Thomas; her siblings Shirley, Joan, and Ernie; and her granddaughter Annalise Franklin.
Connie was born in Calgary, Alberta, on June 21, 1941. She was raised in Rossland, British Colombia, and Calgary, Alberta, and graduated from Western Canada High School in Calgary in 1959. Connie married Gerhard Ludwig “Garry” Engler on October 19, 1968, and they had three children: Pamela, Erich, and Gail. Connie took care of her children while working alongside Garry in pastoral ministry, mission service, and in many aspects of the farm, along with pre-marriage government work with veteran and Indian Affairs and at the GLO Christian Bookstore while they lived in Scotland in 1990-1992. Connie was a creative person who loved to crochet, do puzzles, read, and loved story of all forms. She enjoyed spontaneous “come on over for coffee and pie” visits and hosted many family members, friends, and international students during their ministry years in Regina, Saskatchewan.

Obituary information for Bernice Fairholm
It is with great sadness that the family of Bernice Marie Fairholm announces her peaceful passing on July 20, 2026. 
She is mourned by her children Margaret, Richard (Dallas), Donna (Chris), Karen (Corin), Tanis; her nine grandchildren Kieran (Maria), Abby (Alex), Moriah (Josh), Maygen (Ryder), Jyllian (John), Amira, Seth, Micah and Tristan; her three great-grandchildren Wesley, Wilder and Freya; a loving extended family and friends.
She was predeceased by her husband, Albert, in 2021 and her parents, Dorothy and Orland Bidne.
Bernice was born in Westlock and spent her youth in the Barrhead area. Her mother was a teacher, and Bernice accompanied her as she taught in several rural community schools. As a young adult, Bernice lived in Edmonton for four years, a time she often spoke of fondly. She married Albert Fairholm in 1968, and in 1972, they moved with their children to a farm in Hazel Bluff, where they lived for 36 years.
Bernice was full of zest, energy, and had a great sense of humor. She loved welcoming people into her home and hosting large family gatherings. Bernice loved to serve. She spent many years actively involved with the Westlock Gospel Chapel, AWANA, and the local Christian Women’s Club. She was quick to offer containers of soup, chili, or a batch of homemade cookies to anyone who had need.
Bernice loved to work outside; nothing made her happier than putting on a pair of gardening gloves and “getting to work.” Bernice also loved to sing, whether in a choir or simply around the house. And if Cotton Jenny by Anne Murray came on, there was a good chance she would be singing along, and perhaps even dancing too.
Bernice lived with health challenges that impacted her life in various ways. Her last two years were particularly challenging; however, the devoted care and active advocacy of her daughter, Donna, and her son, Richard, helped her immensely.
We love you, Mom.
A memorial is planned for Bernice on Saturday, August 22, 2026, at 3 p.m. at the Westlock Gospel Chapel. 
In lieu of flowers, donations may be made to The Mental Health Foundation Alberta – Edmonton.

Obituary information for Paul J. Wurz
It is with great sorrow that we announce the passing of our beloved husband, father, brother, grandfather, and friend Paul Joseph Wurz, who was called home by our Lord and Father on July 17, 2026, at the age of 70.
Paul was born on April 21, 1956, to Joseph and Justina Wurz in Beiseker, Alberta. At the tender age of eight, Paul’s mother Justina sadly passed away. He was then lovingly raised by Joseph and Susie, who embraced Paul as her own. Her deep and unwavering love was reflected in the way Paul proudly and affectionately called her Mom.
In 1971, Paul moved with his family to Morinville, where he began a new chapter filled with meaningful relationships and opportunities to showcase his many skills. He was known as a humble, patient, and exceptionally hard working man with a remarkable eye for detail. Paul spent many years tending chickens and later became the Hog Manager at the colony. After a devastating fire destroyed one of the hog barns, Paul continued his dedicated work as the Chicken Manager. His care for animals and his surroundings shone through in every area he oversaw—always kept to the highest standards. Paul also served as a proud member of the Egg Board, approaching his responsibilities with seriousness, dedication, and integrity.
It was here that Paul met his best friend and the love of his life, Susanna. They were joyfully married on June 4, 1978, and together built a beautiful life filled with memories, devotion, and faith. They raised four sons, each of whom proudly carries forward the family’s traditions and reflects Paul’s values through their hard work, love for family, and commitment to walking with God.
He will be remembered for his outstanding work ethic, his unwavering love for his family and friends, and the lasting impressions he left on everyone he met—even creating cherished memories with people in other countries. Paul lived a life devoted to the Christian walk and held close a meaningful quote: “Fight for what is right, and God will fight for you.”
Paul is predeceased by his loving parents Joseph and Justina, and by Joseph’s second wife, who earned the title of Mom. He is also predeceased by his sisters Judy and Rebecca, nephews Jerry, Peter and Johnny, as well as numerous other loved ones.
He will be lovingly remembered and deeply missed by his beautiful wife Susanna; his sons Min. James (Kathy), Mark (Michelle), Levi (Tammy), and Paul; and his cherished grandchildren Jayden, Travis, Tyler, Anthony, Logan, Isabelle, Nicholas, Samara, Ezra, Noah, Jovan, Aliyah, Renea, Leneah, Aiden, Neriah, Emery, Madison, Hayden, and Walker.
Also left to mourn are his siblings: Jake (Sarah), Joe (Becky), Frank (Annie); sisters Bertha (Eddie), Susie (Danny), Helen (John), Esther (Min. Peter), Rachel (Min. Jim), Margaret (Min. Walter), Rosanna (Min. Mark); and his brother in law Josh.
Paul leaves behind a legacy of faith, kindness, and dedication. His impact will continue to be felt by his family, friends, and all who were blessed to know him.

Obituary information for Mary Meldrum
It is with deep sadness that we announce the passing of our beautiful mother, Mary Jean Meldrum (née Tennant), 79, of Westlock, Alberta, shortly before her birthday, on June 25, 2026. 
Mary was born on June 30, 1946, to pioneer parents in the Pembina Heights area. She worked on the family farm and attended school in Pembina Heights and Westlock. Later she went to Edmonton and took a sewing course and got very good at sewing. She married in 1968 and had a family. She raised three children while on the farm in Jarvie until the children came of age for school. She moved with the family in tow back to Westlock. In caring for her family, Mary developed a gift for sewing and later, at 69, learned to quilt. Her craft for sewing went from making clothes for the children to wedding dresses for friends and other family members. Family and friends who have received her quilts will remember her greatly.
Her proudest achievement was raising her children and spoiling her grandchildren and great‑grandchildren. She was also known by others for her kindness, generosity, good judgment, hard work, and great spirit.
Mary was the best mother one could hope for. She will be greatly missed. She is survived by her children Linda Tennant, Holly Meldrum, and William Meldrum; grandchildren Dawson Clark (Mica), Liam (Kristy) Tennant; and great‑grandchildren Oliver, Aurora, and Elyse Tennant.
Celebration of life to take place on Thursday, July 2, 2026, at 2:00 pm, at the Westlock Legion, 1004 106 St, with luncheon to follow. To those who may attend, her favorite colors were shades of blue and pink.
In lieu of flowers or cards, the family wishes for donations to be made to Homestead Fabric and Quilting, RR3 Barrhead, Alberta, T7N 1N4, 1‑(780)‑674‑6022, to go towards the youth sewing classes to help the sewers and quilters alike of the future be made in Mary’s honour.

After facing cancer with remarkable strength and determination, Bertha Clement, aged 79, passed away peacefully on June 25, 2026, in Westlock, Alberta.

The family wishes to express their sincere gratitude to the staff at Westlock and Barrhead Hospitals for the compassionate care and kindness they provided to Bertha during her final days.
In lieu of flowers, memorial donations may be made to the Canadian Cancer Society.

Obituary | Annie Marie Riva of Lethbridge, Alberta
Annie Marie Riva
August 11, 1937 - June 9, 2026
It is with great sadness that we announce the passing of Anna Marie (Manas) Riva on June 9, 2026, at the age of 88. Anna will be remembered as a loving wife, mother, grandmother, great-grandmother and friend. 
Anna leaves behind her children, Bruno (Ashley), Angie (Daryl Craypo), Loretta (Marvin Berg), Dora (Troy Naber), Frank (Marney), and Tina (Sheldon Taylor). Her beloved grandchildren are Crystal, Shelly, Shawna, Tammy, Keekee, Chad, Mikaela, Matthew, Priscilla, Silina, Tiera, Alysha, Tiffany, Alanna, Frankie, April, Shondra, Jordon, and numerous great-grandchildren. 
Anna was born August 11, 1937, in the German speaking village of Slankamen, Yugoslavia, modern day Serbia. Life changed drastically when World War II forced her family to flee to Europe where she attended Culinary School just before her family immigrated to Canada in 1956. Once there, the family worked various jobs on a Saskatchewan farm with Anna cooking, being a nanny, and learning English.
Just down the road she caught the eye of a handsome young dairy farm worker, Paul Riva. He grew up in the Black Forest in Germany, and they shared common interests which became dreams for their future. 
They married on March 23, 1957, and moved to Brooks, Alberta where Paul worked on Harry Veiner’s farm and eventually moved to Rolling Hills when they purchased their own farm. This is where the six children were raised and attended school. 
Shortly after arriving in Rolling Hills, disaster struck one foggy morning, when their house burnt down after a stork built a nest in the chimney. By the time Paul came out of the barn, having just started his chores, the house was gone. They lost everything but were happy to escape with their lives. This was a big setback. Soon friends and the Rolling Hills community joined to help rebuild and establish a new home for the family.
The Riva’s attended the Rolling Hills Church of God, a small country church, where they heard the Gospel of Jesus. “Momma told us, in everything you do, always put God first. In life, the order is faith, family, friends, then the farm.”
Their mixed farming operation focused on raising pigs, which in the 90s had its struggles. While Paul focused on the farm, Anna did the gardening, cooking, baking, chickens, and geese. Her house was always in order, and if you hit your visit just right, her famous sourdough buns, apple strudel, Black Forst cake, and potato dumplings were a treat shared with numerous friends. “We will always cherish the memory of the great cook that you were.”
Anna, or Annie, as she was affectionately known, had a vivacious outgoing personality. She was a beautiful woman, inside and out. She could take a plain outfit, jazz it up with a ribbon or a flower and look like a movie star who walked off the cover of a magazine. Her beauty remained with her even in her last days.
Annie and Paul eventually retired in Hays, Alberta. It was there that her love for flowers blossomed as their yard became a flourishing flower garden. She also planted and watered flowers at the local store, spreading joy and brightness in her community. In 2002 Paul passed away, which left a big void in Annie’s life. 
Then along came Karl Wiebe, from Rosemary, whose spouse had also passed away. As her husband, Karl gave Annie stability and calmness and was a wonderful chauffeur and companion to her. He was a kind, loving, thoughtful man that came with an extended family. Thank you to Karl’s adult children as they accepted and appreciated Annie. This includes Leo (Donna), Mariette (Frank), Linda, Cathy (Gerald), and Lawrance. Karl passed away in 2007 while on a life’s-dream mission trip to Africa. 
Annie always wanted to help those who crossed her path. Her life was an example as she displayed how to love one another, pray for the sick, feed the hungry and help the poor. Having lived through a world war, immigrating to a new country, and other challenges, made her a strong person, but she was always loving, kind, and hardworking. These qualities have been instilled in her children and grandchildren.
Anna’s children would like to say, “Thank you Lord for giving us such a wonderful, sensitive praying mother. She taught us to be humble, love, pray and forgive! We will always love you and miss you dearly. Above all we thank you for your love, grace, and faith in God. We love you Momma. You were a blessing from God.
The family would like to thank and express their gratitude and appreciation to all the wonderful staff on the 4th floor of the Lethbridge Hospital and Cedar Creek Lodge.
The funeral service for Anna Riva will be held Saturday, June 27, 2026, 2:00 p.m. at the Rolling Hills Senior’s Centre. Interment at Rolling Hills Cemetery. Rev. Debbie Daniels officiating.
In lieu of flowers please donate to a Food Bank or Women’s Shelter of your choice.

SERVICES 
Funeral Service
Saturday, June 27, 2026 
2:00 PM
Rolling Hills Senior Citizens Club 
121 2 Street 
Rolling Hills, Alberta T0J 2S0

He was a kind, loving, thoughtful man that came with an extended family. Thank you to Karl’s adult children as they accepted and appreciated Annie. This includes Leo (Donna), Mariette (Frank), Linda, Cathy (Gerald), and Lawrance. Karl passed away in 2007 while on a life’s-dream mission trip to Africa. 

Annie always wanted to help those who crossed her path. Her life was an example as she displayed how to love one another, pray for the sick, feed the hungry and help the poor. Having lived through a world war, immigrating to a new country, and other challenges, made her a strong person, but she was always loving, kind, and hardworking. These qualities have been instilled in her children and grandchildren.

Anna’s children would like to say, “Thank you Lord for giving us such a wonderful, sensitive praying mother. She taught us to be humble, love, pray and forgive! We will always love you and miss you dearly. Above all we thank you for your love, grace, and faith in God. We love you Momma. You were a blessing from God.

The family would like to thank and express their gratitude and appreciation to all the wonderful staff on the 4th floor of the Lethbridge Hospital and Cedar Creek Lodge.

The funeral service for Anna Riva will be held Saturday, June 27, 2026, 2:00 p.m. at the Rolling Hills Senior’s Centre. Interment at Rolling Hills Cemetery. Rev. Debbie Daniels officiating.

In lieu of flowers please donate to a Food Bank or Women’s Shelter of your choice.

Kenneth Raymond Smith
January 22, 1950 - June 3, 2026
It is with profound sadness that we announce the passing of Kenneth Raymond Smith of Brooks, loving husband of Brigitte Smith, on June 3, 2026, in Brooks at the age of 76 years. Ken was born on January 22, 1950, in Bracken, Saskatchewan to Raymond and Vickie Smith. He grew up in Rolling Hills, Alberta, where he learned the value of hard work and dedication from an early age. As a young man, he began trucking alongside his father, a career and lifestyle that reflected his strong work ethic and commitment for his family. Ken was a man who could fix almost anything. He was happiest when helping others, whether repairing something, lending a hand, or sharing his knowledge and skills. His generosity, kindness, and willingness to help will be remembered by all who knew him. He enjoyed driving his truck, hunting with his buddies, crafting knives, camping and fishing, and exploring the mountains. He especially treasured the time spent with his children and grandchildren. Ken was predeceased by his parents, parents-in-law, Sieg and Heidi Wetteskind, brother Darrell, sister and brother-in-law, Carol and Garry Hofmann, brother-in-law Herb Wetteskind, and also his precious grandchildren, Joseph and Katherine Fleck. He leaves behind his loving wife of 56 years, Brigitte, his daughters, Lori (Zed) Noel, and Tina (Mike) Fleck, son Kelly, grandchildren, Ari, Elijah, Avian, and Canaan, brothers Richard (Lisa), Lynden (Tonia), Byron (Janey), Brent (Sue), Elwood (Tammy), Garth (Starla), Leighton (Lilianne), sisters-in-law Jan Wetteskind and Kathy Smith, as well as numerous nieces and nephews. Ken’s legacy lives on through the family he loved and the friendships he cherished. He will be deeply missed and forever remembered. The family wishes to express their sincere gratitude to the staff at the Brooks Health Centre for the compassionate care, comfort, and support they provided during Ken’s final days. Obituary | Margaret Caroline Doble of Brooks, Alberta
Margaret Caroline Doble
May 16, 1936 - June 2, 2026
Today, we gather to honour and celebrate the life of Margaret Caroline Doble, a woman whose kindness, strength, and unforgettable smile touched everyone she met.
Margaret was born on May 16th, 1936, in the small town of Trochu, Alberta. Her early years on the prairies shaped her into the hardworking, compassionate, and resilient woman we all came to know and love.
Margaret married the love of her life, Bob Doble, and together they began their life in Rainier, a small farming community outside of Brooks. There, they raised their two sons, Randy and Shawn, while working side by side on their dairy farm. Margaret was the heart of that farm — helping Bob, supporting her boys, and doing whatever needed to be done. She was never afraid of hard work, and she carried that strength with her throughout her life.
In 1997, due to difficult economic times, the family made the tough decision to sell the farm. Margaret and Bob moved to their acreage on Cassils Road, just east of Brooks. Margaret then took a job in the kitchen at the Brooks Health Centre, where she brought the same dedication, warmth, and care that she had always shown at home. She worked there until illness forced her to retire — a difficult moment for someone who loved to stay active and help others.
Margaret later moved to the Lake Newell Lodge with Bob, and eventually to Sunrise Gardens when her health required permanent care. Through every transition, her spirit remained gentle, loving, and full of grace.
Margaret will always be remembered for her amazing smile — a smile that could light up a room and lift the spirits of anyone near her. She had a gift for connecting with people. It didn’t matter where she was; she either knew someone or made a new friend within minutes. She loved people, and people loved her right back.
She enjoyed playing board games and card games, and yes — she was known to cheat once in a while, which always brought laughter and made the games even more memorable.
Margaret is survived by her two sons, Randy and Shawn, and her four grandchildren — Shaelin, Zachary, Elyse, and Julia — who were a huge part of her life and brought her endless joy. Her love for her family was unwavering, and her pride in them was clear to anyone who knew her.
Margaret will be deeply missed — her spirit, her kindness, and especially her smile that truly lit up the world. But her legacy lives on in her children, her grandchildren, and in every life she touched with her warmth and generosity.
A funeral service will be held at Trinity Lutheran Church on June 15th at 2:00 pm, led by Rev. John Theiss.
Though we feel the weight of her absence, we also feel the blessing of having loved her. Margaret will be truly missed, but her smile — that beautiful, unforgettable smile — will live on through all of us.
Cremation is entrusted to and conducted at
Smith Funeral Home Ltd., Brooks

Obituary | Ralf Klaus Krafft of Brooks, Alberta
Ralf Klaus Krafft
September 17, 1943 - May 27, 2026
With immense gratitude for a life well lived, the family of Ralf Krafft announces his passing on May 27, 2026, in Brooks, Alberta at the age of 82 years. Born in the shadow of war in Europe during WWII on September 17, 1943, Ralf’s family came to Canada when he was 12 years old with little more than hope, determination and a dream of a better life. From those humble beginnings, he went on to build a remarkable life defined by hard work, friendship, and fun. He proudly lived the Canadian dream, building his business, The Clothes Line, that remained one of the great loves of his life. He never dreaded going to work a day in his life and was happiest when connecting with people and creating opportunities. Outside of work, Ralf embraced life fully. He loved rock music, fast cars, motorcycle trips, boating, time at the lake, and winters in Mexico surrounded by family and friends. With his charisma and gift for friendship, he collected lifelong friends wherever he went. A longtime member of the local Kiwanis Club, he valued both the organization’s contributions to the community and the close friendships formed over the years. He leaves behind his wife of 57 years, Maxine Krafft; his daughter Marcy Krafft; son-in-law Tony McGrath; grandchildren Katie Hiscock (Jeremy); Dan McGrath (Claire); great-grandchildren, Chloe Hiscock, who was the apple of his eye; and Teddy Hiscock, who brought joy to his life in his final years. He was predeceased by his parents, Friedel and Fritz Krafft, and his lifelong best friend and cousin, Herb Wetteskind, who was like a brother to him. The family is especially grateful for the many years spent together making cherished memories at the lake and in Mexico. He will be remembered for his zest for life, many great stories and the lasting impact he had on everyone who knew him. We are deeply grateful to the teams at Brooks Health Centre and Arthur J. Child Cancer Centre for caring for him with dignity, compassion, and respect, and for the comfort they provided to our family. In memory of Ralf, if friends so desire, tributes may be made directly to Brooks Animal Protection Service, Box 86, Brooks, Alberta T1R 1B2. A Celebration of Life will be held in Brooks in the fall of 2026.
Cremation is entrusted to and conducted at
Smith Funeral Home Ltd., Brooks

Obituary | Bernard Joseph Koenning of Brooks, Alberta
Bernard Joseph Koenning
July 1, 1941 - May 26, 2026
It is with heavy hearts that we announce the passing of Bernard “Ben” Joseph Koenning of Brooks, on Tuesday, May 26th, 2026, at the Brooks Health Center in Brooks, Alberta, surrounded by his loving family, at the age of 84 years. Ben was born on July 1st, 1941, and was raised on a farm near Cudworth, Saskatchewan. Those who knew Ben will forever cherish his old soul, stoic presence, grace, and humor. He loved spending quality time with loved ones, friends and family alike. Ben may have left the farm, but the farm never left him. He was a mechanic by trade, but he had a knack for fixing anything. Ben had a passion for fishing, hunting and the outdoors. He was musical, loved to dance, and was a living example that silence was not emptiness. Ben is predeceased by his wife Ria; infant daughter Gina; parents John and Maria; brothers, John and Tony; sister, Irene and son-in-law Ken. he is survived by his children, Belinda, Laurie (Dan), Parnell, Clayton (Tammy) and Darla (Darrell); grandchildren; great grandchildren and siblings, Kay, Agnes, Ed (Casey), Theresa, and numerous nieces and nephews. Ben may no longer be with us, but his legacy will live on in the hearts of all who knew him. The family would like to express their sincere thanks to Sunrise Gardens Unit #1, as well as the emergency staff, acute care nursing staff and Dr. Kits at the Brooks Health Center for their exceptional care of Ben. A private family service will be held. Interment to follow in Brooks Cemetery. In memory of Ben, if friends desire, memorial tributes may be made to a charity of choice.

text:
Obituary | Ani Bertha Gunderson (nee Nemeth) of Brooks, Alberta
Ani Bertha Gunderson (nee Nemeth)
November 23, 1955 - May 25, 2026
It is with deep love and heavy hearts that we announce the passing of Ani (Nemeth) Gunderson, on Monday, May 25th, 2026, in Medicine Hat, Alberta a devoted mother, grandmother, and woman of remarkable strength, family and unconditional love. Anica was born in Szombathely, Hungary to Liz and Jim Nemeth on November 23rd, 1955. She began her life in a story of courage in 1957, at just two years old, when they fled Hungary in the wake of the Hungarian revolution, arriving on Canadian soil in search of safety and a brighter future. Her family settled in Rosemary, Alberta, where they worked for a local farmer. From a very young age, Ani learnt responsibility and care for others. Her mother, Elizabeth Nemeth owned and operated the Crystal Café & Steak loft in Brooks, working long 14 hour days to provide for her family as a single mother of three. During those years, Ani helped raise her two younger brothers and, in many ways, they would become her first children. Those early experiences shaped the compassionate, selfless, and deeply devoted woman she would become. Ani attended School in Brooks from Kindergarten to Grade 12, and it was there that she met the man who would become the love of her life. Ani and Terry became inseparable at a young age, building a love story that would span 40 years of marriage. They were married on January 15th, 1975, in Lethbridge, Alberta. A day that marked the beginning of a lifelong partnership. It is fondly remembered that Terry would take Ani out for the evening and when bringing her home he would drive around the block honking his horn repeatedly making sure she and everyone nearby knew just how much he loved her and how proud he was to call her his. The two of them built a close-knit family of 5 children, Richard, Robert, Jackie, Nicole and Terri. If you had seen Ani around, usually one or more of her children were always close by, and in later years her 7 grandchildren. She loved her family with all her being and cherished every moment with them. Ani was a hard-working woman, who spent much of her life caring for and taking pride in creating a loving home for Terry, her children, and the many friends who passed through Momma G’s front door. Later her strong work ethic led her to establish her own residential and commercial cleaning business. She had many long-lasting clients through the years, they became much more than customers-they were dear friends and, in many ways, an extension of her family. It wasn’t uncommon for Ani to leave homemade baking behind after cleaning a client’s home or surprise them with a homemade birthday cake on their special day. In return the love and appreciation people felt for her is something truly special. Ani could often be found at Safeway picking up her daily groceries. What started as a routine became a cherished part of her day, and over the years she became a familiar and beloved face within the store. Whether she was chatting with staff, catching up with friends or meeting someone new. Her kitchen was the heart of her home filled with countless hours of traditional family meals or baking, carrying on the talents she learned from her mother. Roy Orbison and Elvis Presley’s songs often drifted through the house as she worked to provide those exceptional meals. Though our hearts are broken, we find comfort in the countless memories Ani leaves behind. She will be forever loved and deeply missed by her children, grandchildren, extended family, and many dear friends. Ani was predeceased by her beloved husband Terry, who passed away in 2011; her cherished son, Robert Gunderson; parents, Elizabeth (Liz) and James (Jim) Nemeth; brothers, Jack and Steven Nemeth and her fathers-in-law, Richard Gunderson and Robert Bremner. She leaves behind her loving children, Richard Gunderson, Jackie (Steve) Walden, Nicole (Curtis) Lundy and Terri Gunderson; she was a proud and devoted grandmother to Briley, Carter and Kaydee Walden, Trace, Dannika and Blakely Lundy and Devyn Gunderson each of whom she loved beyond measure. She also leaves behind her mother-in-law Carole Gunderson; sisters in-law, Kim (Dennis) Moreau and Penny Gunderson; niece Jennifer Denholm and nephews Jason and Daniel Fleischer and John and Mitch Haldane. The family would like to extend their heartfelt gratitude to the staff of the Brooks Health Centre emergency department and the Intensive Care Unit at Medicine Hat Regional Hospital for their exceptional care shown to our mother during her final days. Your work and dedication brought comfort to our entire family, and for that we are grateful. A Celebration of Life will be held on Thursday, June 4th, 2026, at 2:00 PM from the Heritage Inn Hotel and Convention Centre in Brooks. A luncheon and time of fellowship will follow the service. Family and friends are warmly invited to gather, share memories, and celebrate Ani’s life.
Cremation is entrusted to and conducted at
Smith Funeral Home Ltd., Brooks

Mary Christina Wilson
November 2, 1967 - May 15, 2026
Mary Christina Wilson of Jenner, beloved wife of David Wilson, passed away in Jenner on Friday, May 15th, 2026 at the age of 58 years. Mary was born on November 2nd, 1967 in Saskatoon, Saskatchewan to Leslie and Donna McDiarmid. The family moved to Alberta when Mary was very young. She married David Wilson in 1991 and they resided in Shepard, Alberta from 1987 until 1993, when they moved to Wardlow, Alberta. Mary and David lived in Wardlow from 1993 until 1994 when they moved to Jenner, where Mary resided until her passing. She will be fondly remembered for her giving spirit and love for her community. Mary could be counted to volunteer her time whenever an event was held in her community. She was predeceased by brother Gordon McDiarmid. Mary is survived by her loving husband of 35 years, David Wilson; children, Jaremy, Crystal and Lorn; daughter-in-law, former daughter-in-law Amanda (Jeff); granddaughter Mischa, brothers, David (Fran) and Stanley (Tracey); sister-in-law Kyla and various nieces, nephews and cousins. Obituary | Dixie Kay Alberts of Brooks, Alberta
Dixie Kay Alberts
August 27, 1938 - May 18, 2026
With profound sadness, we announce the passing of our beloved wife, mother, grandmother, and great-grandmother, Dixie Kay Alberts. Dixie passed away peacefully at the Brooks Health Centre on May 18, 2026, with her family by her side. Dixie was born on August 27, 1938, in Iron Springs, Alberta, to Roy and Mable Wright. She was the youngest of 15 siblings and grew up surrounded by a large, close-knit family. Dixie had a lifelong passion for fashion and always took pride in being beautifully dressed for every occasion. Over the years, she worked in several ladies' wear stores in Calgary and Brooks. Later, alongside her daughter Lynsey, she proudly co-owned and operated their bouquet Styles III, in Brooks. Family was at the center of Dixie’s life. She found immense joy in spending time with her children, grandchildren, and great-grandchildren, who were truly the love of her life. She will be remembered for her warmth, kindness, and the constant smile she shared with everyone around her. Dixie also leaves behind many lifelong friends who will cherish her memory. Dixie leaves to cherish her memory her loving husband, Dick Alberts; her children, Richard (Marlene) of Lethbridge, Rod (Carrie) of Brooks, Don (Maria) of Barrhead, and Lynsey (Henry) of Brooks; along with her grandchildren, great-grandchildren, and many nieces and nephews. She will be deeply missed and lovingly remembered by all who knew her. In memory of Dixie, if friends so desire, memorial tributes in Dixie’s name may be made to a charity of one’s choice. A Celebration of Life will be held in Brooks in the summer of 2026.
Cremation is entrusted to and conducted at
Smith Funeral Home Ltd., Brooks

Obituary | Larry Verner Jasperson of Brooks, Alberta
Larry Verner Jasperson
July 21, 1943 - May 14, 2026
Live Streaming of the Funeral Services is scheduled to be available to the public.
You can view the Funeral Service by clicking on “Live Video” on the top right-hand side of 
Smith Funeral Home’s Website or clicking on the “Click Here” in blue letters, 
just below recent obituaries.
Streaming is scheduled to start approximately 10 – 15 minutes prior to services.
Larry Verner Jasperson was born July 21, 1943, in Nanaimo while his father was serving in the Canadian military during the war. He grew up in Tilley, Alberta and spent most of his life in southern Alberta, with a few important years in Kitimat, BC. Larry met his wife Carol Bergum while attending the Canadian Lutheran Bible Institute. While Carol trained as a nurse in Edmonton, Larry worked at Alcan in Kitimat and made the long drives back to see her whenever he could. They married in 1969 and built a life together that lasted 57 years. In 1977, Larry and Carol moved back to Alberta with their children, Theresa and Timothy. Larry worked as a heavy-duty mechanic for PanCanadian until retiring in 1998, though he liked to joke that he “hadn’t worked since.” Together they built a home and farm near Tilley from bare prairie land, planting trees, raising animals, growing huge gardens, and always finding another project that needed doing. Larry was a longtime member of Bethany Lutheran Church, serving on council and teaching Sunday school and confirmation over the years. Larry loved reading, pipe smoking, conversations with strangers, and staying home more than travelling, though he was always supportive of Carol’s adventures. He could be opinionated, stubborn, independent, and very sure of his own views, but he was also hardworking, dependable, and deeply committed to the life he and Carol built together. He is survived by his wife Carol; daughter Theresa Patenaude and husband Tony and their children Oliver and Lilly; son Timothy Jasperson and wife Milena and their daughters Mariana and Juliana; brother Norman Jasperson and wife Renate; sister Audrey Flatla and husband Raymond; brother-in-law Terry Hagen and many nieces, nephews, cousins, and friends. He was predeceased by his parents, Niels and Lilly Jasperson. Larry lived a practical life shaped by hard work, faith, routine, family, and the prairie land he loved. The funeral will be at the Heritage Inn and Convention Centre, Brooks on June 19 at 1:00 pm. In lieu of flowers, donations can be made to the Canadian Cancer Society at https://cancer.ca/en/ or to Canadian Lewy Body Dementia research at https://www.canadianlbdinfo.ca

Larry Verner Jasperson was born July 21, 1943, in Nanaimo while his father was serving in the Canadian military during the war. He grew up in Tilley, Alberta and spent most of his life in southern Alberta, with a few important years in Kitimat, BC. Larry met his wife Carol Bergum while attending the Canadian Lutheran Bible Institute. While Carol trained as a nurse in Edmonton, Larry worked at Alcan in Kitimat and made the long drives back to see her whenever he could. They married in 1969 and built a life together that lasted 57 years. In 1977, Larry and Carol moved back to Alberta with their children, Theresa and Timothy. Larry worked as a heavy-duty mechanic for PanCanadian until retiring in 1998, though he liked to joke that he “hadn’t worked since.” Together they built a home and farm near Tilley from bare prairie land, planting trees, raising animals, growing huge gardens, and always finding another project that needed doing. Larry was a longtime member of Bethany Lutheran Church, serving on council and teaching Sunday school and confirmation over the years. Larry loved reading, pipe smoking, conversations with strangers, and staying home more than travelling, though he was always supportive of Carol’s adventures. He could be opinionated, stubborn, independent, and very sure of his own views, but he was also hardworking, dependable, and deeply committed to the life he and Carol built together. He is survived by his wife Carol; daughter Theresa Patenaude and husband Tony and their children Oliver and Lilly; son Timothy Jasperson and wife Milena and their daughters Mariana and Juliana; brother Norman Jasperson and wife Renate; sister Audrey Flatla and husband Raymond; brother-in-law Terry Hagen and many nieces, nephews, cousins, and friends. He was predeceased by his parents, Niels and Lilly Jasperson. Larry lived a practical life shaped by hard work, faith, routine, family, and the prairie land he loved. Obituary | Mary Kathleen Davidison of Brooks, Alberta
Mary Kathleen Davidison
July 31, 1964 - May 10, 2026
It is with profound sadness that the family of Kathleen “Petey” Davidson announces her passing in Brooks, on May 10, 2026 at the age of 61. Petey was born in New Westminster, BC and was adopted to Don and Marianne Peters and grew up in Kelowna, BC. Kathie was a loving mother, grandmother, sister and friend. Kathie moved to Brooks in 1991 and married Curtis Davidson and they loved each other to the end. Her love of agriculture landed her a job at the Horticultural Center in Brooks, where she worked for 25 years. Gardening and growing plants was where she found peace, and it was always plentiful with the kids raiding it on a regular basis. Her beet pickles and jams, were her crowning jewels. Petey was excellent at baseball and played with passion. There are boxes full of trophies to back it up. Her friendships made through ball endured till the end. Her close friends describe her as a kind hearted soul and will always miss her huge laugh and welcoming ways. She loved to dance to her and Bear’s classic rock and was famous for her signature “high kicks’’. Family and friends will miss her baking and were always excited when she came out with a platter of goodies. Dustin and Andy were her proudest achievements and she glowed when describing their latest successes. The grandkids will always remember her big smile and loving ways. Kathie is predeceased by Don and Marianne Peters. Survived by her husband Curtis “Bear” Davidson; brother Allen Peters; sons, Dustin and Andrew; grandkids Jace, Rylen, Kara, King and Amelia. Kathie had just recently found her biological family on her father’s side through DNA and was excited to meet them in person. On that side of the family Kathie is survived by her father George Pound, brother Nathan Pound, sister Kimberly Pound, brother Jordan Pound, sister Laura Brancheau and sister Kylie Pound. She will be forever loved by her family and anyone she touched throughout her life. A Celebration of Life will be held on August 1, 2026, 2:00 pm at the Bow City Campground. Kathleen Laura McCauley
December 9, 1933 - July 21, 2026
Kathleen Laura McCauley of Brooks, loving wife of the late Patrick McCauley, passed away on Tuesday, July 21st, 2026 in Brooks at the age of 92 years She was born on December 9th, 1933 in a stone house in Gainsborough, SK, by midwife. Kathleen was the youngest of 6 children born to James and Kathleen Simpson. She attended Newlyn School for most of her schooling and obtained grade 11 at Oxbow High. In February 1953, Kay married Mac Moore and moved to Regina. There she had her 3 children Lynn, Doug and Mike. In 1965, she left Regina with her 3 kids and moved to Duchess, AB. Kay worked in Brooks at Ingram’s Department Store. After 20 years she retired and started babysitting for some young families in the area. In April 2000, Kay married Pat McCauley her partner of 28 years. Kay and Pat enjoyed several vacations together and many trips to Blood Indian to camp and fish. Kay was predeceased by her parents, her sister, all 4 brothers, her husband Pat and her granddaughter Raina. She is survived by her daughter Lynn (Mel); sons, Doug and Mike (Darlene); grandchildren, Justin (Robyn), Scott (Kendra), Dara (Tyler) and Faith (Kyle); great grandchildren, Skylar (Shenai), Rhylan, Kiara, Briea, Hunter, Mikala (Calvin) Colby, Addie, Nash, Cruz and Kora; great great grandchildren, Waylen, Scarlett, Kennah and Caspian as well as numerous nieces and nephews. Mom’s heart and home was always open to the many friends of her nieces and her children she was Aunt Kathy and Mom to many. She will be missed. A Celebration of Life will be held on Wednesday, July 29th at 1:00 PM at the Heritage Inn and Convention Centre. Interment at Duchess Cemetery.

Obituary | Edward (Ed) McDonald Follett of Brooks, Alberta
Edward (Ed) McDonald Follett
December 29, 1952 - July 18, 2026
It is with heavy hearts that we announce the passing of Edward (Ed) Follett on Saturday, July 18th, 2026, in Medicine Hat, Alberta, after a short illness, at the age of 73 years. Ed was born in Buchans, Newfoundland on December 29th, 1952, to Edward and Francis Follett. He moved to Springdale, Newfoundland in 1969, then moved to Sudbury, Ontario where he started his career as an automotive body man. Ed moved to Lynn Lake, Manitoba to work as a miner. He moved back to Newfoundland in 1980.Ed became a proud entrepreneur, opening Ed’s Ultramar, performing mechanical and autobody repair. In 1998, Ed moved to Brooks and worked as a mechanic until his retirement. He was a very dedicated and hardworking man and was a great provider for his family. Everyone who knew him was aware of his love for his family. Ed enjoyed spending time with his family, especially his grandchildren whom he cherished. He had a passion for vehicles, new and old, and loved restoring antique cars. Ed also enjoyed travelling to tropical places. He was predeceased by his son Danny; parents, Edward and Francis; brother, Clayton; sisters, Eleanor, Joan and Judy; daughter-in-law, Kelsey; father-in-law, Lloyd and brothers-in-law Ken, Brendan, Roy and Richard. Ed leaves to mourn his wife Dianne; children, David (Mallory) and Stephanie (Terry); daughter-in-law, Julie; grandchildren, Maddison, Katie, Cooper, Holden, Teller, Emery and Felix; sisters, Bertha, Mary, Linda (Georgio), Wavey (Harvey), Rose, (Clayton), Lorraine (Bram) and Sheila; brothers, Cyril (Ada) and Bill (Marilyn); mother-in-law Evelyn; sisters-in-law, Cora, Ella (Eldon) and Tavis (Larry); brother-in-law Ewen (Shiela) and a large circle of extended family and friends. The family would like to thank the Brooks Health Centre Emergency Department and the Medicine Hat Regional Hospital Intensive Care Unit for their treatment of Ed. He will be dearly missed and forever remembered. As per his wishes, cremation will take place. A Celebration of Life will be announced at a later date. text:
Obituary | Marion Agnes Freimuth of Rainier, Alberta
Marion Agnes Freimuth
February 20, 1946 - May 9, 2026
With heavy hearts and deep love, we announce the passing of Marion Agnes Freimuth of Rainer, AB, on May 9, 2026, at the age of 80. Marion was born in Medicine Hat, AB, on February 20, 1946, alongside her best friend and twin sister, Marlyne. She grew up in and around Medicine Hat, where she also received her education. On September 21, 1963, Marion married the love of her life, Albert Freimuth. Together they welcomed three children—Andrea, Kyle, and Tanya. As a family, they enjoyed camping, fishing, and countless hours in the kitchen, where Marion was always eager to pass along her skills and love of cooking. Over the years, the family lived in Maple Creek, Medicine Hat, Tilley, and eventually made their home in the Rainer area. Marion spent many years working as a cook in various restaurants and even operated her own venues from time to time. Alongside her passion for cooking, she built a remarkable 47‑year career as a school bus driver before retiring. In her younger years, she enjoyed curling, and in later years she rarely missed watching a game—family plans were often made around when the curling match would end. She also loved a good game of crib and made sure to be in town every Wednesday to play, even travelling as far as Mayerthorpe for a tournament. Marion was predeceased by her parents, Norman and Martha Kurpjuweit; her sister Alethea Wutch; her twin sister, Marlyne Houston; her husband, Albert Freimuth; her daughter, Andrea Freimuth; and her grandson, Devin Saunders. To cherish her memory, Marion leaves behind her children Kyle (Paula) Freimuth and Tanya (John) Saunders; her 7 grandchildren Tyffany, Tyler (Ariel), Jesse (Natalie), Zandra, Daphne, Dustin (Krisy), and Cody (Madi); as well as 19 great‑grandchildren and 2 great‑great‑grandchildren. She is also survived by her sisters Bea and Edna, along with numerous nieces and nephews. A cherished mom, grandma, great‑grandma, and sister, Marion touched the lives of everyone who knew her with her kindness, humour, and unwavering strength. A Celebration of Life will be held to honour her memory on Saturday, May 23 at 2:00 PM from the Prairie Pioneers Center, 420 1st Ave W, Brooks, AB. Family and friends are warmly invited to join us in remembering Marion, sharing stories, and celebrating a life so deeply loved.

Obituary | Harold Marvin Christianson of Pollockville, Alberta
Harold Marvin Christianson
September 7, 1945 - April 25, 2026
Harold Marvin Christianson of Pollockville, passed away on Saturday, April 25,2026 after losing his battle with cancer. Harold was born September 7,1945 in Hanna, AB to Marvin and Leona Christianson. Harold lived in the Pollockville area his whole life. He married Karol Kinsman on July 2,1966 and brought his bride home to live on the farm and start their family. They spent 53 wonderful years together until Karols’ passing in 2019. Harold drove truck all his life, hauling everything from gravel, cattle, equipment oilfield fluids and everything in between. When he wasn’t driving truck, you could find him either having coffee in the office, farming, or checking his cattle herd on his side by side. One of his favorite past times was camping and spending time with his family. Harold and Karol shared a lot of adventures travelling the United States and Western Canada. Harold is predeceased by his wife Karol and parents, Marvin and Leona Christianson. He is survived by his three children, Kathy (Darcy) Miller, Wesly (Michele) Christianson and Clinton (Colleen) Christianson; his six grandchildren, Vaylene (Mathew) Fuller, Matthew Miller, Adam (Ashley) Miller, Lacey (Jas) Purewal, Dustin (Lisa) Christianson, and Taylor Christianson; six great grandchildren, Asher Fuller, Charlee Miller, Finley and Hailey Purewal, and Peyton and Layne Christianson. He will missed by an aunt and several nieces, nephews, and cousins. Harold was a quiet patient man. He was known to be kind and thoughtful and will be forever missed. Obituary | Teresa Mary Treiber of Bassano, Alberta
Teresa Mary Treiber
October 9, 1929 - July 14, 2026
It is with heavy hearts that we announce the passing of Teresa Mary Treiber (nee Kirwan) in Bassano, Alberta on Tuesday, July 14th, 2026 at the age of 96 years. Teresa was born on October 9th, 1929 in Gull Lake, Saskatchewan to Joseph and Amy Kirwan. She was the 8th of 10 children and as a young lady she ventured to Bassano to live with her sister Mabel, where she helped out with her young family and hotel cafe business. Teresa met Reuben at a dance and their life together began. They were married on December 16th, 1950 and at that time were residing in Chancellor. They lived in many different CPR stations in southern Alberta before settling in Bassano. During these years they were blessed with three children, Bonnie, Gloria and Alan. Teresa was a stay-at-home Mom until her children were all school age and then she went to work for her sister Frances at her cake board factory. After Frances sold her business, Teresa continued to work for the new owners until she retired at age 63. In retirement, Reuben and Teresa took many trips with their motorhome. They travelled to numerous destinations in Canada and the US. There were probably many tense moments on these trips when they travelled through large cities, as this was pre-GPS and Teresa was not a good map reader. Once they got to their evening destination and set up camp, they would always enjoy a beverage together. Navigating was her weakness but packing her holiday trailer and knowing where everything was located, was a skill that she possessed. If Teresa didn't have it in her trailer, chances are you didn't need it. Camping was a big part of their lives and they enjoyed lots of time with family and friends, especially at the Shuswap in the early years and Crawling Valley in the later years. Teresa was a very loyal member of Bassano Royal Purple and during that time she received a 25 Year Perfect Meeting Attendance Award. Teresa was a wonderful host, her door was always open and she was welcoming to everyone. The Saturday Night Supper tradition at Reuben and Teresa’s was a huge part of their children’s, grandchildren’s and great grandchildren's lives. She was the most loving and caring Mom and Grandma and was very involved in all of her family's extra-curricular activities. “Spitfire” was Teresa’s childhood nickname and that feisty side stayed with her all through her life. Occasionally you would get a “special salute” from Teresa and for those of you that knew her well, know what it was. She will truly be remembered for just being herself and for being kind, honest, fair and loving. Reuben passed away in 2011 and after living 5 years alone in her home, Teresa moved into Playfair Lodge. From there she moved into Sunrise Gardens in Brooks and then back to Long Term Care in Bassano, for her last couple of years. Teresa was predeceased by her loving husband of 60 years Reuben; parents Joseph and Amy Kirwan; mother and father-in-law Dena and Herb Treiber; siblings Bart, Kay, Mable, Bill, Francis, Joey, Lee, Jim and Mary; brothers and sisters-in-law, Mary Kirwan, Dick O’Connor, Ralph Eckman, Florence Moen, Henry Schaffer, Athlone Cooper and Joe Silbernagel and Cliff and Ina Trieber, Bob Heryford and Andy Gordichuck on the Treiber side of the family. She is lovingly remembered by her children; Bonnie, Gloria (Kerry) and Alan (Monique); grandchildren, Corey Ann (Joel), Tanis (Pat), Stacie (Quinton), Monica (Kyle), Keith (Paige), Stephen, Austin (Rianne) and Lucas; 16 great grandchildren, sisters-in-law Darlene Kirwan, Verna Heryford and Judy Gordichuck; brother-in-law Rick Trieber and numerous nieces and nephews. Teresa’s family would like to extend their heartfelt appreciation to the staff at the Bassano Health Centre fort the wonderful care Teresa received during her stay. Your kindness brought comfort to Teresa and her family during a difficult time and are grateful to you. A Celebration of Life will be held on Saturday, August 22nd at 2:00 PM from the Elks Hall in Bassano. In memory of Teresa, if friends desire, memorial tributes may be made directly Bassano and District Health Foundation, Box 120, Bassano, Alberta T0J 0B0.

Robbin Lee Colbens of Brooks, loving wife of the late Lloyd Colbens, passed away in Brooks on Friday, July 11th, 2026 at the age of 72 years. Robbin was born on November 17th, 1953 to Russell and Arvie Jones in Minneapolis, Minnesota, the second oldest of five children. Robbin grew up independent, strong-willed, goofy and generous, all attributes she carried into adulthood. Robbin had her first and only child Kristine at the age of 17 years and even at such a young age, Robbin considered her daughter her purpose in life and was determined to do right by her. During her marriages, time as a single parent and the years that followed, Robbin consistently put her daughters’ needs before her own. During a vacation in Mazatlán, Mexico, Robin met a farmer from Tilley, Alberta, who became the love of her life, Lloyd Colbens. In 1989, Robin immigrated to Canada to marry and share her life with Lloyd. Kristine would follow her to Canada, living only 20 minutes away to start her own family 4 years later. Robbin was predeceased by her loving husband Lloyd and parents, Russell and Arvie Jones. She is survived by her daughter, Kristine Tancowny (Clint); grandchildren; Sydney (Eric) and Grace; siblings, Linda Bauman (Boe), Michael Jones, Barb Narawa and Carol Baker (John), along with numerous nieces, nephews and friends whom she all cherished as they were family. Robbin, with her humour, kindness and all that she was that cannot be easily expressed through words, will be dearly missed. A private family service will be held. In memory of Robbin, if friends desire, memorial tributes may be made to either Special Olympics, Brooks, 272 Uplands Avenue, Brooks, Alberta TR1K1 or Brooks Animal Protection Agency, 415 – 1st Avenue West, Brooks, Alberta T1R 1B2.

Obituary | Ronald Stewart Thompson of Bassano, Alberta
Ronald Stewart Thompson
October 4, 1953 - July 4, 2026
Ronald "Ron" Stewart Thompson, beloved partner, father, grandfather, great-grandfather, cowboy, and friend, passed away on Saturday, July 4th, 2026 in Medicine Hat, at the age of 72 years. Ron was the only child of Shorty and Elaine Thompson. He was born on October 4th, 1953, in Bassano, Alberta, where his lifelong love of ranching and rodeo began. Although he spent much of his life living and working in the Bassano and Strathmore areas, he returned to his hometown five years ago to be closer to family. Ron attended Bassano School and graduated in 1973. While he never pursued post-secondary education, some of his most valuable lessons were learned long before graduation—often while checking cattle on the lease under the watchful eye of Jack Peake, even on days he was supposed to be in school. As a teenager, Ron embraced the rodeo lifestyle, trying nearly every event. He even rode the occasional buffalo at convention rodeos when they were short of riders. In 1974, Ron married Darlene Stewart, and they welcomed two sons, Cody and Tyler. In 1995, he met Shirley Boucher, and they began their 31-year partnership. Throughout his career, Ron worked for several well-known operations, including LK Ranches, Snake Lake Ranches, Western Feedlots, and the Calgary Stockyards. A cowboy through and through, he found great satisfaction working with cattle and horses. He was a patient teacher who generously shared his knowledge of rodeo, livestock, and agriculture with anyone eager to learn, especially young people. Ron was equally generous with his time and dedicated many years to supporting the rodeo community. He served on numerous rodeo committees, was an Event Director with the Foothills Cowboys Association, a respected rodeo judge and clinician, an active member of the Canadian Classic Rodeo Association where he competed in team roping, and a valued member of the Bassano Rodeo Committee. Known for his kind heart, friendly smile, and willingness to strike up a conversation, Ron never met a stranger. He loved to visit, tell stories, and share his remarkable knowledge of the history of the Bassano area. Ron was predeceased by his parents, Shorty and Elaine Thompson. He is lovingly remembered by his partner, Shirley Boucher; his sons, Cody (Traci) and Tyler (Riley); his grandsons, Riley (Caitlyn), Scott (Taylor), and Lachlan and his great-granddaughter, Michaela. A Celebration of Ron's Life will be held on Saturday, July 11th, 2026, at 2:00 p.m. at the Bassano Community Hall in Bassano, Alberta. Refreshments will follow the program.

Lawrence "Larry" Seitz
September 27, 1936 - July 3, 2026

- www.stmarysbrooks.ca/livestream

Lawrence “Larry” Seitz—beloved husband, father, grandfather, great‑grandfather, and friend—passed away peacefully on July 3, 2026, in Brooks, Alberta, after living a long, full, and remarkable life. Larry was born in Duchess, Alberta, on September 27, 1936, and grew up in the Clancy/Duchess area. He attended school in Clancy, Rosemary, and Duchess, carrying the values of rural Alberta with him throughout his life: honesty, hard work, loyalty, and a deep commitment to community.
Larry was predeceased by his parents, Clarence and Mildred Seitz; his brothers CJ Seitz, Tom Seitz, and Ed Seitz; his sisters-in-law Irene Seitz and Carol Seitz; and his brother‑in‑law Lorne Lutic. He is lovingly remembered by his brother Earl (Velma) Seitz and his sisters Dianna (Al) Hutchinson and Sharlene Lutic, who continue to carry forward the family’s stories, humour, and shared history.
On November 25, 1961, Larry married the love of his life, Renee. Together they built a beautiful life and raised five sons: Rick (Cheryl), Darcy (Julie), Les (Shelly), Scott (Stasha), and Michael (Lisa). Larry was blessed with many grandchildren and great‑grandchildren, each of whom brought him immense joy and pride. His family was the heart of his world.
In his early years, Larry farmed alongside his father, Grandpa Seitz, learning the value of hard work and the satisfaction of a job done right. Eventually, he transitioned to full‑time work with the County of Newell, where he dedicated over 35 years of service. He began as a bus driver, later becoming a grader operator, assistant supervisor, and ultimately Supervisor of Public Works. Larry’s work ethic was unmatched, and his pride in serving the community was evident to all who worked with him.
Larry also devoted many years to faith and fellowship. He was a Charter Member of the Knights of Columbus Brooks Council 5116 and served as the Financial Secretary for over 30 years. His commitment, reliability, and quiet leadership were deeply valued by all who served alongside him.
Outside of work and community service, Larry poured his energy into the things he loved. He was an active hockey referee for many years, known for his fairness, quick wit, and ability to keep the game moving. When his reffing days came to an end, he joined the Brooks Bandits as part of their security team. Larry and Renee were devoted Bandits fans and season ticket holders, cheering loudly and faithfully from their seats.
Larry was also a gifted storyteller—he could turn any moment into a tale worth hearing. And when he wasn’t telling stories, he was cooking. After taking a Chinese cooking course years ago, Larry became a master chef in his own right, famous for creating the best homemade Chinese food around. His meals were legendary, and his kitchen was a place of joy and gathering.
For many years, Larry also served as an “uber/taxi driver” for rodeo kids across Western Canada. He didn’t just drive them—he supported them, encouraged them, and became one of their biggest fans. His presence at rodeos was always welcomed, and his impact on the young athletes he transported will be remembered fondly.
Larry lived a life defined by service, humour, generosity, and love. He touched countless lives through his work, his volunteerism, his cooking, his stories, and most of all, through the family he cherished. To know Larry was to know kindness, reliability, and a man who always showed up when needed.
We would like to extend our heartfelt appreciation to all the nurses and care aides in Ward B at the Brooks Hospital who cared for Larry with compassion, dignity, and gentleness. Your kindness brought comfort to him and to our family during a difficult time, and we are deeply grateful.
In lieu of flowers, please consider making a donation to a charity of your choice directly, or to the Brooks Health Foundation for Palliative Care Unit, Bag 300, Brooks, Alberta T1R 1B3, in Larry’s memory.
A Funeral Mass for Lawrence “Larry” Seitz will be celebrated on Tuesday, July 14th at 11:00 a.m. at St. Mary’s Roman Catholic Church, Brooks. Rev. Kelvin Chukwurah Celebrant. Interment at Brooks Cemetery. May he rest in peace.

text:
Obituary | Chrystal Dawn Rausch of Medicine Hat, Alberta
Chrystal Dawn Rausch
January 5, 1980 - June 28, 2026
It is with profound sadness that we announce the passing of Chrystal Dawn Rausch, who passed away in Medicine Hat, Alberta on Sunday, June 28th, 2026, at the age of 46 years. Chrystal was born on January 5th, 1980, in Beckley, West Virginia. She was someone who embraced life wholeheartedly. Chrystal found peace on the water with a fishing rod in her hands and could happily spend hours talking about fishing and planning her next trip. She had a love for all things “witchy” and found beauty and meaning in the world around her. Chrystal was a passionate writer who filled journals with her thoughts, dreams, and reflections, and she proudly accomplished one of her dreams by writing a book. Chrystal lived life with a free spirit, a compassionate heart, and a love that left a lasting mark on everyone fortunate enough to know her. She adored tattoos, not only the artwork. but the memories made during girls’ trips spent getting them together. She was known for her long, beautiful hair that people often complimented and for her confidence and infectious sense of humor. She would have smiled knowing she was remembered for always having “the biggest boobies in the room.” It was part of her charm, she never took herself too seriously and made the people around her laugh. Chrystal’s greatest legacy is the love she leaves behind. Her family and friends will remember her not only for the things she loved, but for the way she made people feel. seen, accepted, and loved. More than anything, she was a devoted mother. Her greatest pride and purpose were her children; Joshua, Mikayla, Shannon, and Logan; her many adopted children, Johnathon, Mellissa, Caitlyn, Jessica, Taya, Emily, Mackenzie. She was also a proud grandmother to Emery and Frankie, who brought endless joy and light into her life. Chrystal was predeceased by her beloved grandmother, Betty Jean, and her soul sister, Gisselle Caron. Though they are gone, there is comfort in imagining their reunion. In her memory, we hope everyone who reads this carries one message forward: hug the people you love. Tell them how much they mean to you. Cherish every laugh, every conversation, every ordinary moment, because life can change in the blink of an eye. One day, the memories you make today may become your most treasured possessions. A private family service will be held in Brooks at a later date. Though our hearts are broken, we are forever grateful for the years we shared with Chrystal. Her love, laughter, strength, and beautiful spirit will live on through her children, her grandchildren, and everyone whose life she touched.
“Forever loved. Forever missed. Forever in our hearts.”
Cremation entrusted to and conducted at
Smith Funeral Home Ltd. and Crematorium, Brooks

text:
Rocky Funeral Home
Is embalming required?
No.
If not embalmed, the deceased must be buried or cremated within 72 hours of death.
Where can cremated remains be scattered?
Cremated remains can be scattered anywhere except in a National Park. They can also be buried in a cemetery, on the family farm or any other location chosen by family.
Is a grave liner required?
This depends on the selected cemetery. All cemeteries have their own regulations for grave liners and monuments. Most cemeteries have Perpetual care fees that cover the upkeep of the cemetery. The use of a grave liner assists in the maintenance of the cemetery by decreasing the settling of the graves.
Is it necessary to have a funeral service?
No. However, having a service whether it is a traditional funeral, a memorial service or a come-and-go tea, gives the family an opportunity to share their grief and memories with their community.
A service also provides a forum for friends to assist those who mourn by supporting them with their friendship.
The average cost of a funeral?
The average cost of funeral is determined by the type of casket selected and the place of burial.
Is cremation cheaper than an earth burial?
Yes. Cremation is less expensive due to the fact that a casket or cemetery plot is not required. If a casket is desired for the purpose of viewing or the deceased being present at the funeral service, we have a rental casket.
Is visitation or viewing possible with a cremation service?
Yes. It is recommended. If at all possible viewing should take place. This provides a chance for the family to say their final goodbyes and also provides the funeral home with positive identification before cremation takes place.
Is it necessary to buy a casket to have viewing before cremation takes place?
No. We use a draped stretcher or the rental casket is requested.
Can we view or take part in the cremation process?
For this to happen, special arrangements need to be made. We would require that a disclaimer be signed regarding the possibility of delayed stress reaction.
Will you come to my home to make funeral arrangements?
Yes, we will attend your home to make funeral arrangements on request.
Sometimes it is more convenient for you to come to the funeral home to make arrangements especially when a casket or urn needs to be selected. We do have pictures you can view but pictures can be deceiving and may not accurately represent the product.
Will you assist with obituaries?
As part of the arrangements, we will assist you with preparing obituaries and emailing them to the respective newspaper along with a picture.
Do you schedule funerals on Sunday?
We only do Sunday funerals under special circumstances and there may be additional charges for a Sunday service, i.e. overtime by cemetery owner for opening and closing grave, overtime by the vault company if vault required.
Why is pre-planning important?
Planning ahead is one of the most considerate and compassionate things you can do for your family. You can spare them the burden of having to make complex arrangements at a most difficult time.
Consult with us at any time about your wishes.
To assist with this process, please download our planning document (PDF).
