Rocky Funeral Home
At Home
Natural or Unexpected
When the passing was not expected, the RCMP can be called. They will come to the home to ensure nothing is suspicious. Then they will contact the Chief Medical Examiners Office to determine if they want the deceased brought to them for ‘autopsy’. Possibly the family doctor will say it is not necessary. After the Medical Examiner has cleared the scene, the Funeral Home (or removal company who works for the Medical Examiner's Office), is called in to remove the deceased. They will either take the body to the Medical Examiner's Office in Calgary or to the local funeral home.
Expected
If the deceased was in a doctor's care and the death was expected there is no need to call 9-1-1. The funeral home can be called to come in and removed the deceased from the home, taking them to the funeral home. The family doctor cared for the deceased will sign a “medical” that states the cause of the death.
In Hospital
Non-Emergency
When someone passes while in hospital, the doctor will sign a "medical" stating the cause of death. The family or the hospital can call the funeral home to advise of the passing. When the body is ready for release, the hospital will call to let the funeral home know.
Emergency
When there is a sudden passing, the doctor may call for a more complete examination, which may include a autopsy. Then the body would be moved to Calgary. This lengthens the process by a few days, but the reason for the death maybe made more clear. Alternatively, if the deceased had a medical history, the doctor might sign the "medical" immediately. In that case the funeral home can be contacted for pickup.
In a Care Facility, Nursing Home or Hospice
The doctor will be informed of the person’s passing, and they will sign a "medical" stating the cause of death. The funeral home will be called by the family or the care centre staff, for the removal of the deceased, to the funeral home.
In a Tragic Accident
The police will be on scene. When they have gathered all the investigative information, the Medical Examiner's Office is called for permission to remove the body. Then a removal company or the funeral home is called to transport the deceased to the Medical Examiners Office in Calgary. When the body is released, the Medical Examiner’s Office contacts the deceased's family and advises them to contact the funeral home to pick up the body.
We'll Help You Through the First Steps
Contact us, to tell us that your loved one has passed away and where they are. We will contact the facility where the deceased is, to see if a “medical” form is completed by a doctor. Or, if the deceased is in your home, we will make sure the proper people have been notified. When all the legal requirements are satisfied we will pick up your loved one.
We will set up a time for your family to meet with us to make arrangements. We can meet at your home if you prefer.
We'll ask you for life information, obituary and photo.
During arrangements, we'll discuss information needed for the Registration of Death, and sign paperwork for the government agencies and paperwork for cremation, if you decide on that option.
Then we'll discuss your thoughts on funeral, memorial, or celebration of life services and choose a service date.
We'll help you select a casket that best suits your loved one and fits your family’s budget. We look at casket sprays, as well.
For burials we'll help you order a plot at a cemetery. If there is a surviving spouse who wants to rest beside the deceased then a second plot will be need to be reserved.
Regardless of your circumstances we'll be there for you every step of the way.

# Rocky Funeral Home

### At Home

##### Natural or Unexpected

When the passing was not expected, the RCMP can be called. They will come to the home to ensure nothing is suspicious. Then they will contact the Chief Medical Examiners Office to determine if they want the deceased brought to them for ‘autopsy’. Possibly the family doctor will say it is not necessary. After the Medical Examiner has cleared the scene, the Funeral Home (or removal company who works for the Medical Examiner's Office), is called in to remove the deceased. They will either take the body to the Medical Examiner's Office in Calgary or to the local funeral home.

##### Expected

If the deceased was in a doctor's care and the death was expected there is no need to call 9-1-1. The funeral home can be called to come in and removed the deceased from the home, taking them to the funeral home. The family doctor cared for the deceased will sign a “medical” that states the cause of the death.

### In Hospital

##### Non-Emergency

When someone passes while in hospital, the doctor will sign a "medical" stating the cause of death. The family or the hospital can call the funeral home to advise of the passing. When the body is ready for release, the hospital will call to let the funeral home know.

##### Emergency

When there is a sudden passing, the doctor may call for a more complete examination, which may include a autopsy. Then the body would be moved to Calgary. This lengthens the process by a few days, but the reason for the death maybe made more clear. Alternatively, if the deceased had a medical history, the doctor might sign the "medical" immediately. In that case the funeral home can be contacted for pickup.

### In a Care Facility, Nursing Home or Hospice

The doctor will be informed of the person’s passing, and they will sign a "medical" stating the cause of death. The funeral home will be called by the family or the care centre staff, for the removal of the deceased, to the funeral home.

### In a Tragic Accident

The police will be on scene. When they have gathered all the investigative information, the Medical Examiner's Office is called for permission to remove the body. Then a removal company or the funeral home is called to transport the deceased to the Medical Examiners Office in Calgary. When the body is released, the Medical Examiner’s Office contacts the deceased's family and advises them to contact the funeral home to pick up the body.

### We'll Help You Through the First Steps

Contact us, to tell us that your loved one has passed away and where they are. We will contact the facility where the deceased is, to see if a “medical” form is completed by a doctor. Or, if the deceased is in your home, we will make sure the proper people have been notified. When all the legal requirements are satisfied we will pick up your loved one.

During arrangements, we'll discuss information needed for the Registration of Death, and sign paperwork for the government agencies and paperwork for cremation, if you decide on that option.

Then we'll discuss your thoughts on funeral, memorial, or celebration of life services and choose a service date.

We'll help you select a casket that best suits your loved one and fits your family’s budget. We look at casket sprays, as well.

For burials we'll help you order a plot at a cemetery. If there is a surviving spouse who wants to rest beside the deceased then a second plot will be need to be reserved.

Regardless of your circumstances we'll be there for you every step of the way.

# Rocky Funeral Home

A traditional funeral is a funeral where the deceased is present for the service followed by either burial in a cemetery or cremation.

### Non-traditional Funeral

A non-traditional funeral is a funeral that meets the needs of different ethnic groups such as the First Nations people.

### Memorial Service

A memorial service is a funeral where the deceased in not present because burial or cremation has taken place before the actual service. Sometimes this type of service would be called a "Service of Remembrance" or "A Celebration of Life".

### Cremation

Cremation is the disposition of a deceased person by burning of the body in a special retort built for that purpose. A cremation can take place following a funeral service or before a service. The ashes can then be buried, scattered or kept at home.

text:
Rocky Funeral Home
The loss of a loved one places you in a very difficult emotional space. The grief can disrupt your frame of reference and make you feel disoriented, affecting your judgment.
Your loss might make you feel uncertainty and ambiguity, which are very uncomfortable. This can cause you to be very vulnerable to people who propose to create stability by making you feel better, feel certain.
Unfortunately, fraudsters and scammers target people who are in mourning. Personal information is provided in obituaries and scammers can use this information to learn additional details through social media. Being armed with so much knowledge makes it easier for scammers to convince a potential victim that their request is legitimate.
Personal Information
Most scams involve getting someone's personal information under false pretenses. The scammer usually portrays a sense of urgency, pretending to be someone legitimate to trick someone into providing personal information.
You may be asked to help a dear friend or family member, with sacrifices that go beyond what is reasonable. Criminals can pose as a family member, using the emotional vulnerability caused by a death to obtain money. In some cases the scammer tells the victim they are stranded while trying to return home for a funeral. Be sure that the person asking is who they say they are, and possibly confer with trusted advisers about the reasonableness of any such request.
Social Media
If you use social media to connect with your friends at this difficult time remember that the lines between personal and public are easily blurred on social media sites. Unless you are very confident in your understanding of privacy settings, beware of revealing personal information during your online conversations.
A Little Extra Caution
Be extra cautious about giving out any personal information at this time. Whether responding to a phone caller or entering condolences on our website, do not reveal personal information to strangers.
Possibly you should seek advice from trusted friends before making any major decisions, entering agreements, or sending money to anyone.
If you think a member of your family is vulnerable, consider reaching out with a gentle warning about the possibility of scams. Often simple awareness is the best protection.

# Rocky Funeral Home

The loss of a loved one places you in a very difficult emotional space. The grief can disrupt your frame of reference and make you feel disoriented, affecting your judgment.

Your loss might make you feel uncertainty and ambiguity, which are very uncomfortable. This can cause you to be very vulnerable to people who propose to create stability by making you feel better, feel certain.

Unfortunately, fraudsters and scammers target people who are in mourning. Personal information is provided in obituaries and scammers can use this information to learn additional details through social media. Being armed with so much knowledge makes it easier for scammers to convince a potential victim that their request is legitimate.

### Personal Information

Most scams involve getting someone's personal information under false pretenses. The scammer usually portrays a sense of urgency, pretending to be someone legitimate to trick someone into providing personal information.

You may be asked to help a dear friend or family member, with sacrifices that go beyond what is reasonable. Criminals can pose as a family member, using the emotional vulnerability caused by a death to obtain money. In some cases the scammer tells the victim they are stranded while trying to return home for a funeral. Be sure that the person asking is who they say they are, and possibly confer with trusted advisers about the reasonableness of any such request.

### Social Media

If you use social media to connect with your friends at this difficult time remember that the lines between personal and public are easily blurred on social media sites. Unless you are very confident in your understanding of privacy settings, beware of revealing personal information during your online conversations.

### A Little Extra Caution

Be extra cautious about giving out any personal information at this time. Whether responding to a phone caller or entering condolences on our website, do not reveal personal information to strangers.

Possibly you should seek advice from trusted friends before making any major decisions, entering agreements, or sending money to anyone.

If you think a member of your family is vulnerable, consider reaching out with a gentle warning about the possibility of scams. Often simple awareness is the best protection.

Rocky Funeral Home
Rocky Funeral Home is owned and operated by Gordon and Diane Flinn. They have lived in Rocky Mountain House for more than 30 years. They have four children and six grandchildren.
Gordon was born and raised in Innisfail and has been involved in the funeral industry since he was 16 years old. His father also worked at the funeral home in Innisfail. Gordon has worked for several funeral homes in Central Alberta so has a vast array of experiences.
Diane was raised on a farm at Clive, Alberta and started her career in the funeral industry by answering phones when Gordon worked for Fenton and Kirkman Funeral Home in Lacombe. After moving to Rocky Mountain House in 1987, she began to work full time at Rocky Funeral Home doing office work and became a licensed funeral director.
The Flinn Family
Gordon and Diane’s 3 of their 4 children have taken over the running of the family business (basically letting them retire), so they can spend some well earned years doing things they would like to do. Gordon, spends his time going for coffee and working in the garage on woodworking projects. Diane, loves to be at home, taking care of things she put off for years, as well as baking, reading, puzzle making, and walking Rueben, their beloved King Charles Cavalier dog.
Running the day to day operations now is Laurie and Nancy, who are co-managing. They have big shoes to fill, but with a lifetime of watching and doing, they hope to keep up the legacy of caring for families.
Laurie is a licensed funeral director & the business manager, as well as a Celebrant- she will officiate for families that do not have religious ties. In her free time, she loves to tend to her orchids, and to putter around in her yard in the warm spring and summer.
Nancy is a licensed funeral director, our Remco representative, and licensed Pre Need Advisor, plus she does most of the behind the scenes paperwork. Nancy is a busy mom of four children, so she is rarely at home, busy taking them to their activities. If around home, she enjoys being with her kids and tending to her flower beds in the summer.
John works mainly out of our Sylvan Lake Funeral Home as a funeral attendant, assisting around the funeral home and cemetery set ups. In John’s free time, he loves coaching Pee Wee Football with the Sylvan Lake Bears and going out camping/ hiking in the west country.
Gordon and Diane’s second daughter Karen resides in Edmonton. She has her funeral directors license, so she can step in if we ask her. Her life in Edmonton is filled with her two dogs Oreo and Twix, plus relaxing around home or in her backyard.
Our Staff
Dee Greening - Licensed Embalmer & Funeral Director
Dee has been with us since 2016. Coming from a background that included hospitality and management, her skill set translated into the funeral industry well. Dee is however, mostly a mom who loves being with her kids and day dreaming about Halloween.
Bonnie Hewitt - Funeral Director
I’ve been a part of the Flinn Funeral Services Ltd since 2020. I started my journey as a volunteer. Knowing at a young age I wanted to have all the experience needed in order for me to successfully succeed in the field. Once I knew that I was going to have a career, I registered with the University of Mount Royal where I graduated from the Funeral Service Program.
Prior to my new career I was a caregiver, and I am very honoured to be able to extend the care I can give to families, in their time of grief.
I am the proud mom of two adult children and even prouder grandma of my two grandsons.
Renee Edwards
Renee is a dedicated professional with a strong focus on family and personal well-being. Married with two grown children, she brings a grounded and thoughtful perspective to her work.
Outside of her professional life, Renee enjoys reading, paddleboarding, and spending time with her small dog, Lily.
Loy Asplund
Loy is a dedicated professional known for her creativity, strong work ethic, and passion for community connection. In addition to her primary role, Loy serves as a barista at Rocky Mountain Mudd, where her warm personality and attention to detail brighten the day for every customer. A proud wife and mother of grown children, Loy balances her professional life with a rich array of personal interests.
She is an avid gardener, talented painter, and skilled furniture restorer, with a love for crafting and all things thrifted. Her eye for beauty in the everyday infuses her work and hobbies with charm and originality. Whether she’s restoring a vintage piece, tending to her garden, or crafting a new project, Loy approaches every endeavor with care, creativity, and a deep appreciation for life’s simple pleasures.
Mathew Larocque
Mathew is a Funeral Service student currently completing his practicum placement as part of his professional training. He is committed to serving families with empathy, respect, and care during times of loss.
With a background that includes teaching overseas and community volunteering, Mathew brings a broad perspective and a strong sense of compassion to his work. His calm, thoughtful approach is shaped by diverse life experiences and a genuine dedication to supporting others.
Mathew values professionalism, dignity, and meaningful connection in all interactions. He is focused on continuing to grow within the funeral profession, with a long-term commitment to providing respectful, personalized service to every family he assists.
Charles Komm
Born and raised in Southern Alberta, Charles began his funeral career in Red Deer in 1989 following in his uncle's footsteps.
Charles 35 year journey in funeral service has led him to many different funeral homes in Alberta and he has gained experience, knowledge and friendships during this time.
Charles enjoyed instructing new students coming into the funeral industry. When asked why Charles chose this career, his response was "I just like to be there for the families and friends to help them through a difficult time". Which keeps him going today.

Charles 35 year journey in funeral service has led him to many different funeral homes in Alberta and he has gained experience, knowledge and friendships during this time.

Charles enjoyed instructing new students coming into the funeral industry. When asked why Charles chose this career, his response was "I just like to be there for the families and friends to help them through a difficult time". Which keeps him going today.

Carol Barbara Thorkelson
Carol was born in Gimli, MB to August (Gusti) and Thora.
Carol set the standard for being one of the most loving and selfless mothers.
Carol worked a handful of jobs; she chose to give back to her community by being a foster parent for much of her adult life. Carol and her loving husband, Hal, welcomed the children into our home with open arms. She enjoyed cooking and baking and loved watching her children (foster and biological) eat and enjoy her amazing food. Her Friday night pizza nights were legendary. Service

Obituary
Lorri Ann Bott (Rolfsen)
December 17, 1967 - July 15, 2026 
It is with broken hearts that we announce the passing of Lorri Bott on July 15, 2026, surrounded by the love of her family following a short and courageous battle with cancer. 
Born in Rocky Mountain House on December 17, 1967, Lorri built a life centred on kindness, compassion and family. She spent many years working for the school division where her caring nature, dedication and genuine love for others touched the lives of countless students, families and colleagues. 
Above all else, Lorri was a devoted mother. Her daughters, Ashley, Kelsey and Jenna were her greatest accomplishment and the centre of her world. She loved them fiercely and taught them, through her own example, the importance of strength, kindness and unconditional love. 
Later in life, becoming “Grandma” to Brennix and Jaix filled her heart in a way only grandchildren can. They brought endless smiles, laughter and pride, and she treasured every moment spent with them. 
Lorri had a gift for finding beauty in every day. She never missed a rainbow after the rain and loved warm summer evenings spent watching the fireflies and admiring the moon. Those quiet moments became treasured memories for her family, and now every rainbow, every firefly and every moonlit night will bring thoughts of her and the love she leaves behind.
Lorri will be deeply missed by her daughters Ashley (Derek), Kelsey, and Jenna (Bryce); her beloved grandsons, Brennix and Jaix; as well as many extended family members and dear friends.
She was predeceased by her parents, Allan and Viola Rolfsen, and sister Charlotte. 
In keeping with Lorri's wishes, no formal funeral service will be held. 
Forever loved, forever missed and forever in our hearts.
Condolences
Laurie (Mason) Herold:
My deepest sympathy to Lorri's family. She was a beautiful person, with a quick smile.
Natalie Nielsen :
I’m so sad to read of the passing of such a beautiful lady!! She helped 3 of my children in elementary school, and made such a lasting impact that my oldest ( now 15) always said hi to her and remembered her anytime we were out and about around town. She remembered her too, which made it even more heartwarming. 
She always had the brightest eyes and biggest smile around the kids she worked with. 
My condolences to her family on such a devastating loss ! 
Mackenzie Nielsen will be sad to her of this, as will the rest of our children. 
Barbara Donnelly:
Lorri was an amazing EA and I am thankful I got to work with her. She was a caring person and will be truly missed. 
Sandra Luoma:
Lorri and I grew up together and we spent many days exploring around Leslieville. She truly was a bright light and a wonderful friend. May she rest easy now… my deepest condolences to her daughters and grandsons and all her family and friends. 
Laura Henning:
I am so saddened to hear of Lori's passing. I had the privilege and honor of working alongside her. Lori treated everyone with love, compassion, kindness, and respect. Her bright, beautiful smile lit up the halls and every room she walked into.
She spoke of you girls and her grandbabies with such pride, love, and adoration. It was always clear how deeply she loved her family.
I will forever consider it an honor and a privilege to have known your mom. She will be deeply missed, and I will always treasure the memories of the time we shared.
I am so incredibly sorry that you have to say goodbye. My thoughts and heartfelt condolences are with you and your family during this difficult time.
Marlene Levinsky:
Condolences to Lorri’s family. She was such a pleasant person. She was always so proud of her girls. 
Corry Woods:
I had the great pleasure of working with Lorri at ERE. My deepest condolences to her girls and their families. Her soft, caring and compassionate nature along with that beautiful smile will be missed by the all lives she touched.
RIP my friend.
Dawn& Donn Mason:
So sorry to learn of Lorri’s passing…thinking of you all at this especially difficult time….

jsonLd.articleBody:
PROUDLER, Barb

1932 – 2026


Alice ‘Barb’ Proudler passed away at the Red Deer Hospice Society, Red Deer Alberta on Sunday, July 5, 2026 at the age of 93 and a half years (as she said), after a short but courageous battle with illness. All the nurses in the hospital and hospice loved her, she was always pleasant, had a big smile, liked to joke around and never complained.

Barb was born on December 1, 1932 at the Stettler Municipal Hospital, Stettler, Alberta. She was the daughter of Ray and Alice Thomas. Barb was the only girl in the family and she had four brothers. This dynamic creates a strong, feisty, stubborn woman. It definitely came in handy throughout her adult years right up till the end. In 1940, the family moved to Erskine, Alberta, where Barb completed her schooling. She moved to Red Deer, Alberta where she worked and completed her nurses training and later worked as a Sense Training Therapist. It was there that she met and married Don Proudler. Barb worked at the Michener Center in Red Deer, she ended her career teaching cooking to residents with high capabilities. She also wrote a cookbook for these students.

In 1985, Barb and Don retired and moved to the Proudler homestead at Caroline, Alberta. Barb was a very active volunteer while in Caroline. She became active as a member of the Wheels of Time Museum, Caroline Seniors Drop-In, Caroline Legion and other organizations in Caroline. When Barb volunteered, she didn't just volunteer, she was able to spearhead many campaigns. Give her a job and you know it would be done to perfection. During their retirement they became snowbirds and traveled to Apache Junction in Arizona to escape the cold winters in Canada and made many new friends. It was there that she learned to paint pictures in acrylics and oil.

Barb enjoyed growing a huge garden (we think she planted enough potatoes to feed the whole village of Caroline). She loved all things in nature, the birds, especially the hummingbirds and chickadees. She also had a herd of deer who would drop in to say hello. Barb has hosted a Thomas family reunion at her place each year for many years, where lots of fun and shenanigans go on. She also researched and prepared a Thomas history book for all to keep. Barb is lovingly remembered by her son, Steve Proudler and his wife Barb, her grandchildren, Drew (Amanda Bougerolle) and Jennifer Wilkinson (Cory Buffett), her great grandchildren, Zoey Wilkinson, Payton Wilkinson, Alex Hyryck, Kennedy Hyryck (Jordan Morin), and her great granddaughter, Autumn Morin, her brothers, Jim Thomas, Don (Linda) Thomas, Al (Carol) Thomas as well as many nieces and nephews. She is predeceased by her parents, Ray and Alice Thomas, her in-laws, Albert and Ada Proudler, her husband, Don Proudler and her son, David Proudler, as well as her brother and sister-in-law, Larry and Ann Thomas, and sister-in laws, Dorothy Proudler, and Agnes Thomas . She leaves us today with fond memories of a life well lived and those who she loved.

A Celebration of Barb’s Life will be held on Saturday, July 11, 2026 at 1:00 pm at the Caroline Royal Canadian Legion, Branch No. 177, 5116 - 49 Street, Caroline, Alberta. If desired, Memorial Donations in Barb’s honour may be made to the Red Deer Hospice Society at 99 Arnot Avenue, Red Deer, Alberta, T4R 3S6 or at https://reddeerhospice.com/. Condolences, memories and photos may be shared and viewed at www.parklandfuneralhome.com. Cremation entrusted to Parkland Funeral Home and Crematorium, Red Deer, Alberta. Arrangements in care of Parkland Funeral Home and Crematorium, 6287 – 67 A Street (Taylor Drive), Red Deer. 403.340.4040.

# Alice 'Barb' Barbara Proudler (Thomas) Obituary | Parkland Funeral Home (Red Deer) | 1932

PROUDLER, Barb

1932 – 2026

Alice ‘Barb’ Proudler passed away at the Red Deer Hospice Society, Red Deer Alberta on Sunday, July 5, 2026 at the age of 93 and a half years (as she said), after a short but courageous battle with illness. All the nurses in the hospital and hospice loved her, she was always pleasant, had a big smile, liked to joke around and never complained.

Barb was born on December 1, 1932 at the Stettler Municipal Hospital, Stettler, Alberta. She was the daughter of Ray and Alice Thomas. Barb was the only girl in the family and she had four brothers. This dynamic creates a strong, feisty, stubborn woman. It definitely came in handy throughout her adult years right up till the end. In 1940, the family moved to Erskine, Alberta, where Barb completed her schooling. She moved to Red Deer, Alberta where she worked and completed her nurses training and later worked as a Sense Training Therapist. It was there that she met and married Don Proudler. Barb worked at the Michener Center in Red Deer, she ended her career teaching cooking to residents with high capabilities. She also wrote a cookbook for these students.

In 1985, Barb and Don retired and moved to the Proudler homestead at Caroline, Alberta. Barb was a very active volunteer while in Caroline. She became active as a member of the Wheels of Time Museum, Caroline Seniors Drop-In, Caroline Legion and other organizations in Caroline. When Barb volunteered, she didn't just volunteer, she was able to spearhead many campaigns. Give her a job and you know it would be done to perfection. During their retirement they became snowbirds and traveled to Apache Junction in Arizona to escape the cold winters in Canada and made many new friends. It was there that she learned to paint pictures in acrylics and oil.

Barb enjoyed growing a huge garden (we think she planted enough potatoes to feed the whole village of Caroline). She loved all things in nature, the birds, especially the hummingbirds and chickadees. She also had a herd of deer who would drop in to say hello. Barb has hosted a Thomas family reunion at her place each year for many years, where lots of fun and shenanigans go on. She also researched and prepared a Thomas history book for all to keep. Barb is lovingly remembered by her son, Steve Proudler and his wife Barb, her grandchildren, Drew (Amanda Bougerolle) and Jennifer Wilkinson (Cory Buffett), her great grandchildren, Zoey Wilkinson, Payton Wilkinson, Alex Hyryck, Kennedy Hyryck (Jordan Morin), and her great granddaughter, Autumn Morin, her brothers, Jim Thomas, Don (Linda) Thomas, Al (Carol) Thomas as well as many nieces and nephews. She is predeceased by her parents, Ray and Alice Thomas, her in-laws, Albert and Ada Proudler, her husband, Don Proudler and her son, David Proudler, as well as her brother and sister-in-law, Larry and Ann Thomas, and sister-in laws, Dorothy Proudler, and Agnes Thomas . She leaves us today with fond memories of a life well lived and those who she loved.

A Celebration of Barb’s Life will be held on Saturday, July 11, 2026 at 1:00 pm at the Caroline Royal Canadian Legion, Branch No. 177, 5116 - 49 Street, Caroline, Alberta. If desired, Memorial Donations in Barb’s honour may be made to the Red Deer Hospice Society at 99 Arnot Avenue, Red Deer, Alberta, T4R 3S6 or at [https://reddeerhospice.com/](https://reddeerhospice.com/). Condolences, memories and photos may be shared and viewed at www.parklandfuneralhome.com. Cremation entrusted to Parkland Funeral Home and Crematorium, Red Deer, Alberta. jsonLd.articleBody:
YOUNG, Dorothy

1936 – 2026


Dorothy ‘Dottie’ Anne Young of Red Deer passed away on Friday, July 3, 2026 at the age of 89 years.


Dottie was born on November 1, 1936 in Rose Prairie, British Columbia joining her brother, Robert and her sister, Mary on the family farm. She was a true farm girl to the end who loved all the baby animals, gardening, the rodeo, cowboys and a comfy pair of blue jeans.


She spent her years not just in Rose Prairie and Fort St. John, but lived in Whitehorse and finally, Red Deer, where she could be close to her sons and their families. She was forever proud of ‘her three sons’ and was broken hearted when Randy passed away in 2024.


Dottie cherished her time spent with good friends and family. Whether it be a road trip, a shared glass of wine or fresh raw oysters on the pier in Vancouver, she treasured those days. And of course she was always ‘well put together’. She loved her colourful, tailored clothing and was, without fail, fresh and fashionable and most definitely co-ordinated! Anywhere with sunshine was her favourite place to sit, warming her heart and her hands.


Dottie spent many years volunteering in her lifetime and was a part of making the North Peace Historical Society; the Fort St. John North Peace Museum what it is today. It still houses treasures from her mother’s time as the first Red Cross nurse/midwife in the North Peace region. In more recent years Dottie volunteered countless hours with the Red Deer Christmas Bureau Society. Numerous families were able to enjoy Christmas a bit more thanks to her and many others. Closer to home, friends and neighbours were often the recipients of cookies and muffins or squares, her wonderful baking, that she so generously delivered to their door.


We will all remember Dottie as an astute businesswoman, who owned and operated several businesses at different times in her life. Her business savvy was apparent along with her attention to detail and her efficiency and organizational skills were to be admired.


Dottie is survived by her two sons, Rocky (Marie) Snippa and Shane (Cora) Snippa; her two grandsons, Christopher Freeman and Joshua Snippa: two great grandsons, Hayden and Sidney; her sister, Mary (Tom) Mickey and sister-in-law, Gerry Ann Young. And of course many relatives and so many special friendships that meant the world to her.


Dottie was predeceased by her parents, Jim and Anne Young, her brother, Robert and her son, Randy.


A Come and Go Celebration of Dottie’s Life will be held on Friday, September 18, 2026 at Parkland Funeral Home, 6287 – 67A Street, Red Deer, Alberta from 1:00p.m. to 3:00 p.m.


If desired, Memorial Donations may be made in memory of Dottie to either the Fort St. John Peace Museum at www.fsjmuseum.com or to the Red Deer Christmas Bureau Society at www.reddeerchristmasbureau.com.


When I come to the end of the road

And the sun has set for me

I want no rites in a gloom filled room

Why cry for a soul set free?

Miss me a little, but not too long

And not with your heads bowed low

Remember the love that we all shared

Miss me, But let me go.

This is a journey that we all must take

And each must go alone

It’s all a part of the Master’s plan

A step on the road to home.

When you are lonely and sick at heart

Go to the friends we know

Bury your sorrows in doing good deeds

Miss me - but let me go.



Cremation entrusted to Parkland Funeral Home and Crematorium, Red Deer, Alberta.

Condolences, memories and photos may be shared and viewed at www.parklandfuneralhome.com. Arrangements in care of Parkland Funeral Home and Crematorium, 6287 – 67 A Street (Taylor Drive), Red Deer. 403.340.4040.

jsonLd.articleBody:
GOODALL, Ninon

1934-2026

With heavy hearts we announce the passing of Ninon Hildegard Goodall (Shaw) on Friday, June 26, 2026. She was the only child of Walter and Traute Shaw, born in Vancouver, British Columbia on May 3, 1934. Sadly, she lost her father in World War 2 at the age of 9. Ninon’s mother struggled to make ends meet by taking in college students and did her best to raise a spirited and strong-willed child. At a young age, Ninon gave birth to a child who was later placed for adoption. A difficult experience that shaped her life and demonstrated her resilience. (She would reunite with her firstborn child in the mid 1980’s).


In her late teens, Ninon married Norman Latham and moved to Fort Nelson, British Columbia. She and Norman had four children together. (Colleen, Shawn, Pat and Mike) After the conclusion of that relationship, she met Stan in 1961 at a Valentine’s dance and their romance blossomed. In the early years, they managed to keep their heads above water by running a motel and dairy bar with everyone pitching in. Ninon and Stan welcomed their son Glen in 1970. Ninon went on to operate a daycare in her home for several years.


In 1979 they decided to make the long trek to Thompson, Manitoba. Ninon then took a job in the kitchen of a local hotel. The work was demanding and exhausting, but she loved it! The friends and memories she made in Thompson were some of her fondest.


In 1997, Stan and Ninon retired, packed up, and moved to Red Deer, Alberta. They embraced their family, the community, and became quite involved at the Good Shepherd Church. In 2012, they moved to Sylvan Lake and loved spending time around the waterfront. Ninon basking in the sun and Stan with a book in the shade.


Some of Ninon’s biggest joys in her life were her grandchildren and great grandchildren. She spent countless hours dedicating her time and attention to their activities and interests. Ninon has always loved animals of every kind. She has welcomed many household pets over the years and has never met a wet nose she wouldn’t kiss. She took pride in her baking and was a wonderful cook. Knitting and quilting were frequent past times that she also enjoyed.


Ninon’s greatest joy was giving to others, whether through a thoughtful gift, a helping hand, or simply her time and kindness. One of her treasures was the many lifelong friendships she nurtured over the years. Those that knew her will remember her vibrant spirit and unforgettable personality. She had a gift for making people laugh, a warmth that drew others to her, and a kindness that left a lasting impression.


She is predeceased by her mother and father, as well as her son-in-law Herb. Left to cherish her memory is her husband of 51 years, Stan Goodall; brother-in-law Donnie; her children, Blair (Allison), Colleen, Shawn, Pat, Mike (Lisa), and Glen (Jennifer); her grandchildren, Toni, Terry, Lawrence (Soleil), Melaina (Dimitrius), Derek (Shari), Stacy (Ed), Michelle, Chantelle, Rebecca, Kassidy and Jacksyn; great grandchildren: Quinton, Carly, Ben, Lucas, Deone, Megan, Tallis, Calvin, Cassandra, and Lillian. Nephew; Ron, Niece; Cheryl. In lieu of flowers, the family kindly requests that donations be made in Ninon's memory directly to Next Chapter Animal Rescue. Condolences, memories and photos may be shared and viewed at www.parklandfuneralhome.com. GOODALL, Ninon
1934-2026
With heavy hearts we announce the passing of Ninon Hildegard Goodall (Shaw) on Friday, June 26, 2026. She was the only child of Walter and Traute Shaw, born in Vancouver, British Columbia on May 3, 1934. Sadly, she lost her father in World War 2 at the age of 9. Ninon’s mother struggled to make ends meet by taking in college students and did her best to raise a spirited and strong-willed child. At a young age, Ninon gave birth to a child who was later placed for adoption. A difficult experience that shaped her life and demonstrated her resilience. (She would reunite with her firstborn child in the mid 1980’s). 
In her late teens, Ninon married Norman Latham and moved to Fort Nelson, British Columbia. She and Norman had four children together. (Colleen, Shawn, Pat and Mike) After the conclusion of that relationship, she met Stan in 1961 at a Valentine’s dance and their romance blossomed. In the early years, they managed to keep their heads above water by running a motel and dairy bar with everyone pitching in. Ninon and Stan welcomed their son Glen in 1970. Ninon went on to operate a daycare in her home for several years.
In 1979 they decided to make the long trek to Thompson, Manitoba. Ninon then took a job in the kitchen of a local hotel. The work was demanding and exhausting, but she loved it! The friends and memories she made in Thompson were some of her fondest.
In 1997, Stan and Ninon retired, packed up, and moved to Red Deer, Alberta. They embraced their family, the community, and became quite involved at the Good Shepherd Church. In 2012, they moved to Sylvan Lake and loved spending time around the waterfront. Ninon basking in the sun and Stan with a book in the shade.
Some of Ninon’s biggest joys in her life were her grandchildren and great grandchildren. She spent countless hours dedicating her time and attention to their activities and interests. Ninon has always loved animals of every kind. She has welcomed many household pets over the years and has never met a wet nose she wouldn’t kiss. She took pride in her baking and was a wonderful cook. Knitting and quilting were frequent past times that she also enjoyed. 
Ninon’s greatest joy was giving to others, whether through a thoughtful gift, a helping hand, or simply her time and kindness. One of her treasures was the many lifelong friendships she nurtured over the years. Those that knew her will remember her vibrant spirit and unforgettable personality. She had a gift for making people laugh, a warmth that drew others to her, and a kindness that left a lasting impression. 
She is predeceased by her mother and father, as well as her son-in-law Herb. Left to cherish her memory is her husband of 51 years, Stan Goodall; brother-in-law Donnie; her children, Blair (Allison), Colleen, Shawn, Pat, Mike (Lisa), and Glen (Jennifer); her grandchildren, Toni, Terry, Lawrence (Soleil), Melaina (Dimitrius), Derek (Shari), Stacy (Ed), Michelle, Chantelle, Rebecca, Kassidy and Jacksyn; great grandchildren: Quinton, Carly, Ben, Lucas, Deone, Megan, Tallis, Calvin, Cassandra, and Lillian. Nephew; Ron, Niece; Cheryl. In lieu of flowers, the family kindly requests that donations be made in Ninon's memory directly to Next Chapter Animal Rescue. Condolences, memories and photos may be shared and viewed at www.parklandfuneralhome.com. Arrangements in care of Parkland Funeral Home and Crematorium, 6287 – 67 A Street (Taylor Drive), Red Deer. 403.340.4040.

text:
Our History
Parkland Funeral Home and Crematorium was founded in 1999 to serve families in the Red Deer area with compassion, dignity, and respect. In 2010, ownership was assumed by Gordon and Barb Mathers, who brought with them years of experience and a deep commitment to providing meaningful care to families during life’s most difficult moments.
Gordon began managing funeral homes in Red Deer in 1998 and quickly earned the trust of the community through his professionalism and dedication to service. Under his leadership, Parkland Funeral Home and Crematorium grew into a place known for its warmth, integrity, and personal attention to detail. For nearly a decade and a half, Gordon guided the funeral home with a strong sense of responsibility to both the families he served and the broader community.
In 2024, the Mathers family proudly welcomed the next generation of leadership when their son, Nash R. Mathers, assumed management of the funeral home. As a licensed second-generation funeral director, Nash continues the legacy established by his parents—honouring the traditions of the past while also bringing fresh perspective and dedication to serving families with care and compassion.
Today, Parkland Funeral Home and Crematorium remains family-owned and operated, committed to upholding the values of trust, dignity, and compassion that have been at the heart of the business since its beginning.
We are proud to embrace traditional values, diversity and innovation in honouring the spirit and life of each person we serve. We offer a full selection of:
Funeral and memorial services, ranging from traditional to uniquely innovative and personal
Affordable burial services and cremation options
Celebrant Services
Letting go of a loved one is usually a very difficult process. In order to provide your family peace-of-mind, our funeral home offers complete care, so you can focus on comforting each other as you prepare to say goodbye to someone dear to you.

jsonLd.articleBody:
FAWCETT, Dennis

1949-2026

Dennis Dwight Fawcett passed away peacefully at the Red Deer Hospice in Red Deer, Alberta On Sunday, June 21, 2026. Dennis is survived by his wife Lona; his sons David (Cori) and Dale (Tania), their mother Dolores, and Kenny; stepchildren Lisa (Teresa), Greg and Melissa; 9 grandchildren; 7 great- grandchildren; his sister Barbara Keller, nieces Shauna and Monica; numerous friends, neighbours and acquaintances; and his shadow and best friend Lexy. Dennis is predeceased by his mother Gladys; his father Norris; numerous aunts, uncles, cousins; his son Terry; and his brother-in-law Ken Keller. Dennis was born on March 16, 1949 in Castor, Alberta and grew up on a farm west of there. He loved being outside and was a well-liked, handsome fella with a great sense of humour, right up to the end. In his 20s, he started working for the County of Paintearth. His trucking career took him all over Alberta, Saskatchewan, NWT and northern BC. Dennis and his brother-in-law Ken were partners in a trucking business (D&K Trucking) for many years. After Ken passed away, Dennis continued to operate the business for about 10 more years. According to Dennis, he clocked a whopping 5 million miles - having driven more miles backwards than others had forwards. Dennis was always there to help. Whether it was providing directions anywhere to helping stranded family or friends get back on the road. As a result of his many miles travelled (even taking Lexy to the dog park in Sylvan Lake) he made friends and acquaintances everywhere. Dennis (Denny) will be dearly missed by family, friends, neighbours and those he met along the way. A Celebration of Dennis’ Life will be held at the Benalto Community Hall, 38520 Range Rd 25A (NW 31-038-02-W5) Box 36 Benalto, AB T0M 0H0 on Sunday, July 12, 2026 from 1:00pm - 4:00pm. In lieu of flowers, please consider making a donation in his memory directly to the Red Deer Hospice Society at https://reddeerhospice.com/ . Cremation arrangements entrusted to the care of Parkland Funeral Home and Crematorium in Red Deer. Condolences, memories and photos may be shared and viewed at www.parklandfuneralhome.com. Arrangements in care of Parkland Funeral Home and Crematorium, 6287 – 67 A Street (Taylor Drive), Red Deer. 403.340.4040.

Last Updated: January 2021
We take privacy seriously 
FrontRunner Professional ULC (“FrontRunner,” “we,” “us,” “our”), is committed to protecting your personal information. This Privacy Notice describes the personal information that we collect about you, how we use and disclose this information, and the steps we take to protect this information. For purposes of this Privacy Notice, “personal information” means any information that relates to you as an individual and could reasonably be used to identify you. This Privacy Notice applies to our collection and use of personal information through this website and any related websites, applications, tools, or platforms (the “Services”), as well as through any other means where a link or reference to this Privacy Notice is provided at the time of collection.
Our Services 
FrontRunner is a provider of software services to funeral homes and crematories (our “Clients”), including website, payment processing, ecommerce, funeral management, search engine optimization and marketing services. In connection with the provision of these services, FrontRunner collects and stores personal information regarding individuals who visit and utilize certain functions or features of our Clients’ websites (“End Users”). This Privacy Notice applies to FrontRunner’s collection and use of Client and End User personal information but not to our Clients use of such personal information. This Privacy Notice also applies to other personal information collected directly by FrontRunner, including through use of our website or otherwise in connection with the Services. 
Personal Information We Collect 
When you access or use the Services or otherwise interact with us, whether as a Client, End User, or other individual, we may collect certain categories of personal information about you from a variety of sources. 
Categories of personal information that we may collect from you directly include:
Contact information (for example, name, job title, phone number, mailing address, email address)
Payment-related details (for example, banking information, billing address or other credit card details)
Account information (for example, username and password and transaction history)
Communications (for example, submitted questions or other posts and marketing preferences)
Recruitment data (for example, resumes and other details regarding an applicant’s qualifications)
Categories of personal information that we may collect automatically when you use the Services include:
Technical information (for example, browser type, IP address, date and time of visit, cookies, geolocation and operating system)
Usage information (for example, pages visited, search terms entered, and frequency of visits)
Categories of personal information that we may collect from other sources, including from our Clients in connection with their use of the Services, include:
End User contact information (for example, name, phone number, mailing address, email address)
End User payment-related details (for example, billing address and other credit card details)
End User funeral contributions, including memorial video data, obituaries and posts and comments
End User funeral administration data, including personal details regarding the deceased such as dates of birth and death and data used to identify the deceased virtually (including photos), affidavits certifying the identification of the deceased and data related to the location from which such identification is made, life insurance claim forms and affidavits to ensure dispersal of funds to cover funeral costs and other medical costs or living expenses and data required to file death certificates
Lead data, including business contact data
We use Google Analytics to collect and analyze information about the use of the website and to help us understand activities and trends, this includes the use of Google Analytics performance reports relating to demographics and interests. As part of this service, we share a unique identifier with Google Analytics. You may opt-out of Google Analytics by installing a Google Analytics opt-out browser add-on available for download here: https://tools.google.com/dlpage/gaoptout
Finally, we may collect personal information pursuant to a legal or contractual requirement, and failure to provide such information may impact our ability to fulfill our obligations.
How We Use Your Personal Information 
We may use the personal information we collect for the following purposes: 
Provide and improve the Services. We may use your personal information to provide and improve the Services, including to fulfill your orders and requests and to post your comments and other funeral contributions. We may also use your personal information for the administration of our business, for business development purposes, and to fulfill our contractual obligations.
Risk mitigation and security. We may use your personal information for risk mitigation and security purposes, including to maintain the privacy and security of our data, to conduct internal audits or investigations, for data security testing and business continuity planning purposes, to prevent fraud and abuse, and to ensure the safety and security of our Clients, staff and assets.
Communication and marketing. We may use your personal information to communicate with you about the Services, respond to your questions, or offer you additional products or services. 
Comply with the law and exercise our rights. We may use your personal information as reasonably necessary to assess and ensure compliance with applicable laws, legal requirements, and company policies; to protect our assets or to investigate or defend against any claims of illegality or wrongdoing (including to obtain legal advice or to establish, exercise or defend legal rights); and in response to a court order or judicial or other government subpoena or warrant.
Corporate transaction. We may use your personal information in the event we undertake or are involved in or contemplating any merger, acquisition, reorganization, sale of assets, bankruptcy, or insolvency event. 
Recruitment and hiring. We may use your personal information to evaluate your candidacy when you apply for a job with us. 
We may also aggregate, anonymize, or otherwise de-identify your personal information and use it for any purpose permitted by applicable law.
Use of Cookies 
When you use the Services, we may send one or more cookies (which are small text files containing a string of alphanumeric characters) to your computer or mobile device, to help analyze our web page flow (including tracking user sessions), customize our content, measure promotional effectiveness, and promote trust and safety. You are always free to decline our cookies if your browser permits, although doing so may interfere with your ability to use the Services or certain features of the Services. We may also use Google Analytics or a similar service that uses cookies to help us analyze how users use the Services. 
We may also allow certain third parties such as advertising, analytics providers, and widget providers to place cookies in order to collect information about your online activities over time and across different websites when you access or use the Services. Currently, various browsers offer a “Do Not Track” option, but there is no standard for how “Do Not Track” should work on commercial websites. Where possible, we honor Do Not Track signals. 
How and When We Disclose Your Personal Information 
We may disclose your personal information to the following categories of recipients, to be used only for legitimate purposes in keeping with this Privacy Notice: 
Group companies and affiliates. We may disclose, share, or transfer your information to any business entity that is part of our corporate family. 
Clients. We may share your information with our Clients in connection with our Clients provision of services to you.

Parkland Funeral Home | Red Deer | Eckville
1. Notify the Proper Authorities
If the death occurs at home and was not expected, call emergency services immediately. If the death was anticipated, such as during palliative care, contact the attending physician or nurse. In a hospital or care facility, staff will guide you through the next steps.
2. Contact a Funeral Home
A licensed funeral director will assist with transferring your loved one into their care and help guide you through the arrangement process. They can also coordinate with hospitals, care homes, and other professionals on your behalf.
3. Inform Family and Close Friends
Reach out to immediate family members and close friends. It may be helpful to designate one person to help communicate with others and share updates.
4. Locate Important Documents
Gather essential documents such as a will, identification, insurance policies, and any pre-arrangement paperwork. These documents will help guide decisions and next steps.
5. Arrange the Funeral or Memorial Service
Whether you choose to work with a funeral home or plan the arrangements yourself, the service should reflect your loved one’s wishes and values. Options may include burial or cremation, as well as a formal service, celebration of life, or a private gathering.
6. Register the Death and Obtain Certificates
The funeral home will assist in registering the death and obtaining official death certificates, which are required for legal and financial matters.
7. Notify Government and Financial Institutions
Inform agencies such as Service Canada, banks, insurance providers, and pension programs. This helps ensure benefits are processed and accounts are properly managed.
8. Take Care of Yourself and Seek Support
Grief affects everyone differently. Lean on family, friends, faith communities, or bereavement support services. Taking care of your emotional well-being is just as important as handling practical matters.
A Final Thought
While there is no way to fully prepare for the loss of a loved one, having a basic understanding of what to do can provide reassurance and direction. Funeral professionals and community resources are available to support families every step of the way.

text:
Pre-Arrangement Process
What Happens During a Pre-Arrangement
A pre-arrangement is an opportunity to thoughtfully plan your funeral or final wishes in advance, ensuring your preferences are clearly documented while easing the burden on your loved ones during a difficult time.
During a pre-arrangement meeting, you will sit down with a licensed funeral director in a comfortable, no-pressure environment to discuss your wishes. The process typically begins with gathering basic personal information and reviewing the type of service you prefer, such as burial or cremation, as well as whether you would like a traditional funeral, memorial service, or a more informal gathering.
You will also have the opportunity to make personalized choices, including music selections, readings, clergy or celebrant preferences, and any special touches that reflect your life, values, and beliefs. Details such as casket or urn selection, final resting place, and obituary preferences can also be discussed.
Financial options are reviewed as part of the pre-arrangement process, including the opportunity to prepay for services. Prepayment allows you to lock in today’s prices and helps relieve your family of financial responsibility in the future.
At our funeral home, we offer secure prepayment options through TruStage. Funds are placed into a guaranteed insurance policy, ensuring they are protected and will be available when needed. These plans also offer flexibility, as they can be transferred should you move or your circumstances change.
For those who prefer, you may choose to set funds aside independently or simply document your wishes without any financial commitment. Your funeral director will guide you through each option, helping you make informed decisions that align with your needs and budget.
Once your wishes are recorded, they are kept on file at the funeral home and can be updated at any time. Having a pre-arrangement in place provides peace of mind, knowing your family will have clear guidance and support when it matters most.

# Record Your Wishes

There are many benefits to **end-of-life planning**. Here are the top ten reasons why you should consider making your funeral arrangements ahead of time:

*   It means there will be fewer opportunities for argument and indecision about your funeral arrangements among family members after you're gone.
*   Your survivors will never have to worry about doing the wrong thing when finalizing your funeral arrangements. You will have told them exactly what you want.
*   No mistakes and no oversights. After you're gone, everything will be done your way.
*   You have peace-of-mind now knowing that we will follow through with your wishes.
*   After your death, no one can make any decisions you wouldn't want.
*   Funeral pre-planning is the responsible thing to do. It removes the burden from family members.
*   You can make complex decisions ahead of time when you have the time to think things through.
*   Funeral pre-planning can involve pre-payment. This will save your family money and avoid any financial burdens.
*   Funeral pre-planning involves an awareness of the reality of death.
*   You are almost guaranteed to get what you want.

## Get it Done... and Then Relax

End-of-life planning makes sense. [Call us](https://www.parklandfuneralhome.com/contact-us) today to learn how we can help or get started now with our online pre-planning tool, [Pre-Arrange Online](https://www.parklandfuneralhome.com/pre-arrange-online).

## Advance Directives

We spend a lot of time talking about the importance of living responsibly, which involves preparing for the realities of life. While we believe making the decisions involved in [funeral pre-planning](https://www.parklandfuneralhome.com/pre-planning) is one reflection of a responsible mindset, we also know the critical importance of completing an **advance directive**.

## What is an Advance Directive?

Sometimes called advance care directives, these document ensure that your wishes will be carried out in the future.

Defined as "a written statement of a person's wishes regarding medical treatment," advance directives, when properly signed and witnessed, will provide guidance for medical and health care decisions in the event the individual becomes incompetent and can no longer make such decisions.

## Other Things to Know About Advance Directives

*   Advance directives are legal throughout Canada.  
    
*   Governing laws vary so be sure to obtain an advance directive that complies with your province's laws.  
    
*   You do not need an attorney to complete an advance directive.  
    
*   If you reside in more than one province, you should complete an advance directive for each province where you spend a significant amount of time.  
    
*   There are no time limitations on advance directives. A signed advance directive remains in force until a new one is completed.  
    
*   Periodically review your advance directive to make sure it still reflects your desires. If it doesn't, don't try to amend it; simply complete a new one.  
    
*   Paramedics and emergency medical technicians cannot recognize or honour a living will or medical power of attorney. They are obligated to do their best to stabilize the patient and get them to the hospital. When you are in the care of hospital personnel, your advance directive becomes valid.  
    

### What's Involved in Preparing an Advance Directive?

[Dying with Dignity Canada](http://www.dyingwithdignity.ca/) explains that "writing an Advance Care Plan involves much more than simply filling out a form. It is essential to take time for reflection and discussion to ensure your Plan reflects your values, beliefs and wishes."

There are many resources available online to assist and guide you in writing your Advance Directive. 

### Where to Obtain an Advance Directive Form

It's fairly easy to get a copy of the advance care directive form for your province. Your local hospital is a reliable source, as federal law requires every hospital to not only provide information about advance directives to people in their service area, they are also required to share valuable information about the related laws in your province. Contact your local hospital to learn more. Your family physician may also have advance directive forms available for patients.

You will need to have the advance directive witnessed and notarized. If you do not have access to a notary, you can find one using either of the following websites:

*   [Red Seal Notary](https://www.redsealnotary.com/)  
    
*   [Dying With Dignity Canada](http://www.dyingwithdignity.ca/)  
    

Dying with Dignity Canada also offers Advance Care Planning Kits to assist you in making your advance care directive.

Blackfalds Location
We are proud to introduce our new Blackfalds location, thoughtfully designed to provide comfort, convenience, and a welcoming atmosphere for families and friends.
This intimate space can accommodate up to 50 guests, making it ideal for both funeral services and reception gatherings. Whether you are planning a traditional service, a celebration of life, or a quiet time of remembrance, the setting offers flexibility to suit your needs.

text:
Preparing for a Funeral Service
Preparing for a Funeral Service
Could there be anything more difficult than preparing for a funeral? Certainly, such an end-of-life event is hard to look forward to with any great enthusiasm. And it doesn't matter if you're a member of the bereaved inner circle of close family, a co-worker, neighbour or family friend; preparing for a funeral service takes time and forethought.
If you're preparing to attend a funeral, memorial service, or celebration of life, the following tips and suggestions can certainly help in your funeral preparations. Naturally, if you have any questions about preparing for a funeral, you should call us. We would be pleased to serve you in any way we can.
What Does "Get Prepared" Really Mean?
There's a line in William Shakespeare's play "Henry V", which cuts to the heart of preparedness: "All things are ready, if our mind be so." Readying your mind means strengthening it for what's ahead: all the people, sights, sounds and strong emotions of the day.
In other words, getting ready to attend an end-of-life service is not just a matter of picking out the right clothes to wear; it's also essential to prepare physically, mentally and emotionally for the occasion. After all, you are going to be there to support the bereaved family, as well as the others who attend; and that takes inner strength and emotional fortitude. Never underestimate the importance of your presence there—to everyone in attendance. 
To make it simple for you to find the information you need, we've grouped those details together under two headings: Dressing for the Occasion and Getting Physically, Mentally and Emotionally Prepared.
Dressing the Occasion
What is expected of us when attending a funeral service today is far different from the expectations of those living in the Victorian era. According to Alison Petch, a researcher Oxford University, "In those years, black clothing was worn for the funeral and for a year following the death...by close relatives, gradually being replaced by other dark colours." 
As we moved into the twentieth century, the Roman and Victorian demands became less strict. "People attending a funeral wore semi-formal clothing, which for adult men would usually mean a suit and tie in dark colours".
Without a doubt, these strict special dress requirements have fallen by the wayside, at least to some degree. Although many websites proclaim that black is the right colour to wear for a funeral today, wearing a colour other than black isn't seen as disrespectful; but you want to avoid wearing brightly coloured or wildly patterned fabrics (unless actually requested to do so by the family). And for women or girls, a modest appearance is preferred.
Certainly, if you've got additional questions about what to wear to a funeral, call us.
Get Physically, Mentally, and Emotionally Prepared
The death of a loved one is among the most stressful experiences we will ever endure. The early days of bereavement, are a time of frayed nerves, when emotions run high and hours of restful sleep are hard to find. These difficult days are then followed by the funeral service (where, even though you're grief stricken, you're expected to perform with some social grace). How can you possibly survive; or better yet thrive, during such trials as these? Here are some suggestions we believe you'll find valuable.
Maintain a state of "mindful awareness."
The tendency when something bad happens to us, like the death of a loved one, is to detach from our physical, emotional and social selves. To "get numb, and stay that way" - but this effort to separate ourselves from what's happening isn't always in our best interest. Instead, you should seek to be "mindful": to keep your awareness on the present moment (not the past, and certainly not the future); all the while acknowledging (and accepting) your feelings, thoughts, and bodily reactions to your loss. Only then can you, in the words of Reinhold Niebuhr's Serenity Prayer, accept the things that cannot be changed, have the courage to change the things which can (and should) be changed, and the wisdom to distinguish the one from the other. Certainly, you cannot change the fact your loved one has died; but you can change (at least to some degree) the way you react to the loss—and that takes a certain sense of mindful self-awareness. 
Do everything you can to stay physically healthy.
The list of physical symptoms of grief is long: fatigue, body aches and pains, loss or change of appetite, shortness of breath, digestive issues, feelings of heaviness, and tightness in your throat or chest. When faced with an onslaught of physical symptoms like these, it's hard to know exactly how to deal with them. The first step is to recognize and name what your body is experiencing. Only then can you do something to change the way you're reacting to the loss. During these days before the funeral:
Stay hydrated: drink eight (8 ounce) glasses of water.
Eat regularly: small meals and snacks are often better-accepted than large, calorie-laden ones.
Rest regularly: you may find nights are long and sleepless, so don't be adverse to taking short cat-naps throughout the day.
Move your body: take a walk or hike, go to the gym, or enjoy a leisurely swim.
Nurture your senses: listen to music or the sounds that abound in nature.
Engage in prayer or meditation: tap into, or get reacquainted with, your spiritual side.
Reduce your list of necessary activities and chores: now is the time to delegate tasks to others, so you can devote your time to self-care.
Reach out to your support network.
Neighbours, friends and family members can be your lifeline right now - and some of them may even be coming to you right now to see how they can help. Don't turn them away; instead, give them the opportunity to give the gift of service. Allow them to walk this path with you for as long as, and in whatever ways, they can. The same goes for the network of professional caregivers: don't neglect to turn to clergy, your family physician, therapist, or grief counsellor if you feel your bereavement to be more than you can handle (now, or at any time in the future).
Prepare to speak less and listen more.
End-of-life ceremonies (whether a "traditional" funeral, memorial service or celebration of life) offer those gathered the chance to share their feelings, tell stories and take comfort from one another. Don't spend too much time talking, unless it's to share something truly meaningful (about the deceased and your relationship to him or her) with others; instead, be ready to listen with a whole heart. This is a time for respectful interactions with other mourners; a time for focusing on the life of the deceased, and also a time for renewing the ties which brought you all together in the first place.
Let Us Help with Your Preparations
Who better to turn to for assistance in preparing for a funeral? We've got the experience and insights which could make this situation easier for you and those you love. If you have questions about preparing for a funeral service—either as a member of the family or as a guest—we're here to support you in any way we can. We're standing at the ready; simply call us.
Sources:
Shakespeare, William, "Henry V" 
Petch , Alison, "Funeral and Mourning Clothing", England, the Other Within, accessed March, 2015

# Planning a Cremation Service

Planning a Cremation Service

## How to Plan a Cremation Service

## Before the Decision to Cremate is Made

1.  **Learn about your cremation options.** Review the [cremation](https://www.parklandfuneralhome.com/cremation-services) information found on our website.   
    
2.  **Engage your family in a discussion.** We urge you to bring your family into the conversation to get a better idea about how they feel about cremation and what they would prefer.  
    
3.  **Speak with a funeral professional.** If there are any questions or concerns, please [turn to us](https://www.parklandfuneralhome.com/contact-us) for the insights you may need at this point.  
    
4.  **Document your cremation intentions in writing.** There are a number of forms we can provide to take this step. [Call us](https://www.parklandfuneralhome.com/contact-us) to learn more.  
    
5.  **Arrange for the transportation of your loved one's physical remains.** We can escort them to our facility or directly to the crematory.  
    

## After Deciding on Cremation

1.  **Consider what kind of ceremony you would like to have.** You can plan for a traditional funeral followed by the cremation or delay the ceremony until you have the time to plan a memorial service, celebration-of-life, or scattering ceremony.  
    
2.  **Ask for assistance from your family and friends.** When making plans for a meaningful event, encourage everyone to get involved. Ask them to gather family photos, write down the stories they'd like to share, and talk to them about the best location for the event. If you would like a eulogy, this is the time to ask someone special to take on that task.  
    
3.  **Select the music, prayers, or other readings.** You don't have to have any of these things but you should decide exactly what you and your guests will do at this event. There are endless possibilities.  
    
4.  **Contact guests well ahead of time.** This is especially important if they will need to travel or request time off from work.  
    
5.  **Decide what will be done with the cremated remains.** Commonly the urn is a visual focal point of a celebration-of-life. Will you then take it home? Will the scattering of ashes be a part of the event? You may want to purchase keepsake urns for family members.  
    

## Call On Us

We've had years of experience helping other families make cremation service arrangements. Never hesitate to pick up the phone to [call us](https://www.parklandfuneralhome.com/contact-us). We would be privileged to serve you and your family. Simply call to speak with one of our funeral professionals.

text:
Planning a Celebration of Life
Planning a Celebration of Life
How to Plan a Celebration of Life
It's really a process of asking–and answering–questions. Sit down with other family members, at least once—but maybe even more than once—to explore the celebration of life ideas which arise from answering these questions:
Who will be invited? The number of guests define the where, when, and how of your celebration of life. Write down the names of everyone you think would want to be there and then set it aside. You can add new names to the list as you go along.
Where, and when, should the event take place? Here's where your imagination is tempered by any scheduling or travel-related issues facing those who will be invited. Be sure to check in with out-of-town relatives and friends about their situation before settling on these critical details.
Who will orchestrate or conduct the event? If your loved one was religious, you may opt to have their pastor or church minister perform these tasks. However, many families today hire a non-denominational celebrant to oversee the celebration of life.
Who wishes to speak at the event? Many times family members or friends will be very direct about their desire to make a short presentation at the celebration of life; other times you need to come out and ask folks if they would be willing to publicly share their thoughts and feelings. Either way, you'll want to select those people who have shared a close relationship with the deceased and have something meaningful to contribute.
What group activities would be appropriate? We've heard some exciting celebration of life ideas over the years. This question involves thinking about what your loved one liked most about their life and gives everyone a remarkable space to share memories, laugh, and even cry together.
What food or beverages should be served? What you serve may depend on the theme of your celebration of life, or may be based on your loved one's favorite dishes. It's entirely up to you; we've even seen "pot luck" celebrations of life where guests actually sign up to bring select foods and beverages.
What readings and music should you include? Music is an integral part of life for many people, and a celebration of life is the perfect event in which to showcase the meaningful music of your loved one's life. But, if your loved one didn't appreciate music (and lots of folks don’t), it may be more appropriate to read chosen spiritual selections, or excerpts from literature.
What details of your loved one's life do you want to share with guests? Not every biographical detail needs to be highlighted; rather you're trying to capture their essence by telling revealing anecdotes or stories. Sometimes you can reveal their character by detailing one short moment in their life experience.
What decorations will you have? Many families create a tribute video and use it as the centerpiece of the event. Others choose to use a memory table of photographs and other memorabilia instead.
Let Us Help with the Celebration of Life
We know that's a lot to think about. But we urge you to take your time; be thoughtful, and don't hesitate to explore all the celebrations of life ideas which arise as part of this experience.
As we've said, we've got the experience to help make things easier for you and your family. Don't hesitate to pick up the phone and call us. Let's talk about your loved one's life; share some stories with us. We're confident that, together, we can come up with the perfect celebration of life event to suit your needs and expectations.

4.  **Who wishes to speak at the event?** Many times family members or friends will be very direct about their desire to make a short presentation at the celebration of life; other times you need to come out and ask folks if they would be willing to publicly share their thoughts and feelings. Either way, you'll want to select those people who have shared a close relationship with the deceased and have something meaningful to contribute.  
    
5.  **What group activities would be appropriate?** We've heard some exciting celebration of life ideas over the years. This question involves thinking about what your loved one liked most about their life and gives everyone a remarkable space to share memories, laugh, and even cry together.  
    
6.  **What food or beverages should be served?** What you serve may depend on the theme of your celebration of life, or may be based on your loved one's favorite dishes. It's entirely up to you; we've even seen "pot luck" celebrations of life where guests actually sign up to bring select foods and beverages.  
    
7.  **What readings and music should you include?** Music is an integral part of life for many people, and a celebration of life is the perfect event in which to showcase the meaningful music of your loved one's life. Funeral Service Trends
The needs and expectations of our families are changing and we've responded with funeral service options tailored to these new expectations.
Two generations ago, traditional funerals(visitation, funeral service and service at the cemetery) were common. It was what everyone expected.
But, as the demand for cremation services increased, there has been a shift in the types of services available. Many more families are choosing cremation and holding a memorial service afterwards. Family members and friends still came together to pay their respects to the deceased and find emotional support but they did so in less formal ways.
Today, another funeral service option, the celebration of life service, has become quite popular because there are no limits to the how, where, and when the life of a loved one can be celebrated. 
Thinking About Your Funeral Service Options
The arrangements you make will be influenced by the lifestyle of your deceased family member: the time of year, your budget, and the number of people in attendance.
