text:
Perspectives of Crematorium/Funeral Home Costs | Extra Knowledge
Author: Jeff Chancellor, CFSP
I am usually amused when I pick up a magazine or newspaper or turn on the television and see “news” reports on the high cost of dying. Almost every year a few fledgling reporters make their personal mission to reveal the fact that funerals are expensive or go as far as saying they are unjustifiably expensive. It seems that no matter where I travel these kinds of articles and stories seem to fill the vacuum during an otherwise dull day of news. 
Not so long ago I returned to my old stomping grounds for a reunion. It was nice to see familiar faces and listen to stories of back in the day. After the usual comparing loss of hair and gains in weight the topic usually turned to one another’s work. I was often asked if I was “still in the undertaking business.” When I answered in the affirmative most people shared their recent death experiences with me. A few made comments about how I must be rich now due to the high cost of dying. Having little desire to discuss funeral costs or my personal finances I usually changed the subject to their businesses or careers. 
One fellow was particularly vocal about his perception of funeral costs saying, “You guys sure know how to charge!” When I asked what he was doing he replied: “I am the donut man in town.” You see he had purchased a franchise for a donut store. He openly bragged about the line-up of people at his drive-through window and at the counter every morning, lunch and evening. He spoke about his high employee turnover and how he believed the minimum wage law was unfair to his business because young people show no commitment these days. When I asked him if there was good money in selling obesity, heart disease and diabetes he laughed and told me he had recovered his seven-figure investment in 36 months! 
I began to ponder the thinking style of any businessperson who thinks funerals are expensive and embarked upon a project involving local small businesspeople, the backbone of the North American economy. I decided to shop and compare the fees of non-funeral businesses in our community that offer similar services. 
Facilities to serve: 
A chapel is little more than a multi-purpose room like those found in a local hotel or conference centre. So I inquired at hotels. I asked for some very simple things. A room set up with chairs, parking spaces, display stands and equipment to play music, an LCD projector and screen and a public address system. I also asked for staff members to direct attendees and ensure our reserved parking spots stayed reserved. 
Could anybody answer my questions? Nope, it was usually telephone tag with a few people who had to check with others. Time investment to get three quotes for the above: more than a dozen telephone calls over two days. 
“Sorry sir, we don’t have a projector.” Or, “We do not offer staff to help you usher people.” And, “We can’t guarantee the parking spaces,” were the usual replies. No one was able to facilitate my requests with less than 72-hours notice. 
When I asked about the cost of meeting rooms it ranged between $400 and $800 per half-day. 
The rental price for an LCD projector, screen, stereo and cordless microphone system ranged between $350 and $600 per day. 
For simplicity, let’s use an average chapel cost figure of $1,000 for a half-day. 
Ambulatory services: 
I wondered what would be closest to facilitating a transfer of the deceased into our care so I tried two strategies: 
• A biohazard waste company to pick up 250 pounds of medical waste in a hotshot service. 
• A patient transport service to pick up a 250-lb. paralyzed person and transport them 20 miles in a hotshot service. 
Not one company would quote me unless I gave them an exact pick up and delivery address and then they told me which day and what time they would come. Both types of companies were not interested in dealing with me “right now, immediately, today” and all firms told me they would no doubt charge me for waiting time if we are not ready at the moment they arrived. 
Time investment: more than six telephone calls over two days. 
The average price was $275 with an advanced booking. When I asked for an after-business hours pick-up or for an immediate response, the price more than doubled. 
Embalming and decedent care: 
Embalming is difficult to compare so I decided to compare the services of two very different companies. 
• A beauty shop asking for an outcall service in my house. 
• A full-service spa for a half-day treatment. 
For the beauty shop I requested to get a shampoo, colour treatment, haircut, manicure and facial. No one would drop what they were doing to help me. They all offered to call me back later with a quote when it was convenient for them. All did and all offered to come at their convenience with prices from $275 to $500. A premier salon even quoted $1,000. 
The spa people were a little bit more service-oriented and knowledgeable. For a half-day treatment (3-3.5 hours), which consisted of a 1.5-hour massage, facial, exfoliation skin treatment, manicure and pedicure, charged between $275 and $600. No after-hours or walk-in service available. 
Let’s use the average of $500 for both groups. 
Professional consultation or arrangements: 
I have often believed that we undervalue our knowledge in funeral service so it was my decision to speak with three different professionals and see what their knowledge is worth. 
• An accountant about tax planning 
• A lawyer about estate planning 
• A contractor to estimate replacing a water heater 
The accountants would not quote me any advise on planning or filing or even opinions for free. Not one would give me an estimate on costs to do my taxes, even when I furnished them with a lot of information about how uncomplicated my return would be. All were more than happy to tell me they could offer a better service than the “chain stores.” And all quoted their fee: average hourly “consultation” rate for a junior was $100/hour. All could see me “in a few days” during office hours if I cared to make an appointment. 
It was the same with the lawyers. Some claimed to make wills for $100 but said they had to talk it over in person first because they did not want to mislead me with a low price if the estate was complicated. Average hourly consultation rate for a junior was $125. All would see me within one working day during office hours if I made an appointment. 
The contractors all had to come and see the job first, none would quote even when I explained in detail the model we had, how to access it and where we lived because they believed there is always something the customer misses or something that breaks during the removal or installation that the customer would have to pay for. The average hourly rate was $80. Those who actually called me back had higher rates for after-hours and claimed to be there to respond within one working day. 
I am sure that you are not surprised by my experience when I say that none of the above professionals was reachable when I called, and none returned my call promptly. In fact several didn’t even call me back. 
Without exception, all of the professionals I spoke to were resentful of me requesting they come to me at my convenience or work after-hours. All laid down clear boundaries of what they would tell me on the phone. When I told them they were more expensive than another professional there was no mention of a discount or any discussion as to why, it was simply explained: “These are our fees, sir.” 
Considering the average arrangements conference is 1.5 hours whether pre-need or at-need, let’s go with $175 during normal business hours. 
Girl Friday services: 
I’ve read that to facilitate the average traditional funeral involves more than 80 man-hours of work. Clerical duties, telephone work, typing, filing of documents and running around that we all do to make a funeral happen averages 40 hours; once remove the arrangements conference and decedent transfer and embalming. To hire non-professional staff, neat in appearance, who are able to perform receptionist duties, type, operate a computer, drive and have sufficient people skills to handle funeral attendees hired from a temp agency ranged from $25 to $35 per hour. 
So, 40 hours at $30/hour is an even $1,200. 
Professional vehicles: 
Let’s agree we are looking at 25 miles for a transport vehicle carrying our staff and the casket to our rental meeting space. To rent a full size SUV for a day runs about $125 with gas and insurance, a full size car runs about $85 with gas and insurance. 
Let’s also agree we are looking at four hours of driving time and waiting time to facilitate a family pick-up, have a service and return the family home. Limousine rentals are $75 hourly with minimums averaging $175 in my area. 
Rolling stock as above $385. 
Stationary: 
I decided to look at wedding invitations for a comparison to our memorial stationary packages. Average cost of invitations was more than $2 a piece with several days waiting time. Let’s say we have 200 printed plus a book – average cost was $450. 
I am certain that we can go on with other services we offer to a family in need but lets just stop here and total the services we have compared – $3,785. With the average cost of a funeral in North America being about $5,000 including merchandise and requiring a lot more service and facility than described above, it seems to me that our prices are unjustifiably low. 
Upon fee comparison it occurred to me that we do not value our services and merchandise as confidently as these other so called professional groups. 
I am sure that each reader has encountered many similar people. People who tell us they “could never do what we do.” I have been privileged to travel a lot of this world, and have had the pleasure of visiting funeral providers in 28 countries. Truthfully, there is not a single place where I have been where the story is any different. 
Consider another large professional challenge. I am sure many readers will agree that there exists a shortage of quality people who desire to do this kind of work. While considering this I asked my local Costco store manager if I could do a one-hour market survey in his parking lot about the “high cost of funerals.” He agreed since he was offering caskets and urns for sale. 
It was a Saturday morning. I took a clipboard, a set of car keys and a hand-drawn map with directions to a local veterans hospital. I stopped quite a number of people and asked them a simple question: “Would you be willing to drop what you are doing right now, take my car and go to the hospital, proceed to the morgue and pick up the dead body of a man, then immediately return to my location?” I said it would likely take less than two hours. I also explained that I would be willing to pay them $100 per hour for the service.” Not one person would do it. When increased the rate to $500, I again had no volunteers. 
Perhaps it is time that we in funeral service reconsider our price structuring for the services we render. I am quite certain that our charges are under “market value.” 
Jeff began his funeral service career in the pre-need sales division of a large cemetery/funeral chain in 1985. He graduated first in his class from the Alberta School of Mortuary Science in 1989. Jeff’s working experience is varied and includes work on a project establishing mortuary embalming in Japan, manager of a high volume mortuary, owner of a safety training company, instructor at the Center for Funeral Service Education at Mount Royal College in Calgary, Alberta, and representative for Dodge Company, traveling Western Canada, Nevada, California, Hawaii and Guam. He is a qualified embalmer, crematory operator and a certified funeral celebrant. Jeff has lectured to professional funeral service associations and businesses in eight countries on three continents. He was a contributing author to Edition Three of the Embalming, History, Theory and Practise textbook and has articles published in The Mortuary Science Monitor, Canadian Funeral News, Canadian Funeral Director, The Australian Funeral Director and the Dodge Magazine. Jeff is the chairman of the Pacific Center for Advanced Studies in Cebu City, Philippines, acts as director of Far East operations for Blake Emergency Services and serves on advisory boards of several mortuary colleges. He resides in California and continues to travel extensively as a funeral service lecturer and educator.

A friend has experienced the death of someone loved. How can you help? The following articles provide many practical suggestions for helping others with grief:

## Helping Yourself with Grief

Someone you love has died. You are now faced with the difficult, but important, need to mourn. Mourning is the open expression of your thoughts and feelings regarding the death and the person who died.  It is an essential part of healing. Planning Insights
Most of us are not prepared to plan and carry out a funeral ceremony for someone we love. And so much of the information available on this critically important subject fails to focus on what is most important: having a personalized, meaningful funeral that helps families and friends begin the healing process of mourning after the death of someone we love.
This section includes information that will help provide insights necessary to help you and your family create a meaningful funeral experience that both honors the life of your loved one and starts you on the path to healing from your loss. Some of the content on these pages is adapted from a website called www.MeaningfulFunerals.com and the teachings of Dr. Alan Wolfelt, a noted grief expert.

Click here to listen to Dr. Alan Wolfelt describe why it's important to have a funeral.
To learn more about Dr. Wolfelt, please visit www.centerforloss.com
Our funeral homes dedicated staff wants to help you and can play a critical role in planning and carrying out a meaningful funeral or memorial service. Our licensed funeral directors are intimately familiar with the funeral planning process, key decisions a grieving family must make, and necessary legal documentation that is required during this difficult time. Our funeral professionals can handle all of the details and help you create a unique service that fits your needs and values.

Obituary | Gertrude Levasseur of Falher, Alberta
C'est avec tristesse que la famille annonce le décès de Gertrude Levasseur, survenu le 27 janvier 2026, à l'âge de 96 ans.
Gertrude est née le 5 avril 1929 de Aurelle et Marie-Anne Caron.
Gertrude restera dans le souvenir de tous pour sa bonté, sa force tranquille, ainsi que pour l'amour et le dévouement qu'elle a prodigués à sa famille tout au long de sa longue et belle vie. Femme de foi profonde, elle était entièrement dévouée à Dieu et puisait dans sa foi la force, le réconfort et les conseils qui l'ont guidée tout au long de sa vie. Sa chaleur humaine, sa compassion et sa douceur ont marqué la vie de tous ceux qui l'ont connue et continueront de vivre dans le cœur de ceux qui l'ont aimée.
Elle est allée rejoindre son époux bien-aimé, Fortunat Levasseur, décédé en 1990, ainsi que ses parents, Aurelle et Marie-Anne Caron, de même que ses cinq frères et ses deux sœurs.
Elle laisse dans le deuil ses deux enfants bien-aimés, Morris et Yvette, ainsi que les membres de sa famille élargie, ses amis et tous ceux dont elle a touché la vie.
Une messe commémorative aura lieu à la paroisse Sainte-Anne de Falher, en Alberta, le vendredi 31 juillet 2026 à 13 h 30. La famille accueillera parents et amis pour rendre hommage à Gertrude, partager de précieux souvenirs et prier à sa mémoire.
La famille tient à exprimer sa plus sincère gratitude à tous ceux et celles qui leur ont témoigné leur soutien, leur gentillesse et leurs prières durant cette période de deuil.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
It is with sadness that the family announces the passing of Gertrude Levasseur, who passed away on January 27, 2026, at the age of 96 years.
Gertrude was born on April 5, 1929, to Aurelle and Marie-Anne Caron.
Gertrude will be remembered for her kindness, quiet strength, and the love and devotion she gave to her family throughout her long and meaningful life. A woman of deep faith, she was devoted to God and found strength, comfort, and guidance in her faith throughout her life. Her warmth, compassion, and gentle spirit touched the lives of all who knew her and will remain a lasting legacy in the hearts of those she loved.
She was predeceased by her beloved husband, Fortunat Levasseur, in 1990; by her parents, Aurelle and Marie-Anne Caron; and by her five brothers and two sisters.
She leaves to cherish her memory her two loving children, Morris and Yvette, along with extended family, friends, and all whose lives she touched.
A Memorial Mass will be held from the Ste. Anne Parish in Falher, Alberta, on Friday, July 31, 2026, at 1:30 p.m. Family and friends are warmly invited to attend as they gather to remember Gertrude's life, share memories, and offer prayers in her honor.
The family wishes to express their heartfelt gratitude to everyone who has offered their support, kindness, and prayers during this time of loss.

To plant Memorial Trees in memory of Gertrude Levasseur, please click here to visit our sympathy store.

text:
Obituary | Paul Bogner of Berwyn, Alberta
Paul Joseph Bogner, long time resident of the Berwyn, Alberta, Canada area, passed away peacefully on June 27, 2026, at the age of 91.
Paul was born on March 5th 1935 in Fort Benton Montana USA to Cornelius Sylvester Bogner and Mary Elizabeth Dickman Bogner. The 6th of 9 children, he arrived 5 minutes before his twin brother Donald.
Paul grew up on the family farm in the Elim District East of Fort Benton. He graduated from Fort Benton High School in 1953. Paul was a devote Catholic all his life.
Paul married Frances Lillian Terry on June 1st, 1959 at St. Margaret Mary’s Catholic Church, Big Sandy Montana. In February 1960, Paul and Frances immigrated to Canada and became Canadian Citizens in 1969. Their early years in Alberta were spent farming in the Bingley District near Rocky Mountain House.
In 1969, Paul took employment as a correctional officer in Nordegg and in 1972 transferred to the Peace River Correctional Institute in Northwestern Alberta. They purchased a farm Southwest of Berwyn, which became their family home for 50 years. Paul resigned from the Correctional Institute in 1979 to farm full-time. In 1986, Paul, Frances, and their son Mathew formalized the operation as Bogner Farms. In 1998 Bogner Farms was recognized by the Municipal District of Peace as Farm Family of the Year. Paul was especially proud when his feed barley was judged the highest quality in Alberta.
Paul broke his hip in 2022, requiring Paul & Frances to move into Stonebrook Assisted Living in Grimshaw Alberta. On June 1st, 2026 they celebrated their 67th wedding anniversary, a deeply meaningful time when all of their children and spouses were able to spend precious days with them.
Paul is survived by his loving wife, Frances; his children Stephen (Audrey), Annette (Peter deBoer), Matthew (Susan), Sylvia “Paulette”, Philip (Joan), Sarah (Allan Hart), and Paul “Christopher”; 18 grandchildren; 15 great-grandchildren; his sister Maryanne Kostelnik; sister-in-laws Josie Bogner, Rita Bogner, Bonnie Terry, Walterena Terry, and RuthAnn Paul; brother-in-law Floyd (Marlene) Terry; and many nieces and nephews.
Paul was predeceased by his parents, Cornelius and Mary Bogner; two granddaughters Katelyn Turner and Melody Carter (nee deBoer) and his siblings Mary Cecilia Schramm (Edward), Vincent Bogner (Marie), Mary Therese Mousel (Raymond), Mary Catherine Bernadine Dostal (Stanley), Cornelius Anthony Bogner (Julie), Donald Joseph Bogner (Josie), and Michael Bogner (Rita).
A Prayer Service & Viewing will be held on Thursday July 2nd at 7:00 p.m. from the Holy Family Catholic Church in Grimshaw, AB. 
A funeral Mass will be celebrated at the Holy Family Catholic Church in Grimshaw, AB on Friday July 3rd at 1:00 p.m.
The family extends a heartfelt thanks to Peace River Hospital staff and The Peace Palliative Care Society.

Obituary | Dennis Keyte of Peace River, Alberta
It is with deep sadness that the family of Dennis E.W. Keyte announces his passing on July 11, 2026, at the age of 79.
Dennis was born on November 24, 1946, in Calgary, Alberta. His interest in forestry led him to study at the University of British Columbia, where he met the love of his life, Norma Cherry. They were married in 1970 and shared 56 wonderful years together.
Dennis built a career in forestry, taking his family to Edson, Lac La Biche, and Whitecourt before they made Peace River, Alberta, their home in 1988.
After retiring in 2011, Dennis fulfilled a lifelong dream by earning his private pilot's license. Together, he and Norma embarked on many adventures, flying their little four-seat Cherokee across Canada. Their love of travel also took them around the world, with memorable trips to the United Kingdom, Europe, New Zealand, and Australia.
Dennis had a love of the outdoors and was an avid fisherman.
Dennis was predeceased by his parents, Bud and Olive Keyte.
He will be lovingly remembered by his wife, Norma; his daughters, Lori Keyte and Joanne Glendenning (Chad); his sister, Connie Curtis (Dick); his grandchildren, Ashton, Emer, Sarah, and Manissa; and his great-grandchildren, Admadeis and Killeagh. He also leaves behind many extended family members and friends.
In keeping with Dennis's wishes, no memorial service will be held.
In lieu of flowers, the family invites those wishing to honour Dennis's memory to make a donation to the charity of their choice.

Obituary | Philippe Gosselin of Smoky River, Alberta
Obituary for Philippe Gosselin
August 30, 1948 – June 26, 2026
It is with great sadness that the family of Philippe Gosselin announce his passing on June 26th, 2026 in Guy, Alberta at the age of 77.
Philippe was born on August 30, 1948 in McLennan, Alberta and was raised on the family farm in Guy, Alberta. Philippe attended Langlois School in Guy and ended up graduating at the High School in Falher. After graduation, Philippe worked on the farm with this father during seeding and harvest. Summers he worked for Gérard Paradis beekeeping and winters he worked on the oil rigs.
In 1972 Philippe purchased 3 quarters of land and continued farming with his father. Upon his father’s retirement Philippe purchased the home quarter. Philippe also purchased cattle and became a cattle farmer as well as a grain farmer. Philippe remained on the homestead upon his retirement in January 2013.
In 1977 Philippe met his future wife Lucie (Rey) Hebert and they married in 1981 when he became an instant father. Philippe enjoyed family life.

We are sadden to announce the passing of our mom, sister, grandmother & great grandmother.
Edith Margaret Green (nee Sigman) passed away peacefully in Peace River at the age of 92, on June 30, 2026.
We celebrate her life with our love and great admiration for the life she lead.
In 1953 she married George L. (Joe)Green and together they made their life in Red Deer. There they raised two daughters until in 1967 they made the move north to Peace River. Settling then to lower west peace. In 1971 they built the house adding the garage/shop where they worked together until the passing of dad in 1986 mom proudly maintained the house and huge yard by herself for the next forty years. She worked out doing housework all while fixing whatever needed, grew a massive garden with everything from a kiwi to a gourd. She would spade the garden every year by hand say working in the dirt was her spring therapy.
If she wasn’t in the garden she was busy doing her many other favorite things, her woodwork of all sorts, needlepoint, tapestries, knitting and most important coffee with her dear friends.
She was predeceased by her husband George Green, grandsons Patrick M Green & Tyler J Stranaghan.
She leaves behind her daughters Lynda (Kurt) Hansen, Lesly (Barry) Stranaghan. Four Grandchildren Steven(Trista)Stranaghan, Stacy Stranaghan, Kimberly(Mike) Chartrand, Kailei (Chase)Stranaghan. Plus seven great grandchildren. Kimberly, Brooke, Taylor, Georgia, Nixon, Ryder, & Tanner.

text:
Obituary | Clement 'Clem' Laurin of Tangent, Alberta
We are saddened to announce that on April 22, 2026, surrounded by his wife and family, Clement (Clem) Joseph André Laurin, age 90, of Tangent, Alberta, passed away in the Peace River Hospital.
Clement Laurin was born October 7th, 1935, in the community of Nipissing, Ontario, to French-Canadian parents Donat Ignace Laurin (b. 1898) and Marie-Louise Agnes (called Agnes) Laurin née Shank (b. 1908); who were married in 1926. He was welcomed into a busy household of Laurins: he was the sixth of nine children, preceded by his sister Juliette, and brothers Victor, Omer, Girard (bébé) (d. 1933), and Roger. In the next six years, the family welcomed his brothers Maurice, Émile, and sister Françoise.
In 1942, his father, Donat, passed away. A few years later, Clement and his family moved to a farm in Tangent, Alberta, after his mother, Agnes, married Théophile Legault. The family quickly grew to include Marie, Bernard (Bernie), Jacqueline (Jacquie), André (Andy), Raymond, Diane, and Murielle Legault.
As a young adult, around 1956, Clement left Tangent, and began work on the coast of British Columbia: felling trees for highways and transmission line right-of-ways. In his later years, he often recounted vivid memories of how his crew felled gigantic redwoods over the sides of cliffs, directly into the ocean. Not long after, Clem began working for a contractor, building roadways in Europe and later, during the Algerian War, rebuilding roads that had been bombed in Africa.
It was in France, in the late 1950s, in a little café in Paris, that he met the first love of his life: Annie Françoise Marcelle Rémond (b. 1940). He once said he loved her so much, he married her twice: first, around 1958 in Africa; then again, not long after, in France. Clement and Annie had three children together: Richard (b. 1959), and Alexandre (b. 1964).
Clement was a world traveler for most of his life—at one point, even building an airport in Tahiti—and he often encouraged his family to see the world. He, Annie, and the children frequently relocated due to Clem's work. They came 'home' to Canada in 1965, where some of the projects he worked on included widening The Welland Canal in Ontario, and building roads for the James Bay Hydro Project in Quebec and a hydro dam in Manitoba. Even the earliest dirt work at Syncrude, near Fort McMurray, was managed by Clem. After decades spent working across the world, the family decided it was time to put down roots, and settled in Tangent, AB, in 1976; purchasing a farm just across the road from the Legault family farm.
On October 1, 1997, his wife, Annie, passed away when she was 57 years old. They were married for nearly 40 years.
In 2004, his son, Alex, moved onto the family farm, with his wife and three children. Clement and Alex farmed together for many years, before Clem retired from farm work in 2015.
In 2008, while visiting Hawaii, he met Greta Botham from Sundre, Alberta. The two were married in 2022, at the Saints Martyrs Canadiens Church, in Tangent, AB.
The last years of his life were marked by a difficult battle with dementia. This made the moments when he felt most like himself all the more precious. He enjoyed good wine, family meals, complaining about the weather, sneaking sweets, and a daily cup of coffee shared with his son, Alex. Every once in a while, he would share stories from his life. These stories were a rare gift to those who heard them: the history of a truly incredible man, whose life was colourful, adventurous, and well-lived.
Clem is predeceased by his father Donat Laurin and mother Agnes Legault née Shank; grandparents William Laurin & Philomène Laurin née LaPrairie, Edmond Shank & Célanise Shank née Valade; his wife, Annie Laurin née Rémond; his sisters Juliette Portelance née Laurin, Françoise Yaremko née Laurin; his brothers Victor Laurin, Omer Laurin, Girard Laurin, Maurice Laurin, Bernard Legault, Émile Legault; his granddaughter Angella Laurin.
He is survived by his wife, Greta; his children, Richard Laurin (Debbie), Alex Laurin (Lynne); his grandchildren, William Laurin, Krystian Laurin, Danielle Henry née Laurin (Travis), Mackenzie Laurin, and Alexis Laurin; great-grandchildren Levi Laurin, Cecilia Clementine Henry, and Finn Henry; his siblings, Jacqueline Purcha née Legault, André Legault (Jeanie), Raymond Legault, Roger Laurin, Diane Grenier née Legault, and Murielle Marceau née Legault.
We want to express our heartfelt gratitude to the care staff of the Peace River Hospital, who worked to give our loved one peace and dignity during his last days.
We will be hosting Clem's Funeral Service on Saturday, July 4, 2026, at 2pm, at the Saints Martyrs Canadiens Church in Tangent, AB. He will be laid to rest beside his beloved wife, Annie Laurin, in Saints Martyrs Canadiens Cemetery.

text:
Obituary | Rose Henderson of Peace River, Alberta
Rose Henderson, long-time resident of Grimshaw, passed away on July 19th, 2026 in Peace River at the age of 99 years.

Rose was born and raised in Rycroft of Ukrainian parents and the youngest of five daughters. She was raised on a farm north of Rycroft. Despite Depression era hardship, she grew up with culture and music. She played piano and the mandolin.

She met and married her husband, Keith Henderson of Berwyn in 1949. They were together for 47 years until his passing in 1996. They had one son, John, born in 1967. Rose worked primarily as a bookkeeper for many businesses in Grimshaw, some being Grimshaw Trucking, Houlder’s, and Jonson Drugs. She also volunteered extensively, including the Royal Purple and the curling club.

Rose had an extensive post-retirement life of cards, travel, golf and most importantly, an extensive network of friends and neighbours.

She is predeceased by husband Keith Henderson, parents George and Sophia Rosko, sisters Mary Johnston, Anne Favine, Sadie Hudyma and Elizabeth, nephew Jerry Rosko, nieces Bettie Davison and Ronaye.

Rose is survived by son John, daughter-in-law Annette, and grandsons Brendan, Deston and Payton. Nieces Marlene, Wanda, Marilyn and Louise.

She counted Keith’s parents, brothers and sisters as her own even long after her passing.

Rose’s family wishes to thank and offer gratitude to those continued to stay close to her despite late in life challenges. The hard-working staff of Heritage Towers and Peace River hospital nurses and doctors. Thank you to the many friends of Rose. 
A celebration of life will be held on Monday, July 27 at 2:00 pm at the Grimshaw Legion with lunch to follow. Interment will be done privately by family.

To plant Memorial Trees in memory of Rose Henderson, please click here to visit our sympathy store.

text:
Obituary | Gerald Monette of Faro, Yukon
Gerald Joseph Monette, resident of Faro, Yukon, passed away April 10, 2026 at the age of 68, at the Vancouver General Hospital, surrounded by family and friends. Born in McLennan, Alberta, he was the sixth of eight children of Raymonde (Simard) and Guy Monette.
Affectionately known as “Frenchie”, Gerald will be remembered for his adventurous spirit, love of the open road, and deep loyalty to those he cared for. Raised on a farm west of Jean-Côté, Gerald’s independent nature and sense of adventure were evident from a young age.
It was there that his passion for exploration began to take shape, eventually leading him to pursue a life beyond the traditional classroom. Leaving school in the 10th grade, he followed his calling and built a life of trucking—embracing the freedom and challenge of the road he loved so much.
Gerald’s life was defined not only by his work, but by the strong connections he built along the way. He loved summer fishing and spent several weeks each fall hunting in the bush with friends. He will be fondly remembered for his loyalty, his warmth, and the many friendships he nurtured over the years.
He was predeceased by his wife Caroline and daughter Angele; his parents, Guy and Raymonde; his brothers, Richard and Roger; and, his sisters Carmen and Jeanine.
Gerald is survived and will be dearly missed by his loving sons Dustin and Ronnie; his sisters Henriette, Gaetane, and Linda (Catherine); as well as many nieces, nephews, and dear friends.
Gerald’s life was one of independence, resilience, and connection. Though he has taken his final journey, his presence will remain in the stories shared, the memories held close, and in the hearts of all who knew him.

A Graveside Service will take place on Monday, July 6, 2026 at 1:30 p.m. from Jean-Côté Cemetery.

To plant Memorial Trees in memory of Gerald Monette, please click here to visit our sympathy store.

Obituary | Clinton Nichols of Salt Prairie, Alberta
It is with great sadness that we announce the sudden passing of Clint Nichols of Salt Prairie on June 6, 2026 after a short stay in the High Prairie Health Complex.
Clint was born on December 22, 1949, in High Prairie, Alberta to Phil Nichols and Doris (Walker) Nichols. He was a middle child of four sons to Doris and Phil Nichols of Salt Prairie. 
On May 2, 1981, Clint married Kim (Bissell) in Enilda, Alberta. They lived in Salt Prairie where they raised their family, farmed, and worked, while being active members of the community.
Clint was an unstoppable force when he set his mind to something. He helped host many of the Walker-Hoffman family reunions. He was a long-serving member of the Salt Prairie Settlement Community Club. He worked in the area in the oilfield and in forestry. He farmed in the area alongside his brothers and longtime neighbours for most of his life.
Clint was predeceased by his parents, Phil and Doris, and brothers Rodney and George. Clint leaves behind his wife Kim, children Kyle Nichols and Cailyn (Cody) Pillipow, grandsons Chase and Mason Pillipow, brother Duane (Luann) Nichols, and countless family members.
Clint is lovingly remembered by his wife, children, grandchildren, and extended family and friends.
A celebration of Clint’s life will be held on July 18, 2026, at the Salt Prairie Hall.

Obituary | Francis Lessard of McLennan, Alberta
Francis Jean Lessard
January 6, 1953 – June 29, 2026
It is with deep sadness that we announce the passing of Francis Jean Lessard, born January 6, 1953, in McLennan, Alberta.
Francis will be lovingly remembered by his four children and their spouses: Kristen and Alain, Taryn and Justin, Celty and Mathieu, and Justin and Tamarra. He also leaves behind his former wife, Marion his eight cherished grandchildren: Melody, Maelle, Nate, Ellie, Rosalynn, Nash, Tye, and Remy. His family was a constant source of pride and joy, and he treasured the time he spent with each of them.
Francis dedicated much of his life to education as a teacher at McLennan Providence School, Alberta Vocational College, and E.W. Pratt High School, where he inspired countless students through his patience, knowledge, and commitment to helping others succeed. His influence reached far beyond the classroom. He was a passionate advocate for his community, generously giving his time and energy to local organizations, programs, and initiatives. Francis believed in the importance of building strong communities and worked
tirelessly to make a positive difference in the lives of those around him.
He will be remembered for his kindness, generosity, unwavering dedication to others, and
his belief in the potential of every person he met. Francis always brought joy and humor into
every situation. His legacy lives on through the many students he taught, athletes he
coached, the community he helped strengthen, and the family he loved so deeply. Everyone
will remember his joy de vie; quite fondly.
Francis will be greatly missed by his family, friends, former colleagues, students, and all
whose lives were touched by his compassion and service. Francis is predeceased by his
parents; brother-in-laws, niece and nephew. He is survived by his brother and four sisters.
The family extends their heartfelt gratitude to everyone who has shared their love, support,
and memories during this difficult time.
In lieu of flowers, donations can be made to the Terry Fox Foundation or the McLennan Royal Canadian Legion Branch #153 (mclennan153@hotmail.com).
A funeral service will be held at St. John the Baptist Cathedral in McLennan, July 30th at 2:00 pm.

It is with profound sadness that the family of Brennen Walker announces his sudden passing on July 7, 2026, at the age of 29.

Obituary | Audrey Langer of Three Creeks, Alberta
Audrey Pearl Langer passed away peacefully at the Peace River Hospital on July 9, 2026, at the age of 84.
Born in Bedeque, Prince Edward Island, Audrey brought her brave, hardworking spirit to Three Creeks, Alberta, in 1957. Together with her husband, Richard, she built a beautiful life on the family farm. She was a woman of deep warmth, quick wit, and endless devotion to her family and community.
Audrey was born on December 17, 1941, in Bedeque, Prince Edward Island, at the home of her Aunt Pearl. She was the fifth of six children born to Rena and Annie Stordy. She grew up calling Cape Traverse, P.E.I., home. In the winter of 1957, she made a courageous journey across the country to start a brand-new life in Three Creeks, Alberta, with her husband, Richard.
In her youth, Audrey worked as a waitress in Summerside before fully embracing the role of a dedicated farmer's wife, becoming an expert tractor driver, root picker, and livestock manager. Her vibrant interests included tending to her famously successful vegetable garden, baking her beloved thimble cookies, and leading the music program for the Community Christmas Concert. She also loved annual camping trips to Jasper and Banff, attending regional rodeos and chuckwagon races, and passionately following hockey and curling as an avid Edmonton Oilers fan.
Alongside her husband, Richard, Audrey successfully built up their family farm quarter by quarter and transitioned it into raising purebred animals. Her ultimate and proudest life accomplishment was her family: successfully raising her children and serving as the devoted, loving, foundational anchor for multiple generations of grandchildren, great-grandchildren, and great-great-grandchildren.
Audrey was a pillar of her local community, most notably directing and managing the music arrangements and rehearsals for the annual Community Christmas Concert, bringing the neighborhood children together every year.
Audrey was predeceased by her daughter Merna; her infant daughter Connie Langer; and her parents Rena and Annie Stordy.
She is lovingly remembered by her husband Richard Langer; her children Barb (Wayne), Carmen, Mark (Dana), and Tammy (Don); her eight grandchildren Cherene, Brad, Clayton, Ricky, Candice, Darcy, Kyle, and Kayla; multiple generations of great and great-great-grandchildren.
Audry will be interred at the Three Creeks Cemetery.

text:
Obituary | Allan Carroll of Valleyview, Alberta
Born and raised in Portage la Prairie, Manitoba, Al's life was marked by adventure, hard work, service, and an unwavering commitment to family.
As a young man, Al joined the Royal Canadian Mounted Police, a career that brought him to Alberta, where he met and married the love of his life, Sharon (Fell). Over their 56 years of marriage, they embraced new opportunities and along the way raised three children, creating a family rooted in love and support.
After his years with the RCMP, Al and Sharon successfully owned and operated several businesses, including a couple Dairy Queen franchises, one of which brought them to Fort St John, British Columbia where they called home for 10 years. In 1995, they returned to Valleyview, Alberta, where they planted their final roots and became deeply involved in the community they loved. They owned and operated Valley Feeds until they “retired” and sold the business in 2005. Not done yet, Al returned to public service as the Community Peace Officer, continuing his lifelong commitment to helping others and strengthening the community they called home.
Al will be remembered not only for his leadership and strong work ethic, but for his kindness, integrity, and willingness to lend a helping hand. He believed strongly in giving back and dedicated countless hours to charitable service organizations where he lived including the Kinsmen Club of Portage La Prairie and the Rotary Club of Fort St John. In Valleyview he proudly served as an active member of the Elks 321 and Rural Crime Watch where he volunteered on both the local and provincial boards.
Above all else, Al was a devoted husband, father, and grandfather. His family was the centre of his world. He was the kind of dad who was always there - offering guidance, encouragement, and steady support through every stage of life. He rarely missed a sporting event, school activity, or milestone, proudly cheering from the sidelines and celebrating every success, big or small. His love, wisdom, sense of humour, and quiet strength will continue to live on through each of them.
Al leaves behind his beloved wife, Sharon; his daughter Shawna (Shawn); his son Bob (Michelle); and his daughter Kim (Sean). He was a proud and loving grandfather to Devan, Ella, Kadam, Ryan, Laird, and Sloan, each of whom held a special place in his heart.
Al was predeceased by his parents, as well as his brother Brian and sister Ida. He is survived by his sister Anne.
The family would like to extend their heartfelt gratitude to the healthcare professionals who provided compassionate care and support during the past several months.
A celebration of Al's life will be held on August 14th at the Memorial Hall in Valleyview, at 2:00 P.M.
Forever loved, forever missed, and forever in our hearts.

text:
Obituary | June Macmillan of Peace River, Alberta
June Macmillan of Peace River passed away peacefully on July 10, 2026, at the age of 95.
June was born in Grimshaw on June 20, 1931, to William Miller and Margaret Anderson. She attended school in Grimshaw, Berwyn and Peace River, graduating from Peace River High School in 1949.
On May 16, 1950, June married John Macmillan marking the beginning of a loving relationship that spanned many decades. John and June made a home together on the Macmillan farm where they worked the land and established Macmillan Construction. It was during these early years that she found her passion for competitive curling, the Oilwives Club, cooking, gardening, and decorating among countless other hobbies. John and June took time to travel and enjoyed their second home in Summerland, BC.
While on the farm they raised their five children; Archie (Torrie), Bill (Tannis), Linda, Ron (Helen) and Brenda (Brian). June was a proud grandmother of 11 grandchildren and 15 great grandchildren. She is predeceased by her husband John and all of her brothers and sisters.
June was a woman of extraordinary creativity and artistic talent. She took joy in tole painting, producing beautiful hand-crafted pieces. June enjoyed entertaining her many friends and family and took great pride in her home, which was always perfectly decorated for every occasion. She delighted in playing cards and was always ready for a game. June had numerous interests that she loved to share with others, whether it was a good book, a crafting skill or some of her lifestyle wisdom.
June had a radiant smile and an infectious laugh that endeared her to all that knew her. She carried herself with poise and grace, always courteous. June was elegant, with a keen sense of style and was impeccable in all ways. Never taking her life for granted, June left knowing she had lived a grand life.
A private ceremony to honor June will be held at a later date.

text:
Obituary | Herdis Ferguson (née Larsen) of Calgary, Alberta
Herdis Ferguson of Calgary, AB, passed away at home in Calgary on Thursday, June 18, 2026, at the age of 96 years.
Herdis was born in Plaster Rock, NB, on March 24, 1930, to Karl Larsen and Alice Field. As a child, she moved with her family to Apple River, NS. She taught school for a year in the New Salem area before moving to Halifax, NS, to work.
She met Ernest Troup Ferguson in 1952, and in 1954 travelled west, where they were married in Calgary on May 8. Shortly thereafter, circumstances brought them north to settle in Judah, AB, just south of Peace River, where they began their family and where Herdis would spend most of her adult life.
Herdis had very fond memories of working at the Peace River Post Office for a few years after Neil was born, and while Ernest recovered from tuberculosis. She was a full-time mom to Neil, John, and Margaret, and remained a strong presence in the lives of her grandsons, Rorrie and Erin. She was involved with the Judah community, worked for a few years at The Bay, and she supported Ernest with his electrical company until he retired.
She loved people and liked to read, to listen, and to discuss almost anything. Her favourite topics were current affairs and matters of philosophy and metaphysics. She was very interested in interior and exterior design and the world of fashion, and she loved to try new recipes, working around her husband’s meat and potatoes palate to bring to life some great Canadian recipes. She had a tenacious spirit, and an infectious smile and laugh. Herdis loved her family dearly.
She was predeceased by son John Larsen Ferguson (Peace River, 1962-1975), and her husband Ernest Troup Ferguson (Peace River, 1927-2001). She was also predeceased by brothers Peter (Helen) Larsen of High River, AB, Clemm (Phyllis) Larsen of Brandon, MB, and Olaf (Estelle) Larsen of Parrsboro, NS; Edith (Arthur) Fillmore, Advocate Harbour, NS, and her parents, Karl and Alice, interred in Apple River, NS. 
Herdis is survived by her son Neil, and daughter-in-law Heather, of High Prairie, AB; daughter Margaret of Calgary, AB, grandson, Rorrie of High Prairie, AB, grandson, Erin and wife Shelly of Slave Lake, AB; great-grandchildren, Ava, Ethan, and Ash; sister, Laura and her husband David Bezanson of Truro, NS, as well as many beloved nieces and nephews. We recognize all the Ferguson, Troup, Larsen, Field, Bezanson, Davies, and Wartnow families and relatives, nearby and abroad, as well as our friends in Judah, Peace River, Calgary, and elsewhere. Special gratitude to Tony vanden Berg of Calgary, AB, who has assisted the family in so many ways throughout the years.
A funeral service will be held on Saturday, June 27, 2026 at 2:00p.m., from Chapel of Memories Funeral Home, Peace River, AB; viewing will preceding the service. Interment will conclude at Judah Cemetery.
If friends so desire, memorial tributes may be made directly to the Children's Wish Foundation.

text:
Obituary | Elsie McDonnell of Peace River, Alberta
Elsie Mae McDonnell, a longtime resident of the Three Creeks and Peace Region, peacefully passed away on Saturday, July 11, 2026, at the age of 85.
Elsie had a deep love for books and poetry, writing many of her own poems and short stories throughout her life. She also found great joy in making photo albums, which she always beautifully decorated with stickers and personal anecdotes. She was a passionate documenter of both family and local history. Notably, Elsie was integral to the collaboration and editing of the local history book, 'Mosquitoes, Muskegs and Memories', which details the history of Wesley Creek and Three Creeks.
Elsie is lovingly survived by her husband of nearly 29 years, William "Bud" McDonnell; her sons, Ben (Marlene) and Barry (Collin); her daughter, Peggy (Tyler); and her sisters, Gayle (David) and Christine (George). She also leaves behind numerous nieces, nephews, grandchildren, and great-grandchildren who will cherish her memory.
She was predeceased by her parents, Cecil and Margret Harrop; her brothers, Frank, Donald, Hugh, and Jim; her first husband, Ronald Kunstleben; her children, Laverne, Pearl, and Calvin; and her grandson, Dustin.
A simplified graveside service will be held on Saturday, August 15th at 11:00 am at the Three Creeks Cemetery. Family and friends are welcome to join to say a few words about Elsie or to simply support the family with their presence.
