text:
Children | Verses for Funeral Cards
#1C – A Thought, A Wish, A Hope, A Prayer
Author: Unknown
Our child came to us as a thought,
A thought that we had love to share
A thought that we would come to care
So very much for this first child.
Our child came to us with a wish,
A wish that he’d grow strong and proud,
A wish that we would be allowed
To grow with him, with this first child.
Our child came to us with a hope,
A hope that he would laugh and play
Throughout his childhood, day by day,
While we watched over this first child.
Our first child came to us with a prayer,
A prayer that he’d be safe and sound,
A prayer that love would soon abound
Throughout our house for this first child.
Our first child left us with a thought,
A thought that life was not secure,
A thought that nothing is ever sure,
And then he was gone, and with him our thoughts.
Our first child left us with a wish
A wish that time had been more kind,
A wish that we find peace of mind,
And then he was gone, and with him our wishes.
Our first child left us with a hope,
A hope that he was safe above,
A hope that he had known our love,
A hope that he had known our love,
And then he was gone, and with him our prayers.
Our first child left us with a prayer, 
A prayer that we remember him, a prayer that we can start again,
#C2 - God’s Loan
I’ll lend to you for a little time
A child of “mine” He said
For you to love the while he lives
And mourn for when he’s dead.
He may be six or seven years
Or twenty-two or three
But will you, till I call for him
Take care of him for me?
He’ll bring his charms to gladden you
And should his stay be brief
You’ll have his lovely memories
As solace for your grief.
I cannot promise he will stay
Since all from Earth return
But there are lessons taught down there
I want this child to learn.
I’ve looked this wide world over
In my search for Teachers true
And from things that crowd life’s lanes
I have selected you.
Now will you give him all your love
Not think the labour vain
Nor hate me when I come to call
And take him back again.
I fancied that I heard them say
“Dear Lord, Thy Will Be Done”
For all the joys the child will bring
The risk of grief we’ll run.
We’ll shelter him with tenderness
We’ll love him while I may
And for the happiness we’ve known
Forever grateful stay.
But should the angels call for him
Much sooner than we planned
We’ll brave the bitter grief that comes
#C3 - An Angel Never Dies
Don’t let them say I wasn’t born,
That something stopped my heart.
I felt each tender squeeze you gave.
I’ve loved you from the start.
Although my body you can’t hold,
It doesn’t mean I’m gone.
This world was worthy not of me.
God chose that I move on.
I know the pain that drowns your soul,
What you are forced to face.
You have my word, I’ll find your arms,
Someday we will embrace.
You’ll hear that it was “meant to be”
“God doesn’t make mistakes”.
But that won’t soften your worst blow,
Or make your heart not ache.
I’m watching over all you do,
Another child, you’ll bear.
Believe me when I say to you
That I am always there.
There will come a time, I promise you,
When you will hold my hand,
Stroke my face and kiss my lips,
And then you’ll understand.
Although I’ve never breathed your air,
Or gazed into your eyes,
That doesn’t mean I never “was”
An angel never dies.
#C4 - Child’s Prayer
“Now I lay me down to sleep;
I pray Thee, Lord, my soul to keep.
If I should die before I wake,
I pray Thee, Lord, my should to take.”
#C5
He has gone to be an angel
Secure in our Father’s care,
And his dear little feet now patter along
The beautiful streets up there.
#C6
Tiny little hands
So busy from the start
Reach up to touch your face-
Reach out to touch your heart.
“______” touched our hearts with wonder
#C7 - Heaven’s Very Special Child
A meeting was held quite far from Earth
“It’s time again for another birth”
Said the angels to the Lord above,
“This Special Child will need much love.”
His progress may seem very slow,
Accomplishment he may not show;
And he’ll require extra care
Form the folks he meets down there.
He may not run or laugh or play,
His thoughts may seem quite far away
In many ways he won’t adapt
And he’ll be known as handicapped.
So let’s be careful where he’s sent;
We want his life to be content.
Please, Lord, find the Parents who
Will do a special job for you.
They will not realize right away
The leading role they’re asked to play.
But with this child sent from above
Comes stronger faith and richer love.
And soon they’ll know the privilege given
In caring for the gift from Heaven.
Their precious charge, so meek and mild
Is Heaven’s Very Special Child.
#C8 - Our Precious Angel
We have a child that few ever will know
She was here just a moment and then had to go.
She had curly dark hair and a perfect little nose.
The face of an angel, as beautiful as a rose.
She watches and helps us now from above.
She has others with her that surround her with love.
With a perfect little halo and wonderful wings,
She guides us through all life’s difficult things.
We wish she were here, in our arms.
For us to enjoy all her exceptional charms.
We ache for her with all of our heart.
Life moves on, but ours just won’t start.
We love you sweet ________, so precious and dear.
We will miss you forever, and more with each tear.
#C9 - Little Angels
When God calls little children to dwell with Him above,
We mortals sometime question the wisdom of His love.
For no heartache compares with the death of one small child
Who does so much to make our world, 
seem wonderful and mild
Perhaps God tires of calling the aged to his fold,
So He picks a rosebud, before it can grow old.
God knows how much we need them, 
and so He takes but few
To make the land of Heaven more beautiful to view.
Believing this is difficult still somehow we must try,
The saddest word mankind knows will always be "Goodbye."
So when a little child departs, we who are left behind
Must realize God loves children, Angels are hard to find.
#C10 - Little Angels 
Change the name, age and gender for your own situation
God sent an angel to the earth...
The sweetest angel too
and for such a tiny little thing,
she had so much to do.
She knew she did not have
much time upon this earth to stay,
so she did not waste a second;
she got started right away.
Her eyes were bright and sparkly,
she took in every turn.
She did not miss a single thing,
because Angel came to learn!
God sent her here to touch the
hearts of those he could not reach...
She taught them courage, strength and faith,
because Angel came to teach.
Her tiny little body
was so full of God above,
you felt it when you held her,
because “Kaitlyn” came to love.
In eleven short months she managed
what many never will.
When she went home to Jesus,
her purpose was fulfilled.
She learned and taught, loved and played,
she learned her lessons well.
I know he was so proud of her
when she went home to dwell.
#C11 – A Baby’s Secret
I’m just a little person
And I didn’t quite make it there
I went straight to be with Jesus
And I’m waiting for you here
Don’t you fret about me, mommy
I’m of all Gods lamb’s most blest
I’d have loved to have stayed there with you
But our Shepherd knows what’s best
Many dwellings here where I live
Waited years to enter in
Struggled through a world of sorrow
And their lives were marred with sin
So sweet Mommy don’t you sorrow
Chase the gloom and whip the tears;
I went straight to Jesus’ bosom
May your heartache disappear
#C12 – A Prayer for A Baby and Its Family
Oh Lord God, thank you for this precious child who now rests gently in your loving arms
We know from your Word that you form each one and you do not forget us. We rejoice that this little angel is with the heavenly chorus in the company of all the angels praising you forever
Dearest Lord, we ask your comfort for this child’s parents, grandparents, and extended families who grieve the loss of this little one. Grant them your strength and courage to trust in your power to transform all sorrow and suffering into blessing and hope
Sustain these parents and their families with your Holy Spirit. Supply their every need in abundance. Surround each one with an added measure of your love. And give them knowledge of your peace.
This we ask in the name of your Son, Jesus Christ, Amen.
“He will swallow up death in victory and the Lord God will wipe away the tears from all faces.” (Isiah 25:8) 
#129 – It’s Not the Time
It’s not the time that you have on Earth,
It’s what you do while you’re here,
It’s what you do with what you’ve got
And the standards you hold dear.
What matters most when someone hurts
Is what you choose to do
And who comes first in your scheme of life,
The other fellow or you.
We know not the day or the hour that comes
For us to leave this earth:
What matters is what we leave behind,
A sigh of relief or dearth.
Today is the time to make your choice,
How will you live your life,
To help somebody who stands in need, 
Or leave that person in strife?

she got started right away.

Her eyes were bright and sparkly,  
she took in every turn.  
She did not miss a single thing,  
because Angel came to learn!  
God sent her here to touch the  
hearts of those he could not reach...  
She taught them courage, strength and faith,  
because Angel came to teach.

Her tiny little body  
was so full of God above,  
you felt it when you held her,  
because “Kaitlyn” came to love.

In eleven short months she managed  
what many never will.  
When she went home to Jesus,  
her purpose was fulfilled.  
She learned and taught, loved and played,  
she learned her lessons well.  
I know he was so proud of her  
when she went home to dwell.

**#C11 – A Baby’s Secret**

I’m just a little person

And I didn’t quite make it there

I went straight to be with Jesus

And I’m waiting for you here

Don’t you fret about me, mommy

I’m of all Gods lamb’s most blest

I’d have loved to have stayed there with you

But our Shepherd knows what’s best

Many dwellings here where I live

Waited years to enter in

Struggled through a world of sorrow

And their lives were marred with sin

So sweet Mommy don’t you sorrow

                     Chase the gloom and whip the tears;

I went straight to Jesus’ bosom

May your heartache disappear

**#C12 – A Prayer for A Baby and Its Family**

Oh Lord God, thank you for this precious child who now rests gently in your loving arms

We know from your Word that you form each one and you do not forget us.  We rejoice that this little angel is with the heavenly chorus in the company of all the angels praising you forever

Dearest Lord, we ask your comfort for this child’s parents, grandparents, and extended families who grieve the loss of this little one.  Grant them your strength and courage to trust in your power to transform all sorrow and suffering into blessing and hope

Sustain these parents and their families with your Holy Spirit.  Supply their every need in abundance.  Surround each one with an added measure of your love.  And give them knowledge of your peace.

This we ask in the name of your Son, Jesus Christ, Amen.

_“He will swallow up death in victory and the Lord God will wipe away the tears from all faces.” (Isiah 25:8)_ 

**#129 – It’s Not the Time**

It’s not the time that you have on Earth,  
It’s what you do while you’re here,  
It’s what you do with what you’ve got  
And the standards you hold dear.

What matters most when someone hurts  
Is what you choose to do  
And who comes first in your scheme of life,  
The other fellow or you.

We know not the day or the hour that comes  
For us to leave this earth:  
What matters is what we leave behind,  
A sigh of relief or dearth.

Today is the time to make your choice,

_How will you live your life,  
To help somebody who stands in need,   
Or leave that person in strife?_

Obituary | Albert Dumont of McLennan, Alberta
Obituary for Albert Hector Dumont
It is with deep sorrow that the family of Albert Hector Dumont announce his peaceful passing on March 22nd, 2026 at the McLennan hospital at the age of 93.
Albert was born on October 20th, 1932 on the family homestead in Girouxville. He was the youngest of the six children born to Léon Dumont and Adrienne Brien.
Albert attended school in Girouxville for 8 years, then went on to obtain his high school diploma in Falher. After his graduation, Albert worked odd jobs in the area, and would help with the Dumont family farm operation. In 1953, he married Denise Maure of Falher, and they made their first home living in a small house in the yard of his father’s homestead. In 1967, Albert bought a quarter section half a mile from the homestead, and built a new home where he would reside with his family.
In 1984, Albert would sell his farm after 30 years of farming, and move to an apartment in Falher and a few years later bought a house. It is during these years that he would enjoy many of his retirement activities. His love of farming would remain as his number one activity, and it continued for the next forty years. During seeding and harvest time, Albert would regularly visit with local farmers to check various crops, take rides on combines and tractors to see how the crop was progressing. He also spent many hours quadding along his lease to check his own crop, and eventually down to Dumont’s Flats for some target shooting.
Some of Albert’s favourite activities were playing cards at Club Allouette and enjoying coffee at the Girouxville Co-Op. He regularly attended events like, Pioneer Days in Triangle, Wanham Tractor Pull, High Prairie Rodeo, local music festivals, Mud Boggs, Car shows, as well as fairs and trade shows. Camping, fishing, and partridge hunting were always a big part of his life. In August he would always save the date for the Annual Pilgrimage in Girouxville.
Albert enjoyed travelling to Miette, Fairmont, Kelowna and Jasper with his truck and trailer. He also took the opportunity to travel to Costa Rica, Mazatlan and North Dakota. One of his favourite trips was his Alaskan cruise in 2008 with his son, Gilbert.
In 2016 Albert moved to the Villa Beausejour. He made his home at the Villa until 2021, when closer monitoring of his diabetic health required his move to Manoir du Lac in Mclennan.
Albert is survived by his son Gilbert Dumont, daughter Joanne (Richard) Fournier, grand-daughters Kristel (Aidan) O’Connor and Angèle (Paul) Boutlier, and his five great-grandchildren, Audrey and William O’Connor, and Oswin, Beau and Emmett Boutilier.
Albert was predeceased by Denise (Maure) Dumont, his parents Léon and Adrienne Dumont, his brothers Edouard, Paul, Fred, Jean, and his sister Jeanette (Leonard) Garneau.
The family takes this time to thank Dr. deWet for his exceptional care and compassion provided to Albert throughout the years. Also, we express a heartfelt thank you to all nurses, staff and volunteers at Manoir du Lac for their care, compassion and kindness over the last four years.
A Memorial Mass will be held from Notre-Dame de Lourdes Catholic Church in Girouxville on Thursday July 9, 2026 at 10:30 AM.

text:
Obituary | Joy Gauvreau of Grimshaw, Alberta
Margaret Rose Joyce “Joy” Gauvreau (Manitowabi) — beloved wife, mom, grandma, sister, aunt, and long-time resident of Peace River—was called to rest on April 12, 2026, at the Marshall Eliuk Peace River Community Health Centre.
Born on July 12, 1947, on the traditional lands of Wiikwemkoong Unceded Territory, Ontario, Joy was the sixth child of David and Agatha (Mendoshkong) Manitowabi. Her roots on Manitoulin Island remained close to her heart throughout her life.
In April 1967, while visiting Grimshaw, Alberta, Joy met the love of her life, Gordon. He would become her partner in every sense, and, as love and luck would have it, they married just months later on September 16, 1967. Their life together took them from an eight-foot-wide trailer along the ditches of the Northwest Territories and Alberta, to Joy’s cherished Manitoulin Island, and through many communities in between—including Castor, Whitecourt, Grande Prairie, and Peace River. In time, the Peace River Valley became the place she called home.
Together, Joy and Gordon raised three children—Darlene (Herman) Wiebe, Karen (Jeff) Schoettler, and Don (Lindsay) Gauvreau—and were blessed with six grandchildren: Louis, Cassandra, Riley, Rachel, Averi, and Hayden.
Joy leaves behind her husband; her children and their spouses; her grandchildren; her eldest sister, Medora (Don) Hicks; her brothers, David (Susan) Manitowabi and Ronald Manitowabi; her sisters-in-law, Judy (Roy) Kezema, Laura (Steve) Kraft, Ruth Gauvreau, and Shelly Gauvreau; her brothers-in-law, Henry (Joy) Gauvreau, Andy (Carmen) Gauvreau, and James McGregor; as well as many nieces, nephews, great-nieces, and great-nephews. Jacinta (Jessie) and Rudy Corbiere held a very dear and special place in her heart.
She is reunited with those who went before her: her parents; her older sisters and their spouses—Catherine Manitowabi, Shirley (Don) McKay, Mary-Grace (Don) MacGregor, and Veronica Jacko (Andy Manitowabi); her younger brother, Peak Sr. (Dominic) Manitowabi; and her father and mother-in-law Laurie and Helen Gauvreau.
Joy was gifted in so many ways. Her beadwork—moccasins, gauntlets, and other pieces—found homes across Canada and around the world. She was a talented quilter, sewer, crocheter, and knitter, and she was happiest when she could gift something handmade to someone she loved. She was also an exceptional cook, baker, and soup maker. “Mom taught us how to cook and whenever anyone would say the kids are good cooks, Dad would always say, ‘well, they learned from the best!’”
Some of Joy’s other pastimes were playing cards, camping, golfing, boating, fishing, and bowling with family and friends. Joy also loved her furry 4-legged friends, so please consider a donation to your local SPCA in lieu of flowers.
We would like to extend our heartfelt thank you to the Doctors and Nurses in Acute Care for their compassion, kindness, and attentive care. Your support and comfort meant so much to Joy and to our family during this difficult time.
A Mass to honour Joy’s life will be held on July 10, 2026, at 1:00 p.m. at Our Lady of Peace Catholic Church in Peace River, with interment to follow at Judah Hill Cemetery.
Her life was a tapestry—
threads of courage, colour, and care.
Every stitch placed with purpose,
every gift a quiet prayer.
Now her hands are resting,
but her patterns carry on—
in the lives she shaped with kindness,
and the love that keeps her memory strong.

text:
About Us | Chapel of Memories Ltd
A Legacy in Alberta's North
Peace River's first recorded formal funeral service was provided by a known George Fields, who operated an undertaking business in a small building on Main Street. He constructed caskets, prepared the decedents-from washing and dressing, casketing-and offered horse-drawn carriage processions for the funeral service.
The first documented record of a funeral in the northern Peace Country comes from Griep and Humphries Funeral Home (1947). Benny Griep & John Humphreys (Griep & Humphreys) carried forward the Field business. They operated offices in High Prairie, Peace River, Fairview and McLennan. In 1963, a family from Calgary (the Allan Nixon family) acquired the operation. In Fairview, Keith Moran and Moran Funeral Home served families.
In 1967, Roger Winnicky became the proprietor; therefore, bringing forth "Chapel of Memories". The funeral home(s) ran an ambulance services until 1973. 'Vern' Weber, in 1979, became a stakeholder and operating manager. Moran Funeral Home, in Fairview, soon became a subsidiary, following the retirement of Keith Moran. In the same year of 1985, Arnold Patterson, whom had taken partnership in High Prairie, sold his shares to Vern Weber. In the early 2000s, Slave Lake's (Brian) Wilton Funeral Service also merged with Chapel of Memories.
In 2010, understanding that Vern (and Marion) Weber so well-served their local communities, Chester Dodgson and Rémi Tardif stepped forward, in continuing the care that the Pioneers of the Peace Country have come to expect. In 2021, Chester Dodgson retired by selling to Rémi Tardif.
A new crematorium was functional in April 2018. Based at the Peace River location, it is Alberta's northernmost crematorium.
In the lobby Peace River's Chapel's foyer, a pillar of brick supports a plaque indicating: "Show me the manner in which a nation or community cares for its dead and I will measure with mathematical exactness the tender sympathies of its people, their respect for the laws of the land and their loyalty to high ideals." - Gladstone.

# About Us | Chapel of Memories Ltd

### A Legacy in Alberta's North

Peace River's first recorded formal funeral service was provided by a known George Fields, who operated an undertaking business in a small building on Main Street. He constructed caskets, prepared the decedents-from washing and dressing, casketing-and offered horse-drawn carriage processions for the funeral service.

The first documented record of a funeral in the northern Peace Country comes from Griep and Humphries Funeral Home (1947). Benny Griep & John Humphreys (Griep & Humphreys) carried forward the Field business. They operated offices in High Prairie, Peace River, Fairview and McLennan. In 1963, a family from Calgary (the Allan Nixon family) acquired the operation. In Fairview, Keith Moran and Moran Funeral Home served families.

In 1967, Roger Winnicky became the proprietor; therefore, bringing forth "Chapel of Memories". The funeral home(s) ran an ambulance services until 1973. 'Vern' Weber, in 1979, became a stakeholder and operating manager. Moran Funeral Home, in Fairview, soon became a subsidiary, following the retirement of Keith Moran. In the same year of 1985, Arnold Patterson, whom had taken partnership in High Prairie, sold his shares to Vern Weber. In the early 2000s, Slave Lake's (Brian) Wilton Funeral Service also merged with Chapel of Memories.

In 2010, understanding that Vern (and Marion) Weber so well-served their local communities, Chester Dodgson and Rémi Tardif stepped forward, in continuing the care that the Pioneers of the Peace Country have come to expect. In 2021, Chester Dodgson retired by selling to Rémi Tardif.

A new crematorium was functional in April 2018. Based at the Peace River location, it is Alberta's northernmost crematorium.

In the lobby Peace River's Chapel's foyer, a pillar of brick supports a plaque indicating: "Show me the manner in which a nation or community cares for its dead and I will measure with mathematical exactness the tender sympathies of its people, their respect for the laws of the land and their loyalty to high ideals." - Gladstone.

Smith Funeral Home : Brooks, Alberta (AB)
Kelly Tanigami
Director / Embalmer
Email: kelly@sfh.ca
Phone: 403.362.4636
Cell Phone: 403.501.8821
Kelly Tanigami has been with Smith Funeral Home Ltd. since July, 1996. He was born in Brooks and raised in Rosemary. Kelly graduated from Rosemary High School in 1984 and later attended Medicine Hat College, Brooks Campus and Lethbridge Community College. He worked for Prins Brothers, Alpha Dairies and in Edmonton for Canada Safeway and also worked as a Massage Therapist in Calgary. Kelly is the first Japanese Licensed Funeral Director and Embalmer in Alberta, obtaining his Funeral Director and Embalmer’s License in 1999 from Mount Royal College, Calgary. Kelly is married to Shani and together have 3 daughters and 1 son. He is serving a second term with the Brooks Bandits Jr. A Hockey Club as Director previously serving as Director, Treasurer and Secretary. Kelly was also a member of Brooks’ Safe Communities and served as a Trustee of The Brooks and District Health Foundation. He enjoys hockey in winter and golf in the summer.
Joel Cyr
Director / Embalmer
Email: joel@sfh.ca
Phone: 403.362.4636
Cell Phone: 403.501.9106
Joel Cyr has been with Smith Funeral Home Ltd. since July, 2011. Joel was born in Edmonton and grew up in Beaumont, Alberta and raised in Red Deer, Alberta. He attended SAIT in Calgary to become a Journeyman Welder and worked as a Welder for 5 years. Joel then attended Mount Royal University, receiving a his Certificate as a Funeral Director and Embalmer in 2015. He is married to Keeley and has 3 daughters. Joel is a past Board Member of the Brooks Medieval Faire, serving in 2014 and 2016. He also is a member of the Brooks Library Board and a part time volunteer tutor for ABLE and ESL. Joel enjoys playing baseball, golfing, watching hockey and baseball, and most of all spending time with his girls.
Larry Regner
Funeral Attendant
Larry Regner, a Hanna native, graduated from the University of Calgary in 1972. He served thirty-two years in the Brooks area as a teacher and administrator at Berry Creek School, Brooks Junior High School, Griffin Park School, and Rolling Hills School, retiring in June 2005. Larry then spent some time in the equipment rental industry and joined Smith Funeral Home in 2008. Larry and Linda have been married since 1974. Together they have four children, ten grandchildren and one great-granddaughter. In addition to his contributions at Smith Funeral Home, travelling and family time, Larry enjoys sharing his musical talents at community events, charitable endeavors, and senior residences.
Follie Post
Funeral Attendant
Follie Post came to the Brooks area in 1979 as a member of the RCMP and holds the title as longest serving RCMP Member in Brooks, serving Brooks for 23 years. Follie retired from the RCMP in 2010 and joined Smith Funeral Home Ltd. in 2015. Follie is married to Debbie Tiegs and has 3 daughters, and 4 grandchildren. Follie has been involved with several businesses in Brooks, as well as serving on numerous Community Boards.
Grant Conrad
Funeral Attendant
Grant Conrad was born in Estevan, Saskatchewan and raised in Wadena, Saskatchewan. He joined the RCMP in 1979 and once training was completed was posted to Alberta where he served in the communities of Fairview, Peace River, Provost, Brooks, Lethbridge and Redcliff. In 2010, Grant retired in Brooks after 31 years of service. Grant is married to Peggy and together they have 3 sons and 2 grandchildren. Grant started working for Smith’s Funeral Home Ltd. in 2016. Grant enjoys woodworking year round, golfing and fishing in the summer and curling in the winter.
Jim Brack
Funeral Attendant
Jim Brack was raised in Indian Head, Saskatchewan and joined the Canadian Navy in 1961. In 1970, with an honourable discharge, he then moved to Kitchener, Ontario and worked as a Maintenance Electrician. Jim later moved to Alberta in 1973 and worked in the Oil and Gas industry, until 2007. In 2007, Jim started working as a Pastoral Assistant at St. Mary’s Catholic Church, Brooks, until retiring in 2019. Jim is also an active member of the Knights of Columbus. He joined Smith Funeral Home in 2019. Jim and his wife Christine have 3 children and 9 grandchildren. Jim enjoys camping, golfing, fishing, and watching the Brooks Bandits.
Kallie Parson
Apprentice
Email: kallie@sfh.ca
Phone: 403-362-4636
Kallie Parson is proud to announce that she is the newest Apprentice Funeral Director/Embalmer at Smith Funeral Home Ltd. and Crematorium. Born in Brooks, she takes great pride in serving the community she grew up in.
Kallie is currently enrolled in Mount Royal University’s Funeral Service Diploma program, while gaining hands-on experience within the funeral home. She is committed to learning every aspect of the profession and maintaining high standards of care.
Outside of her apprenticeship, Kallie values continuous learning and community involvement. She looks forward to growing within the funeral service profession and contributing to meaningful, compassionate end-of-life care.
Ron Amundson
Funeral Attendent
Ron Amundson grew up in Naicam, SK. He moved to Biggar, SK, where he was a co-owner of a grocery store. There he met and married his wife, Denise. He is the father of one son and 2 daughters. In 1997, after selling their share in the grocery store, Ron, Denise and their family moved to Brooks, AB to start up The $1 Store Plus, which was located in The Cassils Centre Mall. Together, Ron and Denise operated the store, as well as an annual Christmas Store, until the mall was closed in 2006. Ron and Denise then operated Tim Hortons until their retirement in 2020. Ron enjoys golfing, camping, and spending time with his family. He is recently a very proud grandpa of 2 little girls!

Kelly is the first Japanese Licensed Funeral Director and Embalmer in Alberta, obtaining his Funeral Director and Embalmer’s License in 1999 from Mount Royal College, Calgary. Kelly is married to Shani and together have 3 daughters and 1 son. He is serving a second term with the Brooks Bandits Jr. A Hockey Club as Director previously serving as Director, Treasurer and Secretary. Kelly was also a member of Brooks’ Safe Communities and served as a Trustee of The Brooks and District Health Foundation. He enjoys hockey in winter and golf in the summer.

![Joel Cyr](https://www.sfh.ca/fh_live/13800/13823/images/9_33367.jpg "Joel Cyr")

### Joel Cyr

##### Director / Embalmer

Email: [joel@sfh.ca](mailto:joel@sfh.ca)  
Phone: 403.362.4636  
Cell Phone: 403.501.9106  

Joel Cyr has been with Smith Funeral Home Ltd. since July, 2011. Joel was born in Edmonton and grew up in Beaumont, Alberta and raised in Red Deer, Alberta. He attended SAIT in Calgary to become a Journeyman Welder and worked as a Welder for 5 years. Joel then attended Mount Royal University, receiving a his Certificate as a Funeral Director and Embalmer in 2015. He is married to Keeley and has 3 daughters. Joel is a past Board Member of the Brooks Medieval Faire, serving in 2014 and 2016. He also is a member of the Brooks Library Board and a part time volunteer tutor for ABLE and ESL. Joel enjoys playing baseball, golfing, watching hockey and baseball, and most of all spending time with his girls.

![Larry Regner](https://www.sfh.ca/fh_live/13800/13823/images/9_33369.jpg "Larry Regner")

### Larry Regner

##### Funeral Attendant

Larry Regner, a Hanna native, graduated from the University of Calgary in 1972. He served thirty-two years in the Brooks area as a teacher and administrator at Berry Creek School, Brooks Junior High School, Griffin Park School, and Rolling Hills School, retiring in June 2005. Larry then spent some time in the equipment rental industry and joined Smith Funeral Home in 2008. Larry and Linda have been married since 1974. Together they have four children, ten grandchildren and one great-granddaughter. In addition to his contributions at Smith Funeral Home, travelling and family time, Larry enjoys sharing his musical talents at community events, charitable endeavors, and senior residences.

![Follie Post](https://www.sfh.ca/fh_live/13800/13823/images/9_33370.jpg "Follie Post")

### Follie Post

##### Funeral Attendant

Follie Post came to the Brooks area in 1979 as a member of the RCMP and holds the title as longest serving RCMP Member in Brooks, serving Brooks for 23 years. Follie retired from the RCMP in 2010 and joined Smith Funeral Home Ltd. in 2015. Follie is married to Debbie Tiegs and has 3 daughters, and 4 grandchildren. Follie has been involved with several businesses in Brooks, as well as serving on numerous Community Boards.

![Grant Conrad](https://www.sfh.ca/fh_live/13800/13823/images/9_33372.jpg "Grant Conrad")

### Grant Conrad

##### Funeral Attendant

Grant Conrad was born in Estevan, Saskatchewan and raised in Wadena, Saskatchewan. He joined the RCMP in 1979 and once training was completed was posted to Alberta where he served in the communities of Fairview, Peace River, Provost, Brooks, Lethbridge and Redcliff. In 2010, Grant retired in Brooks after 31 years of service. Grant is married to Peggy and together they have 3 sons and 2 grandchildren. Grant started working for Smith’s Funeral Home Ltd. in 2016. Grant enjoys woodworking year round, golfing and fishing in the summer and curling in the winter.

![Jim Brack](https://www.sfh.ca/fh_live/13800/13823/images/9_43073.png "Jim Brack")

### Jim Brack

##### Funeral Attendant

Jim Brack was raised in Indian Head, Saskatchewan and joined the Canadian Navy in 1961. In 1970, with an honourable discharge, he then moved to Kitchener, Ontario and worked as a Maintenance Electrician. Jim later moved to Alberta in 1973 and worked in the Oil and Gas industry, until 2007. In 2007, Jim started working as a Pastoral Assistant at St. Mary’s Catholic Church, Brooks, until retiring in 2019. Jim is also an active member of the Knights of Columbus. He joined Smith Funeral Home in 2019. Jim and his wife Christine have 3 children and 9 grandchildren. Jim enjoys camping, golfing, fishing, and watching the Brooks Bandits.

![Kallie Parson](https://www.sfh.ca/fh_live/13800/13823/images/9_56667.jpg "Kallie Parson")

### Kallie Parson

##### Apprentice

Email: [kallie@sfh.ca](mailto:kallie@sfh.ca)  
Phone: 403-362-4636  

Kallie Parson is proud to announce that she is the newest Apprentice Funeral Director/Embalmer at Smith Funeral Home Ltd. and Crematorium. Born in Brooks, she takes great pride in serving the community she grew up in.

Kallie is currently enrolled in Mount Royal University’s Funeral Service Diploma program, while gaining hands-on experience within the funeral home. She is committed to learning every aspect of the profession and maintaining high standards of care.

Outside of her apprenticeship, Kallie values continuous learning and community involvement. She looks forward to growing within the funeral service profession and contributing to meaningful, compassionate end-of-life care.

### Ron Amundson

##### Funeral Attendent

Ron Amundson grew up in Naicam, SK. He moved to Biggar, SK, where he was a co-owner of a grocery store. There he met and married his wife, Denise. He is the father of one son and 2 daughters. In 1997, after selling their share in the grocery store, Ron, Denise and their family moved to Brooks, AB to start up The $1 Store Plus, which was located in The Cassils Centre Mall. Together, Ron and Denise operated the store, as well as an annual Christmas Store, until the mall was closed in 2006. Ron and Denise then operated Tim Hortons until their retirement in 2020. Ron enjoys golfing, camping, and spending time with his family. He is recently a very proud grandpa of 2 little girls!

Obituary | Frances Christine Mortensen of Bassano, Alberta
Frances Christine Mortensen
April 30, 1940 - June 15, 2026
It is with heavy hearts that we announce the passing of Frances Mortensen, who left this world peacefully on the morning of June 15, 2026 at the age of 86 years. Fran was born in Dickson, Alberta on April 30th, 1940 to Peter and Dorothy. She was the heart of the family. Fran was a wife, mother, sister, cousin, grandmother, great grandmother and friend. She touched the lives of everyone who knew her. She always greeted you with smile, a big hug and usually one of her funny little “Grandma-isms”. Nearing the end, Fran, in her playful, carefree way, told us “If you don’t know something for sure, just make it up and make it sound good”. Fran met Don in early 1958 and were married that spring. Not long after they had their daughter, Carolynn, then Wayne, and a few years later, Loralee. She spent a lot of those years caring for Don after he got sick with kidney failure. Fran was so blessed to have such caring friends and family that stepped in to care for the kids when needed. She said many times how lucky she felt to have the people she did that helped out in many ways throughout those challenging years. It didn’t matter what Fran was facing, she did it with faith and an unwavering positivity. Don and Fran moved off the farm in Tilley into Brooks in the early 1980’s. They enjoyed their time in Brooks as they were so close to a lot of the family and friends. Their journey took them to Calgary in December 1996 where Don needed to be closer to the hospital as his kidney failure progressed. It was just before Christmas when they moved in, and everything was still packed up but Fran had to have a Christmas Tree. She found the decorations and got the tree set up just in time to host her big Christmas dinner. In 2006, Don and Fran’s journey then took them to Medicine Hat so he could continue his dialysis treatment there. Sadly, Don passed away a few years later in January 2008. Fran then moved to Bassano. She settled in quickly and enjoyed living in with her daughter, Carolynn. She had lots of family and friends nearby which was always so important to her. You could pop by anytime for a visit and guaranteed she have a chocolate or sweet treat to offer. Fran was diagnosed with cancer in January 2016. She endured a very long, challenging few months during and after her treatment. But, she was determined to get healthy and back to travelling. That next year, she celebrated her clean bill of health with taking her entire family on a cruise. There were a lot of good memories made on that trip. Fran loved her garden, sitting out in the sunshine on her beautiful patio surrounded by her flowers, she loved ice cream treats, chocolate, and everything Christmas. Up until a few years ago, she still baked us all a Christmas Cookie tray with her favourite treats. In years prior, when she still in good health, she sure enjoyed travelling. She enjoyed many of her golden years with her travel partner and good friend, Jim Ion. They went on some pretty spectacular adventures that she never expected to experience. Fran was humble, kind, caring and sometimes a little worry wart. She always wanted to make sure everyone else was okay and taken care of. Fran passed away peacefully on the morning of June 15, 2026. Her last days and moments were surrounded by so much love. Her family gathered around her, sharing stories, favourite memories, looked through old photo albums, had some tears, and had a lot of laughs. She left an amazing legacy behind that lives throughout her family. We will forever cherish her memory and carry forward all that she taught us. Rest peacefully, Grams. You were so deeply loved, and you will be greatly missed. Fran is survived by her children, Carolynn, Wayne, Loralee (Scot); sister, Pat Duckett; grandchildren, Julie (Dustin), Suzy (Shaun) Jody, Kayla (Aidan), Casey and Mason (Katie); great grandchildren, Marley, Lochlyn, Gabrielle, Courtney, Emry and Macy and her much loved nieces and nephews. She was pre-deceased by her husband of almost 50 years, Donald Mortensen; parents, Peter and Dorothy Skau; Don’s mother, Marie Mortensen; brothers and sisters-in-law, Arthur and Kathy Skau, Kathy and Charlie Palmer, Bill Mortensen, Bob Duckett and grandson, James Mortensen. A private graveside service will be held at Bethany Lutheran Church Cemetery. Rev. John Theiss officiating. A Celebration of Life will be held on Saturday, June 20th at 2:00 PM from Bassano Pioneer Damsiter Drop In Centre, 317 – 2nd Avenue, Bassano, Alberta. In memory of Fran, if friends desire, memorial tributes may be made directly to Canadian Cancer Society, 325 Manning Road NE, Calgary, Alberta T2E 2P5.

SERVICES 
Celebration of Life
Saturday, June 20, 2026 
2:00 PM
Bassano Pioneer Damsiter Drop In Centre 
317 – 2nd Avenue 
Bassano, Alberta

It is with deep sorrow that we announce the passing of Vernon ‘Joe’ James LaRue Brown. Joe passed away at home at the age of 86 years. Joe, or ‘Pop’ to Angie and Rayne Jackson or ‘Mr. CAT’ as Sam Glover used to call him, was born to Don and Agnes Brown of Delburne, Alberta on May 20, 1940. Joe spent eighty-five of his eighty-six years at Delburne. Much of his pre-school years were spent riding on a “CAT” with his dad, breaking land for local farmers. That set a precedent for Joe. He was running his own “CAT” at seventeen and continued working for farmers until he was seventy-seven years old. He always said, “I loved every minute of it!”. Joe took his schooling in Delburne, then went to both NAIT and SAIT where he obtained his Red Seal in Automotive and Heavy Duty Mechanics. He was always proud about going from his 2nd year automotive to being a direct entry into 3rd year Heavy Duty and being top of the class! That is something to be proud of for sure! After working all day on the CAT, brushing or road building, he spent many more hours in the shop working on tractors, vehicles, motorbikes or snowmobiles, or anything else. Ang remembers many phone calls or guys coming over to have Pop fix something for them. Joe and his dad, Don Brown, had the Ford dealership and a Kawasaki dealership in Delburne. Joe loved most things “antique”, but his favorite was the 1936 Diamond T he found in Manitoba. It is much the same as his dad trucked with in the 1930’s and 1940’s when Browns Transport was the first trucking company on Highway 21. It was his pride & joy. He drove his Diamond T or the 1916 McLaughlin Buick in the Delburne parade for many years. Joe visited Ireland a couple of times, and said it felt like he was home. He had hoped to return there. Joe didn’t have any children of his own, but Angie Jackson was lucky to call him Dad for the last fifty years and Rayne Jackson called him Pop. Joe was so proud of his granddaughter Rayne. He taught her to drive the McLaughlin and loved to boast about how good she drove it. Joe is lovingly remembered by his daughter Angie (Lèo) and granddaughter, Rayne (Philip), his sister, Elaine Smith (Bill) and his brother, Jack Brown and his sister-in-law, Mavis Brown, as well as numerous nieces and nephews and lots of people that loved him. Lots of Angies’ friends called Joe their second dad. He was predeceased by his parents, Don and Agnes Brown, his sisters, Vera Jefferies and Marion Walker, and his brother, Marl Brown. A Celebration of Joe’s Life will be held at a later date.

Condolences, memories and photos may be shared and viewed at www.parklandfuneralhome.com. Arrangements in care of Parkland Funeral Home and Crematorium, 6287 – 67 A Street (Taylor Drive), Red Deer. 403.340.4040.

Obituary | Albert (Bud) Wald of Clairmont, Alberta
Albert (Bud) Wald, long-time resident of Grimshaw, died peacefully on June 21, 2026 at the age of 82.
Bud was born August 28, 1943 in Last Lake, Alberta and grew up in the Brownvale area. He was the next to youngest of Frank and Pearl Wald’s 13 children. Bud was raised on the Blue Hawk farm and his parents instilled a love for the land and animals, and also a strong work ethic.
On July 30, 1965 Bud married Anita Sheehan, and together they raised four children – Monica Brown (Gary) of Red Deer, Colleen Sklapsky (Kevin) of Grimshaw, Deidre Livingston of Grande Prairie and Aaron, who resides in Sparks, Nevada. Bud was blessed with three beautiful granddaughters and five amazing great grandchildren.
Not long after the arrival of their first child, Bud and Anita relocated to Enterprise Northwest Territories where Bud worked building railroad beds for Thornhill. Not long after, Bud’s work on the railroad brought him back to the Peace Country, finally settling in Grimshaw in 1967. After some time spent building railroad beds in the Grande Prairie area, Bud joined his brother Dick and brother-in-law Martin Sheehan in their trucking and oilfield company Sheehan & Wald. Eventually, Bud bought out Martin’s interest in Sheehan & Wald and Wald Bros Trucking Ltd. was born. Bud and Dick ran that business for many successful years with the help of a number of loyal long-term employees who Bud always considered friends first and foremost.
In December 1988, the brothers sold Wald Brothers and Bud returned to his roots and retired to a life on the farm. Bud’s adventures in farming involved many animals over the years – from horses, Amos the Bull and the rest of his Gelbvieh cattle, the infamous pig Shirley, Thunder the rooster and his hens, ducks, a llama, a sheep and pretty much anything with four legs and fur. There was always a continual stream of his beloved dogs including Chester, Hannah and Trixie. If an animal needed a good home, everyone for miles around knew the best place was Bud’s farm!!
One of Bud’s retirement hobbies was Chuckwagon racing. It kept him close to animals and fed his love of everything from the old west. It also brought him many great friends from the wagon racing world, and he enjoyed livestreaming every event through the year. After leaving chuckwagon racing behind, Bud ventured into raising purebred Gelbvieh cattle. His cattle were always top notch selling all over Norh America, and did well every year in Edmonton at Farmfair International, including winning Grand Champion Gelbvieh female in 2002.
In 2006 Bud and Anita sold the farm and settled into their new home at the Fish Pond. The house was strategically placed to allow an unobstructed view from the recliner in the living room, where Bud would watch the fish jump, and keep a keen eye out for “rats” trying to poach from his pond. He also had two greenhouses, a large garden and too many fruit trees and berry bushes to count. Bud also built three cabins at the Fish Pond and the place became a magnet for friends and family
to spend days fishing, barbecuing and playing games. Bud also built an icehouse, and winter get togethers at the cabin always meant cutting ice from the pond to fill it.
Finally, last year, Bud and Anita moved to Clairmont to Lakeview Seniors home to be closer to their daughter, and as importantly for Bud, her garden and her dog Finn. In his short time there, Bud engaged with all the planting and watering and helped install his homemade irrigation system. And Bud would always have a treat in his pocket for Finn who followed Bud around the yard all day long. In the winter and when he wasn’t gardening you could find Bud in his puzzle room, likely putting together one version or another of Snoopy and the rest of the Charlie Brown gang.
Bud is predeceased by his parents, Frank and Pearl, his siblings Eleanor Coates, Ed, John, Jack, Dick, Florence Quinney, Ted, Frank, Dune, and Herman.
He is survived by his wife of 60 years Anita, and his four children, his grandchildren Alicia Zumbusch (Daniel), Kayln (Kurt) Shug and Ashley Sklapsky, and great grandchildren Camara, Madison, Reese, Brooklynn and Sydnee. He is also survived by his sister Rose (Sheehan) and brother Hubert.
A funeral service will be held on Saturday, June 27, 2026 at the Holy Family Catholic Church in Grimshaw, AB at 11:00 am. Funeral Arrangements are under the direction of Chapel of Memories Peace River.
If friends so desire, donations can be made to the Alberta Cancer Foundation or the charity of one’s choice.

To plant Memorial Trees in memory of Albert (Bud) Wald, please click here to visit our sympathy store.

text:
Obituary | Mary Hryniuk of Fairview, Alberta
Mary Hryniuk was born in Innisfail, Alberta on July 30, 1927. Tragically her mother passed away while giving birth to her. Later her father remarried, and Mary was pleased to welcome 3 brothers (Wilfred, Elmer, and Walter). Growing up on the family farm the children shared in the many chores and responsibilities of early homesteading life. Mary attended a one room school at Peers, Alberta, however had to leave schooling at the age of 13 to start work in order to support the family.
While employed with Northern Alberta Railways, she met Stan Hryniuk. Their marriage was blessed with 2 sons, Larry (Brenda) and Brian (Donna). Marry and Stan worked for the railway until Stan changed careers and began working for the Province of Alberta. In 1967 the family moved to Fairview, Alberta where stan worked for the Fairview College.
In the spring of 1968, tragedy struck when a highway accident claimed the lives of Wilfred and his wife Adeline leaving behind five children, Deloris Schmidek (Dale), Stanley Schmidek, Sharon (Brian Noullett), Gerry Schmidek, and Terry Schmidek. The family immediately grew from 4 to 9 however with the love and support of Mary and Stan the family prospered and grew as one family.
In 1971, Mary and Stan together with the 3 youngest children moved to Lethbridge, Alberta. After the children left the household Mary and Stan moved back to Edmonton, Alberta and upon retirement moved to Kelowna, British Columbia, where family members enjoyed family vacations.
In 1996, Stan passed away and in 1997 Mary moved to Peace River, Alberta, where Larry and Brenda resided and closer to Fairview, Alberta. Mary loved nothing better than having a house full for meals and get togethers.
Mary loved playing crib, arguing politics, enjoying friends at the legion, and camping at 5 Star.
In October of 2024 Mary moved to Heritage Towers before being transferred to Fairview Long Term Care in March of 2026 where she later passed.
Mary was predeceased by Terry Schmidek (2024) however was blessed in addition to her surviving children with 11 grandchildren and 18 grandchildren.
Mary lived a full and healthy life. She will be missed by her family and friends however all will celebrate that Mary was part of their life.
A Celebration of Life will be held at the Peace River Legion at 1:00 P.M. on Saturday October 3rd.

To plant Memorial Trees in memory of Mary Hryniuk, please click here to visit our sympathy store.

Father | Verses for Funeral Cards
#F1 – What is a Farmer
Author: Unknown
Farmers are found in fields, tilling,
Seeding, fertilizing, spraying,
Dairying and harvesting.
Wives help them, little boys follow them,
The Agricultural Department
Confuses them, city relatives visit them,
Salesmen detain them, meals wait for them,
Weather can delay them, but it takes
Heaven to stop them!
#F2 – Parents
Author: Unknown
Because God knew your work was o’er
Your children taught and grown,
He called you both to come and dwell
Where no more work is done.
Where the golden sun doth never set,
And the sky’s forever blue.
It’s there, we hope, in God’s good time,
#F3 – Here’s to the Farmer
Author: Frank Pavlick
Here’s to the farmer whose work never stops,
Out forecasting cattle and combines and crops.
Surrounded by problems, he does what he can,
To feed and provide though he’s only one man.
Here’s to the famer at work every day,
Out earning his living the honorable way,
Not fancy or better, just hours on the land.
Out doing his darndest to give God a hand.
Here’s to the farmer who patiently goes,
Courageously hoping to reap what he sows,
And as he receives he is willing to share,
The kindness a farmer exhibits is rare.
Here’s to the farmer, whatever his name,
Each farmer belongs in the Heart Hall of Fame,
Helping the health of the world sink or swim,
Whatever it takes, he will do, that’s just him.
Here’s to the farmer, in short, that is it.,
His motto is build in a birth, Never Quit,
There’s one thing for sure, a good man can be found,
#F4 – I’ve Planted a Kernel
Author: Unknown
I’ve planted many a kernel of wheat,
Welcomed many a morning sun.
I’ve eaten the dust and tested the wind,
And I’ve gotten many a good job done.
I’ve climbed off the tractor with dirt on my face,
And pain in my weary bones,
But somehow, I always can master a grin,
When I see the light of home.
Where my family waits, and the love of my life.
Sets a table fit for a king.
With her smile, and a hug, and a coffee mug.
I know I have everything.
As I trudge once more through the field of my years,
And separate the chaff from the grain,
I thank the good Lord, I can say in my heart
That is’ do it all over again.
#F5 – From Parent to Child
Author: Unknown
I gave you life,
But I cannot live it for you.
I can teach you things,
But I cannot make you learn.
I can give you directions, but
I cannot be there to lead you.
I can allow you freedom,
But I cannot account for it.
I can take you to church,
But I cannot make you believe.
I can teach you right from wrong,
But I cannot always decide for you.
I can buy you beautiful clothes,
But I cannot make you beautiful inside.
I can offer you advice
But I cannot accept it for you.
I can give you love
But I cannot force it upon you.
I can teach you to share,
But I cannot make you unselfish.
I can teach you to respect, but I cannot
Force you to show honour.
I can advise you about friends,
But I cannot choose them for you.
I can teach you about kindness,
But I cannot force you to be gracious.
I can warn you about sins,
But I cannot make your morals.
I can pray for you,
#F6 – Cowboy’s Prayer
Author: Unknown
Heavenly Father, we pause mindful at the many blessings
You have bestowed upon us.
We ask that you guide us in the arena of life.
We don’t ask for special favours,
We don’t ask not to draw around a chute-fighting horse
Or to never break a barrier
Nor do we ask for all daylight runs
Or not to draw a steer that won’t lay.
Help us Lord, to live our lives in such a manner
That when we make that last inevitable ride
To the country up there where the grass grows
Lush, green, and stirrup high;
And the water runs cool, clear and deep
That you as our last judge will tell us
That our entry fees are paid
#F7 – Fisherman’s Lament
Author: H. McCormick
Let me gather my tackle and fishing gear
And go down to the water’s edge
Let me catch the big one that got away
As I fished from the rocky ledge;
I cast my line in a likely spot
It becomes entangled and entwined
But I pull and tug to get it free
For I’m not the quitting kind;
I break my line and I lose my lure
And the boat springs a leak or two
The sun wreaks vengeance; mosquitoes bite
Before the day is through;
I’ve had enough to drive me mad
Just fisherman’s luck I suppose
But I have gone to another place
#F8 – To My Dad
Author: Frank Pavlick
I’d like to say Thank you Dad, for everything you’ve done,
If anybody helped me grow I know you are the one.
It isn’t easy to express, exactly how I feel,
But there’s one thing I know for sure,
The feelings are for real.
I think of all the special help, your knowledge and advice,
Just doing everything you can,
To make my whole world nice.
And though I know that discipline, is something Dad’s must do,
Please understand I never meant,
To do things to hurt you.
No matter what the future holds, in happy times or bad,
Some words will always stay the same,
Like these…
#F9 – A Cowboy’s Prayer
Author: Unknown
Oh Lord,
I’ve never lived where the churches grow.
I love creation better as it stood
That a day you finished it so long ago
And looked upon Your work and called it good.
I know that others find You in the light
That’s sifted down through tinted window panes,
And yet I seem to feel You near tonight.
In this dim, quiet starlight on the plains.
I thank you Lord, that I am placed so well,
That You have made my freedom so complete;
That I’m no slave to whistle, clock or bell,
Nor weak-eyed prisoner of wall and street.
Just let me live my life as I’ve begun
And give me work that’s open to the sky;
Make me a partner of the wind and sun,
And I won’t ask a life that’s soft or high.
#F10 – Our Family is a Circle
Author: Unknown
Our family is a circle
Without a beginning or an end,
Always bending, never breaking,
In this love we can depend.
Love holds us together
As in life we travel round,
From one generation to another
Years of love are handed down.
When crisis comes upon us
And pulls us end to end,
If God is our center
We know that we will mend.
So, remember in this family
You are a special part
Of a love that starts with God
#F11 – Dad
Author: Unknown
To the man who guided the way,
I only wonder why you couldn’t stay.
We didn’t even get to say goodbye,
Within ourselves we can’t help wondering why.
In your silent way you gave us hope,
When life seemed to go in a downward slope.
Your smile that we remember best,
#F12 – A Farmer’s Creed
Author: Unknown
I believe a man’s greatest possession is his dignity and that
No calling bestows this more abundantly that farming.
I believe hard work and honest sweat
Are the building blocks of a person’s character.
I believe that farming, despite its hardships and disappointments
Is the most honest and honorable way
A man can spend his days on this earth.
I believe faming provides education for life and that no other
Occupation teaches so much about birth, growth
And maturity in such a variety of ways.
I believe that many of the best things in life are indeed free;
The splendor of a sunrise, the rapture of a wide-open spaces,
The exhilarating sight of your land greening each spring.
I believe true happiness comes from watching
Your crops ripen in the field,
Your children grow tall in the sun, your whole family
Feeling the pride that springs from their shared experience.
I believe that by my toil I am giving more to the world
Than I am asking from it
An honor that does not come to all men.
I believe my life will be measured ultimately by what I have done for my fellow man, and by this standard I fear no judgement.
I believe when a man grows old and sums up his days,
He should be able to stand tall and feel pride in the life he’s lived. 
I believe in farming because it makes all this possible.
#F13 – A Dad
Author: Unknown
A Dad gives,
A Dad shares
A Dad helps
Because he cares.
A Dad teaches
And gives praise,
And lends support
In so many ways.
A Dad listens
To hopes and fears
As he guides you
Through the years,
Then he gently
Let you go –
His love is greater
#F14 – A Man’s Last Ride
Author: Albertine Kiyawasew
The tall man softly brushes
The stallion’s shining coat.
He is careful as he combs and braids the mane.
As he walks towards the saddle rack
A sudden smile comes over his face,
As he thinks of his loved ones
He says a silent prayer for them.
As he pulls the blanket
Over the horse’s broad back,
He settles his dark, brown eyes
On the west, towards the setting sun.
Thinking of all his happy moments
He gently puts the saddle on,
Careful not to pinch the animal.
When he’s done he looks up with pride
For his old body hasn’t let him down.
The man slowly pulls himself up
Onto the horse in a tall erect pose.
He looks one last time around
And his voice, carried in the wind
Whispers one last goodbye to his family.
And like lightning, the horse carries him off
Towards the sun and his Creator.
#F15 – Daddy’s Girl
Author: Unknown
Daddy’s gone to Heaven
He left with God today
Flying on the wings of Angels
When God took him away
God called and Daddy answered
God needs him more than I
I had him but a little while
Before he said goodbye
Daddy knows I love him
Though I never got to say
I love you to my Daddy
Before he went away
Now Daddy flies with Angels
And someday I will see
The outstretched arms of Daddy
Reaching out for me.

Obituary | Harry Batt of Fort Vermilion, Alberta
It is with sadness that the family of Harry Batt announces his passing on June 15, 2026, at the age of 86 years.
Harry spent much of his life farming and took great pride in the land, the work he did, and the life he built. His strong work ethic, dedication, and commitment to his family and community were evident in everything he did. Farming was more than an occupation to Harry—it was a way of life that he cherished for many years.
Harry will be remembered for his kindness, strength, and the many friendships he formed throughout his life. He touched the lives of many with his warm spirit and generous heart. Whether spending time with family and friends, sharing stories, or lending a helping hand, Harry left a lasting impression on everyone who knew him.
He will be deeply missed and lovingly remembered by his family, friends, and all whose lives he enriched.
A Funeral Service will be held on Saturday, June 20, 2026, at 2:00 p.m. at the Rocky Lane Agricultural Hall in Rocky Lane, Alberta. A viewing will take place one hour prior to the service, beginning at 1:00 p.m.
The family extends their heartfelt gratitude to everyone for their support, prayers, and expressions of sympathy during this difficult time.
Forever remembered, forever missed.

To plant Memorial Trees in memory of Harry Batt, please click here to visit our sympathy store.

Obituary | Bertram 'Bert' Wienss of Manning, Alberta
Bertram (Bert) Wienss, long-time residence of Hawk Hills, Alberta, passed away on July 10, 2026, at the age of 70 years.
Bert was predeceased by his parents Walter and Christel Wienss.
He is survived by a sister Sigrid Quinn (Harry) of St. Albert, AB and Renate McAlorum (John) of Cobble Hill, BC. A niece (Kristina) and her son (Dawson), nephews (Brendan and Josh), as well as his stepmother Elizabeth Wienss of Abbotsford, BC.
Bert was born in Red Deer in 1955 and moved to Hawk Hills with his family as a young boy when his father Walter started to homestead in Hawk Hills.
Bert worked on the farm his entire life, as well as trucking for many years in between harvest and seeding. He worked on the land in Hawk Hill side by side with his father until Walter retired to Abbotsford.
Bert leaves behind many good friends throughout the entire Peace Country.
A sincere thank you to the doctors, nurses, and support staff of the Manning Hospital, who showed compassion and care, and made Bert’s final months comfortable. Bert was able to make many day trips with friends and family, going for lunch or coffee, checking on the farm and area crops, and keeping tabs on repairs to his Dodge and Kenworth trucks.
A small memorial for family and friends will be held at a later date.

# Obituary | Bertram 'Bert' Wienss of Manning, Alberta

Bertram (Bert) Wienss, long-time residence of Hawk Hills, Alberta, passed away on July 10, 2026, at the age of 70 years.

 Bert was predeceased by his parents Walter and Christel Wienss.

 He is survived by a sister Sigrid Quinn (Harry) of St. Albert, AB and Renate McAlorum (John) of Cobble Hill, BC. A niece (Kristina) and her son (Dawson), nephews (Brendan and Josh), as well as his stepmother Elizabeth Wienss of Abbotsford, BC.

 Bert was born in Red Deer in 1955 and moved to Hawk Hills with his family as a young boy when his father Walter started to homestead in Hawk Hills.

 Bert worked on the farm his entire life, as well as trucking for many years in between harvest and seeding. He worked on the land in Hawk Hill side by side with his father until Walter retired to Abbotsford.

 Bert leaves behind many good friends throughout the entire Peace Country.

 A sincere thank you to the doctors, nurses, and support staff of the Manning Hospital, who showed compassion and care, and made Bert’s final months comfortable. Bert was able to make many day trips with friends and family, going for lunch or coffee, checking on the farm and area crops, and keeping tabs on repairs to his Dodge and Kenworth trucks.

 A small memorial for family and friends will be held at a later date.

  
To plant Memorial Trees in memory of **Bertram 'Bert' Wienss**, please [click here to visit our sympathy store](https://www.northernalbertafunerals.com/obituary/bertram-bert-wienss/gifts?campaign=obituaryThemed-gifts-textLink-obitText).

HUGHES, Randolph ‘Randy’ Joseph Kevin Harley

(Bowie)

1961 – 2026


It is with great despair to announce the sudden passing of our father, grandfather, brother, uncle, and friend to many. Randolph ‘Randy’ Joseph Kevin Harley Hughes passed away Monday, July 6, 2026. Randy was born to parents Daniel and Ida (nee Schreader) Hughes on Thursday, November 16, 1961, in Montreal, Quebec. Randy lovingly leaves behind sons, Kevin Hughes (Ashley Lazzarotto), Shane Netrefa (Leanne Brown) and Sheldon Netrefa; and his sole daughter, Jennifer Sawyer (Kris Sawyer). Randy was also a proud grandfather to eight grandchildren; Malina Renaud, Trinty Brown, Capri Fraser, Hannah Brown, Isabelle Fraser, Ayden Umbach, Ryder Foster, Jackson Foster. Randy leaves behind siblings; Deborah Hughes, Donald Hughes (Sue Hughes) Cindy Fancie, Jack Hughes and Joey Hughes (Caroline Hughes). He leaves behind former wife and dear friend, Jacqueline ‘Jacci’ Izat. Randy is predeceased by his parents, Daniel and Ida (nee Schreader) Hughes; and brother-in-law, Sonny Fancie


Colossians 3:12–14

“Therefore, as God’s chosen people, holy and dearly loved, clothe

yourselves with compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness and patience.

Bear with each other… And over all these virtues put on love, which binds

them all together in perfect unity.”


Randy was a kind and loving man, his time most cherished was with family especially his grandchildren. He offered love and laughter to all those who crossed his path and will be deeply missed. Randy had a gift of turning any stranger into a friend and creating unforgettable connections with everyone he met. We can learn from Randy’s loving demeanor; take the time to say hello to someone new, check in on your loved ones, and remember life moves quickly so capture all the small moments. A Celebration of Life in Randy’s honour will be held at the Eckville Community Center, 5305 - 52 Street, Eckville, Alberta.on Saturday, August 22, 2026 at 1:00 p.m. A moment of Fellowship and Remembrance will follow the Celebration of Life. We invite all those who knew Randy to come celebrate and remember his time with us. Condolences, memories and photos may be shared and viewed at www.parklandfuneralhome.com. Arrangements in care of Parkland Funeral Home and Crematorium, 6287 – 67 A Street (Taylor Drive), Red Deer. 403.340.4040.
